english: but chiefly those who walk after the flesh in the lust of defilement and despise authority. Daring, self-willed, they are not afraid to speak evil of dignitaries,

paite: Angel hatna leh thilhihtheihna neite'n amaute dem in Toupa ma ah agense ngei kei uhi.
english: whereas angels, though greater in might and power, don’t bring a slanderous judgment against them before the Lord.

paite: Himahleh hiaite'n bel ganhing ngaihtuahna nei lou, mat a hihman dingte bang in, thil atheihlouhte uh agensia uhi.
english: But these, as unreasoning creatures, born natural animals to be taken and destroyed, speaking evil in matters about which they are ignorant, will in their destroying surely be destroyed,

paite: Amau diktatlouhna gah lou in asegawp ding ua, suntang lai a zu leh sa kham a buai nuamsami ahi uh. Na kiang ua ankuang alui un, amau kikhemna ankuanglui ahih ziak un, thanghuaina gensiatna ahi uhi.
english: receiving the wages of unrighteousness; people who count it pleasure to revel in the daytime, spots and defects, reveling in their deceit while they feast with you;

paite: Mit angkawmna a dim, khelhna tawpsan theiloute anei ua; mikiploute akhempuk ua; en hat lungsim apu ua; hamsethuak tate ahi uhi.
english: having eyes full of adultery, and who can’t cease from sin, enticing unsettled souls, having a heart trained in greed, accursed children!

paite: Beor tapa Balaam, thilhihkhelhna, loh deihpa lampi atot ziak un lam dik paisan in avakmang uhi.
english: Forsaking the right way, they went astray, having followed the way of Balaam the son of Beor, who loved the wages of wrongdoing;

paite: Himahleh amah atatlekna ziak in taihilh in a-omta a; sabiltung pau thei lou mihing pau in ahong pau a, zawlnei haina akham hi.
english: but he was rebuked for his own disobedience. A speechless donkey spoke with a man’s voice and stopped the madness of the prophet.

paite: Hiaite tuikhuk tui om lou leh tuimei huihpi mutleng ahi ua; amaute a ding in nuailam mial sah meuhmouh sit ahita hi.
english: These are wells without water, clouds driven by a storm, for whom the blackness of darkness has been reserved forever.

paite: Thugina lou chiak zen a gen in gitlouhna lak a kipan a taikhete, taksa utna ah hukna in akhempuk nak uhi.
english: For, uttering great swelling words of emptiness, they entice in the lusts of the flesh, by licentiousness, those who are indeed escaping from those who live in error;

paite: Amau siatna sikha hi kawmpi in mite sikha suahtakna thu achiam nak uhi; mite'n zohsa achihte mah in amau sikha in abawl nak hi.
english: promising them liberty, while they themselves are bondservants of corruption; for a man is brought into bondage by whoever overcomes him.

paite: Toupa leh Hondampa Jesu Khrist atheih ziak ua khovel thanghuainate ataikhiaksan nung ua, huai mah a apuk nawn ua, zoh a a-om nawn ualeh zaw, amasa sang in a-omdan nanung uh ahong hoih keizaw hi.
english: For if, after they have escaped the defilement of the world through the knowledge of the Lord and Savior Jesus Christ, they are again entangled in it and overcome, the last state has become worse for them than the first.

paite: Diktatna lampi pen theih nung a, thupiak siangthou akiang ua kepsak nungngatsan sang in, diktatna lampi thei lou hi le uh amau a ding in ahoihzaw ding hi.
english: For it would be better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than after knowing it, to turn back from the holy commandment delivered to them.

paite: "Ui ama luak ah akik nawn a, vokpi kisilsiangsa leng buannawi ah kisil ding in akik nawn chih paunak diktak amaute tung ah atungta hi.”
english: But it has happened to them according to the true proverb, “The dog turns to his own vomit again,” and “the sow that has washed to wallowing in the mire.”

paite: Deihtakte aw, tua na kiang ua ka gelh laikhak nihna ahi. Hiaite gel ah theih thak nawnna in na lungsim siang uh ka tokthou hi.
english: This is now, beloved, the second letter that I have written to you; and in both of them I stir up your sincere mind by reminding you

paite: Zawlnei siangthoute thugenkholh leh na sawltakte uh kam a Toupa leh Hondampa thupiak na theihgigena ding un.
english: that you should remember the words which were spoken before by the holy prophets and the commandment of us, the apostles of the Lord and Savior,

paite: Hiai thei masa un, ni nanungte ah, misimmoh hatte amau utna bang a om in, simmoh kawm in ahong pai ding uhi.
english: knowing this first, that in the last days mockers will come, walking after their own lusts

paite: Ahong pai nawnna thuchiam koi ah? Siam tung a kipan bangkim a-om ngeingei bang in pi-le-pute ihmut ni a kipan in a-om zel ngal a! ahon chi ding uhi.
english: and saying, “Where is the promise of his coming? For, from the day that the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation.”

paite: Pathian thu in nidanglai pek in vante ahong om achih akitheihmohbawl ua, tui a kipan leh tui zang a leitung kibawl ahi a,
english: For they willfully forget that there were heavens from of old, and an earth formed out of water and amid water by the word of God,

paite: huai tui mah in atum a, amangthangta hi.
english: by which means the world that existed then, being overflowed with water, perished.

paite: Himahleh tua vante leh lei omte huai thu mah in Pathian limsak lou mite vaihawm leh manthat ni a ding a sit in mei hihsiat ding a kholkhawm ahita hi.
english: But the heavens that exist now and the earth, by the same word have been stored up for fire, being reserved against the day of judgment and destruction of ungodly men.

paite: Himahleh deihtakte aw, hiai thu kam khat pen mangngilh kei un, Toupa ngaih in ni khat tuh kum sangkhat bang ahi a, huan kum sangkhat leng ni khat bang ahi, chih.
english: But don’t forget this one thing, beloved, that one day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day.

paite: Mi khenkhat in zekai asak bang un Toupa zaw athuchiam ah azekai kei hi; kuamah manthat deih lou a, mi tengteng hong kisik deih in noumau lam ah adohzou zaw ahi.
english: The Lord is not slow concerning his promise, as some count slowness; but he is patient with us, not wishing that anyone should perish, but that all should come to repentance.

paite: Himahleh Toupa ni zaw guta bang in ahong tung ding; huai ni chiang in nakpitak a ging in vante amangthang ding, thilbulte mei a haitui in a-om ding a, lei leh asung a nasep omte, akangtum ding hi.
english: But the day of the Lord will come as a thief in the night, in which the heavens will pass away with a great noise, and the elements will be dissolved with fervent heat; and the earth and the works that are in it will be burned up.

paite: Huai thilte huchibang a mangthang vek ding uh ahi chih na theih un, omdan siangthou leh Pathian limsakna lam ah mi bangchibang hi ding na hi ua.
english: Therefore, since all these things will be destroyed like this, what kind of people ought you to be in holy living and godliness,

paite: Pathian' Ni ahong tun baihna ding lamen leh phatuamngaitak a ngak in; huai ni atun ziak in vante hong kang in amangthang dia, thilbulte leng mei a haltui in a-omta ding hi.
english: looking for and earnestly desiring the coming of the day of God, which will cause the burning heavens to be dissolved, and the elements will melt with fervent heat?

paite: Himahleh athuchiam bang in van thak leh lei thak, asung a diktatna omte i lamen hi.
english: But, according to his promise, we look for new heavens and a new earth, in which righteousness dwells.

paite: Huaiziak in deihtakte aw, huai bang thilte na lamet ziak un nin baang lou leh gensiatbei in, khamuangtak a na om uh ahon muhtheihna ding in thanop suah un.
english: Therefore, beloved, seeing that you look for these things, be diligent to be found in peace, without defect and blameless in his sight.

paite: Huan i unaupa deihtak Paul in leng akiang a pilna piak bang zel a na kiang ua agelh bang in Toupa dohzohna hotdamna in sim un.
english: Regard the patience of our Lord as salvation; even as our beloved brother Paul also, according to the wisdom given to him, wrote to you,

paite: Alaikhak tengteng ah huai thute gen in, huai mah bang in agelh hi. Huai ah thu theihhak thu thukte a-om a, huaite mipil lou leh mikiploute'n Laisiangthou dang angaihkawi bang un angaikawi ua, amau leh amau siatna ding in azang uhi.
english: as also in all of his letters, speaking in them of these things. In those, there are some things that are hard to understand, which the ignorant and unsettled twist, as they also do to the other Scriptures, to their own destruction.

paite: Huchi in deihtakte aw, noute'n tua thute na theihkholh ziak un pilvang un, huchi lou in zaw migiloute diklouhna a pimang a om in, na kipna ua kipan na pukkha ding uhi.
english: You therefore, beloved, knowing these things beforehand, beware, lest being carried away with the error of the wicked, you fall from your own steadfastness.

paite: Himahleh i Toupa leh Hondampa Jesu Khrist hehpihna leh theihna ah hong khang un. Tu leh tangtawn in amah kiang ah thupina om hen, Amen.
english: But grow in the grace and knowledge of our Lord and Savior Jesus Christ. To him be the glory both now and forever. Amen.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, Saul sih nung in Amalekte zou khin David ahong kik nawn a, Ziklag ah David ni nih a-om hi.
english: After the death of Saul, when David had returned from the slaughter of the Amalekites, and David had stayed two days in Ziklag,

paite: Hichi ahong hi a, ani thum ni in, ngai in, mi khat Saul panmun a kipan apuante bohkeksa leh alu a lei kai niaunuau in ahong pai hi.
english: on the third day, behold, a man came out of the camp from Saul, with his clothes torn and earth on his head. When he came to David, he fell to the earth and showed respect.

paite: David kiang ahong tun in lei a bokkhup in zahtakna apia hi. David in akiang ah, "Koi a pan hong pai na hia?" achi hi. Ama'n akiang ah, "Israel mite panmun a pan hong taikhia ka hi," achi hi.
english: David said to him, “Where do you come from?” He said to him, “I have escaped out of the camp of Israel.”

paite: David in akiang ah, "Bangchibang in thil a-om a? Hon hilh dih ve," achi hi. Ama'n adawng a, "Kidouna a pan mite ataikek ua, mi tampi puk in asi uh. Saul leh atapa Jonathan leng asi tuaktuak uh," achi hi.
english: David said to him, “How did it go? Please tell me.” He answered, “The people have fled from the battle, and many of the people also have fallen and are dead. Saul and Jonathan his son are dead also.”

paite: David in amah hilhpa tangval kiang ah, "Bangchi in ahia Saul leh atapa Jonathan asih uh na theih?" achi hi.
english: David said to the young man who told him, “How do you know that Saul and Jonathan his son are dead?”

paite: Ahilhpa tangval in, "Bangchi chi hiam in Gilboa tang ah ka na om kha zenzen hi. Ngai in, ateipi ngai a Saul dingh ka mu a, kangtalaite leh sakol tungtuang mite'n hon naihta uhi.
english: The young man who told him said, “As I happened by chance on Mount Gilboa, behold, Saul was leaning on his spear; and behold, the chariots and the horsemen followed close behind him.

paite: Anunglam angatleh ahon mu a, hon sam hi. Ke'n, 'Hiai ah ka om,' chi in ka dawng hi.
english: When he looked behind him, he saw me and called to me. I answered, ‘Here I am.’

paite: Ka kiang ah, 'Kua na hia?' ahon chi hi. Ke'n, Amalek mi ka hi, chi in ka dawng hi.
english: He said to me, ‘Who are you?’ I answered him, ‘I am an Amalekite.’

paite: Ama'n ka kiang ah, 'Ka kiang ah hong dingh inla hong that mai dih, ka hing lai vanglak a, lungdonna in lah hon manta ngal a,' achi hi.
english: He said to me, ‘Please stand beside me, and kill me, for anguish has taken hold of me because my life lingers in me.’

paite: Akiang ah ka dingh a, huchi a pukgawp khinsa, damzou nawn lou ding chih ka theih ziak in ka thatta mai hi. Alu a lallukhu leh aban a tau ka la a, ka pu kiang ah ka hon tawi hi,” achi hi.
english: So I stood beside him and killed him, because I was sure that he could not live after he had fallen. I took the crown that was on his head and the bracelet that was on his arm, and have brought them here to my lord.”

paite: David in apuansilhte abotkekta a, huchi mah bang in akiang a mi om tengteng in leng ahih uhi.
english: Then David took hold of his clothes and tore them; and all the men who were with him did likewise.

paite: Saul leh atapa Jonathan leh TOUPA mite leh Israel inkuante asuun ua, akah ua, nitaklam tan in an angawl ua, namsau a thah ahih ziakun.
english: They mourned, wept, and fasted until evening for Saul and for Jonathan his son, and for the people of Yahweh, and for the house of Israel, because they had fallen by the sword.

paite: David in amah va hilhtu tangval kiang ah, "Koilam mi na hia?" achi hi.
english: David said to the young man who told him, “Where are you from?” He answered, “I am the son of a foreigner, an Amalekite.”

paite: Ama'n, "Gamdangmi, Amalek mi tapa ka hi," chi in adawng hi. David in akiang ah, "TOUPA thaunilh hihmang dia atung a khut khak bangchidan a lau lou na hia le?" achi hi.
english: David said to him, “Why were you not afraid to stretch out your hand to destroy Yahweh’s anointed?”

paite: David in tangval khat asam a, "Va naih inla, that in," achi a, ama'n ava sat a, asita hi.
english: David called one of the young men and said, “Go near, and cut him down!” He struck him so that he died.

paite: David in akiang ah, "Na sisan nangmah lutung ah om hen. Nangmah kam ngei in, TOUPA thaunilh ka that ahi, chi a na puan tak man in," achi hi.
english: David said to him, “Your blood be on your head, for your mouth has testified against you, saying, ‘I have slain Yahweh’s anointed.’”

paite: David in Saul leh atapa Jonathan hiai kahtam in asuun hi:
english: David lamented with this lamentation over Saul and over Jonathan his son

paite: Thalkapdan Judah suante sinsak ding in asawl a, ngai in, Jasher laibu ah hiai gelh ahi:
english: (and he commanded them to teach the children of Judah the song of the bow; behold, it is written in the book of Jashar):

paite: Aw Israel, na kilawmna mun sangte ah athat ua, na mihatte apukta uh.
english: “Your glory, Israel, was slain on your high places! How the mighty have fallen!

paite: Gath ah gen kei unla, Ashkelon kongzingte ah puang kei un. Huchi lou in zaw Philistia tanute akipak ding ua, Ezeksum louh tanute avualzou kha ding uhi.
english: Don’t tell it in Gath. Don’t publish it in the streets of Ashkelon, lest the daughters of the Philistines rejoice, lest the daughters of the uncircumcised triumph.

paite: Nou Gilboa tangte aw, na tung uah daitui leh vuah ke kei hen. Thillat dingte leng suah sam ke'n. Huai ah lah mihat lum Saul lum, thaunilh louh mi lum bang mai in giloutak in apaimang uhi.
english: You mountains of Gilboa, let there be no dew or rain on you, and no fields of offerings; for there the shield of the mighty was defiled and cast away, the shield of Saul was not anointed with oil.

paite: Thah a omte sisan a pan leh mihat thau a pan Jonathan thal akik nawn kei a, Saul namsau avuak in akik nawn kei hi.
english: From the blood of the slain, from the fat of the mighty, Jonathan’s bow didn’t turn back. Saul’s sword didn’t return empty.

paite: Saul leh Jonathan hindan adeihhuai in akilawm a, asih un leng akikhen kei uh. Mupite sang in ahatzaw ua, humpinelkaite sang in ahatzaw uhi.
english: Saul and Jonathan were lovely and pleasant in their lives. In their death, they were not divided. They were swifter than eagles. They were stronger than lions.

paite: Nou Israel tanute aw, Saul kah un, puansan kilawmte na tung uah abaang a, na puan uah dangka-eng a zephoihnate hon koihsakpa ahi.
english: You daughters of Israel, weep over Saul, who clothed you delicately in scarlet, who put ornaments of gold on your clothing.

paite: Kidou laitak a mihatte apuk maizen uh! Aw, Jonathan, na mun sangte ah nang ahon thatta uhi.
english: How the mighty have fallen in the middle of the battle! Jonathan was slain on your high places.

paite: Ka unaupa Jonathan, na tungthu ah ka lungzing petmah hi. Ka tung ah na hoih mahmah a, N'on itna alamdang a, numei itna akhup hi.
english: I am distressed for you, my brother Jonathan. You have been very pleasant to me. Your love to me was wonderful, surpassing the love of women.

paite: Mihatte apuk ua, kidouna galvante leng amangthang khinta!
english: How the mighty have fallen, and the weapons of war have perished!”

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, huai nung in Ammon suante kumpipa asi a, atapa Hanun in amun ah vai ahawm hi.
english: After this, the king of the children of Ammon died, and Hanun his son reigned in his place.

paite: David in, "Apa'n hon na hehpih bang in ke'n leng Nahash tapa Hanun ka hehpih sam ding," achi hi. Huchi in David in apa tungtang thu a lungmuan ding in amah mite asawl a, huchi in David mite Ammon suante gam ava tung uhi.
english: David said, “I will show kindness to Hanun the son of Nahash, as his father showed kindness to me.” So David sent by his servants to comfort him concerning his father. David’s servants came into the land of the children of Ammon.

paite: Himahleh Ammon suante makaite'n atoupa uh Hanun kiang ah, "David in na pa azahtak ziak a na kiang a lungmuanmi hon sawl hi in na um a hia? David in na mite khuate ahong hihsiatna dia zongkhe ding leh enkhe dia hon sawl ahi kei a hia?" achi uhi.
english: But the princes of the children of Ammon said to Hanun their lord, “Do you think that David honors your father, in that he has sent comforters to you? Hasn’t David sent his servants to you to search the city, to spy it out, and to overthrow it?”

paite: Huchi in Hanun in David mite aman a, akhamul langkhat uh ametsak a, apuansilhte uh alaitak ah ataw uh phazou lel in atansak a, asawlkheta hi.
english: So Hanun took David’s servants, shaved off one half of their beards, and cut off their garments in the middle, even to their buttocks, and sent them away.

paite: David ahilhtak un, amau dawn ding mi asawl hi; amau lah azum mahmah ngal ua. Kumpipa'n, "Na khamul uh asau nawn ma in Jeriko ah om tadih unla, huai nung in hong paikik un," achi hi.
english: When they told David this, he sent to meet them, for the men were greatly ashamed. The king said, “Wait at Jericho until your beards have grown, and then return.”

paite: Ammon suante'n David huat lam ana hihta uh, chih atheih un, Ammon suante'n Beth-rehob a Siriate leh Zobah a Siriate sepaih singnih leh kumpipa Maka mi sangkhat, Tob mite singkhat-le-sangnih toh thukhak in aguai uhi.
english: When the children of Ammon saw that they had become odious to David, the children of Ammon sent and hired the Syrians of Beth Rehob and the Syrians of Zobah, twenty thousand footmen, and the king of Maacah with one thousand men, and the men of Tob twelve thousand men.

paite: David in huai azak in Joab leh sepaih hangsan tengteng asawl hi.
english: When David heard of it, he sent Joab and all the army of the mighty men.

paite: Ammon suante ahong kuan ua, kholutna kongkhak lam ah panmun akhoh uh. Zobah a mite leh Rehob a Siriate leh Tob leh Maakahte bel atuam in loubuk ah a-om uhi.
english: The children of Ammon came out, and put the battle in array at the entrance of the gate. The Syrians of Zobah and of Rehob and the men of Tob and Maacah were by themselves in the field.

paite: Huchi in amalam uh leh anunglam uah ahon sual ding uh chih Joab in atheih in, Israel mite lak a mihoih tata atelkhia a, Siria mite sual ding in panmun ana khoh hi.
english: Now when Joab saw that the battle was set against him before and behind, he chose of all the choice men of Israel and put them in array against the Syrians.

paite: Midang tengteng a-unaupa Abishai khut ah akoih vek a, Ammon suante sual ding in panmun akhoh hi.
english: The rest of the people he committed into the hand of Abishai his brother; and he put them in array against the children of Ammon.

paite: "Siria mite ka zoh kei dingleh, nang na hon huh dia, Ammon suante na zoh kei dingleh ke'n ka hon huh ding hi.
english: He said, “If the Syrians are too strong for me, then you shall help me; but if the children of Ammon are too strong for you, then I will come and help you.

paite: Hangtak in om unla, i mite leh i Pathian khua hum in i kipasalsak ding uh. TOUPA'N hoih asak bangbang in hih hen," achi hi.
english: Be courageous, and let’s be strong for our people and for the cities of our God; and may Yahweh do what seems good to him.”

paite: Huchi in Joab leh akiang a mite'n Siria mite sual ding in kidouna mun anaih ua; ama uah ataikek uhi.
english: So Joab and the people who were with him came near to the battle against the Syrians, and they fled before him.

paite: Ammon suante'n Siria mite ataikek uh chih atheih un amau leng Abishai ma ah ataikek samta ua, khosung ah alut uhi. Joab in Ammon suante akiksan a, Jerusalem ah apaita hi.
english: When the children of Ammon saw that the Syrians had fled, they likewise fled before Abishai, and entered into the city. Then Joab returned from the children of Ammon and came to Jerusalem.

paite: Siria mite'n Israelte ma ah thah in a-om uh chih akitheih un akikaikhawm uhi.
english: When the Syrians saw that they were defeated by Israel, they gathered themselves together.

paite: Hadadezer in mi asawl a, Lui khen lam a Siria mite apikhia a, Hadadezer sepaih heutu Shobak in ma kai in lehlam ah ahong pai uhi.
english: Hadadezer sent and brought out the Syrians who were beyond the River; and they came to Helam, with Shobach the captain of the army of Hadadezer at their head.

paite: Huai David ahilh ua, ama'n Israel mi tengteng asamkhawm a, Jordan lui kan in Helam ah apai uhi. David dou ding in Siria mite'n panmun khoh in ahong dou uhi.
english: David was told that; and he gathered all Israel together, passed over the Jordan, and came to Helam. The Syrians set themselves in array against David and fought with him.

paite: Israelte ma ah Siria mite ataikek ua, David in Siria mi kangtalai zasagih tung a tuang leh sakol tungtuangmi singli athat a, asepaih heutu uh Shobak leng athat a, huai ah asita hi.
english: The Syrians fled before Israel; and David killed seven hundred charioteers of the Syrians and forty thousand horsemen, and struck Shobach the captain of their army, so that he died there.

paite: Huchi in Hadadezer sikha a om kumpipa tengteng in Israelte ma ah tamtak thah ahi uh chih atheih un, Israelte toh kilemna abawl ua, asikha un a-omta uh. Huchi in Siria mite'n Ammon suante apanpih ngam nawn kei uhi.
english: When all the kings who were servants to Hadadezer saw that they were defeated before Israel, they made peace with Israel and served them. So the Syrians were afraid to help the children of Ammon any more.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, kum ahong kivei a, kumpipate galdou dia akuankhiak lai un, David in Joab leh asikhate tengteng asawl a, Ammon suante ahihmang ua, Rabbah khua a-umkhum uhi. Himahleh David bel Jerusalem ah a-om nilouh hi.
english: At the return of the year, at the time when kings go out, David sent Joab and his servants with him, and all Israel; and they destroyed the children of Ammon and besieged Rabbah. But David stayed at Jerusalem.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, nitaklam ninem in alupna a pan David athoukhia a, kumpipa' inn tung ah akahtou hi. Inn tung a pan numei khat kisil lai amu hi. Huai numei bel melhoihtak ahi.
english: At evening, David arose from his bed and walked on the roof of the king’s house. From the roof, he saw a woman bathing, and the woman was very beautiful to look at.

paite: David in huai numei tanchin dongtel ding in mi asawl hi. Huai mi in, “Eliam tanu, Bathsheba, Hit mi Uriah zi ahi kei maw?" achi hi.
english: David sent and inquired after the woman. One said, “Isn’t this Bathsheba, the daughter of Eliam, Uriah the Hittite’s wife?”

paite: David in thupote asawl a, ava pita uh. Akiang ahong tung a, ana kithuahpihta hi. Asianlouhna a pan siansak khit ahita hi, huchi in a-inn ah paikikta hi.
english: David sent messengers, and took her; and she came in to him, and he lay with her (for she was purified from her uncleanness); and she returned to her house.

paite: Huchi in numei ahong gaita a, "Nau ka paita," chi in David atheisak hi.
english: The woman conceived; and she sent and told David, and said, “I am with child.”

paite: David in Joab kiang ah, "Hit mi Uriah ka kiang ah hon sawl in," chi in athukhak hi. Joab in David kiang ah Uriah asawlta hi.
english: David sent to Joab, “Send me Uriah the Hittite.” Joab sent Uriah to David.

paite: Uriah akiang atun in David in, "Joab leh mite bang achi ua, kidouna ah bang achi ua?" chi in adong hi.
english: When Uriah had come to him, David asked him how Joab did, and how the people fared, and how the war prospered.

paite: David in Uriah kiang ah, “Na inn ah pai inla, na khete va sil in," achi hi. Huchi in kumpipa' inn a pan Uriah apawtkhia a, kumpipa'n an nek ding thawnpiak azuisak hi.
english: David said to Uriah, “Go down to your house and wash your feet.” Uriah departed out of the king’s house, and a gift from the king was sent after him.

paite: Himahleh atoupa sikha tengteng lak a kumpipa' inn kongkhak bul ah Uriah agiak a, a-inn ah apai kei hi.
english: But Uriah slept at the door of the king’s house with all the servants of his lord, and didn’t go down to his house.

paite: "A-inn ah Uriah apai kei," chi a David ahilhtak un, David in Uriah kiang ah, "Khualzin hong tung hilou na hi maw? Bangziak a na inn a pai lou na hia?" achi hi.
english: When they had told David, saying, “Uriah didn’t go down to his house,” David said to Uriah, “Haven’t you come from a journey? Why didn’t you go down to your house?”

paite: Uriah in David kiang ah, "Pathian bawm, Israelte leh Judahte aidakbuk a om gige ua, ka toupa Joab leh ka toupa sikhate gamlak ah akikulh uh. Kei ka inn a pai in ka ne in ka ta in, ka zi kiang ah ka lum ding maw? Na hinna leh na kha ahin bang in ka gen ahi, huai zaw ka hih kei ding," achi hi.
english: Uriah said to David, “The ark, Israel, and Judah, are staying in tents; and my lord Joab and the servants of my lord are encamped in the open field. Shall I then go into my house to eat and to drink, and to lie with my wife? As you live, and as your soul lives, I will not do this thing!”

paite: David in Uriah kiang ah, "Tuni leng hiai ah om lai inla, zingchiang in na pai na ding,” achi hi. Huchi in Uriah huai ni leh azingchiang leng Jerusalem ah a-omta hi.
english: David said to Uriah, “Stay here today also, and tomorrow I will let you depart.” So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem that day and the next day.

paite: David in amah asam a, ama ah ne in adawn hi. Adawn khamsak hi. Nitaklam in a-inn a pai lou in atoupa sikhate lak ah agiak hi.
english: When David had called him, he ate and drank before him; and he made him drunk. At evening, he went out to lie on his bed with the servants of his lord, but didn’t go down to his house.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, azingchiang in David in Joab lai akhak a, Uriah aposak hi.
english: In the morning, David wrote a letter to Joab and sent it by the hand of Uriah.

paite: Huai laikhak ah, "Gal khawkna pen ah Uriah ma phusak inla, athah ua asihna ding in kikhinsan un,” chi in agelh hi.
english: He wrote in the letter, saying, “Send Uriah to the forefront of the hottest battle, and retreat from him, that he may be struck and die.”

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, Joab in khua a-um lai in, mihangsante omna hi a atheihna ah Uriah apangsak hi.
english: When Joab kept watch on the city, he assigned Uriah to the place where he knew that valiant men were.

paite: Khua a mite apawtkhia ua, Joab asual ua, David sikhate khenkhat asi ua, Hit mi Uriah leng asi hi.
english: The men of the city went out and fought with Joab. Some of the people fell, even of David’s servants; and Uriah the Hittite died also.

paite: Huchi in Joab in mi asawl a, kidou tungtang thil tengteng David ahilhsak hi.
english: Then Joab sent and told David all the things concerning the war;

paite: Amisawl kiang ah, Kumpipa kiang a kidou tanchin tengteng na gen khit in,
english: and he commanded the messenger, saying, “When you have finished telling all the things concerning the war to the king,

paite: ahong heh guih a, "Bangziak a dou dia huchibang a khobul chin a hoh na hi ua? Kulh a pan a hon kap ding uh chih thei lou na hi uh maw?
english: it shall be that, if the king’s wrath arise, and he asks you, ‘Why did you go so near to the city to fight? Didn’t you know that they would shoot from the wall?

paite: Jerubeseth tapa Abimelek that kua ahia? Buh gawizanna suang tungnungpen numei in kulhbaang tung a pan atung ah akhesuk a, Thebez a si ahi kei maw? Bangziak a hichibang a kulh kiangchin a pai na hi ua?" achihleh, “Na sikha Hit mi Uriah leng si ei ve, na chi ding uh," chỉ in thu apia hi.
english: Who struck Abimelech the son of Jerubbesheth? Didn’t a woman cast an upper millstone on him from the wall, so that he died at Thebez? Why did you go so near the wall?’ then you shall say, ‘Your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead.’”

paite: Huchi in amisawl akuanta a, ava tung a, Joab in asawlsan tengteng David ahilh hi.
english: So the messenger went, and came and showed David all that Joab had sent him for.

paite: Amisawl in David kiang ah, "Mite'n ahon na zou ua, loubuk ah hon sual ua, kou akho lutna kongkhak tanpha in ka nohkik uhi.
english: The messenger said to David, “The men prevailed against us, and came out to us into the field; and we were on them even to the entrance of the gate.

paite: "Thalkap mite'n kulh a pan na sikhate ahon kap ua, huchi in kumpipa sikha khenkhatte asi ua, na sikha Hit mi Uriah leng asi," achi hi.
english: The shooters shot at your servants from off the wall; and some of the king’s servants are dead, and your servant Uriah the Hittite is also dead.”

paite: Huchi in David in misawl kiang ah, Joab kiang ah huchi in va gen in, "Hiaite'n na lungsim kipaklousak kei hen. Namsau in kuamah akhentuam ngal kei a, naksem in khua sual unla hihsia un, chi in hanthawn in," achi hi.
english: Then David said to the messenger, “Tell Joab, ‘Don’t let this thing displease you, for the sword devours one as well as another. Make your battle stronger against the city, and overthrow it.’ Encourage him.”

paite: Uriah zi in apasal Uriah asi chih azak in apasal asuun hi.
english: When Uriah’s wife heard that Uriah her husband was dead, she mourned for her husband.

paite: Asuun hun abei nung in David in a-inn ah api a, azi ahong hita a, tapa khat aneihsak hi. Himahleh David thilhih in TOUPA akipaksak kei hi.
english: When the mourning was past, David sent and took her home to his house, and she became his wife and bore him a son. But the thing that David had done displeased Yahweh.

paite: Huan TOUPA'N David kiang ah Nathan asawl hi. Akiang ah ava hoh a, hichi in achi, "Khua khat ah mi nih a-om ua; khat pen mihausa ahi a, khat pen mizawng ahi.
english: Yahweh sent Nathan to David. He came to him, and said to him, “There were two men in one city: the one rich, and the other poor.

paite: Mihausa in belamhon tampi leh ganhon tampi anei hi.
english: The rich man had very many flocks and herds,

paite: Mizawng in bel belamnou anu neuchik khat lei a, avulh kia lou ngal bangmah dang anei kei hi. Amah leh atate toh khangliankhawm in akuang sawkpih leh anou kikoppih, a-angsung a om, atanu bang geih a angaihtuah ahi.
english: but the poor man had nothing, except one little ewe lamb, which he had bought and raised. It grew up together with him and with his children. It ate of his own food, drank of his own cup, and lay in his bosom, and was like a daughter to him.

paite: Mihausa kiang ah khualzinmi khat ava tung hi. Akiang a mikhual tung ama belam leh gan goh ding phal lou in mizawngpa belamnou leh ganhon a pan agohsak zawta hi," achi hi.
english: A traveler came to the rich man, and he didn’t want to take of his own flock and of his own herd to prepare for the wayfaring man who had come to him, but took the poor man’s lamb and prepared it for the man who had come to him.”

paite: Huchi in huai mi tung ah David aheh mahmah a, Nathan kiang ah, "TOUPA ahin bang in ka gen ahi, huai thilhihmi asih ngeingei ding ahi.
english: David’s anger burned hot against the man, and he said to Nathan, “As Yahweh lives, the man who has done this deserves to die!

paite: Hichibang thil ahih ziak leh hehpihna aneih louh ziak in abelamnou amun li a adit ding ahi," achi hi.
english: He must restore the lamb fourfold, because he did this thing and because he had no pity!”

paite: Nathan in David kiang ah, "Huai mipa nangmah na hi. TOUPA, Israelte’ Pathian in hichi in achi: Israelte kumpipa ding in thau ka hon nilh a, Saul khut a pan ka hon hunkhia hi.
english: Nathan said to David, “You are the man! This is what Yahweh, the God of Israel, says: ‘I anointed you king over Israel, and I delivered you out of the hand of Saul.

paite: Na pu in ka hon luahsak a, na pu zite na angsung ah ka koih hi. Israel leh Judah inkote ka hon pia a; huaite atawm luat uleh thil dangte leng hon piakbeh lai ding ka hi.
english: I gave you your master’s house and your master’s wives into your bosom, and gave you the house of Israel and of Judah; and if that would have been too little, I would have added to you many more such things.

paite: Bangziak a TOUPA thupiak ngaineu a, amitmuh a thil hoih lou na hih maizen? Hit mi Uriah namsau in na that a, azi na zi ding in na neihsak a, Ammon suante namsau in amah na that hi.
english: Why have you despised Yahweh’s word, to do that which is evil in his sight? You have struck Uriah the Hittite with the sword, have taken his wife to be your wife, and have slain him with the sword of the children of Ammon.

paite: Huaiziak in namsau in na insung anuse ngei nawn kei ding. Kei hon ngaineu a, Hit mi Uriah zi na zi dia na lak ziak in.
english: Now therefore the sword will never depart from your house, because you have despised me and have taken Uriah the Hittite’s wife to be your wife.’

paite: TOUPA'N hichi in achi: Ngai in, nangmah inkote mah nang kalh ding thil hoih lou ka tungkhe dia, na mitmuh mahmah in na zite ka hon laksak dia, na inveng ka pe dia, ama'n hiai sun khovak in na zite akithuahpih ding.
english: “This is what Yahweh says: ‘Behold, I will raise up evil against you out of your own house; and I will take your wives before your eyes and give them to your neighbor, and he will lie with your wives in the sight of this sun.

paite: Nang aguk in na hih a, ke'n Israel mite tengteng mitmuh in sun khovak in ka hih ding," achi hi.
english: For you did this secretly, but I will do this thing before all Israel, and before the sun.’”

paite: David in Nathan kiang ah, "TOUPA tung ah ka khialta," achi hi. Nathan in David kiang ah, "TOUPA'N leng na khelhna akoihmangta. Na si kei ding.
english: David said to Nathan, “I have sinned against Yahweh.” Nathan said to David, “Yahweh also has put away your sin. You will not die.

paite: Himahleh hiai na thilhih a Pathian gensiatna dia hun lemtang thupitak TOUPA melmate na piak ziak in nang a pan hong piang ding naupang asi ngeingei ding," achi hi.
english: However, because by this deed you have given great occasion to Yahweh’s enemies to blaspheme, the child also who is born to you will surely die.”

paite: Huchi in Nathan in a-inn ah apaisanta hi. Uriah zi in David asuansak naupang tung ah TOUPA'N akhut kha in, achi ana mahmahta hi.
english: Then Nathan departed to his house. Yahweh struck the child that Uriah’s wife bore to David, and he was very sick.

paite: Huaiziak in David in naupang a ding in Pathian kiang ah angen ngutngut a, an angawl a, alut a, zankhua in lei ah alum hi.
english: David therefore begged God for the child; and David fasted, and went in and lay all night on the ground.

paite: A-inkote lak a upate athou ua, lei a pan kaithou ding in akiang ah adingh uhi. Himahleh athou nuam kei a, akiang uah leng ane sam kei.
english: The elders of his house arose beside him, to raise him up from the earth; but he would not, and he didn’t eat bread with them.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, ani sagih ni in naupang asita hi. David sikhate'n naupang asita chih ahilh ngam kei uh, "Ngai in, naupang adam lai in akiang ah thu i gen ua, angaikhe nuam kei a. Naupang asita chih bangchi in i hilh ngamta ding ua? Bangchi hiam in thil hoih lou akihih kha ding," achi uhi.
english: On the seventh day, the child died. David’s servants were afraid to tell him that the child was dead, for they said, “Behold, while the child was yet alive, we spoke to him and he didn’t listen to our voice. How will he then harm himself if we tell him that the child is dead?”

paite: Himahleh David in asikhate kisimhou amuh in naupang asita chih atheita hi. David in asikhate kiang ah, "Naupang sita hia?" achi a, amau, "Asita,” achi uh.
english: But when David saw that his servants were whispering together, David perceived that the child was dead; and David said to his servants, “Is the child dead?” They said, “He is dead.”

paite: Huchi in David lei a pan athou a, akisil a, sathau akinilh a, apuante akheng a; TOUPA' inn ah ahoh a, Pathian abia hi. A-inn ah apai nawn a, an akan a, ama ah alui ua, aneta hi.
english: Then David arose from the earth, and washed and anointed himself, and changed his clothing; and he came into Yahweh’s house, and worshiped. Then he came to his own house; and when he requested, they set bread before him and he ate.

paite: Huchi in asikhate'n akiang ah, "Na thilhih bangchidan ahia? Naupang adam lai in an na ngawl a, na kap a, himahleh naupang asihtak in na thou a, an na ne a," achi uhi.
english: Then his servants said to him, “What is this that you have done? You fasted and wept for the child while he was alive, but when the child was dead, you rose up and ate bread.”

paite: Ama'n, "Naupang adam lai in an ngawl in ka kap hi. Naupang adamna ding in TOUPA'N hon hehpih khamoh kei ding chih kua ahia thei? Ka chi hi.
english: He said, “While the child was yet alive, I fasted and wept; for I said, ‘Who knows whether Yahweh will not be gracious to me, that the child may live?’

paite: Himahleh tu in asita ngal a, bang ding in an ka ngawl dia? Ka pikik nawn thei dia hia? Akiang ah ka pai dia, himahleh amah ka kiang ah ahong kik nawn kei ding," achi hi.
english: But now he is dead. Why should I fast? Can I bring him back again? I will go to him, but he will not return to me.”

paite: Huchi in David in azi Bathsheba alungmuan a, akiang ah alut a, akithuahpih a, tapa asuang a, amin Solomon asa hi. TOUPA'N amah a-it hi.
english: David comforted Bathsheba his wife, and went in to her, and lay with her. She bore a son, and he called his name Solomon. Yahweh loved him;

paite: Huchi in zawlnei Nathan athukhak a, ama'n TOUPA ziak in amin Jedidiah asa hi.
english: and he sent by the hand of Nathan the prophet, and he named him Jedidiah, for Yahweh’s sake.

paite: Huchi in Joab in Ammon suante khopi Rabbah sim in alata hi.
english: Now Joab fought against Rabbah of the children of Ammon, and took the royal city.

paite: Joab in David kiang ah mi asawl a, "Rabbah ka sim a, tuite khopi ka lata hi.
english: Joab sent messengers to David, and said, “I have fought against Rabbah. Yes, I have taken the city of waters.

paite: Tu in mi om lai teng kaikhawm inla, khopi sual tum in zuan inla, la in. Ke'n khopi la leng ka min apu kha ding," achi hi.
english: Now therefore gather the rest of the people together, and encamp against the city and take it; lest I take the city, and it be called by my name.”

paite: Huchi in David in mi tengteng akaikhawm a, Rabbah ah ahoh ua, ava sim ua, alata uhi.
english: David gathered all the people together and went to Rabbah, and fought against it and took it.

paite: Akumpipa uh lallukhu khuk lai alaksak a, agikdan dangka-eng talent khat ahi a, suangmantamte leng atel hi. David akhusak ua, khopi ah gallak tampi ala uhi.
english: He took the crown of their king from off his head; and its weight was a talent of gold, and in it were precious stones; and it was set on David’s head. He brought a great quantity of plunder out of the city.

paite: Huchi in asung a om mipite apikheta a, sing-atnate, leilehna sikzumte leh sik heipite zang in nna asemsak hi. Lei haltakte abawlsak a; Ammon suante khopi tengteng ah huchibang in ahih hi. Huchi in David leh mi tengteng Jerusalem ah apaikik nawnta uhi.
english: He brought out the people who were in it, and put them to work under saws, under iron picks, under axes of iron, and made them go to the brick kiln; and he did so to all the cities of the children of Ammon. Then David and all the people returned to Jerusalem.

paite: Huai nung in hichi ahong hi a, David tapa Absalom in sanggam numei melhoih khat anei a, amin Tamar ahi. David tapa Amnon in amah a-it hi.
english: After this, Absalom the son of David had a beautiful sister, whose name was Tamar; and Amnon the son of David loved her.

paite: Huchi in asanggamnu Tamar ziak in Amnon abuai mahmah a; achi ana hi. Amah lah nungak siangthou ahih ziak in atung a thil banghiam hih haksapi ahi chi in Amnon in angaihtuah hi.
english: Amnon was so troubled that he became sick because of his sister Tamar, for she was a virgin, and it seemed hard to Amnon to do anything to her.

paite: Himahleh Amnon in lawm anei a, amin Jonadab ahi. Amah David unaupa Shimea tapa ahi. Jonadab migitlouhpil mahmah mi khat ahi.
english: But Amnon had a friend whose name was Jonadab the son of Shimeah, David’s brother; and Jonadab was a very subtle man.

paite: Ama'n Amnon kiang ah, "Aw, nang kumpipa tapa bangchidan ahia, aniteng a na gawn hulhul mawk? Hon hilh lou ding maw?" achi hi. Amnon in akiang ah, "Ka unaupa Absalom sanggamnu Tamar ka it a ahi," achi hi.
english: He said to him, “Why, son of the king, are you so sad from day to day? Won’t you tell me?” Amnon said to him, “I love Tamar, my brother Absalom’s sister.”

paite: Jonadab in akiang ah, "Na lupna ah lumlum inla, kichinasak in. Na pa'n ahong veh chiang in akiang ah, Hehpih in ka sanggamnu Tamar ka kiang ah hong hoh henla, tanghou nek ding hong pia hen. Ka muh theih in ka mitmuh mahmah in nek ding hon bawlsakleh, akhut ngei ah ka na ne ding, na chi in," achi hi.
english: Jonadab said to him, “Lay down on your bed and pretend to be sick. When your father comes to see you, tell him, ‘Please let my sister Tamar come and give me bread to eat, and prepare the food in my sight, that I may see it and eat it from her hand.’”

paite: Huchi in Amnon alum a, akichinasakta hi. Kumpipa'n amah ava et in Amnon in akiang ah, "Hehpih in ka sanggamnu Tamar hong pai henla, ka mitmuh mahmah in tanghou pek nih hiam hon bawlsak henla, amah khut mahmah ah ka ne ding," achi hi.
english: So Amnon lay down and faked being sick. When the king came to see him, Amnon said to the king, “Please let my sister Tamar come and make me a couple of cakes in my sight, that I may eat from her hand.”

paite: Huchi in David in Tamar kiang ah, "Na sanggampa Amnon inn ah hoh inla, nek ding va bawlsak dih ve," chi ding in a-inn ah mi asawl hi.
english: Then David sent home to Tamar, saying, “Go now to your brother Amnon’s house, and prepare food for him.”

paite: Huchi in Tamar, asanggampa Amnon inn ah ahoh hi. Amah ana lum hi. Tangbuang ala a, amek a, amitmuh a tanghou pek bawl in akang hi.
english: So Tamar went to her brother Amnon’s house; and he was lying down. She took dough, kneaded it, made cakes in his sight, and baked the cakes.

paite: Akanna bel ala a, ama ah abungkhia hi. Himahleh ama'n ane nuam kei hi. Huan Amnon in, "Mi tengteng in hon pawtkhiaksan uhen," achi hi. Huchi in apawtkhiaksan vek uhi.
english: She took the pan and poured them out before him, but he refused to eat. Amnon said, “Have all men leave me.” Then every man went out from him.

paite: Huan Amnon in Tamar kiang ah, "Na khut mahmah a ka nektheihna ding in nek ding dantan ah hon la in," achi hi. Tamar in atanghou pek bawl ala a, asanggampa Amnon kiang ah dantan ah alalut hi.
english: Amnon said to Tamar, “Bring the food into the room, that I may eat from your hand.” Tamar took the cakes which she had made, and brought them into the room to Amnon her brother.

paite: Nesak dia akiangnai a ava paipih in ana len a, akiang ah, "Ka sanggamnu, ka kiang ah hong lum in," achi hi.
english: When she had brought them near to him to eat, he took hold of her and said to her, “Come, lie with me, my sister!”

paite: Ama'n adawng a, "Hilou e, ka sanggampa, hon chi teitei ke'n. Israelte lak ah hichibang thilhih ding ahi kei. Hiai thil gilou haihuaitak hih ke'n.
english: She answered him, “No, my brother, do not force me! For no such thing ought to be done in Israel. Don’t you do this folly!

paite: Ke'n ka maizumna koi ah ka paisak dia? Nang leng Israelte lak a mihaite lak a khat na hi ding. Huaiziak in tu in kumpipa houpih zaw in, na hon neih anial kei ding," achi hi.
english: As for me, where would I carry my shame? And as for you, you will be as one of the fools in Israel. Now therefore, please speak to the king; for he will not withhold me from you.”

paite: Himahleh athu azui kei a, amah sang in ahatzaw ngal a, thagum in akithuahpih teiteita hi.
english: However, he would not listen to her voice; but being stronger than she, he forced her and lay with her.

paite: Huchi in Amnon in huat chihtak in ahota a, a-itna sang in ahuatna alianzaw hi. Huchi in Amnon in akiang ah, "Thou inla, paimang in," achi hi.
english: Then Amnon hated her with exceedingly great hatred; for the hatred with which he hated her was greater than the love with which he had loved her. Amnon said to her, “Arise, be gone!”

paite: Ama'n akiang ah, "Huchi ding ahi kei. Hichibang a dikloutak a na hon delhkhiak ka tung a na gamtatsa sang in ahoih kei zaw hi,” achi hi. Himahleh azui nuam tuan kei hi.
english: She said to him, “Not so, because this great wrong in sending me away is worse than the other that you did to me!” But he would not listen to her.

paite: Huchi in anasem sikha asam a, "Hiai numei ka kiang a pan pawtsak inla, kong khak bikbek in," achi hi.
english: Then he called his servant who ministered to him, and said, “Now put this woman out from me, and bolt the door after her.”

paite: Minu'n puanaktual ze tuamtuam a gial asilh hi. Huchibang puanaktual kumpipa nungak siangthoute'n asilh uh ahi. Huchi in asikha in apikhia a, kong akhak bikbekta hi.
english: She had a garment of various colors on her, for the king’s daughters who were virgins dressed in such robes. Then his servant brought her out and bolted the door after her.

paite: Tamar in alu ah meivu akoih a, apuanaktual silh ze tuamtuam abotkek a, asip ah akhut akoih a, ngaihtak a kap kawm in apaita hi.
english: Tamar put ashes on her head, and tore her garment of various colors that was on her; and she laid her hand on her head and went her way, crying aloud as she went.

paite: Asanggampa Absalom in akiang ah, "Na sanggampa Amnon na kiang a om ahi maw? Himahleh tu in dai mai in, ka sanggamnu, na sanggampa aka, limsak dah in," achi hi. Huchi in Tamar asanggampa Absalom inn ah nguitak in akikhumta hi.
english: Absalom her brother said to her, “Has Amnon your brother been with you? But now hold your peace, my sister. He is your brother. Don’t take this thing to heart.” So Tamar remained desolate in her brother Absalom’s house.

paite: Himahleh kumpipa David in huai tengteng azak in aheh mahmah hi.
english: But when King David heard of all these things, he was very angry.

paite: Absalom in Amnon kiang ah asia-apha hitaleh bangmah agen nuam kei hi. Asanggamnu Tamar achih teitei ziak in Absalom in Amnon aho mahmah hi.
english: Absalom spoke to Amnon neither good nor bad; for Absalom hated Amnon, because he had forced his sister Tamar.

paite: Kum nih vengveng abei nung in hichi ahong hi a, Ephraim kiang a Baal-hazor ah Absalom in belam mul ametsak hi. Hiai ah kumpipa tapa tengteng achial hi.
english: After two full years, Absalom had sheep shearers in Baal Hazor, which is beside Ephraim; and Absalom invited all the king’s sons.

paite: Kumpipa kiang ah Absalom ahoh a, “Ngai in, na sikha in belam mul ametsak a, kumpipa leh asikhate na sikha kiang ah hoh le uh akei dia,” achi hi.
english: Absalom came to the king and said, “See now, your servant has sheep shearers. Please let the king and his servants go with your servant.”

paite: Kumpipa'n Absalom kiang ah, "Hilou e, ka tapa, ka vek un hoh lou e, ka hon hihtuailuai lo kha ding uh," achi hi. Huchi in ama'n chial teitei mahleh a-ut tuan kei a, himahleh avualzawl hi.
english: The king said to Absalom, “No, my son, let’s not all go, lest we be burdensome to you.” He pressed him; however he would not go, but blessed him.

paite: Huchi in Absalom in, “Ahihkeileh ka unaupa Amnon bek ka kiang uah hong hohleh ake," achi hi. Kumpipa'n akiang ah, "Bang ding in ahong hoh tuamse dia?" achi hi.
english: Then Absalom said, “If not, please let my brother Amnon go with us.” The king said to him, “Why should he go with you?”

paite: Himahleh Absalom in angen teitei a, huchi in Amnon leh kumpipa tapa tengteng azuisak hi.
english: But Absalom pressed him, and he let Amnon and all the king’s sons go with him.

paite: Absalom in, asikhate kiang ah, "Ngai un, Amnon uain dawn a nuam asak lai in na kiang ua Amnon that un, ka hon chihleh, that unla, lau kei un, thu ka hon pe khin hilou hia? Hangsantak in om unla, kipasalsak un," chi in thu apia hi.
english: Absalom commanded his servants, saying, “Mark now, when Amnon’s heart is merry with wine; and when I tell you, ‘Strike Amnon,’ then kill him. Don’t be afraid. Haven’t I commanded you? Be courageous, and be valiant!”

paite: Huchi in Absalom sikhate'n Amnon tung ah Absalom thupiak bang in ahih uhi. Huchi in kumpipa tapa tengteng athou ua, asabiltung uah atuang chiat ua, ataimangta uhi.
english: The servants of Absalom did to Amnon as Absalom had commanded. Then all the king’s sons arose, and every man got up on his mule and fled.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, lampi a a-om lai un, Absalom in kumpipa tapate tengteng athat vek a, khat lel leng ahawi kei, chi in David kiang ah thu ana tung hi.
english: While they were on the way, the news came to David, saying, “Absalom has slain all the king’s sons, and there is not one of them left!”

paite: Huchi in kumpipa athou a apuansilhte botkek in lei ah alumta hi. Asikha tengteng in leng apuansilhte uh botkek in akiang ah adingh uhi.
english: Then the king arose, and tore his garments, and lay on the earth; and all his servants stood by with their clothes torn.

paite: David unau Shimea tapa Jonadab in adawng a, "Ka toupa'n kumpipa tapa tangval tengteng athat vek uh chih gingta kei hen. Amnon kia ahi asi. Asanggamnu Tamar achih teitei nungsiah Absalom in hichibang a hih atup him ahi.
english: Jonadab the son of Shimeah, David’s brother, answered, “Don’t let my lord suppose that they have killed all the young men, the king’s sons, for Amnon only is dead; for by the appointment of Absalom this has been determined from the day that he forced his sister Tamar.

paite: Huaiziak in tu in ka toupa, kumpipa'n kumpipa tapa tengteng asi uh chih gingta in lunghimoh kei hen. Amnon kia ahi asi," achi hi.
english: Now therefore don’t let my lord the king take the thing to his heart, to think that all the king’s sons are dead; for only Amnon is dead.”

paite: Huai sung in Absalom ataimangta hi. Galvil tangval adak a, a-en a, ngai in, anunglam a tang pang a lampi ah mi tampi ahong pai uhi.
english: But Absalom fled. The young man who kept the watch lifted up his eyes and looked, and behold, many people were coming by way of the hillside behind him.

paite: Jonadab in kumpipa kiang ah, “Ngai in, kumpipa tapate ahong pai uh, na sikha in agen bang geih ana hi na," achi hi.
english: Jonadab said to the king, “Behold, the king’s sons are coming! It is as your servant said.”

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, agen khittak in ngai in, kumpipa tapate ahong tung ua, a-aw uh suah in akap uhi. Kumpipa leng asikhate toh kah petmah in akapta uhi.
english: As soon as he had finished speaking, behold, the king’s sons came, and lifted up their voices and wept. The king also and all his servants wept bitterly.

paite: Himahleh Absalom ataimang a, Geshur kumpipa Ammihud tapa Talmai kiang ah ahoh hi. David in niteng in atapa asuun hi.
english: But Absalom fled and went to Talmai the son of Ammihur, king of Geshur. David mourned for his son every day.

paite: Absalom ataimang a, Geshur gam atung a, huai ah kum thum ava om hi.
english: So Absalom fled and went to Geshur, and was there three years.

paite: Absalom kiang ah kumpipa David hoh a-ut mahmah a, Amnon tungtang thu ah alung amuangta hi. Amah lah asi khinta chih athei ngal a.
english: King David longed to go out to Absalom, for he was comforted concerning Amnon, since he was dead.

paite: Huchi in Zeruiah tapa Joab in kumpipa lungsim Absalom tung ah a-om chih ana thei hi.
english: Now Joab the son of Zeruiah perceived that the king’s heart was toward Absalom.

paite: Huchi in Joab in Tekoa ah mi asawl a, huai a numei pil khat ava pisak hi. Akiang ah, "Lusuun bang in kibawl inla, lusuun puan silh inla, sathau leng kinilh lou in numei sawtpi misi suun bang in om in.
english: Joab sent to Tekoa and brought a wise woman from there, and said to her, “Please act like a mourner, and put on mourning clothing, please, and don’t anoint yourself with oil; but be as a woman who has mourned a long time for the dead.

paite: Kumpipa kiang ah hoh inla, akiang ah hichibang in thu va gen in aw,"” achi hi. Huchi in Joab in akam ah thute amuam hi.
english: Go in to the king and speak like this to him.” So Joab put the words in her mouth.

paite: Tekoa a numei in kumpipa kiang a thu gen ding in amai a lei si in abokkhup a, zahtakna pia in, "Kumpipa aw, hon huh in," achi hi.
english: When the woman of Tekoa spoke to the king, she fell on her face to the ground, showed respect, and said, “Help, O king!”

paite: Kumpipa'n akiang ah, "Bangchidan ahia?" achi hi. Ama'n adawng a, "Meithai petmah ka hi a, ka pasal asita hi.
english: The king said to her, “What ails you?” She answered, “Truly I am a widow, and my husband is dead.

paite: Na sikhanu'n tapa nih anei a, anih un lou ah akisual ua, kuamah phelh ding lah a-om kei a, akhat pen in adang asat a, athatta hi.
english: Your servant had two sons; and they both fought together in the field, and there was no one to part them, but the one struck the other and killed him.

paite: Ngai in, a-inkuan tengteng in na sikhanu adoukhawm ua, a-unaupa thatpa, a-unaupa athah ziak a ka thah sam theihna ding un hon pekhia in, huchi in gouluah dingpa leng ka that pah ngal ding uh, achi uh. Huchibang in ka mei-am omsun amitsak ding ua, ka pasal min nei lou leh leitung a suan himhim nei lou in a-om mai ding," achi hi.
english: Behold, the whole family has risen against your servant, and they say, ‘Deliver him who struck his brother, that we may kill him for the life of his brother whom he killed, and so destroy the heir also.’ Thus they would quench my coal which is left, and would leave to my husband neither name nor remainder on the surface of the earth.”

paite: Kumpipa'n numei kiang ah, "Na inn ah pai inla, na tungtang thu ah thu ka pe mai ding," achi hi.
english: The king said to the woman, “Go to your house, and I will give a command concerning you.”

paite: Tekoa a numei in kumpipa kiang ah, "Ka toupa, kumpipa aw, huai gitlouhna moh ka tung leh ka pa inkote tung ah ke mai hen. Kumpipa leh alaltutphah in moh po kei hen," achi hi.
english: The woman of Tekoa said to the king, “My lord, O king, may the iniquity be on me, and on my father’s house; and may the king and his throne be guiltless.”

paite: Kumpipa'n, "Kuapeuh na tung a banghiam gen peuhmah ka kiang ah hon pi inla, ahon khoih nawn het kei ding uh," achi hi.
english: The king said, “Whoever says anything to you, bring him to me, and he will not bother you any more.”

paite: Ama'n, "Sisan suah mite tung a phula mite'n hihmang nawn lou ding in kumpipa'n TOUPA na Pathian theigige hen aw, huchi lou in zaw ka tapa ahihmang kha ding uh," achi hi. Ama'n, "TOUPA ahin bang in ka gen ahi, na tapa samzang khat lel leng lei ah ake kei ding," achi hi.
english: Then she said, “Please let the king remember Yahweh your God, that the avenger of blood destroy not any more, lest they destroy my son.” He said, “As Yahweh lives, not one hair of your son shall fall to the earth.”

paite: Huchi in numei in, "Na sikhanu in toupa ka kumpipa kiang ah thu kam khat kia ka hon gen nawn peuhmah ding aw," achi hi. Ama'n, "Gen ve," achi hi.
english: Then the woman said, “Please let your servant speak a word to my lord the king.” He said, “Say on.”

paite: Numei in, "Ahihleh bangziak in ahia Pathian mite dou a hichibang a hih tum na hia? Hiai thu a pan kumpipa moh in akilang ahi, kumpipa'n adelhmangpa apikik nawn louh ziak in.
english: The woman said, “Why then have you devised such a thing against the people of God? For in speaking this word the king is as one who is guilty, in that the king does not bring home again his banished one.

paite: Ka si ngeingei ding ua, lei a bosa luah nawn theih louh tuisik bang ka hi uh. Pathian in hinna alamang kei a, adelhmangpa amah a pan hawlkhiak ahihlouhna ding lunggel ahi zaw hi.
english: For we must die, and are like water spilled on the ground, which can’t be gathered up again; neither does God take away life, but devises means, that he who is banished not be an outcast from him.

paite: Huchi in toupa ka kumpipa kiang a hiai thu gen dia ka hong leng mite'n ahon lauhsak ziak uh ahi. Na sikhanu'n, kumpipa kiang ah ka gen phot dia, kumpipa'n asikhanu nget ahihsak khakleh, ka chi a ahi.
english: Now therefore, seeing that I have come to speak this word to my lord the king, it is because the people have made me afraid. Your servant said, ‘I will now speak to the king; it may be that the king will perform the request of his servant.’

paite: Kumpipa'n kei leh ka tapa Pathian gouluah lou dia hihman tum mi lak a na sikhanu hunkhe ding in ana ngaikhe ding, ka chi hi.
english: For the king will hear, to deliver his servant out of the hand of the man who would destroy me and my son together out of the inheritance of God.

paite: Huchi in na sikhanu a ding in, toupa ka kumpipa thu lungmuanhuaitak hi henla; asia-apha na khen ding in toupa ka kumpipa lah Pathian angel bang mai ahi ngal a. TOUPA Pathian na kiang ah om hen, ka chi ahi," achi hi.
english: Then your servant said, ‘Please let the word of my lord the king bring rest; for as an angel of God, so is my lord the king to discern good and bad. May Yahweh, your God, be with you.’”

paite: Kumpipa'n adawng a, numei kiang ah, "K'on dot peuhmah bangmah hon iim ke'n aw," achi hi. Numei in, "Toupa ka kumpipa'n genleh ake," achi hi.
english: Then the king answered the woman, “Please don’t hide anything from me that I ask you.” The woman said, “Let my lord the king now speak.”

paite: Kumpipa'n, "Hiai thu himhim ah Joab in panna anei hia?" achi hi. Numei in adawng a, "Toupa ka kumpipa, na kha ahin bang in ka gen ahi, toupa ka kumpipa'n agensa kuamah in taklam hiam, veilam ah hiam apel thei kei ding uh. Na sikha Joab in hon sawl a, hiai thu tengteng na sikhanu ahon muam vek hi.
english: The king said, “Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?” The woman answered, “As your soul lives, my lord the king, no one can turn to the right hand or to the left from anything that my lord the king has spoken; for your servant Joab urged me, and he put all these words in the mouth of your servant.

paite: Thil omdan hihlamdang ding in hiai thil na sikha Joab in ahih ahi. Ka toupa bel leitung a thil om tengteng theithei Pathian angel bang a pil ahi," achi hi.
english: Your servant Joab has done this thing to change the face of the matter. My lord is wise, according to the wisdom of an angel of God, to know all things that are on the earth.”

paite: Kumpipa'n Joab kiang ah, "Ngai in, ka hih samta hi. Huaiziak in pai inla, tangval Absalom va pi nawn lechin maw," achi hi.
english: The king said to Joab, “Behold now, I have granted this thing. Go therefore, and bring the young man Absalom back.”

paite: Joab in amai a lei si in abokkhup a, kumpipa kiang ah kipahthu agen hi. Joab in, "Toupa ka kumpipa aw, toupa'n asikha ngetna alohchinsak ziak in tuni in na sikha in na mitmuh in deihsakna atang chih ka na theita hi," achi hi.
english: Joab fell to the ground on his face, showed respect, and blessed the king. Joab said, “Today your servant knows that I have found favor in your sight, my lord, O king, in that the king has performed the request of his servant.”

paite: Huchi in Joab athou a, Geshur ah ahoh a, Jerusalem ah Absalom ahon pita hi.
english: So Joab arose and went to Geshur, and brought Absalom to Jerusalem.

paite: Kumpipa'n, "Ama inn ah pai henla, ka mel hong mu kei hen," achi hi. Huchi in ama inn ah Absalom apai a, kumpipa mel amuta kei hi.
english: The king said, “Let him return to his own house, but let him not see my face.” So Absalom returned to his own house, and didn’t see the king’s face.

paite: Israel tengteng lak ah Absalom bang a melhoih a phat loh kuamah a-om kei uh. Akhenuai a pan alusip pha in gensiatna himhim a-om kei hi.
english: Now in all Israel there was no one to be so much praised as Absalom for his beauty. From the sole of his foot even to the crown of his head there was no defect in him.

paite: Asam amet chiang in, kum kivei teng in ametsak a, asam lah agik ziak in amet zel hi, abuk zel a, kumpipa bukna shekel zanih apha hi.
english: When he cut the hair of his head (now it was at every year’s end that he cut it; because it was heavy on him, therefore he cut it), he weighed the hair of his head at two hundred shekels, after the king’s weight.

paite: Absalom in tapa thum leh tanu khat anei a, amin Tamar ahi a, melhoihtak ahi.
english: Three sons were born to Absalom, and one daughter, whose name was Tamar. She was a woman with a beautiful face.

paite: Absalom kum nih hilhial Jerusalem ah a-om a; himahleh kumpipa mel himhim amu kei hi.
english: Absalom lived two full years in Jerusalem, and he didn’t see the king’s face.

paite: Absalom in kumpipa kiang a amah sawl ding in Joab athukhak hi. Himahleh ahoh nuam kei a, athukhak nawn in leng ahoh nuam tuan kei hi.
english: Then Absalom sent for Joab, to send him to the king, but he would not come to him. Then he sent again a second time, but he would not come.

paite: Huchi in asikhate kiang ah, "I aw, Joab lou, kei lou kiang ahi a, barli buh anei a, va hal un," achi hi. Huchi in Absalom sikhate'n lou ava hal uhi.
english: Therefore he said to his servants, “Behold, Joab’s field is near mine, and he has barley there. Go and set it on fire.” So Absalom’s servants set the field on fire.

paite: Huchi in Joab athou a, Absalom kiang ah a-inn ah ahoh a, "Bangziak a na sikhate'n ka lou hal ahi ua?" achi hi.
english: Then Joab arose and came to Absalom to his house, and said to him, “Why have your servants set my field on fire?”

paite: Absalom in Joab adawng a, "Ngai dih, bang ding a Geshur a pan hong pai ka hia? Huai ah omden leng kei a dia hoihzaw mah ding hiven. Kumpipa kiang a sawl dia hon thukhak ka hi. Huaiziak in tu in kumpipa mel hon musak in. Tatlekna nei ka hihleh hon that maileh ake," achi hi.
english: Absalom answered Joab, “Behold, I sent to you, saying, ‘Come here, that I may send you to the king, to say, “Why have I come from Geshur? It would be better for me to be there still. Now therefore, let me see the king’s face; and if there is iniquity in me, let him kill me.”’”

paite: Kumpipa kiang ah Joab ahoh a, ahilh hi. Ama'n Absalom asam a, kumpipa kiang ah ahoh a, kumpipa ma ah amai a lei si in abokkhup a; huchi in kumpipa'n Absalom atawp hi.
english: So Joab came to the king and told him; and when he had called for Absalom, he came to the king and bowed himself on his face to the ground before the king; and the king kissed Absalom.

paite: Huai khit in hichi ahong hi a, Absalom in kangtalai leh sakolte leh mi sawmnga ama a tai ding in abawlkhol hi.
english: After this, Absalom prepared a chariot and horses for himself, and fifty men to run before him.

paite: Absalom zingkhang in athou a, kulh kongkhak lampi nawl ah ana dingh hi. Thubuai khensak dia kumpipa kiang a hong pai peuhmah ana sam a, "Nang koi khopi a kipan na hia?" ana chi zel hi. Amau, "Na sikha Israel namte lak a khat ka hi,” achi zel uh.
english: Absalom rose up early, and stood beside the way of the gate. When any man had a suit which should come to the king for judgment, then Absalom called to him, and said, “What city are you from?” He said, “Your servant is of one of the tribes of Israel.”

paite: Absalom in, "I aw, na thu ahoih in adik hi. Himahleh angaikhe ding mi kumpipa'n kuamah asep kei," ana chi zel hi.
english: Absalom said to him, “Behold, your matters are good and right; but there is no man deputized by the king to hear you.”

paite: Absalom mah in, "Michih thubuai gen ding nei hiam, nget ding nei hiam peuhmah ka kiang a ahong paina ding un, gam vaihawmpa in bawl in om leng chi na tel ing e aw! Huchi in diktak in vai ka na hawmsak ding," ana chi zel hi.
english: Absalom said moreover, “Oh that I were made judge in the land, that every man who has any suit or cause might come to me, and I would do him justice!”

paite: Hichi leng ahi lai a, kuapeuh amah zahtakna pe dia hong paitou peuhmah akhut a sawk in alen a, ana tawp hi.
english: It was so, that when any man came near to bow down to him, he stretched out his hand, took hold of him, and kissed him.

paite: Israel mi kumpipa kiang a thugen dia hong kuan peuhmahte Absalom in huchibang in ana hih zel hi. Huchi in Absalom in Israel mite lungtang aguksak hi.
english: Absalom did this sort of thing to all Israel who came to the king for judgment. So Absalom stole the hearts of the men of Israel.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, kum li ahong bei in Absalom in kumpipa kiang ah, Hebron a TOUPA kiang a ka thuchiam tangtun ding in hon hohsak in.
english: At the end of forty years, Absalom said to the king, “Please let me go and pay my vow, which I have vowed to Yahweh, in Hebron.

paite: "Na sikha in Siria gam a Geshur a ka om lai in Jerusalem a ahon pikik peuhmahleh TOUPA nna ka sem ding, chi in thu ka chiam khinta ngal a," achi hi.
english: For your servant vowed a vow while I stayed at Geshur in Syria, saying, ‘If Yahweh shall indeed bring me again to Jerusalem, then I will serve Yahweh.’”

paite: Kumpipa'n akiang ah, "Khamuangtak in kuan in," achi hi. Huchi in athou a, Hebron ah ahohta hi.
english: The king said to him, “Go in peace.” So he arose and went to Hebron.

paite: Himahleh Absalom in, “Pengkul ging na zak peuhmah chiang un, Hebron ah Absalom kumpipa ahita, na chi ding uh," chi in Israel nam tengteng kiang ah mi asimsawl khinta hi.
english: But Absalom sent spies throughout all the tribes of Israel, saying, “As soon as you hear the sound of the trumpet, then you shall say, ‘Absalom is king in Hebron!’”

paite: Jerusalem a pan asap mi zanih in Absalom azui uhi. Amau bel lungsim siangtak pu in ahoh ua, thil omdan bangmah athei kei uh.
english: Two hundred men went with Absalom out of Jerusalem, who were invited, and went in their simplicity; and they didn’t know anything.

paite: Absalom in kithoihnate alat lai in Gilon mi Ahithophel, David thudotmi, Giloh a pan athukhak hi. Athusawmguk uh athupi mahmah a; Absalom lam ah lah mipite apung hulhul uhi.
english: Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, David’s counselor, from his city, even from Giloh, while he was offering the sacrifices. The conspiracy was strong, for the people increased continually with Absalom.

paite: David kiang ah, Israel mite lungtang Absalom lam ah a-awn mahmah, chih thupotu khat in ahong hilh hi.
english: A messenger came to David, saying, “The hearts of the men of Israel are after Absalom.”

paite: David in Jerusalem a om, asikha tengteng kiang ah, "Thou unla i taikhe ding uh. Kuamah lah Absalom a pan suakta lou ding i hi ngal ua. Pawtkhe meng un. Huchi lou in zaw ahon pha pah mai dia, i tung uah thil hoih loutak ahon tun dia, namsau in khua ahong sual kha ding," achi hi.
english: David said to all his servants who were with him at Jerusalem, “Arise! Let’s flee, or else none of us will escape from Absalom. Hurry to depart, lest he overtake us quickly and bring down evil on us, and strike the city with the edge of the sword.”

paite: Kumpipa sikhate'n kumpipa kiang ah, "Ngai in, na sikhate ka toupa, ka kumpipa un aseh peuhmah hih dia mansa ka hi gige uh," achi uhi.
english: The king’s servants said to the king, “Behold, your servants are ready to do whatever my lord the king chooses.”

paite: Kumpipa apawt a, a-inkote tengteng in azui uhi. Kumpipa'n inn ngak ding in numei sawm, ameite akoih hi.
english: The king went out, and all his household after him. The king left ten women, who were concubines, to keep the house.

paite: Kumpipa apawt a, mi tengteng in azui uh. Gamla kuam mun khat, inn tawpna ah akhawl tadih uhi.
english: The king went out, and all the people after him; and they stayed in Beth Merhak.

paite: Asikha tengteng in apaikheng ua; Kerit mite, Pelet mite, Git mite, mi zaguk Gath a pan amah hon zuite kumpipa ma ah apai uhi.
english: All his servants passed on beside him; and all the Cherethites, and all the Pelethites, and all the Gittites, six hundred men who came after him from Gath, passed on before the king.

paite: Huchi in kumpipa'n Git mi, Ittai kiang ah, "Bangchidan ahia nang na hong tel? Paikik nawn inla, kumpipa kiang ah om in. Nang zaw mikhual gamdangmi leng na hi ngal a, nangmah mun lam ah kik nawn mai in.
english: Then the king said to Ittai the Gittite, “Why do you also go with us? Return, and stay with the king; for you are a foreigner and also an exile. Return to your own place.

paite: Zan zek a hong na hi a, tuni a ka kiang ua asuk atou a hon zui sam ding in ka hon chi ding maw? Ka pai theihtheihna a pai ding ka hi, nang zaw kik nawn inla, na unaute tengteng pikik nawn in. Hehpihna leh thutak na kiang ah om hen," achi hi.
english: Whereas you came but yesterday, should I today make you go up and down with us, since I go where I may? Return, and take back your brothers. Mercy and truth be with you.”

paite: Ittai in kumpipa kiang ah, "TOUPA hinna leh kumpipa, ka toupa ahin bang in ka gen ahi. Kumpipa, ka toupa na omna peuh ah, sih leh sih, dam leh dam, na sikha a-om sam ding," achi hi.
english: Ittai answered the king and said, “As Yahweh lives, and as my lord the king lives, surely in what place my lord the king is, whether for death or for life, your servant will be there also.”

paite: David in Ittai kiang ah, "Pai inla, va galkai in," achi hi. Huchi in Git mi Ittai, amite tengteng leh ataneute tengteng toh agalkai uhi.
english: David said to Ittai, “Go and pass over.” Ittai the Gittite passed over, and all his men, and all the little ones who were with him.

paite: Ngaihtak in huai gammi teng akap ua, mipite apai vek uhi. Gamdai lampi zuan in apai ua, kumpipa'n leng Kidron lui akan a, mipi tengteng in leng akan uhi.
english: All the country wept with a loud voice, and all the people passed over. The king also himself passed over the brook Kidron, and all the people passed over toward the way of the wilderness.

paite: Huan ngai in, Pathian thukhun bawm zawng in Zadok leh Levite tengteng akiang ah ahong pai uhi. Pathian bawm anga ua, mipi in khua apawtkhiaksan vek tan in Abiathar ahohtou hi.
english: Behold, Zadok also came, and all the Levites with him, bearing the ark of the covenant of God; and they set down God’s ark; and Abiathar went up until all the people finished passing out of the city.

paite: Kumpipa'n Zadok kiang ah, "Pathian bawm pen khopi sung ah zawnglut nawn un. TOUPA mitmuh a deihsakna ka tanleh ahon pikik nawn dia, Pathian bawm leh a-omna ahon musak nawn ding.
english: The king said to Zadok, “Carry God’s ark back into the city. If I find favor in Yahweh’s eyes, he will bring me again, and show me both it and his habitation;

paite: Himahleh, nang ah kipahna mahmah ka nei kei achihleh, ngai in, hichi mai ka hi a, hoih asak bangbang in ka tung ah hih mai hen," achi hi.
english: but if he says, ‘I have no delight in you,’ behold, here I am. Let him do to me as seems good to him.”

paite: Kumpipa'n siampu Zadok kiang ah, "Mutheipa na hi kei a hia? Na tapate nih, na tapa Ahimaaz leh Abiathar tapa Jonathan toh lungmuangtak in khopi ah pai nawn un.
english: The king said also to Zadok the priest, “Aren’t you a seer? Return into the city in peace, and your two sons with you, Ahimaaz your son and Jonathan the son of Abiathar.

paite: Ngai in, kei zaw tanchin ahong theihsak masiah uh gamdai a lui kannate ah ka na om ding,” achi hi.
english: Behold, I will stay at the fords of the wilderness until word comes from you to inform me.”

paite: Zadok leh Abiathar in Jerusalem ah Pathian bawm apaipih nawn ua; huai ah a-omta uh.
english: Zadok therefore and Abiathar carried God’s ark to Jerusalem again; and they stayed there.

paite: Olive tang paitouhna ah David akahtou a, apaitouh ka kawm in akap kawmkawm hi. Alu akhuh a, khevuak in apai hi. Akiang a mi om tengteng in alu uh akhuh chiat ua, kap kawmkawm in apaitou uhi.
english: David went up by the ascent of the Mount of Olives, and wept as he went up; and he had his head covered and went barefoot. All the people who were with him each covered his head, and they went up, weeping as they went up.

paite: Kuahiam khat in Ahithophel, Absalom lam a pang in thusawm mite lak ah apang sam, chih David ahilh hi. David in, "TOUPA aw, Ahithophel lemtheihna haina suaksak ding in ka hon ngen hi," achi hi.
english: Someone told David, saying, “Ahithophel is among the conspirators with Absalom.” David said, “Yahweh, please turn the counsel of Ahithophel into foolishness.”

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, Pathian biakna tang vum a David akahkhiak touhleh, ngai in, Arki mi Hushai apuanak bohkek silh a, alu a lei kai niaunuau in amah dawn ding in ahong pai hi.
english: When David had come to the top, where God was worshiped, behold, Hushai the Archite came to meet him with his tunic torn and earth on his head.

paite: David in akiang ah, "Ka kiang a na hong samleh zaw, kei a ding in puakgik na hi ding.
english: David said to him, “If you pass on with me, then you will be a burden to me;

paite: Himahleh khopi a na kik nawn a, Absalom kiang a, toupa aw, na sikha in ka om ding. Tuma lam a na pa sikha a ka om bang in, tu in na sikha in ka om leuleu ding, na va chihleh Ahithophel lemtheihna hon dalsakpa na hi zaw ding hi.
english: but if you return to the city, and tell Absalom, ‘I will be your servant, O king. As I have been your father’s servant in time past, so I will now be your servant; then you will defeat for me the counsel of Ahithophel.’

paite: Huai ah na kiang ah siampu Zadok leh Abiathar leng a-om sam uh ahi kei maw? Huan hichi ahi ding a, kumpipa' inn a thupawt na zak peuhmah siampu Zadok leh Abiathar na hilh zel ding.
english: Don’t you have Zadok and Abiathar the priests there with you? Therefore whatever you hear out of the king’s house, tell it to Zadok and Abiathar the priests.

paite: Ngai in, atapate uh nih Zadok tapa Ahimaaz leh Abiathar tapa Jonathan leng akiang uah a-om uhi. Na thil zak peuhmahte hon theisak ding in amau na hon sawl zel ding," achi hi.
english: Behold, they have there with them their two sons, Ahimaaz, Zadok’s son, and Jonathan, Abiathar’s son. Send to me everything that you shall hear by them.”

paite: Huchi in David lawm, Hushai khopi ah alut a; huchi in Jerusalem ah Absalom alutta hi.
english: So Hushai, David’s friend, came into the city; and Absalom came into Jerusalem.

paite: Huan David in tang vum kahkhiakna akhen zek nung in, ngai in, Mephibosheth sikha Ziba in sabiltung nih toh ana dawn hi. Sabiltung nihte'n tanghou beu zanih, grep phoukeu bawk zakhat, nipithei zakhat leh uain thawl khat apua uhi.
english: When David was a little past the top, behold, Ziba the servant of Mephibosheth met him with a couple of donkeys saddled, and on them two hundred loaves of bread, and one hundred clusters of raisins, and one hundred summer fruits, and a container of wine.

paite: Kumpipa'n Ziba kiang ah, "Hiaite bangchidan ahia?" achi hi. Ziba in, "Sabiltungte kumpipa inkuanpihte tuanna ding ahi, Tanghou leh nipitheite tangvalte nek ding; uain bel gamdai a bah peuhmahte dawn ding ahi," achi hi.
english: The king said to Ziba, “What do you mean by these?” Ziba said, “The donkeys are for the king’s household to ride on; and the bread and summer fruit for the young men to eat; and the wine, that those who are faint in the wilderness may drink.”

paite: Kumpipa'n, "Ahihleh na pu tapa koi ah?" achi hi. Ziba in kumpipa kiang ah, "Ngai in, Jerusalem ah a-om. 'Tuni in Israel inkote'n ka pa lalgam ahon pekik nawn ding uh, chi a angaihtuah ziak in,' " achi hi.
english: The king said, “Where is your master’s son?” Ziba said to the king, “Behold, he is staying in Jerusalem; for he said, ‘Today the house of Israel will restore me the kingdom of my father.’”

paite: Kumpipa'n Ziba kiang ah, "Ngai in, Mephibosheth thil neih tengteng nang a ahi vekta," achi hi. Ziba in, "Ka toupa, kumpipa aw, na mitmuh a deihsakna mu ding in kingainiamtak in ka hon ngen," achi hi.
english: Then the king said to Ziba, “Behold, all that belongs to Mephibosheth is yours.” Ziba said, “I bow down. Let me find favor in your sight, my lord, O king.”

paite: Kumpipa David, Bahurim atun in, ngai in, Saul inkote lak a mi Gera tapa, amin Shimei ahong pawtkhia a; hamsia lou kawmkawm in ahong paitou hi.
english: When King David came to Bahurim, behold, a man of the family of Saul’s house came out, whose name was Shimei, the son of Gera. He came out and cursed as he came.

paite: Suang in David adeng a, kumpipa David sikha tengteng leng; mi tengteng leh sepaih hat tengteng ataklam leh veilam ah a-om uhi.
english: He cast stones at David and at all the servants of King David, and all the people and all the mighty men were on his right hand and on his left.

paite: Shimei in hamsiat in hichi in achi, "Paimang vengveng in, paimang vengveng in, nang sisan suah hat leh Belial mipa:
english: Shimei said when he cursed, “Be gone, be gone, you man of blood, and wicked fellow!

paite: Asik a vai na hawm Saul inkote tengteng sisan TOUPA'N na tung ah ahon kiksak nawnta. TOUPA'N gam na tapa Absalom ana pe khinta. Ngai in, sisan suah hatmi na hih ziak in nangmah siatna na kitun ve," achi hi.
english: Yahweh has returned on you all the blood of Saul’s house, in whose place you have reigned! Yahweh has delivered the kingdom into the hand of Absalom your son! Behold, you are caught by your own mischief, because you are a man of blood!”

paite: Huchi in Zeruiah tapa Abishai in kumpipa kiang ah, "Bangziak a hiai ui sisa in toupa, ka pu hamsiat mawkmawk ahia? Ka kuantou ding a alu ka tansak mai ding?" achi hi.
english: Then Abishai the son of Zeruiah said to the king, “Why should this dead dog curse my lord the king? Please let me go over and take off his head.”

paite: Kumpipa'n, "Nou Zeruiah tapate aw, nou na hon theihsak ding uh bang a-om a? TOUPA'N akiang a, David hamsiat in, achihleh ahamsiat ahi mai kei dia. Bangziak a huchibang a hih kua'n achi dia?" achi hi.
english: The king said, “What have I to do with you, you sons of Zeruiah? Because he curses, and because Yahweh has said to him, ‘Curse David,’ who then shall say, ‘Why have you done so?’”

paite: David in Abishai leh asikhate tengteng kiang ah, "Ngai un, ka tapa, ka gil a gah mahmah in hon thah atum. Hiai Benjamin mi'n nak tup sem na'n chia! Bangmah loh kei unla, hamsia ahihleh loh hen. TOUPA hihsak ahi,
