paite: Haman in akiang uah, ahauhsakna thupina leh atate tamdan leh kumpipa'n akaisansakna thil tengteng leh kumpipa sikhate vaihawmte tung a amasak tuamdan agen hi.
english: Haman recounted to them the glory of his riches, the multitude of his children, all the things in which the king had promoted him, and how he had advanced him above the princes and servants of the king.

paite: Haman in, ahi, "Esther in an nekna abawl ah kumpipa toh kei chih louh ngal mi kuamah ahohsak kei; zingchiang in leng kumpipa toh kei ahon sam hi.
english: Haman also said, “Yes, Esther the queen let no man come in with the king to the banquet that she had prepared but myself; and tomorrow I am also invited by her together with the king.

paite: Himahleh Mordekai huai Juda mipa, kumpipa kongpi a tu ka muh lai teng hiaite tengteng kei a ding in bangmah aphatuam kei,” achi lai hi.
english: Yet all this avails me nothing, so long as I see Mordecai the Jew sitting at the king’s gate.”

paite: Huchi in azi Zeresh leh alawmte'n akiang ah, "Khailupna khuam tong sawmnga a sang kibawl henla, zingsang in nang kumpipa kiang ah thu gen inla, huai a Mordekai khailup ahihtheihna ding in; huchi in vualnuamtak in kumpipa toh an nekna ah na hoh ding uh," achi uhi. Hiai in Haman akipaksak a; huchi in khailupna khuam abawlsakta hi.
english: Then Zeresh his wife and all his friends said to him, “Let a gallows be made fifty cubits high, and in the morning speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on it. Then go in merrily with the king to the banquet.” This pleased Haman, so he had the gallows made.

paite: Huai zan in kumpipa a-ihmu thei kei; tanchin chiamtehna laibu hon tawi ding in thu apia a, huaite kumpipa ma ah asim uhi.
english: On that night, the king couldn’t sleep. He commanded the book of records of the chronicles to be brought, and they were read to the king.

paite: Kumpipa michilgehte lak a mi nih Bigthan leh Teresh, kongkhak vengte'n, kumpipa Ahasueras tung a khut khak sawmte tanchin Mordekai in agen chih kigelhna muh in a-om hi.
english: It was found written that Mordecai had told of Bigthana and Teresh, two of the king’s eunuchs, who were doorkeepers, who had tried to lay hands on the King Ahasuerus.

paite: Huchi in kumpipa'n, "Hiai ziak in Mordekai tung ah bang zahtakna leh thupina hih in a-om a?" achi hi. Kumpipa sikha amah nasemte'n, "Amah a ding in bangmah hih a-om kei,” achi uhi.
english: The king said, “What honor and dignity has been given to Mordecai for this?” Then the king’s servants who attended him said, “Nothing has been done for him.”

paite: Kumpipa'n, "Pisa a om kua ahia?" achi a. Huchi in Haman, kumpipa' inn pisa ponungzaw ah, kumpipa kiang a abawlkholhsa khailupna khuam a Mordekai khai ding thu gen ding in ahong hi.
english: The king said, “Who is in the court?” Now Haman had come into the outer court of the king’s house, to speak to the king about hanging Mordecai on the gallows that he had prepared for him.

paite: Kumpipa sikhate'n akiang ah, "Ngai in pisa ah Haman adingh nilouh hi," achi ua. Kumpipa'n, "Hong lut heh," achi hi.
english: The king’s servants said to him, “Behold, Haman stands in the court.” The king said, “Let him come in.”

paite: Huchi in Haman ahong lut hi. Kumpipa'n akiang ah, "Mi kumpipa'n azahtak nop tung ah bang kihih ding ahia?" achi hi. Haman in alungtang in, Kumpipa'n kei sang a pahtawi dia akipahna kua kiang a bawl nuamzaw ahia? achi hi.
english: So Haman came in. The king said to him, “What shall be done to the man whom the king delights to honor?” Now Haman said in his heart, “Who would the king delight to honor more than myself?”

paite: Haman in kumpipa kiang ah, "Kumpipa'n apahtawi nopmi a ding in,
english: Haman said to the king, “For the man whom the king delights to honor,

paite: kumpipa'n asilh zel kumpi puansilh hon lakhia henla, sakol kumpipa tuan zelna leng, aluzang a lallukhu akoihna zel:
english: let royal clothing be brought which the king uses to wear, and the horse that the king rides on, and on the head of which a royal crown is set.

paite: Huchi in puansilh leh sakol kumpipa vaihawmpih thupi penpente lak a khat khut ah pekheleh, huaite akumpipa'n zahtak a-utpa azeptheihna ding un leh khopi kongzing lak ah sakol tung ah tuangsak henla, ama ah, huchibang in kumpipa'n apahtawi nopte kiang ah hih in a-om ding, chi in puang leng," achi hi.
english: Let the clothing and the horse be delivered to the hand of one of the king’s most noble princes, that they may array the man whom the king delights to honor with them, and have him ride on horseback through the city square, and proclaim before him, ‘Thus it shall be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!’”

paite: Huai laitak in kumpipa'n Haman kiang ah, "Kin inla, na chih bang in, puansilh leh sakol la inla, kumpipa kongpi a tu zel Juda mi Mordekai tung ah hih in: na gen tengteng bangmah vuaksuak kei hen," achi hi.
english: Then the king said to Haman, “Hurry and take the clothing and the horse, as you have said, and do this for Mordecai the Jew, who sits at the king’s gate. Let nothing fail of all that you have spoken.”

paite: Huchi in Haman in puansilh leh sakol ala a, Mordekai azem a, khopi kongzing lak ah atuangsak a, ama ah, "Hichibang in kumpipa'n azahtak nopmi tung a ahih ahi ding,” chi in apuangta hi.
english: Then Haman took the clothing and the horse, and arrayed Mordecai, and had him ride through the city square, and proclaimed before him, “Thus it shall be done to the man whom the king delights to honor!”

paite: Huan kumpipa kongpi ah Mordekai ahong pai nawn hi. Himahleh Haman bel suun leh alutang khuhsa in a-inn lam ah kintak in apai hi.
english: Mordecai came back to the king’s gate, but Haman hurried to his house, mourning and having his head covered.

paite: Huchi in Haman in azi Zeresh kiang leh alawmte tengteng kiang ah atung a thil tung tengteng agen vek hi. Huaitak in amipilte leh azi Zeresh in akiang ah, "Ama a na puk patna Mordekai, Juda chi a mi ahihleh, amah na zou kei ding, himahleh ama ah na puk ngei ding," achi uhi.
english: Haman recounted to Zeresh his wife and all his friends everything that had happened to him. Then his wise men and Zeresh his wife said to him, “If Mordecai, before whom you have begun to fall, is of Jewish descent, you will not prevail against him, but you will surely fall before him.”

paite: Amah toh ahoulim san lai un, kumpipa michilgehte ahong pai ua, Esther in an nek ding abawlna a ding in kintak in hong pita uhi.
english: While they were yet talking with him, the king’s eunuchs came, and hurried to bring Haman to the banquet that Esther had prepared.

paite: Huchi in kumpipa leh Haman kumpinu Esther toh an nekna ah ahong uhi.
english: So the king and Haman came to banquet with Esther the queen.

paite: Uain adawn lai un ani nih ni in kumpipa'n Esther kiang ah, "Bang ahia na thumna, kumpinu Esther? Ahon phalsak ding uh bang ahia na ngetna? Gam kimkhat leng piak in na om ding," achi hi.
english: The king said again to Esther on the second day at the banquet of wine, “What is your petition, queen Esther? It shall be granted you. What is your request? Even to the half of the kingdom it shall be performed.”

paite: Huchi in Esther kumpinu'n adawng a, "Aw kumpipa, na mitmuh a deihsakna ka tan a, kumpipa kipahna ahihleh, ka thumna ah ka hinna leh ka mite hinna piak in om hen:
english: Then Esther the queen answered, “If I have found favor in your sight, O king, and if it pleases the king, let my life be given me at my petition, and my people at my request.

paite: Zuak in ka omta ua, kei leh ka mite, hihgawp a om ding in, thah a om ding in leh hihmang ding in. Sikhapa ding leh sikhanu ding a zuak a om hi le ung zaw, melma in kumpipa siatna gun bawl theita kei mahleh, dai dide ding hi veng in " achi hi.
english: For we are sold, I and my people, to be destroyed, to be slain, and to perish. But if we had been sold for male and female slaves, I would have held my peace, although the adversary could not have compensated for the king’s loss.”

paite: Kumpipa Ahasueras in thu agen a, kumpinu Esther kiang ah, "Kua ahia, koi a om ahia, huchibang a lungtang sung a tum ngam?" achi hi.
english: Then King Ahasuerus said to Esther the queen, “Who is he, and where is he who dared presume in his heart to do so?”

paite: Esther in, "Melma leh gal, hiai giloupa Haman mah," achi hi. Huchi in kumpipa leh kumpinu ma ah Haman alauta hi.
english: Esther said, “An adversary and an enemy, even this wicked Haman!” Then Haman was afraid before the king and the queen.

paite: Huchi in uain dawnkhamna a kipan aheh ziak in kumpipa adingkhia a, inpi huansung ah alut a; huchi in kumpinu Esther kiang a ahinna ngen ding in Haman adingh hi; kumpipa'n asiatna ding in hoih lou a tup a-om chih lah athei ngal a.
english: The king arose in his wrath from the banquet of wine and went into the palace garden. Haman stood up to make request for his life to Esther the queen, for he saw that there was evil determined against him by the king.

paite: Kumpipa Kulhpi huan a kipan uain an nekna mun ah ahong kik a; huchi in Esther omna tutphah nem tung ah Haman apuk hi. Kumpipa'n, "Inn sung a ka ma a kumpinu nangawn sual ding ahi hia?" achi hi. Kumpipa kam a thupawt bang in, Haman maitang atuamsakta uhi.
english: Then the king returned out of the palace garden into the place of the banquet of wine; and Haman had fallen on the couch where Esther was. Then the king said, “Will he even assault the queen in front of me in the house?” As the word went out of the king’s mouth, they covered Haman’s face.

paite: Huai lai in kumpipa ma a om zel michilgehte lak a khat, Harbonah in, "En un, Haman in Mordekai, kumpipa gum a thugenpa a dia abawl, khailupna khuam tong sawmnga a sang, Haman inn ah adingh hi," achi hi. Huan kumpipa'n, "Huai ah amah khailum un," achi hi.
english: Then Harbonah, one of the eunuchs who were with the king, said, “Behold, the gallows fifty cubits high, which Haman has made for Mordecai, who spoke good for the king, is standing at Haman’s house.” The king said, “Hang him on it!”

paite: Huchi in Mordekai a dia abawlkholhsak khailupna khuam ah Haman akhailumta uhi. Huchi in kumpipa thangpaihna adaita hi.
english: So they hanged Haman on the gallows that he had prepared for Mordecai. Then the king’s wrath was pacified.

paite: Huai ni in kumpipa Ahasueras in kumpinu Esther kiang ah Judate melmapa Haman inn apia hi. Kumpipa ma ah Mordekai ahong a; Esther in amah a ding in kua ahia chih agen khinta hi.
english: On that day, King Ahasuerus gave the house of Haman, the Jews’ enemy, to Esther the queen. Mordecai came before the king; for Esther had told what he was to her.

paite: Huchi in kumpipa'n azungbuh asuah a, Haman a kipan alak, Mordekai kiang ah apeta hi. Esther in Haman inkote tung ah Mordekai akoihta hi.
english: The king took off his ring, which he had taken from Haman, and gave it to Mordecai. Esther set Mordecai over the house of Haman.

paite: Esther in kumpipa ma ah thu agen lai a, akhebul a puk in, Agag mi Haman gilou bawl leh Judate siatna ding a alunggel khitsa a lunggelna koihmang ding in khitui toh amah angen ngutngut hi.
english: Esther spoke yet again before the king, and fell down at his feet and begged him with tears to put away the mischief of Haman the Agagite, and his plan that he had planned against the Jews.

paite: Huchi in kumpipa'n Esther lam ah adangka-eng kumpi chiang alen a. Huchi in Esther athou a kumpipa ma ah adingh hi.
english: Then the king held out to Esther the golden scepter. So Esther arose, and stood before the king.

paite: Ama'n, "Kumpipa lungkimna ahih a, amitmuh a deihsakna ka tan a, kumpipa ma a thil dik a alat a, amuh a lungkimhuai ka hihleh, Agag mi Hammedatha tapa Haman in laikhak abawlte kumpipa bial a om Judate hihsiatna ding a agelh sut in om hen.
english: She said, “If it pleases the king, and if I have found favor in his sight, and the thing seems right to the king, and I am pleasing in his eyes, let it be written to reverse the letters devised by Haman, the son of Hammedatha the Agagite, which he wrote to destroy the Jews who are in all the king’s provinces.

paite: Huchi lou in ka mite tung a gilou tung ding ke'n bangchi in ka en ngam dia? Ahihkeileh ka tanaute siatna bangchi in ka mu ngam dia?" achi hi.
english: For how can I endure to see the evil that would come to my people? How can I endure to see the destruction of my relatives?”

paite: Kumpipa Ahasueras in kumpinu Esther kiang leh Juda mi Mordekai kiang ah, "Ngai un, Judate tung a akhut akhak ziak in, Haman inkote leh khailupna khuam a akhailuppa uh amah Esther kiang ah apeta hi.
english: Then King Ahasuerus said to Esther the queen and to Mordecai the Jew, “See, I have given Esther the house of Haman, and they have hanged him on the gallows because he laid his hand on the Jews.

paite: Na deih bang in, kumpipa min in, kumpipa zungbuh a sawn in, Judate kiang ah leng lai gelh un; kumpipa min a lai kigelh, kumpipa zungbuh a kisawn peuhmah, mi kuamah in ahihlamdang thei ngal kei a," achi hi.
english: Write also to the Jews as it pleases you, in the king’s name, and seal it with the king’s ring; for the writing which is written in the king’s name, and sealed with the king’s ring, may not be reversed by any man.”

paite: Huchi in kumpipa laigelhmite asam ua, akha thumna Sivan kha a, ani sawmnih-le-thum ni in; Judate tungtang thu Mordekai in thu apiak bang in gam heutute kiang leh India a kipan Ethiopia pha a om bialte ukpipate leh vaihawmte, bial zakhat sawmnih-le-sagih, huai a kigelhdan bang zel a bial chiteng kiang, mi chih apau uh dungzui zel in, alaigelh uh bang zel a Judate, apau uh bang zel in akiang uah gelh in a-omta hi.
english: Then the king’s scribes were called at that time, in the third month, which is the month Sivan, on the twenty-third day of the month; and it was written according to all that Mordecai commanded to the Jews, and to the local governors, and the governors and princes of the provinces which are from India to Ethiopia, one hundred twenty-seven provinces, to every province according to its writing, and to every people in their language, and to the Jews in their writing, and in their language.

paite: Kumpipa Ahasueras min in agelh a, kumpipa zungbuh in asawn a, kumpipa nasepna a kizangsek sakol man-gang, hoihtak a vulhte a tuang in sakol tung ah dak in laikhakte akhakta hi.
english: He wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, and sealed it with the king’s ring, and sent letters by courier on horseback, riding on royal horses that were bred from swift steeds.

paite: Huai ah kumpipa'n khopi chiteng a om Judate kikhawmkhawm a, ahinna ua dia pang a, amaute sual ding a anau neute uleh anumeite uh, asum uh gallak a la ding a kisa mite leh bial thilhihtheihna hihse ding leh mangthangsak ding in phalna apia hi.
english: In those letters, the king granted the Jews who were in every city to gather themselves together and to defend their lives—to destroy, to kill, and to cause to perish all the power of the people and province that would assault them, their little ones and women, and to plunder their possessions,

paite: Kumpipa Ahasueras bial tengteng ah ni khat in, huai bel, akha sawm-le-nih, Adar kha ahi a, ani sawm-le-thum ni geih in.
english: on one day in all the provinces of King Ahasuerus, on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, which is the month Adar.

paite: Bial chih a piak ding chi a thupiak, kigelh a teisawn mite tengteng kiang ah suah in a-om a, huai ni chiang a Judate'n amelmate uh tung a phu la dia mansa a a-om chiat theihna ding un.
english: A copy of the letter, that the decree should be given out in every province, was published to all the peoples, that the Jews should be ready for that day to avenge themselves on their enemies.

paite: Huchi in dak kumpipa nasepna a zat sakol man-gangte tung a tuangte apaikhia ua, kumpipa thupiak in amau anoh in akhawksak ngal ua; thupiak pen Susa Inpi a piakkhiak ahi.
english: So the couriers who rode on royal horses went out, hastened and pressed on by the king’s commandment. The decree was given out in the citadel of Susa.

paite: Huchi in Mordekai bel kumpi puandum leh kang, dangka-eng lallukhu thupitak toh, puanaktual puanmalngat hoih leh sandup toh kumpipa ma a kipan apaikheta hi: Susa khopi akikou a, akipak hi.
english: Mordecai went out of the presence of the king in royal clothing of blue and white, and with a great crown of gold, and with a robe of fine linen and purple; and the city of Susa shouted and was glad.

paite: Huchi in Judate'n kouzanna leh kipahna, nopna leh zahna anei uhi.
english: The Jews had light, gladness, joy, and honor.

paite: Bial chih leh khopi chih a koi lai peuh a kumpipa thupiak leh athubawl paina peuh ah, Judate'n ankuangluina leh ni hoih kipahna leh nopna anei uhi. Huchi in gam a mite lak a tampite Judate ahong hi ua; Judate launa lah atung uah ahong omta hi.
english: In every province and in every city, wherever the king’s commandment and his decree came, the Jews had gladness, joy, a feast and a holiday. Many from among the peoples of the land became Jews, for the fear of the Jews had fallen on them.

paite: Huan akha sawm-le-nih, Adar kha, huai mah ani sawm-le-thum ni, kumpipa thupiak leh athubawl tangtunna ding ahong nai lai in, Judate melmate'n atung ua vaihawmna neih akilamet ni uh; hinapi a, ahilou lam a hong kilehbut a, Judate'n amau mudahte tung a vaihawmna ahon neih lai un;
english: Now in the twelfth month, which is the month Adar, on the thirteenth day of the month, when the king’s commandment and his decree came near to be put in execution, on the day that the enemies of the Jews hoped to conquer them, (but it turned out that the opposite happened, that the Jews conquered those who hated them),

paite: Kumpipa Ahasueras bial tengteng akhopite uah Judate, amau siatna zongte tung a khut kha ding in, akikhawmkhawm ua: kuamah in lah amaute anangzou kei uhi; mite tengteng tung ah lah amaute launa ahong omta hi.
english: the Jews gathered themselves together in their cities throughout all the provinces of the King Ahasuerus, to lay hands on those who wanted to harm them. No one could withstand them, because the fear of them had fallen on all the people.

paite: Huchi in bialte a vaihawmte leh gamuk mite leh ukpipate leh kumpipa nasemte'n, Judate apanpih ua; Mordekai launa lah atung uah ahong om ngal a.
english: All the princes of the provinces, the local governors, the governors, and those who did the king’s business helped the Jews, because the fear of Mordecai had fallen on them.

paite: Kumpipa' inn ah Mordekai athupi a, bial tengteng ah amin athangkheta hi: hiai mipa Mordekai lah ahong thupi semsem hi.
english: For Mordecai was great in the king’s house, and his fame went out throughout all the provinces, for the man Mordecai grew greater and greater.

paite: Huchi in namsau a sat in Judate'n amelmate tengteng athat ua, thahna leh hihsiatna in, amaute mudahte tung ah ahih ding uh ahihta uhi.
english: The Jews struck all their enemies with the stroke of the sword, and with slaughter and destruction, and did what they wanted to those who hated them.

paite: Susa Inpi ah Judate'n mi zanga athat ua ahihgawp uhi.
english: In the citadel of Susa, the Jews killed and destroyed five hundred men.

paite: Parsandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,
english: They killed Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,

paite: Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,
english: Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,

paite: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, Vajezathate,
english: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vaizatha,

paite: Judate melmapa Hammedatha tapa Haman tapate, athat ua; himahleh gallak ah akhut uh anga kei uhi.
english: the ten sons of Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Jews’ enemy, but they didn’t lay their hand on the plunder.

paite: Huai ni in Susa Inpi a thah a om zah kumpipa ma ah ahon tawi uhi.
english: On that day, the number of those who were slain in the citadel of Susa was brought before the king.

paite: Huan kumpipa'n kumpinu Esther kiang ah, "Judate'n Susa Inpi sung ah mi zanga athat ua ahihsia uh, Haman tapa sawmte toh; kumpipa bial dangte ah bang achi bawlta phet ding uam ah: Khai le, bang ahia na nget? Na kiang ah phal ahi ding; ahihkeileh bang ngetbeh na nei lai a? Suk pichin ahi ding," achi hi.
english: The king said to Esther the queen, “The Jews have slain and destroyed five hundred men in the citadel of Susa, including the ten sons of Haman; what then have they done in the rest of the king’s provinces! Now what is your petition? It shall be granted you. What is your further request? It shall be done.”

paite: Esther in, "Kumpipa' lungkimna ahihleh, zingchiang a tuni a thupiak bangbang a gamtang ding in Susa a om Judate phal inla, Haman tapa sawmte khailupna khuam ah kikhai le uh," achi hi.
english: Then Esther said, “If it pleases the king, let it be granted to the Jews who are in Susa to do tomorrow also according to today’s decree, and let Haman’s ten sons be hanged on the gallows.”

paite: Huchi in huchibang a hih ahi ding chi in kumpipa'n thu apia hi: Susa ah thubawl akipekhia a: huchi in Haman tapa sawmte akhaita uhi.
english: The king commanded this to be done. A decree was given out in Susa; and they hanged Haman’s ten sons.

paite: Adar kha mah ani sawm-le-li ni in Susa a om Judate akikhawmkhawm ua, Susa ah mi zathum athat uh; himahleh gallak tung ah akhut uh anga kei uhi.
english: The Jews who were in Susa gathered themselves together on the fourteenth day also of the month Adar, and killed three hundred men in Susa; but they didn’t lay their hand on the plunder.

paite: Huchi in kumpipa bialte a om Juda dangte akikhawmkhawm ua, ahinna uh ahum ua, amelmate ua kipan khawlna anei ua, amau mudahte lak ah mi singsagih-le-sangnga athat ua; himahleh gallak tung ah akhut uh anga kei uh.
english: The other Jews who were in the king’s provinces gathered themselves together, defended their lives, had rest from their enemies, and killed seventy-five thousand of those who hated them; but they didn’t lay their hand on the plunder.

paite: Adar kha ani sawm-le-thum ni in hiai tuh hih ahi; huai mah ani sawm-le-li ni in akhawl ua, ankuanglui ni leh kipahna ni in azang uhi.
english: This was done on the thirteenth day of the month Adar; and on the fourteenth day of that month they rested and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

paite: Himahleh Susa a om Judate akikhawm ua, ani sawm-le-thum ni in leh ani sawm-le-li ni in; huai mah ani sawm-le-nga ni in akhawlta ua, ankuanglui ni leh kipahna ni in azang uhi.
english: But the Jews who were in Susa assembled together on the thirteenth and on the fourteenth days of the month; and on the fifteenth day of that month, they rested, and made it a day of feasting and gladness.

paite: Huaiziak in khoneute a Judate, kho kulhbaang nei lou a tengte'n, Adar kha ani sawm-le-li ni kipahna ni leh ankuanglui ni in, ni hoih, khat-le-khat tantuan kikhaktuahna ni in azang uhi.
english: Therefore the Jews of the villages, who live in the unwalled towns, make the fourteenth day of the month Adar a day of gladness and feasting, a holiday, and a day of sending presents of food to one another.

paite: Huan Mordekai in hiai thilte agelh a, kumpipa Ahasueras bial tengteng a om Judate, gamla leh nai a omte kiang ah akhak hi.
english: Mordecai wrote these things, and sent letters to all the Jews who were in all the provinces of the King Ahasuerus, both near and far,

paite: Kum teng a, Adar kha ani sawm-le-li leh ani sawm- le-nga ni, kum teng a tan ding ahilhna ding in,
english: to enjoin them that they should keep the fourteenth and fifteenth days of the month Adar yearly,

paite: Judate amelmate ua kipan akhawl ni uh, amau a dia lungkhamna kipahna ahong hihna kha, misi suunna ni hoih ahong hihna kha bang in: huai nite ankuangluina leh kipahna ni a a-om ua, tantuante khat-le-khat akikhaktuah uhi; gentheite kiang a thilpiakte piakna aneihtheihna ding un.
english: as the days in which the Jews had rest from their enemies, and the month which was turned to them from sorrow to gladness, and from mourning into a holiday; that they should make them days of feasting and gladness, and of sending presents of food to one another, and gifts to the needy.

paite: Huchi in Judate'n apatkhitsa bang un leh Mordekai in amaute kiang a agelh khitsa bang in hih ding in atheisiam uhi.
english: The Jews accepted the custom that they had begun, as Mordecai had written to them,

paite: Agag mi Hammedatha tapa Haman, Juda tengteng melmapa'n Juda tengteng siatna ding amau hihse ding, angaihtuah a, amaute hihgawp ding leh amaute hihse ding a, Pur, (huai tuh aisan ahi) ana paih ziak in.
english: because Haman the son of Hammedatha, the Agagite, the enemy of all the Jews, had plotted against the Jews to destroy them, and had cast “Pur”, that is the lot, to consume them and to destroy them;

paite: Himahleh athu kumpipa ma ahong tun in, angaihtuah gilou, Judate siatna ding a angaihtuah, ama lutung mahmah a kibung ding in laikhakte in thu apeta a; huchi a amah leh atapate khailupna khuam a khai a a-omna ding un.
english: but when this became known to the king, he commanded by letters that his wicked plan, which he had planned against the Jews, should return on his own head, and that he and his sons should be hanged on the gallows.

paite: Huchibang ahih ziak in hiai nite Pur min zui in Purim asa uhi. Huaiziak in hiai laikhak thute tengteng ziak leh hiai thu tungtang thu amuhsa uh, atung ua ahong tun ziak in.
english: Therefore they called these days “Purim”, from the word “Pur.” Therefore because of all the words of this letter, and of that which they had seen concerning this matter, and that which had come to them,

paite: Judate'n ahihkip ua, amau tung leh asuante uh tung leh amaute huchibang akizomkhawm bangte tengteng tung ah akisuanta uhi, huchi a pel lou a, huai a laigelh dungzui leh huai a hun sehsa dungzui a, kum chiteng a hiai ni nihte atantheihna ding un.
english: the Jews established and imposed on themselves, on their descendants, and on all those who joined themselves to them, so that it should not fail that they would keep these two days according to what was written and according to its appointed time every year;

paite: Huchi a hiai nite akhang-akhang a, a-inkuankuan a, bial chiteng leh khopi chiteng atheihgigeleh tan a a-omtheihna ding in; huchi a hiai Purim nite Judate lak a kipan a azuau louh a, huaite theihgigena leng asuante uh a kipan amanlouhna ding in.
english: and that these days should be remembered and kept throughout every generation, every family, every province, and every city; and that these days of Purim should not fail from among the Jews, nor their memory perish from their offspring.

paite: Huchi in kumpinu Esther, Abihail tanu leh Juda mi Mordekai in, hiai Purim laikhak nihna sukkipna ding in thuneihna tengteng in agelhta uhi.
english: Then Esther the queen, the daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote with all authority to confirm this second letter of Purim.

paite: Judate tengteng kiang ah, Ahasueras gam a bial zakhat sawmnih-le-sagihte kiang ah, lungmuanna leh thutak thute, laikhakte akhakta hi.
english: He sent letters to all the Jews in the hundred twenty-seven provinces of the kingdom of Ahasuerus with words of peace and truth,

paite: Hiai Purim nite a hun asehsa uh, Juda mi Mordekai leh kumpinu Esther in huaite pha asak uh dungzui leh amau a ding leh asuante uh a dia, an ngawlna leh akahna thu ua ana hihkip bang ua hihkip ding in.
english: to confirm these days of Purim in their appointed times, as Mordecai the Jew and Esther the queen had decreed, and as they had imposed upon themselves and their descendants in the matter of the fastings and their mourning.

paite: Esther thupiak in hiai Purim thute ahihkip a; laibu ah kigelh ahita hi.
english: The commandment of Esther confirmed these matters of Purim; and it was written in the book.

paite: Aigupta gam a hong lut Israel suante, michih leh a-inkote Jakob toh hong tonte min hiaite ahi:
english: Now these are the names of the sons of Israel, who came into Egypt (every man and his household came with Jacob):

paite: Reuben, Simeon, Levi leh Judah,
english: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Judah,

paite: Issakar, Zebulun leh Benjamin,
english: Issachar, Zebulun, and Benjamin,

paite: Dan leh Naphtali, Gad leh Asher,
english: Dan and Naphtali, Gad and Asher.

paite: Jakob khal a pan hong pawtkhia mi tengteng sawmsagih ahi uhi. Joseph bel Aigupta gam ah ana om khinta hi.
english: All the souls who came out of Jacob’s body were seventy souls, and Joseph was in Egypt already.

paite: Joseph leh a-unau tengteng leh asuan tengteng leng asita uhi.
english: Joseph died, as did all his brothers, and all that generation.

paite: Israel suante'n gah asuang ua, tampi in akhang ua, ahong kibehlap zel ua, hat petmah in ahong hatkhia ua; agam hong dimta uhi.
english: The children of Israel were fruitful, and increased abundantly, and multiplied, and grew exceedingly mighty; and the land was filled with them.

paite: Joseph thei lou, Aigupta gam ah kumpi thak ahong omta hi.
english: Now there arose a new king over Egypt, who didn’t know Joseph.

paite: Ama'n amite kiang ah, "En un, Israel suante ei sang in atamzaw ua, ahatzaw uhi.
english: He said to his people, “Behold, the people of the children of Israel are more and mightier than we.

paite: Kisa un, piltak in amaute i bawl ding uh. Huchi lou in zaw ahong kibehlap semsem ding ua, huan, hichi ahong hi ding a, kidouna ahong om chiang in, i melmate lam ah apang ding ua, ei ahon dou kha ding uh, huchi in gam apawtsan kha ding uh," achi hi.
english: Come, let’s deal wisely with them, lest they multiply, and it happen that when any war breaks out, they also join themselves to our enemies and fight against us, and escape out of the land.”

paite: Huaiziak in puakgikte a amau hihgim ding in atung uah nasem heutu akoihta uhi. Huchi in Pharaoh a ding in khopite, Pithom leh Rameses alamta uhi.
english: Therefore they set taskmasters over them to afflict them with their burdens. They built storage cities for Pharaoh: Pithom and Raamses.

paite: Himahleh amau ahihgim semsem uleh, akibehlap semsem ua, akhang semsem uhi. Huchi in Aiguptate'n Israel suante alau mahmah uhi.
english: But the more they afflicted them, the more they multiplied and the more they spread out. They started to dread the children of Israel.

paite: Huaiziak in Aiguptate'n Israel suante gimtak in nna asemsak uhi.
english: The Egyptians ruthlessly made the children of Israel serve,

paite: Nasep haksa in ahinna uh nuamloutak in abawlsak ua, buanman leh teklei bawl in gamlak a nna chiteng sem in, nakpitak in nna asemsak uhi.
english: and they made their lives bitter with hard service in mortar and in brick, and in all kinds of service in the field, all their service, in which they ruthlessly made them serve.

paite: Aigupta kumpipa'n Hebru naudom mite kiang ah thu agen a, huaite lak a khat min Siprah ahi a, adang khat min Puah ahi.
english: The king of Egypt spoke to the Hebrew midwives, of whom the name of the one was Shiphrah, and the name of the other Puah,

paite: "Hebru numeite lak a nau na dop chiang un, tutphah tung ah en unla, tapa ahihleh na that ding ua, tanu ahihleh bel na hawi ding uh,” achi hi.
english: and he said, “When you perform the duty of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them on the birth stool, if it is a son, then you shall kill him; but if it is a daughter, then she shall live.”

paite: Himahleh naudom mite'n Pathian alau ua, Aigupta kumpipa'n thu apiak bang a hih lou in, pasal naupangte ahinghawi uhi.
english: But the midwives feared God, and didn’t do what the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the baby boys alive.

paite: Aigupta kumpipa'n naudom mite asamsak a, akiang uah, "Bangziak a hiai thilhih a pasal naupangte hinghawi na hi ua?" achi hi.
english: The king of Egypt called for the midwives, and said to them, “Why have you done this thing and saved the boys alive?”

paite: Naudom mite'n Pharaoh kiang ah, "Hebru numeite zaw Aigupta numeite bang ahih louh ziak un, atei ngal ua, naudom mite akiang uh atun ma un ana nei khin man zel uh," achi uhi.
english: The midwives said to Pharaoh, “Because the Hebrew women aren’t like the Egyptian women; for they are vigorous and give birth before the midwife comes to them.”

paite: Huaiziak in Pathian in naudom mite a-angvan a, huchi in mite ahong kibehlap ua, ahat mahmah uhi.
english: God dealt well with the midwives, and the people multiplied, and grew very mighty.

paite: Huchi in naudom mite'n Pathian alauh ziak un inkuante abawlsakta hi.
english: Because the midwives feared God, he gave them families.

paite: Pharaoh in asikha tengteng thu pia in, "Tapa hong piang peuhmah lui ah na pai ding ua, tanu hong piang peuhmah na hinghawi ding uh," achi hi.
english: Pharaoh commanded all his people, saying, “You shall cast every son who is born into the river, and every daughter you shall save alive.”

paite: Huan TOUPA'N Mosi kiang ah, “Pharoah kiang ah va lut in. Ama a hiai ka chiamtehnate ka etsak theihna ding in alungtang, asikhate lungtang toh ka khauhsak ahi.
english: Yahweh said to Moses, “Go in to Pharaoh, for I have hardened his heart and the heart of his servants, that I may show these my signs among them;

paite: Na tapa bil leh na tapa' tapa bil a, Aigupta gam a bang thil ahia ka hih, alak ua chiamtehna ka hihte na gen theih a, TOUPA ka hi chih na theihna ding un,” achi hi.
english: and that you may tell in the hearing of your son, and of your son’s son, what things I have done to Egypt, and my signs which I have done among them; that you may know that I am Yahweh.”

paite: Pharaoh kiang ah Mosi leh Aaron alut ua, akiang ah, "Hebrute TOUPA Pathian in hichi in achi, 'Bang tan vei ka ma a kiniamkhiak nial lai ding na hia? Ka nna aseptheihna ding un, ka mite paisak in.'
english: Moses and Aaron went in to Pharaoh, and said to him, “This is what Yahweh, the God of the Hebrews, says: ‘How long will you refuse to humble yourself before me? Let my people go, that they may serve me.

paite: Huchi ahih kei a, ka mite paisak na nialleh ngai in, na tuipiau ah zingchiang in khaukhup ka hon sawl ding hi.
english: Or else, if you refuse to let my people go, behold, tomorrow I will bring locusts into your country,

paite: Lei mai atuam ding ua, mite'n lei amu thei kei ding. Asuakta bang ane ding ua, gial in ahon hawisak teng, lou a pan nang a dia singpou chiteng ane ding uh.
english: and they shall cover the surface of the earth, so that one won’t be able to see the earth. They shall eat the residue of that which has escaped, which remains to you from the hail, and shall eat every tree which grows for you out of the field.

paite: Na innte uah adim ding ua, na sikhate innte leh Aiguptate innte leh leitung om a pan tuni tan a na pate, na pate uh pate un amuh ngei louh uh," achi uhi. Huchi in akihei a, Pharaoh a pan apawtkheta hi.
english: Your houses shall be filled, and the houses of all your servants, and the houses of all the Egyptians, as neither your fathers nor your fathers’ fathers have seen, since the day that they were on the earth to this day.’” He turned, and went out from Pharaoh.

paite: Pharaoh sikhate'n akiang ah, "Bang tan hiai mipa ei a dia thang hi ding ahia? Mite paisak mai in, TOUPA a Pathian uh nna aseptheihna ding un. Aigupta hihsiat a omta ahi, chih thei nai lou na hi hia?" achi uhi.
english: Pharaoh’s servants said to him, “How long will this man be a snare to us? Let the men go, that they may serve Yahweh, their God. Don’t you yet know that Egypt is destroyed?”

paite: Pharaoh kiang ah Mosi leh Aaron ahon pi nawn ua; ama'n akiang uah, “Pai un, TOUPA na Pathian uh nna va sem un. Himahleh apai dingte kuate ahi ua?" achi hi.
english: Moses and Aaron were brought again to Pharaoh, and he said to them, “Go, serve Yahweh your God; but who are those who will go?”

paite: Mosi in, "Ka naupangte uh toh, ka tekte uh toh, ka tapate uleh ka tanute uh, ka ganhonte uleh ka belamhonte uh toh ka pai ding uhi, TOUPA kiang a ankuangluina nei ding ka hih ziak un," achi hi.
english: Moses said, “We will go with our young and with our old. We will go with our sons and with our daughters, with our flocks and with our herds; for we must hold a feast to Yahweh.”

paite: Himahleh ama'n akiang uah, "TOUPA na kiang uah om hen, na numeite uh leh na nau neute uh ka hon paisakleh, en mah un, na ma uah gilou a-om hi.
english: He said to them, “Yahweh be with you if I let you go with your little ones! See, evil is clearly before your faces.

paite: Huchi hilou e, nou pasal piching teng kuan unla, TOUPA nna va sem un. Huai lah na ut ngal ua,” achi hi. Huchi in Pharaoh a pan delhkhiak in a-om uhi.
english: Not so! Go now you who are men, and serve Yahweh; for that is what you desire!” Then they were driven out from Pharaoh’s presence.

paite: TOUPA'N Mosi kiang ah, "Aigupta gam tung ah khaukhupte ahong omna ding in na khut zankhia in. Aigupta gam a ahong paitouh ua, gam a haichi teng, gial in ahawi teng tanpha anektheihna ding un,” achi hi.
english: Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the land of Egypt for the locusts, that they may come up on the land of Egypt, and eat every herb of the land, even all that the hail has left.”

paite: Mosi in Aigupta gam tung ah achiangkhun alik a, TOUPA'Nhuai ni nitum in leh huai zankhua in suahlam huih anungsak a; zingsang ahong hih in suahlam huih in khaukhup ahon tunta hi.
english: Moses stretched out his rod over the land of Egypt, and Yahweh brought an east wind on the land all that day, and all night; and when it was morning, the east wind brought the locusts.

paite: Huchi in Aigupta gam tengteng tung ah khaukhupte a-om ua, Aigupta gam tengteng ah akhawl ua: achimtakhuai mahmah uhi. Amalam uah huchibang khaukhup a-om ngei kei a, anunglam uah leng huchibang a-om kei ding hi.
english: The locusts went up over all the land of Egypt, and rested in all the borders of Egypt. They were very grievous. Before them there were no such locusts as they, nor will there ever be again.

paite: Lei mai tengteng atuam ziak un, gamsung amialta hi. Gam a haichi gial in ahawite, singgahte toh ane uhi. Huchi in singte ah hiam, lou a haichite ah hiam leng thil hing a-omta kei, Aigupta gamsung teng ah.
english: For they covered the surface of the whole earth, so that the land was darkened, and they ate every herb of the land, and all the fruit of the trees which the hail had left. There remained nothing green, either tree or herb of the field, through all the land of Egypt.

paite: Huaitak in Pharaoh in kintak in Mosi leh Aaron asamsak a, "TOUPA na Pathian leh noute tung ah ka na khialta hi.
english: Then Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron in haste, and he said, “I have sinned against Yahweh your God, and against you.

paite: Huaiziak in tu in ka hon ngen ahi. Tutung kia hiai ka khelhna ngaidam inla, kei a pan hiai sihna alakmang theihna ding in, TOUPA na Pathian kiang ah ngen in," achi hi.
english: Now therefore please forgive my sin again, and pray to Yahweh your God, that he may also take away from me this death.”

paite: Huchi in Pharaoh a pan apaikheta a, TOUPA kiang ah angenta hi.
english: Moses went out from Pharaoh, and prayed to Yahweh.

paite: TOUPA'n suahlam huih hat mahmah akhahta a, huai in khaukhupte alamang a, Tuipi San ah ahawllutta hi. Huchi in Aigupta gam tengteng ah khaukhup khat leng a-omta kei hi.
english: Yahweh sent an exceedingly strong west wind, which took up the locusts, and drove them into the Red Sea. There remained not one locust in all the borders of Egypt.

paite: Himahleh TOUPA'N Pharaoh lungtang akhauhsak a, Israel suante apaisak nuam tuan kei hi.
english: But Yahweh hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he didn’t let the children of Israel go.

paite: Huan TOUPA'N Mosi kiang ah, "Aigupta gam tung a khomial, theihtheih ding khop mial sah a- omtheihna ding in, van lam ah na khut liktou in," achi hi.
english: Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand toward the sky, that there may be darkness over the land of Egypt, even darkness which may be felt.”

paite: Mosi in van lam ah akhut aliktou a; huchi in ni thum ah khomial sung Aigupta gam m tengteng bikbek a-omta hi.
english: Moses stretched out his hand toward the sky, and there was a thick darkness in all the land of Egypt for three days.

paite: Kuamah akimutuah kei ua, a-omna ua pan kuamah ni thum sung athoukhe kei uh; himahleh Israel suante tenna ah khua avak hi.
english: They didn’t see one another, and nobody rose from his place for three days; but all the children of Israel had light in their dwellings.

paite: Pharaoh in Mosi asam a, "Pai un, TOUPA nna sem un. Na bawnghonte leh na ganhonte uh kia om uhen. Na nau neute un leng hon zui uhen," achi hi.
english: Pharaoh called to Moses, and said, “Go, serve Yahweh. Only let your flocks and your herds stay behind. Let your little ones also go with you.”

paite: Himahleh Mosi in, “TOUPA ka Pathian uh kiang a ka kithoihtheihna ding un, kithoihnate leh halmang thillatte leng na hon piak ngeingei ding ahi.
english: Moses said, “You must also give into our hand sacrifices and burnt offerings, that we may sacrifice to Yahweh our God.

paite: Ka bawnghonte un leng ahon zuih ding uh ahi. Nunglam ah khechin khat lel leng nutsiat ahi kei ding; huaite a pan TOUPA ka Pathian uh nna sepna dia ka lak ding uh ahih ziak in. Huai mun ka tun masiah uh, bang in ahia TOUPA nna ka sep ding uh, ka thei kei uh," achi hi.
english: Our livestock also shall go with us. Not a hoof shall be left behind, for of it we must take to serve Yahweh our God; and we don’t know with what we must serve Yahweh, until we come there.”

paite: Himahleh TOUPA'N Pharaoh lungtang akhauhsak a, amau apaisak nuam kei.
english: But Yahweh hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he wouldn’t let them go.

paite: Huchi in Pharaoh in akiang ah, "Ka kiang a pan paimang in. Ka mel mu nawn lou ding in pilvang in, ka mel na muh nini a si ding lah na hih ngal a," achi hi.
english: Pharaoh said to him, “Get away from me! Be careful to see my face no more; for in the day you see my face you shall die!”

paite: Mosi in, "Na gen bang in, na mel ka mu nawn kei ding,” achi hi.
english: Moses said, “You have spoken well. I will see your face again no more.”

paite: Huan TOUPA’N Mosi kiang ah, “Pharoah tung leh Aigupta gam tung ah gawtna khat ka tun lai ding. Huai khit chiang in hiai a pan ahon paisakta ding hi. Ahon paisak chiang in, hon hawlkhe siang sipsip ding hi.
english: Yahweh said to Moses, “I will bring yet one more plague on Pharaoh, and on Egypt; afterwards he will let you go. When he lets you go, he will surely thrust you out altogether.

paite: Tu in mite zak in thu gen inla, pasal chih in a-inveng kiang ah ngen hen. Numei chih in a-inveng kiang ah dangka suangmantamte leh dangka-eng suangmantamte ngen hen," achi hi.
english: Speak now in the ears of the people, and let every man ask of his neighbor, and every woman of her neighbor, jewels of silver, and jewels of gold.”

paite: TOUPA'N Aiguptate mitmuh in mite deihsakna apia hi. Huai lou in Aigupta gam ah, Pharaoh sikhate mitmuh leh mite mitmuh in Mosi athupi mahmah hi.
english: Yahweh gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians. Moreover, the man Moses was very great in the land of Egypt, in the sight of Pharaoh’s servants, and in the sight of the people.

paite: Mosi in, "Hiai bang in TOUPA'N achi, zankim chiang in Aigupta gamsung teng ka tawnsuak ding hi.
english: Moses said, “This is what Yahweh says: ‘About midnight I will go out into the middle of Egypt,

paite: Aigupta gam a piang masa tengteng, alaltutphah a tu Pharaoh tapa upapen a pan buhhek a om sikhanu ta masapen leh ganta piang masa tengteng asi ding uhi.
english: and all the firstborn in the land of Egypt shall die, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sits on his throne, even to the firstborn of the female servant who is behind the mill, and all the firstborn of livestock.

paite: Aigupta gam pumpi ah kahna thupitak a-om ding a, huchibang om ngei nai lou, huchibang om ngei nawn lou ding.
english: There will be a great cry throughout all the land of Egypt, such as there has not been, nor will be any more.

paite: Himahleh Israel suante lak a kuamah siatna ding in, mi hiam ganta hiam siatna ding in ui in alei atangsak kei ding a; TOUPA'N Aiguptate leh Israel akhentuamdan na thei ding hi.
english: But against any of the children of Israel a dog won’t even bark or move its tongue, against man or animal, that you may know that Yahweh makes a distinction between the Egyptians and Israel.

paite: Huai hun chiang in ka kiang ah na milian tengteng ahong paisuk ding ua, ahong kun ding ua, 'Nang hon zui mi tengteng toh paikhia un' ahong chi ding uh. Huai khit chiang in ka paikhe ding," chi in hehtak in Pharaoh a pan Mosi apaikhia hi.
english: All these servants of yours will come down to me, and bow down themselves to me, saying, “Get out, with all the people who follow you;” and after that I will go out.’” He went out from Pharaoh in hot anger.

paite: Huan TOUPA'N Mosi kiang ah, "Ka thillamdangte Aigupta gam a apunna ding in Pharaoh in ahon ngaikhe kei ding," achi hi.
english: Yahweh said to Moses, “Pharaoh won’t listen to you, that my wonders may be multiplied in the land of Egypt.”

paite: Mosi leh Aaron in Pharaoh ma ah hiai thillamdang tengteng ahihta ua; TOUPA'N Pharaoh lungtang akhauhsak a, gam a kipan Israel suante apaisak nuam tuan kei hi.
english: Moses and Aaron did all these wonders before Pharaoh, but Yahweh hardened Pharaoh’s heart, and he didn’t let the children of Israel go out of his land.

paite: TOUPA'N Aigupta gam ah Mosi leh Aaron kiang ah thu agen hi.
english: Yahweh spoke to Moses and Aaron in the land of Egypt, saying,

paite: Hiai kha noute a dia khate kipatna ahi ding. Noute a ding in kum khat a akha masapen ahi ding hi.
english: “This month shall be to you the beginning of months. It shall be the first month of the year to you.

paite: Israel omkhawmte kiang ah thu gen in, hiai kha ani sawm ni in apipute inkuan dungzui zel in, michih in amah a ding in belamnou akilak chiat dia, inn khat zel a ding in belamnou khat zel.
english: Speak to all the congregation of Israel, saying, ‘On the tenth day of this month, they shall take to them every man a lamb, according to their fathers’ houses, a lamb for a household;

paite: Belamnou khat a dia inkuan atawm luatleh, ami phazah dungzui in amah leh a-inn zom a-invengte a toh lakhawm hen. Michih in akham ding bang zel in belamnou na sim ding uhi.
english: and if the household is too little for a lamb, then he and his neighbor next to his house shall take one according to the number of the souls. You shall make your count for the lamb according to what everyone can eat.

paite: Na belamnou uh gensiatbei, apa kum khat a upa ahi dia; belamhon lak hiam kelte lak a pan in hiam na lakhe ding uhi.
english: Your lamb shall be without defect, a male a year old. You shall take it from the sheep or from the goats.

paite: Huai kha mah ani sawm-le-li tan na kem ding ua; nitaklam in Israel khawmpi omkhawmte'n agou ding uhi.
english: You shall keep it until the fourteenth day of the same month; and the whole assembly of the congregation of Israel shall kill it at evening.

paite: Asisan na la ding ua, anekna ding uh inn kongkhak biang khuam nihte ah leh kongkhak tung ah na tat ding uhi.
english: They shall take some of the blood, and put it on the two door posts and on the lintel, on the houses in which they shall eat it.

paite: Huai zan in sa mei a haimin, tanghou silngou soh louh toh na ne ding uhi; lou kha toh na ne ding uhi.
english: They shall eat the meat in that night, roasted with fire, with unleavened bread. They shall eat it with bitter herbs.

paite: Sialnek kei unla, tuihuan het kei un, alutang, akhete leh asungkua toh mei ah na haimin zaw ding uhi.
english: Don’t eat it raw, nor boiled at all with water, but roasted with fire; with its head, its legs and its inner parts.

paite: Azingchiang tan in bangmah na valsak kei ding uhi. Azingchiang tan a omlaite mei in na haltum ding uhi.
english: You shall let nothing of it remain until the morning; but that which remains of it until the morning you shall burn with fire.

paite: Hichibang in na ne ding uhi. Na kawng uh gaksa in, na khedap uh na khe ua bulhsa in, na khut ua na chiangkhunte uh tawisa in na kin nek ding uhi. Hiai TOUPA Paikan Ankuang ahi.
english: This is how you shall eat it: with your belt on your waist, your sandals on your feet, and your staff in your hand; and you shall eat it in haste: it is Yahweh’s Passover.

paite: Tuzan chiang a Aigupta gamsung tawnsuak a, Aigupta gam a piang masa teng, mi leh ganta that ding ka hih ziak in, Aigupta pathiante tengteng siatna ding in ka vaihawm ding hi: Kei TOUPA ka hi.
english: For I will go through the land of Egypt in that night, and will strike all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both man and animal. I will execute judgments against all the gods of Egypt. I am Yahweh.

paite: Sisan tuh noute a ding in na omna innte uah chiamtehna ahi ding. Sisan ka muh chiang in, ka hon paikan ding, Aigupta gam ka gawt chiang in, nou hon hihse ding in na tung uah hiai gawtna a-om kei ding hi.
english: The blood shall be to you for a token on the houses where you are. When I see the blood, I will pass over you, and no plague will be on you to destroy you when I strike the land of Egypt.

paite: Hiai ni noute a ding in theihgige ahi ding. Na khang na khang un TOUPA kiang a ankuangluina in na nei ding ua; tangtawn in dan thuseh a ankuangluina in na nei ding uhi.
english: This day shall be a memorial for you. You shall keep it as a feast to Yahweh. You shall keep it as a feast throughout your generations by an ordinance forever.

paite: "Ni sagih sung tanghou silngou soh louh na ne ding ua; ani masapen ni ngei in na innte ua pan in silngou na koihmang ding uhi. Ani masapen ni a kipan ani sagih ni tan, tanghou silngou soh ne peuhmah, huai mi Israel a pan satkhiak ding ahi ngal a.
english: “‘Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread; even the first day you shall put away yeast out of your houses, for whoever eats leavened bread from the first day until the seventh day, that soul shall be cut off from Israel.

paite: Ani masapen ni in kikhopna siangthou a-om dia, ani sagih ni in noute a ding in kikhopna siangthou a-om ding. Huai nite in nek bawl chih louh ngal nna sep louh himhim ding ahi. Nekbawl kia na hihthei ding uh.
english: In the first day there shall be to you a holy convocation, and in the seventh day a holy convocation; no kind of work shall be done in them, except that which every man must eat, only that may be done by you.

paite: Tanghou Silngou Soh Louh Ankuangluina na tang ding ua; hiai ni mah a Aigupta gam a kipan na mite ka pikhiak ziak in. Huaiziak in tangtawn in na khang un dan thuseh in hiai ni na tang ding uh ahi.
english: You shall observe the feast of unleavened bread; for in this same day I have brought your armies out of the land of Egypt. Therefore you shall observe this day throughout your generations by an ordinance forever.

paite: Akha khatna ah, huai kha ani sawm-le-li ni, nitaklam a kipan huai kha nitaklam ani sawmnih-le-khat matan in, tanghou silngou soh louh na ne ding uhi.
english: In the first month, on the fourteenth day of the month at evening, you shall eat unleavened bread, until the twenty first day of the month at evening.

paite: Na insung uah ni sagih sung silngou muh in a-om ding ahi kei. Kuapeuh silngou soh ne, huai mi ngei mikhual hiam hi in, agamsung a piang hitaleh Israel omkhawmte a pan satkhiak ding ahi.
english: There shall be no yeast found in your houses for seven days, for whoever eats that which is leavened, that soul shall be cut off from the congregation of Israel, whether he is a foreigner, or one who is born in the land.

paite: Silngou soh bangmah na ne ding uh ahi kei. Na tenna peuhmah uah tanghou silngou soh louh na ne ding uhi," achi hi.
english: You shall eat nothing leavened. In all your habitations you shall eat unleavened bread.’”

paite: Mosi in Israel upate asamsak a, akiang uah, “Na inkuan dungzui zel un belamnou kaikhia in kilak unla, Paikan Belamnou gou un," achi hi.
english: Then Moses called for all the elders of Israel, and said to them, “Draw out, and take lambs according to your families, and kill the Passover.

paite: "Hissop gaklop na la ding ua, belkuang sung a om sisan ah na diah ding ua, belkuang sung a om sisan in kongkhak biang khuam tuak leh kongkhak tung na zep ding uhi. Zingsang masiah na lak ua kuamah a- inn kongkhak ah ava pawtkhe ding ahi kei;
english: You shall take a bunch of hyssop, and dip it in the blood that is in the basin, and strike the lintel and the two door posts with the blood that is in the basin. None of you shall go out of the door of his house until the morning.

paite: Aiguptate that dia TOUPA hong paisuak ding ahih ziak in. Kongkhak tung a leh kongbiang khuam nihte a sisan amuh chiang in TOUPA'N huai kongkhak apaikan dia, hon that ding in na insung uah hihsemi hong lut aphal kei ding hi.
english: For Yahweh will pass through to strike the Egyptians; and when he sees the blood on the lintel, and on the two door posts, Yahweh will pass over the door, and will not allow the destroyer to come in to your houses to strike you.

paite: Tangtawn in na tapate uh a ding leh noute a ding in dan thuseh in hiai thil na tang ding uh ahi.
english: You shall observe this thing for an ordinance to you and to your sons forever.

paite: Huan achiam bang a, nou ahon piak ding gam na tun chiang un, hichi ahi ding a, hiai biakna thilzek in na nei ding uh ahi.
english: It shall happen when you have come to the land which Yahweh will give you, as he has promised, that you shall keep this service.

paite: Hichi ahong hi ding a, na tate un na kiang ua, hiai biakna thilzek bang na chihna uh ahia? ahon chih chiang un,
english: It will happen, when your children ask you, ‘What do you mean by this service?’

paite: 'Aiguptate athah a, ei innte atatkhiak lai a, Aigupta gam a Israel suante innte paikanpa, TOUPA paikanna theihgigena ahi, " na chi ding uh. Huchi in mite'n alu uh akunsak ua abeta uhi.
english: that you shall say, ‘It is the sacrifice of Yahweh’s Passover, who passed over the houses of the children of Israel in Egypt, when he struck the Egyptians, and spared our houses.’” The people bowed their heads and worshiped.

paite: Israel suante apaimang ua, TOUPA'N Mosi leh Aaron thu apiak bang in ahih ua, huchibang in amau leng ahihta uhi.
english: The children of Israel went and did so; as Yahweh had commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, zankim lai in TOUPA'N Aigupta gam a piang masa tengteng, alaltutphah tung a tu Pharaoh ta masapen a pan suangkul sung a om sal ta masapen tan in, ganhon nou masapen teng toh athatta hi.
english: At midnight, Yahweh struck all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of Pharaoh who sat on his throne to the firstborn of the captive who was in the dungeon, and all the firstborn of livestock.

paite: Huchi in zan in Pharaoh athou a, amah leh asikhate leh Aigupta tengteng, Aigupta gamsung teng ah kahna thupitak a-omta a; inn khat mahmah mi khat sihlouhna a-om louh ziak in.
english: Pharaoh rose up in the night, he, and all his servants, and all the Egyptians; and there was a great cry in Egypt, for there was not a house where there was not one dead.

paite: Zan in Mosi leh Aaron asamsak a, "Thou unla, ka mite lak a pan paikhia un. Noute gel leh Israel suante pai un. Na gensa bang un, TOUPA nna va sem un.
english: He called for Moses and Aaron by night, and said, “Rise up, get out from among my people, both you and the children of Israel; and go, serve Yahweh, as you have said!

paite: Na bawnghonte uleh na ganhonte uh leng, na chih bang un, pi unla, paikhia un. Huchi in kei leng hon vualzawl un," achita hi.
english: Take both your flocks and your herds, as you have said, and be gone; and bless me also!”

paite: Kintak a gam a pan asawlkhiak theihna ding un Aiguptate'n mite anoh mahmah ua, "Si khin vek ding i hi uh," achih ziak un.
english: The Egyptians were urgent with the people, to send them out of the land in haste, for they said, “We are all dead men.”

paite: Mite'n atangbuang uh silngou soh ma in ala ua, aliangzang uah atangbuang haihnate uh puan a khihsawn in.
english: The people took their dough before it was leavened, their kneading troughs being bound up in their clothes on their shoulders.

paite: Mosi thu bang in Israel suante a-omta ua; Aiguptate dangka suangmantam leh dangka-eng suangmantam leh puansilh angen uhi.
english: The children of Israel did according to the word of Moses; and they asked of the Egyptians jewels of silver, and jewels of gold, and clothing.

paite: Aiguptate mitmuh in TOUPA'N mite deihsakna apia a, adeih bang un huai thilte akiang uah apia uhi. Huchi in Aiguptate alok uhi.
english: Yahweh gave the people favor in the sight of the Egyptians, so that they let them have what they asked. They plundered the Egyptians.

paite: Israel suante Rameses a pan Sukkoth atung ua, numei leh naupangte sim louh pasal ngen khe a pai nuaiguk ahi uhi.
english: The children of Israel traveled from Rameses to Succoth, about six hundred thousand on foot who were men, in addition to children.

paite: Mikihelte'n leng bawnghonte, ganhonte leh ganta tampi petmah toh amaute azuitou uhi.
english: A mixed multitude went up also with them, with flocks, herds, and even very much livestock.

paite: Aigupta gam a kipan apuakkhiak uh tangbuangte mek in silngou soh louh tanghou abawl ua, amaute Aigupta gam a kipan kintak a hawlkhiak a om, akizekaisak theih louh ziak un, atanghou uah silngou asoh man kei ua, lamkal a nek ding leng abuaipih man kei uhi.
english: They baked unleavened cakes of the dough which they brought out of Egypt; for it wasn’t leavened, because they were thrust out of Egypt, and couldn’t wait, and they had not prepared any food for themselves.

paite: Huchibang in Aigupta gam a teng, Israel suante taam sung kum zali-le-sawmthum ahi.
english: Now the time that the children of Israel lived in Egypt was four hundred thirty years.

paite: Kum zali-le-sawmthum bei in hichi ahong hi a, huai ni ngei in hichi ahong hi a, Aigupta gam a pan TOUPA mi tengteng apaikheta uhi.
english: At the end of four hundred thirty years, to the day, all of Yahweh’s armies went out from the land of Egypt.

paite: Aigupta gam a kipan amau apikhiak ziak in TOUPA a ding in huai zan zahtak petmah a tan ding ahi. Hiai TOUPA zan Israel suante'n akhang-akhang a, pilvangtak a atan ding uh ahi.
english: It is a night to be much observed to Yahweh for bringing them out from the land of Egypt. This is that night of Yahweh, to be much observed by all the children of Israel throughout their generations.

paite: TOUPA'N Mosi leh Aaron kiang ah, "Hiai Paikan Ankuang zat ding a dan thuseh ahi. Mikhual in hiai anek louh ding ahi.
english: Yahweh said to Moses and Aaron, “This is the ordinance of the Passover. No foreigner shall eat of it,

paite: Himahleh michih sikha sum a leisa, azek na sum nung in hiai ane thei ding hi.
english: but every man’s servant who is bought for money, when you have circumcised him, then shall he eat of it.

paite: Gamdangmi leh sikha goihmi in hiai ane ding ahi kei hi.
english: A foreigner and a hired servant shall not eat of it.

paite: Inn khat a nek ding ahi; inn polam ah sa, abangmah na lathang ding uh ahi kei. Aguh leng na hihtan ding uh ahi kei.
english: It must be eaten in one house. You shall not carry any of the meat outside of the house. Do not break any of its bones.

paite: Israel omkhawmte tengteng in hiai azuih ding uh ahi.
english: All the congregation of Israel shall keep it.

paite: Na kiang ua mikhual a-om a, TOUPA a dia Paikan Ankuang a-um dingleh, pasalte zek sum ding ahi, huai khit chiang in hong pai nai uhenla, um uhen. Amah gamsung a piang bang ahi ding; zeksum louh mi in anek louh ding ahih ziak in.
english: When a stranger lives as a foreigner with you, and would like to keep the Passover to Yahweh, let all his males be circumcised, and then let him come near and keep it. He shall be as one who is born in the land; but no uncircumcised person shall eat of it.

paite: Khotual mi a ding leh na lak ua mi khual taam a ding in dan khat a-om ding ahi," achi hi.
english: One law shall be to him who is born at home, and to the stranger who lives as a foreigner among you.”

paite: Huchibang in Israel suan tengteng in ahih uhi. TOUPA'N Mosi leh Aaron thu apiak bang in ahih uhi.
english: All the children of Israel did so. As Yahweh commanded Moses and Aaron, so they did.

paite: Huai ni mah in hichi ahong hi a, TOUPA'N Aigupta gam a pan Israel suante apawlpi in apikheta hi.
english: That same day, Yahweh brought the children of Israel out of the land of Egypt by their armies.

paite: Huan TOUPA'N Mosi kiang ah thu agen a,
english: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

paite: "Piang masapen tengteng, Israel suante lak a sul hong peuhmah, mihing hi in ganta hitaleh siangthou in sehtuamsak in, kei' a ahi," achi hi.
english: “Sanctify to me all the firstborn, whatever opens the womb among the children of Israel, both of man and of animal. It is mine.”

paite: Mosi in mite kiang ah, "Hiai ni theigige un, Aigupta gam a pan na hong pawtkhiak ni uh, saltanna inn a pan na hong pawtkhiak ni uh ahi; TOUPA'N khut thahat a hiai mun hon tun lah ahi ngal a. Tanghou silngou soh nek louh ding ahi.
english: Moses said to the people, “Remember this day, in which you came out of Egypt, out of the house of bondage; for by strength of hand Yahweh brought you out from this place. No leavened bread shall be eaten.

paite: Hiai ni, Abib kha in na hong paikhia uhi.
english: Today you go out in the month Abib.

paite: Hichi ahong hi ding a, TOUPA'N Kanaante, Hitte, Amorte, Hivte leh Jebuste gam nou hon piak dia, na pipute uh kiang a, akichiamna, bawngnawi leh khuaizu a luang gam ahon tut chiang in, hiai biakna thilzek hiai kha in na tang ding uhi.
english: It shall be, when Yahweh brings you into the land of the Canaanite, and the Hittite, and the Amorite, and the Hivite, and the Jebusite, which he swore to your fathers to give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, that you shall keep this service in this month.

paite: Ni sagih sung tanghou silngou soh louh na ne ding ua, ani sagih ni in TOUPA a ding in ankuangluina a-om ding ahi.
english: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and in the seventh day shall be a feast to Yahweh.

paite: Ni sagih sung tanghou silngou soh louh akine dia; na kiang uah tanghou silngou soh akimu ding ahi kei. Na omna tengteng uah leng silngou muh in a-om ding ahi kei hi.
english: Unleavened bread shall be eaten throughout the seven days; and no leavened bread shall be seen with you. No yeast shall be seen with you, within all your borders.

paite: Huai ni in na tapa na hilh ding a, 'Aigupta gam a pan ka hong paikhiak lai a TOUPA'N kei a dia athilhih ziak a hiai kihih ahi' na chi ding hi.
english: You shall tell your son in that day, saying, ‘It is because of that which Yahweh did for me when I came out of Egypt.’

paite: Na ban ah nang a ding in chiamtehna ahi dia, na mitte kikal ah theihgigena, huchi a na kam a TOUPA dan a-omtheihna ding in TOUPA'N ban thahat a Aigupta gam a pan noute ahon pikhiak ziak in.
english: It shall be for a sign to you on your hand, and for a memorial between your eyes, that Yahweh’s law may be in your mouth; for with a strong hand Yahweh has brought you out of Egypt.

paite: Huaiziak in kum teng in ahunbi in hiai dan thuseh na zui ding uh ahi."
english: You shall therefore keep this ordinance in its season from year to year.

paite: "Huan hichi ahi ding a, TOUPA'N, nang kiang leh na pipute kiang a, akichiam bang a, Kanaante gam ahon tut chiang in, hiai ahon piak chiang in,
english: “It shall be, when Yahweh brings you into the land of the Canaanite, as he swore to you and to your fathers, and will give it to you,

paite: TOUPA a ding in sul hong tengteng na koihtuam ding a, na neih ganta a pan hong om, anou masapen teng; apate TOUPA a ahi ding uhi.
english: that you shall set apart to Yahweh all that opens the womb, and every firstborn that comes from an animal which you have. The males shall be Yahweh’s.

paite: Sabiltungnou masapen teng belamnou in na tankhe dia; huchi a na tatkhiak keileh, angawng na hektan ding. Na tapate lak a mihing tapa masa tengteng na tankhe ding ahi.
english: Every firstborn of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb; and if you will not redeem it, then you shall break its neck; and you shall redeem all the firstborn of man among your sons.

paite: Hun hong tung ding ah hichi ahi ding a, na tapa in, 'hiai bang ahia? chi a hon dot chiang in, nang akiang ah, ban thahat in TOUPA'N Aigupta gam a pan, koltanna inn a pan ahon lakheta' akiang ah na chi ding uhi.
english: It shall be, when your son asks you in time to come, saying, ‘What is this?’ that you shall tell him, ‘By strength of hand Yahweh brought us out from Egypt, from the house of bondage.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, Pharaoh in genhaktak a hon paisak nop louh lai in, TOUPA'N Aigupta gam a piang masa tengteng, mihing apiang masate leh ganta apiang masate athat hi. Huaiziak in pasal, sul hong tengteng, TOUPA kiang a ka lat ahi ua; himahleh ka tapate lak a piang masa tengteng ka tankhia hi.
english: When Pharaoh stubbornly refused to let us go, Yahweh killed all the firstborn in the land of Egypt, both the firstborn of man, and the firstborn of livestock. Therefore I sacrifice to Yahweh all that opens the womb, being males; but all the firstborn of my sons I redeem.’

paite: Huchi in na khut ah chiamtehna ding ahi dia, na mitte kikal a khaukhip ahi ding; TOUPA'N Aigupta gam a pan ban thahat a ahon pikhiak ziak in," na chi ding hi.
english: It shall be for a sign on your hand, and for symbols between your eyes; for by strength of hand Yahweh brought us out of Egypt.”

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, Pharaoh in huai mite apaisak lai in, naizaw mahleh Pathian in Philistiate gam tawn in api kei hi. Pathian in, "Kidouna amuh chiang un mite akisik kha ding ua, Aigupta gam ah akiheikik kha ding uh," achih ziak in.
english: When Pharaoh had let the people go, God didn’t lead them by the way of the land of the Philistines, although that was near; for God said, “Lest perhaps the people change their minds when they see war, and they return to Egypt”;

paite: Huchi in Pathian in mite apikual a, Tuipi San gamdai lampi tawn in api hi. Huchibang in Aigupta gam a pan Israel suante apawlpawl a kizom in apaitou uhi.
english: but God led the people around by the way of the wilderness by the Red Sea; and the children of Israel went up armed out of the land of Egypt.

paite: Mosi in Joseph guhte apua hi. "Pathian in pel lou in ahong veh dia; hiai a pan ka guhte na puak ding uh ahi," chi a Israel suante chihtaktak a, akichiam ziak in.
english: Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for he had made the children of Israel swear, saying, “God will surely visit you, and you shall carry up my bones away from here with you.”

paite: Sukkoth a pan azinkheta ua, gamdai zul ah, Etham mun ah agiak uhi.
english: They took their journey from Succoth, and encamped in Etham, in the edge of the wilderness.

paite: TOUPA ama uah sun in meipi khuampi dingh in, amaute lampi a pi ding in apai a; zan in meikuang khuampi dingh in, amaute vakna pe ding in; sun leh zan in apai hi; huchi a sun leh zan a apaitheihna ding un.
english: Yahweh went before them by day in a pillar of cloud, to lead them on their way, and by night in a pillar of fire, to give them light, that they might go by day and by night:

paite: Mite ma a pan sun a meipi khuampi dingh hiam ahihkeileh zan a meikuang khuampi dingh alamang ngei kei hi.
english: the pillar of cloud by day, and the pillar of fire by night, didn’t depart from before the people.

paite: Huan TOUPA'N Mosi kiang ah thu agen hi.
english: Yahweh spoke to Moses, saying,

paite: "Israel suante kiang ah thu gen in, kihei uhenla, Pi-hahiroth ma ah, Migdol leh tuipi kikal ah, Baal-zephon zawntak ah giak uhen. Ama ah tuipi kiang ah na giak ding uh ahi.
english: “Speak to the children of Israel, that they turn back and encamp before Pihahiroth, between Migdol and the sea, before Baal Zephon. You shall encamp opposite it by the sea.

paite: Israel suante tungtang thu, gamdai in adaltan ziak in gamsung ah tang in abuaigawp uh, Pharaoh in chi ding ahi.
english: Pharaoh will say of the children of Israel, ‘They are entangled in the land. The wilderness has shut them in.’

paite: Amaute nungdelh ding in Pharaoh lungtang ka khauhsak ding. Pharaoh tung leh asepaihte tung ah zahtak in ka om ding hi. Huchi a Aiguptate'n TOUPA ka hi, chih atheihna ding un," achi hi. Huchibang in Israel suante'n ahihta uhi.
english: I will harden Pharaoh’s heart, and he will follow after them; and I will get honor over Pharaoh, and over all his armies; and the Egyptians shall know that I am Yahweh.” They did so.

paite: Mite apaikheta uh, chih Aigupta kumpipa ahilh uhi. Pharaoh lungtang leh asikhate lungtang mite siatna ding in hei in a-om hi. "Eite nna asepna ua pan Israel i paisak uh, bangziak a hiai hih i hi ua!" achi uhi.
english: The king of Egypt was told that the people had fled; and the heart of Pharaoh and of his servants was changed toward the people, and they said, “What is this we have done, that we have let Israel go from serving us?”

paite: Akangtalai amansak a, amite atonpihta hi.
english: He prepared his chariot, and took his army with him;

paite: Kangtalai hoihpen zaguk, Aigupta gam a kangtalai tengteng leh aheutute chiat uh toh atonpih hi.
english: and he took six hundred chosen chariots, and all the chariots of Egypt, with captains over all of them.

paite: TOUPA'N Aigupta kumpipa Pharaoh lungtang akhauhsak a; Israel suante anungdelhta hi. Israel suante hangsantak in apaikheta uhi.
english: Yahweh hardened the heart of Pharaoh king of Egypt, and he pursued the children of Israel; for the children of Israel went out with a high hand.

paite: Himahleh Aiguptate'n Pharaoh sakol tengteng leh kangtalai tengteng, sakol tungtuang mite leh sepaih pawlte toh anungdelh ua, Baal-zephon ma a Pi-hahiroth pam a tuipi kiang a agiahna uah aphata uhi.
english: The Egyptians pursued them. All the horses and chariots of Pharaoh, his horsemen, and his army overtook them encamping by the sea, beside Pihahiroth, before Baal Zephon.

paite: Pharaoh in ahon naih lai in, Israel suante adaktou ua, ngai in, Aiguptate'n amau ahon delhta uhi. Alau mahmah ua, Israel suante TOUPA kiang ah akapkhia uhi.
english: When Pharaoh came near, the children of Israel lifted up their eyes, and behold, the Egyptians were marching after them; and they were very afraid. The children of Israel cried out to Yahweh.

paite: Mosi kiang ah, "Aigupta gam a han a-om louh ziak a gamdai a si dia hon pikhia na hi maw! Bang achia hichibang a hon bawl dia Aigupta gam a kipan hon pikhia na hia?
english: They said to Moses, “Because there were no graves in Egypt, have you taken us away to die in the wilderness? Why have you treated us this way, to bring us out of Egypt?

paite: Aigupta gam a ka hon hilh uh hiai thu ahi kei maw? Om maimai ni, Aiguptate nna i septheihna ding in," chi in. "Gamdai a ka sih sang ua, koute a dia Aiguptate nasep ahoih zawk ding ziak in," achi uhi.
english: Isn’t this the word that we spoke to you in Egypt, saying, ‘Leave us alone, that we may serve the Egyptians’? For it would have been better for us to serve the Egyptians than to die in the wilderness.”

paite: Mosi in mite kiang ah, "Lau kei unla, dingh dinden un, TOUPA hotdamna tuni a nou ahon etsak ding en un; tuni a na muh uh Aiguptate tangtawn a mu nawn lou ding na hih ziak un.
english: Moses said to the people, “Don’t be afraid. Stand still, and see the salvation of Yahweh, which he will work for you today; for you will never again see the Egyptians whom you have seen today.

paite: TOUPA'N nou a ding in ahon dousak dia, na pau kei ding uh," achi hi.
english: Yahweh will fight for you, and you shall be still.”

paite: TOUPA'N Mosi kiang ah, "Bang achia ka kiang a kap na hia? Malam a apaina ding un, Israel suante kiang ah thu gen in.
english: Yahweh said to Moses, “Why do you cry to me? Speak to the children of Israel, that they go forward.

paite: Na chiangkhun lik inla, tuipi tung ah na khut zankhia in, kikhensak in. Huchi in Israel suante tuipi laizang ah leihul ah apaisuak ding uhi.
english: Lift up your rod, and stretch out your hand over the sea and divide it. Then the children of Israel shall go into the middle of the sea on dry ground.

paite: Ngai in, ke'n Aiguptate lungtang ka khauhsak ding a; amaute adelhzui ding uhi. Pharaoh tung ah, akangtalaite tung ah leh asakol tungtuang mite tung ah zahtakhuaina ka kimuh ding hi.
english: Behold, I myself will harden the hearts of the Egyptians, and they will go in after them. I will get myself honor over Pharaoh, and over all his armies, over his chariots, and over his horsemen.

paite: Pharaoh tung, akangtalaite tung leh asakol tungtuang mite tung a zahtakhuaina ka kimuh chiang in, kei TOUPA ka hi, chih Aiguptate'n athei ding uh," achi hi.
english: The Egyptians shall know that I am Yahweh when I have gotten myself honor over Pharaoh, over his chariots, and over his horsemen.”

paite: Israelte giahphual ma a pai, Pathian angel akisuan a, anunglam uah apai a; amailam ua kipan meipi dingh akisuan a, anunglam uah adinghta hi.
english: The angel of God, who went before the camp of Israel, moved and went behind them; and the pillar of cloud moved from before them, and stood behind them.

paite: Aiguptate giahphual leh Israelte giahphual kikal ah ahong omta a; amaute a ding in meipi leh khomial ahi a; himahleh zan in hiaite a ding in vak apia hi; huchi a zankhua a kuamah kinaihtuah thei zaw sam a-omlouhna ding un.
english: It came between the camp of Egypt and the camp of Israel. There was the cloud and the darkness, yet it gave light by night. One didn’t come near the other all night.

paite: Mosi in tuipi tung ah akhut azankhia a; TOUPA'n zankhua in suahlam huih hat in tuipi apaikiksak a, gam hul in tuipi abawl a, tuite akikhenta hi.
english: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and Yahweh caused the sea to go back by a strong east wind all night, and made the sea dry land, and the waters were divided.

paite: Tuipi lak a gam hul tung ah Israel suante apai ua; akhut taklam uh leh akhut veilam uah amau a ding in tuite baang ahong hita uhi.
english: The children of Israel went into the middle of the sea on the dry ground; and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.

paite: Aiguptate'n adelh ua, Pharaoh sakol tengteng, akangtalai tengteng leh asakol tungtuangmi tengteng nangawn tuipi lak ah amau nung ah apailut uhi.
english: The Egyptians pursued, and went in after them into the middle of the sea: all of Pharaoh’s horses, his chariots, and his horsemen.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, zingsang ahong hihtak in TOUPA'N meikuang khuampi dingh leh meipi khuampi dingh kawm ah Aigupta sepaihte lam a-en a, Aigupta sepaihte ahihbuaita hi.
english: In the morning watch, Yahweh looked out on the Egyptian army through the pillar of fire and of cloud, and confused the Egyptian army.

paite: Akangtalai khete uh alakkhiaksak a, haksapi in ahawl ua; Aiguptate'n, "Israelte ma a pan taikek ni; amaute a ding in TOUPA'N lah Aiguptate siatna ding in adousak ngal a," achi uhi.
english: He took off their chariot wheels, and they drove them heavily; so that the Egyptians said, “Let’s flee from the face of Israel, for Yahweh fights for them against the Egyptians!”

paite: TOUPA'N Mosi kiang ah, "Aiguptate tung leh akangtalaite tung leh asakol tungtuang mite tung a tuite ahong kizop nawn theihna ding in, tuipi tung ah na khut zankhia in," achi hi.
english: Yahweh said to Moses, “Stretch out your hand over the sea, that the waters may come again on the Egyptians, on their chariots, and on their horsemen.”

paite: Mosi in tuipi tung ah akhut azankhia a, zingsang ahong hih in tuipi ahatna ah ahong kik nawn a; Aiguptate alak ah ataikek ua; tuipi lak ah TOUPA'N Aiguptate athalpaihta hi.
english: Moses stretched out his hand over the sea, and the sea returned to its strength when the morning appeared; and the Egyptians fled against it. Yahweh overthrew the Egyptians in the middle of the sea.

paite: Tuite ahong kik nawn ua, kangtalaite, sakol tungtuang mite leh Pharaoh sepaih anung ua hong lut tengteng tui in akhuhta hi. Alak uah khat lel leng dam a suakta a-om kei uh.
english: The waters returned, and covered the chariots and the horsemen, even all Pharaoh’s army that went in after them into the sea. There remained not so much as one of them.

paite: Himahleh tuipi lak ah gam hul tung ah Israel suante apai ua; akhut taklam uleh, aveilam uah tuite amaute a ding in baang ahita hi.
english: But the children of Israel walked on dry land in the middle of the sea, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.

paite: Huchibang in TOUPA'N huai ni in Aiguptate khut a pan Israelte ahondamta hi. Israelte'n tuipi piau ah Aiguptate' misi amu uhi.
english: Thus Yahweh saved Israel that day out of the hand of the Egyptians; and Israel saw the Egyptians dead on the seashore.

paite: Aiguptate tung a anasep thupi Israelte'n amu ua, huchi in TOUPA leh asikha Mosi agingtata uhi.
english: Israel saw the great work which Yahweh did to the Egyptians, and the people feared Yahweh; and they believed in Yahweh and in his servant Moses.

paite: Huai khit in Mosi leh Israel suante'n TOUPA kiang ah hiai la asa uhi: Thupitak a avualzoh ziak in, TOUPA kiang ah la ka sa ding. Sakol leh atung a tuangmi tuipi ah apaikheta.
english: Then Moses and the children of Israel sang this song to Yahweh, and said, “I will sing to Yahweh, for he has triumphed gloriously. He has thrown the horse and his rider into the sea.

paite: TOUPA ka hatna leh ka la ahi, ka hotdamna ahong hi a; ka Pathian ahi, omna ka bawlsak ding. Ka pa' Pathian, huchi in amah ka tawisang ding hi.
english: Yah is my strength and song. He has become my salvation. This is my God, and I will praise him; my father’s God, and I will exalt him.

paite: TOUPA galhatpa ahi: TOUPA amin ahi.
english: Yahweh is a man of war. Yahweh is his name.

paite: "Pharoah kangtalaite leh asepaihte tuipi ah apaikheta: aheutute uh leng, Tuipi San ah akelum uhi.
english: He has cast Pharaoh’s chariots and his army into the sea. His chosen captains are sunk in the Red Sea.

paite: Thukna in amaute akhuhta: Suang bang in ataw ah atumta uhi.
english: The deeps cover them. They went down into the depths like a stone.

paite: "TOUPA aw, na khut taklama thilhihtheihna thupi ahong hita: TOUPA aw, na khut taklam in melma agawizanta hi.
english: Your right hand, Yahweh, is glorious in power. Your right hand, Yahweh, dashes the enemy in pieces.

paite: Na hoihna thupina in nang hon dou dia thoute azouta: na thangpaihna na sawlkhia a, huai in amaute buhpawl bang in akangta hi.
english: In the greatness of your excellency, you overthrow those who rise up against you. You send out your wrath. It consumes them as stubble.

paite: Na nakvangte mut in tuite kaihkhawm in a-om ua, tui tampite vum bang a chian in a-om, huchi in tuipi sunggil ah thuknate kipsak in a-om hi.
english: With the blast of your nostrils, the waters were piled up. The floods stood upright as a heap. The deeps were congealed in the heart of the sea.

paite: Melma in, ka delh ding a, ka pha dia, gallak ka hawm ding: Huaite ah ka duhgawlna atai ding, ka namsau ka phawi dia, ka khut in amau ka hihgawp ding," achi hi.
english: The enemy said, ‘I will pursue. I will overtake. I will divide the plunder. My desire will be satisfied on them. I will draw my sword. My hand will destroy them.’
