paite: Rakil leng akithuahpih a, Leah sang in Rakil a-itzawa, Laban nna kum sagih dang asemta hi.
english: He went in also to Rachel, and he loved also Rachel more than Leah, and served with him seven more years.

paite: TOUPA'N Leah pen huat in a-om chih athei a, asul ahonsak a; Rakil bel achiing hi.
english: Yahweh saw that Leah was hated, and he opened her womb, but Rachel was barren.

paite: Leah agai a, tapa anei a, amin Reuben asa hi. "TOUPA'N ka gimdan amuta. Tu'n zaw ka pasal in hon itta ding, " achi hi.
english: Leah conceived, and bore a son, and she named him Reuben. For she said, “Because Yahweh has looked at my affliction; for now my husband will love me.”

paite: Agai nawn a, tapa anei nawn a, “TOUPA'N huat a ka om azak ziak in hiai leng ahon pia hi,” achi hi. Huchi in amin Simeon asa hi.
english: She conceived again, and bore a son, and said, “Because Yahweh has heard that I am hated, he has therefore given me this son also.” She named him Simeon.

paite: Agai nawn a, tapa anei nawn a, "Tu in tapa thum ka neihsak ziak in, ka pasal in hon zuita ding, achi hi. Huaiziak in amin Levi asa hi.
english: She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “Now this time my husband will be joined to me, because I have borne him three sons.” Therefore his name was called Levi.

paite: Agai nawn a, tapa anei nawn a, "Tutung in zaw TOUPA ka phat ding," achi hi. Huaiziak in amin Judah asa a; ta anei nawn tadih kei hi.
english: She conceived again, and bore a son. She said, “This time I will praise Yahweh.” Therefore she named him Judah. Then she stopped bearing.

paite: Huan TOUPA Pathian in gamsa abawl tengteng lak ah gul agitlouhpil pen hi. Ama'n numei kiang ah, "Pathian in, 'Huan a singgah himhim na ne ding uh ahi kei chi ahi maw?" achi hi.
english: Now the serpent was more subtle than any animal of the field which Yahweh God had made. He said to the woman, “Has God really said, ‘You shall not eat of any tree of the garden’?”

paite: Numei in gul kiang ah, "Chi lou e, huan a singgahte ne thei mah ung,
english: The woman said to the serpent, “We may eat fruit from the trees of the garden,

paite: himahleh huan laizang a singgah pen ahihleh Pathian in, 'Na ne ding uh ahi kei, khoih leng na khoih ding uh ahi kei, huchi lou in zaw na si ding uh chi aka, " achi hi.
english: but not the fruit of the tree which is in the middle of the garden. God has said, ‘You shall not eat of it. You shall not touch it, lest you die.’”

paite: Gul in numei kiang ah, "Si zenzen lou e.
english: The serpent said to the woman, “You won’t really die,

paite: Na nek ni ua pat na mit uh ahong vak dia, asia leh apha thei in Pathian na hong bang ding uh, chih Pathian in thei kilkel ei ve," achi hi.
english: for God knows that in the day you eat it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, knowing good and evil.”

paite: Numei in singgah nek theih ahi chih leh mit hiptak ahi chih leh mi pilsak ding a singgah etlahhuai ahi, chih atheih in agah alou a, aneta hi. Akiang a om apasal leng apia a, aama'n leng aneta hi.
english: When the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was a delight to the eyes, and that the tree was to be desired to make one wise, she took some of its fruit, and ate. Then she gave some to her husband with her, and he ate it, too.

paite: Anih un amit uh ahong vakta a, vuaktang ahih lam uh hong kithei ua; theipi nah khuikhawm in, puan akibawltawm uhi.
english: Their eyes were opened, and they both knew that they were naked. They sewed fig leaves together, and made coverings for themselves.

paite: TOUPA Pathian, nitaklam ninem a huan a vak thawmging aza ua; Adam leh azi in huan a sing lak ah TOUPA Pathian ana kibuksan uhi.
english: They heard Yahweh God’s voice walking in the garden in the cool of the day, and the man and his wife hid themselves from the presence of Yahweh God among the trees of the garden.

paite: TOUPA Pathian in Adam asam a, akiang ah, "Koi a om na hia?" achi hi.
english: Yahweh God called to the man, and said to him, “Where are you?”

paite: Ama'n, "Huan ah na thawmging ka za a, vuaktang ka hih ziak in ka lau a; ka na kibuta," achi hi.
english: The man said, “I heard your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I was naked; so I hid myself.”

paite: Ama'n, "Vuaktang na hih kua'n hon hilh ahia? Singgah nek louh ding ka chih ne na hita maw?" achi hi.
english: God said, “Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?”

paite: Adam in, "Hon ompih dia na hon . piak numei in singgah hon pia a, ka . neta hi," achi hi.
english: The man said, “The woman whom you gave to be with me, she gave me fruit from the tree, and I ate it.”

paite: TOUPA Pathian in numei kiang ah, "Na thilhih bangchidan ahia?" achi hi. Numei in, "Gul in hon zekhem a, ka neta hi," achi hi.
english: Yahweh God said to the woman, “What have you done?” The woman said, “The serpent deceived me, and I ate.”

paite: TOUPA Pathian in gul kiang ah, "Hichibang a na hih ziak in ganhing tengteng leh gamsa chiteng lak ah hamsiat na hi tuanse ding a, bokvak in na pai gigeta ding a, na damsung in leivui na neta ding.
english: Yahweh God said to the serpent, “Because you have done this, you are cursed above all livestock, and above every animal of the field. You shall go on your belly and you shall eat dust all the days of your life.

paite: Nang leh numei ka hon kidousak ding a, na suante leh asuante leng ka kidousak lai ding. Huai in na lutang asidupsak ding a, nang akhetul na sidupsak ding," achi hi.
english: I will put hostility between you and the woman, and between your offspring and her offspring. He will bruise your head, and you will bruise his heel.”

paite: Numei kiang ah, "Na haksatna leh na naupaina nakpi in ka pungsak ding a; haksatak in tate na nei ding. Huan na lunggulh na pasal a ahi ding a, ama'n na tung ah thu anei ding," achi hi.
english: To the woman he said, “I will greatly multiply your pain in childbirth. You will bear children in pain. Your desire will be for your husband, and he will rule over you.”

paite: Adam kiang ah, "Na zi thu na man a, singgah na ne ding ahi kei, chi a, ka hon thupiak na nek ziak in nang ziak in leitung hamsiat in a-omta. Na damsung teng in gimtak a sem in agah na neta ding.
english: To Adam he said, “Because you have listened to your wife’s voice, and have eaten from the tree, about which I commanded you, saying, ‘You shall not eat of it,’ the ground is cursed for your sake. You will eat from it with much labor all the days of your life.

paite: Ling leh louling neite leng ahon omsak ding a, lei a anteh na neta ding hi.
english: It will yield thorns and thistles to you; and you will eat the herb of the field.

paite: Lei a na kik nawn masiah na mai a kho-ul luang puappuap in an na neta ding. Lei a pan lakkhiak na hi; leivui na hi a, leivui ah na kik nawn ding," achi hi.
english: You will eat bread by the sweat of your face until you return to the ground, for you were taken out of it. For you are dust, and you shall return to dust.”

paite: Adam in azi, mihing tengteng' nu ahih ziak in, amin Evi asa hi.
english: The man called his wife Eve because she would be the mother of all the living.

paite: TOUPA Pathian in Adam a ding leh azi a ding in savun puanaktual bawlsak in, asilhsak hi.
english: Yahweh God made garments of animal skins for Adam and for his wife, and clothed them.

paite: TOUPA Pathian in, "Ngai un, mihing in asia leh apha thei in eite bang ahong hita, tu in akhut ua sawk in hinna singgah lou a ne in, tangtawn in ahing kha ding uh," achi hi.
english: Yahweh God said, “Behold, the man has become like one of us, knowing good and evil. Now, lest he reach out his hand, and also take of the tree of life, and eat, and live forever—”

paite: Huaiziak in TOUPA Pathian in amah alakkhiakna lei let ding in Eden huan a kipan ahawlkheta hi.
english: Therefore Yahweh God sent him out from the garden of Eden, to till the ground from which he was taken.

paite: Mihingte adelhkheta a; hinna sing lampi veng ding in Eden huan suahlam pang ah cherubte leh mei namsau kilek zualzual a-omsakta hi.
english: So he drove out the man; and he placed cherubim at the east of the garden of Eden, and a flaming sword which turned every way, to guard the way to the tree of life.

paite: Rakil in Jakob ta himhim aneihsak kei chih akitheih in asanggamnu ahazata hi. Jakob kiang ah, "Tate hon pia in, huchi ahihkeileh ka si ding," achi hi.
english: When Rachel saw that she bore Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister. She said to Jacob, “Give me children, or else I will die.”

paite: Rakil tung ah Jakob aheh a, "Gilgah hon pe lou Pathian bang ka hi a hia?" achi hi.
english: Jacob’s anger burned against Rachel, and he said, “Am I in God’s place, who has withheld from you the fruit of the womb?”

paite: Ama'n, "En in, ka sikhanu Bilhah kithuahpih in. Huchi a ke'n leng amah a kipan tate ka neih sam theihna ding in ka phei tung ah ta ka hon nei ding hi," achi hi.
english: She said, “Behold, my maid Bilhah. Go in to her, that she may bear on my knees, and I also may obtain children by her.”

paite: Huan azi ding in asikhanu Bilhah apia a, Jakob in amah ana kithuahpih hi.
english: She gave him Bilhah her servant as wife, and Jacob went in to her.

paite: Bilhah agai a, Jakob ta aneihsakta hi.
english: Bilhah conceived, and bore Jacob a son.

paite: Rakil in, "Pathian in hon ngaihtuah a, ka aw leng aza, tapa ahon pia,” achi hi. Huaiziak in amin Dan asa hi.
english: Rachel said, “God has judged me, and has also heard my voice, and has given me a son.” Therefore she called his name Dan.

paite: Rakil sikhanu Bilhah agai nawn a, Jakob tapa dang aneihsak nawn hi.
english: Bilhah, Rachel’s servant, conceived again, and bore Jacob a second son.

paite: Rakil in, "Nakpitak in ka sanggamnu ka buan a, ka zouta," achi a; amin Naphtali asa hi.
english: Rachel said, “I have wrestled with my sister with mighty wrestlings, and have prevailed.” She named him Naphtali.

paite: Leah in ta dang anei nawn kei chih akitheih in, asikhanu Zilpah api a, azi ding in Jakob kiang ah apia hi.
english: When Leah saw that she had finished bearing, she took Zilpah, her servant, and gave her to Jacob as a wife.

paite: Huan Leah sikhanu Zilpah in Jakob tapa aneihsak hi.
english: Zilpah, Leah’s servant, bore Jacob a son.

paite: Leah in, "Vangphathuai ei," achi a; amin Gad asa hi.
english: Leah said, “How fortunate!” She named him Gad.

paite: Leah sikhanu Zilpah in Jakob tapa dang aneihsak nawn hi.
english: Zilpah, Leah’s servant, bore Jacob a second son.

paite: Leah in, "Hampha hi na tel ing e! Numeite'n hampha hon chi ding uh ei ve," achi a, amin Asher asa hi.
english: Leah said, “Happy am I, for the daughters will call me happy.” She named him Asher.

paite: Buh lak hun lai in Reuben in gamlak ah zawl-ai ava mu a; anu Leah kiang ah hon tawi hi. Rakil in Leah kiang ah, "Hehpih in na tapa zawl-ai akhen hon pe dih ve," achi hi.
english: Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to his mother, Leah. Then Rachel said to Leah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”

paite: Ama'n akiang ah, "Ka pasal na hon suhsak thil namai ahi hia? Ka tapa zawl-ai leng hon suhsak na tum nawn lai maw?" achi hi. Rakil in, "Na tapa' zawl-ai sik in tuzan nang ahon kithuahpih ding," achi hi.
english: Leah said to her, “Is it a small matter that you have taken away my husband? Would you take away my son’s mandrakes, also?” Rachel said, “Therefore he will lie with you tonight for your son’s mandrakes.”

paite: Nitaklam in Jakob gamlak a kipan ahong tung a, adawn ding in Leah akuan a, "N'on kithuahpih ding ahi. Ka tapa zawl-ai in ka hon guaita ngal a," achi hi. Huai zan in amah akithuahpih hi.
english: Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him, and said, “You must come in to me; for I have surely hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” He lay with her that night.

paite: Pathian in Leah thumna angaikhia a, agai a, Jakob tapa ngana aneihsak nawn hi.
english: God listened to Leah, and she conceived, and bore Jacob a fifth son.

paite: Leah in, “Ka sikhanu ka pasal kiang a ka piak ziak in Pathian in ka loh hon pia ei ve,” achi a; amin Issakar asa hi.
english: Leah said, “God has given me my hire, because I gave my servant to my husband.” She named him Issachar.

paite: Leah agai nawn a, Jakob tapa gukna aneihsak nawn hi.
english: Leah conceived again, and bore a sixth son to Jacob.

paite: Leah in, "Pathian in thil hoihtak hon neisak a; tu in zaw ka pasal tapa guk ka neihsak tak ziak in, ka kiang ah atengta ding," achi a; amin Zebulun asa hi.
english: Leah said, “God has endowed me with a good dowry. Now my husband will live with me, because I have borne him six sons.” She named him Zebulun.

paite: Huai nung in tanu anei nawn a, amin Dinah asa hi.
english: Afterwards, she bore a daughter, and named her Dinah.

paite: Pathian in Rakil atheigige a, Pathian in athumna angaikhia a, asul ahonsak hi.
english: God remembered Rachel, and God listened to her, and opened her womb.

paite: Amah agai a, tapa anei a, "Pathian in ka minsia alamangta," achi hi.
english: She conceived, bore a son, and said, “God has taken away my reproach.”

paite: "TOUPA'N tapa dang hon piakbeh ding," chi in amin Joseph asa hi.
english: She named him Joseph, saying, “May Yahweh add another son to me.”

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, Rakil in Joseph aneih nung in, Jakob in Laban kiang ah, "Kei ka omna ngei ah, ka gam ah hon paisakta in.
english: When Rachel had borne Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, “Send me away, that I may go to my own place, and to my country.

paite: Na nna ka sepsan ka zite leh ka tate hon pia inla, hon paisak in; na nna ka hon sepsakdan lah na thei ngal a,” achi hi.
english: Give me my wives and my children for whom I have served you, and let me go; for you know my service with which I have served you.”

paite: Laban in akiang ah, "Na mitmuh a deihsakna ka tanleh hehpih in om tadih lai ve. nang vang in TOUPA'N kei ahon vualzawl, chih ka thiltuahte a kipan in ka sinkhia hi,” achi hi.
english: Laban said to him, “If now I have found favor in your eyes, stay here, for I have divined that Yahweh has blessed me for your sake.”

paite: Amah mah in, “Na thaman ding gen inla, hon hilh dih, ka hon pe ding," achi hi.
english: He said, “Appoint me your wages, and I will give it.”

paite: Ama'n akiang ah, "Bangchi in na nna ka sem a, bangchi in ka kiang ah na gantate a-om ua, na thei akei hiam?
english: Jacob said to him, “You know how I have served you, and how your livestock have fared with me.

paite: Ka hong ma in tawmchik kia na nei a, tu'n zaw tampi ahong phata uh. Ka kalsuanna peuh ah TOUPA'N nang hon vualzawl hi. Himahleh chikchiang in ahia ka inkuante a ding a ka sepkhiak sam ding?" achi hi.
english: For it was little which you had before I came, and it has increased to a multitude. Yahweh has blessed you wherever I turned. Now when will I provide for my own house also?”

paite: Ama'n, "Bang ka hon pe dia?" achi a. Jakob in, "Bangmah na hon piak ding ahi kei. Hiai thil na hon hihsakleh na gantate ka khah dia ka ching nawn ding hi.
english: Laban said, “What shall I give you?” Jacob said, “You shall not give me anything. If you will do this thing for me, I will again feed your flock and keep it.

paite: Tuni in na gantate ka va enkhe vek ding a, belam lak a, avom gial petmah a gial leh avom a gial zekzek leh avom peuhmah, kel lak a, akang a gial petmah agial leh akang a gial zekzekte huai a kipan ka pituam zel ding hi. Tuban huchibang a hong piang peuhmah ka loh ahita ding hi.
english: I will pass through all your flock today, removing from there every speckled and spotted one, and every black one among the sheep, and the spotted and speckled among the goats. This will be my hire.

paite: Tunung a nang toh kal a ka thaman en ding a na hong pai hun chiang in, ka diktatna in ahon dawng mai ding. Kel lak a akang a gial petmah a gial lou leh akang a gial zekzek lou leh belam lak a avom lou ka kiang a na muh peuhmah ka guk in na sep mai ding," achi hi.
english: So my righteousness will answer for me hereafter, when you come concerning my hire that is before you. Every one that is not speckled and spotted among the goats, and black among the sheep, that might be with me, will be considered stolen.”

paite: Laban in, "Ngai in, na gen bang geih in hi hen aw," achi hi.
english: Laban said, “Behold, let it be according to your word.”

paite: Huai nitak in keltal akang a gial leh akang a gial zekzek teng leh kelnu akang gial petmah a gial leh akang a gial zekzek teng akanna om peuhmah, belam lak a avom tengteng toh apituam a, atapate khut ah apia hi.
english: That day, he removed the male goats that were streaked and spotted, and all the female goats that were speckled and spotted, every one that had white in it, and all the black ones among the sheep, and gave them into the hand of his sons.

paite: Amah leh Jakob kikal ah ni thum lam a-omsak a; Jakob in Laban ganhon dangte aching nawn hi.
english: He set three days’ journey between himself and Jacob, and Jacob fed the rest of Laban’s flocks.

paite: Jakob in hiangzau sing leh makha sing leh sesing chiang hing ala a, ahawng akhokngou chiat a, chiangte ah angoute akilangsak hi.
english: Jacob took to himself rods of fresh poplar, almond, and plane tree, peeled white streaks in them, and made the white appear which was in the rods.

paite: Achiang hawng khohte ganhonte'n tui ahong dawnna zel tuikuangte ah, tui luannate ah leh gantate mazawn zel ah akoih hi; tui dawn ding a ahong pai chiang ua againa ding un.
english: He set the rods which he had peeled opposite the flocks in the watering troughs where the flocks came to drink. They conceived when they came to drink.

paite: Gantate chiangte ma ah agai panta ua, agialte, gial petmah a gialte, agial zekzekte hon neikhia uhi.
english: The flocks conceived before the rods, and the flocks produced streaked, speckled, and spotted.

paite: Jakob in belamnoute akoihtuam a, ganhonte Laban ganhon lak a, agial leh avom tengteng lam angasak zel a; amah ganhonte akoihtuam zel a, Laban ganhon lak ah akoih kei hi.
english: Jacob separated the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks toward the streaked and all the black in Laban’s flock. He put his own droves apart, and didn’t put them into Laban’s flock.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, gannu hatzawte ahuk chiang un, agaitheihna ding un Jakob in tuiluanna ah, ganhonte mitmuh in chiangte akoih zel hi.
english: Whenever the stronger of the flock conceived, Jacob laid the rods in front of the eyes of the flock in the watering troughs, that they might conceive among the rods;

paite: Himahleh gannu hatloute mai ah akoih kei hi. Anou hatloute Laban a ahi ua, ahatte Jakob a ahi zel uhi.
english: but when the flock were feeble, he didn’t put them in. So the feebler were Laban’s, and the stronger Jacob’s.

paite: Jakob nakpi in ahong pung a, ganhon thupitak, sikhanute, sikhapate, sangawngsaute leh sabiltungte aneita hi.
english: The man increased exceedingly, and had large flocks, female servants and male servants, and camels and donkeys.

paite: Huan Laban tapate'n, "Jakob in i pa neihsate lamang in, i pa neihsa a kipan hiai thupina tengteng amu,” achih uh Jakob in ana zata hi.
english: Jacob heard Laban’s sons’ words, saying, “Jacob has taken away all that was our father’s. He has obtained all this wealth from that which was our father’s.”

paite: Jakob in Laban mel a-en a, ngai in, tuma lam bang in atung ah ahoih nawn kei chih athei hi.
english: Jacob saw the expression on Laban’s face, and, behold, it was not toward him as before.

paite: TOUPA'N Jakob kiang ah, "Na pipute gam ah leh na tanaute kiang ah pai nawnta in. Na kiang a om ding ka hi,” achi hi.
english: Yahweh said to Jacob, “Return to the land of your fathers, and to your relatives, and I will be with you.”

paite: Jakob in mi asawl a, gamlak a aganhon omna ah Rakil leh Leah asamsak a, akiang uah,
english: Jacob sent and called Rachel and Leah to the field to his flock,

paite: "Na pa uh mel ka muh in, tuma lam bang in ka tung ah ahoih nawn kei chih ka thei hi. Himahleh ka kiang ah ka pa' Pathian a-om hi.
english: and said to them, “I see the expression on your father’s face, that it is not toward me as before; but the God of my father has been with me.

paite: Ka theihtawp in na pa uh nna ka sem chih na thei uh.
english: You know that I have served your father with all of my strength.

paite: Himahleh na pa un hon khem a, ka loh lah sawmveitak ahihlamdang a; himahleh Pathian in ka siatna ding akhoih aphal kei hi.
english: Your father has deceived me, and changed my wages ten times, but God didn’t allow him to hurt me.

paite: Gial petmah a gialte na loh ahi ding, achihleh, ganta tengteng in gial petmah a gialte anei uh. Agialte na loh ahi ding achihleh, ganta tengteng in agialte anei zel uhi.
english: If he said, ‘The speckled will be your wages,’ then all the flock bore speckled. If he said, ‘The streaked will be your wages,’ then all the flock bore streaked.

paite: Huchibang in Pathian in na pa gantate alaksak a, kei ahon peta hi.
english: Thus God has taken away your father’s livestock, and given them to me.

paite: "Huan hichi ahong hi a, gantate agai pat lai un, ka mang in ka dak a, ngai in, apa, ganhonte, agialte, gial petmah a gialte, agial a gial iik-iakte ahi uh chih ka mu hi.
english: During mating season, I lifted up my eyes, and saw in a dream, and behold, the male goats which leaped on the flock were streaked, speckled, and grizzled.

paite: Ka mang in Pathian angel in, 'Jakob,' hon chi a; ke'n, 'hiai ah ka om' ka chi hi.
english: The angel of God said to me in the dream, ‘Jacob,’ and I said, ‘Here I am.’

paite: Ama'n, 'dak inla, en in, apa gantate tengteng agialte, gial petmah a gialte, agial a gial iik-iakte ahi uh. Laban in na tung a athilhih tengteng ka mu hi.
english: He said, ‘Now lift up your eyes, and behold, all the male goats which leap on the flock are streaked, speckled, and grizzled, for I have seen all that Laban does to you.

paite: Kei, suangphuh a sathau na nilh a, ka kiang a thu na chiamna Bethel, huai Bethel Pathian ka hi. Tu in thou inla, hiai gam a kipan pawt inla, na pianna gam ah pai nawnta in,' " achi hi.
english: I am the God of Bethel, where you anointed a pillar, where you vowed a vow to me. Now arise, get out from this land, and return to the land of your birth.’”

paite: Rakil leh Leah in adawng ua, akiang ah, "Ka pa uh inn ah koute a ding in tantuan leh gouluah ding a-om lailai a hia?
english: Rachel and Leah answered him, “Is there yet any portion or inheritance for us in our father’s house?

paite: Ama'n mikhual bang lel a hon sim hita lou maw? Ahon khawng khinta a, ka man uh lah ane khinta hi.
english: Aren’t we considered as foreigners by him? For he has sold us, and has also used up our money.

paite: Pathian in ka pa uh hauhna alaksak tengteng ei leh i tate a ahi. Pathian in na kiang a agen peuhmah hih in,” achi uhi.
english: For all the riches which God has taken away from our father are ours and our children’s. Now then, whatever God has said to you, do.”

paite: Jakob athou a, sangawngsau tung ah atapate leh azite atuangsak hi.
english: Then Jacob rose up, and set his sons and his wives on the camels,

paite: Kanaan gam a apa Isak kiang a pai ding in aganta tengteng leh alamkhiak tengteng, aganta muhte, Padan-aram gam a akholte apaipih vek hi.
english: and he took away all his livestock, and all his possessions which he had gathered, including the livestock which he had gained in Paddan Aram, to go to Isaac his father, to the land of Canaan.

paite: Laban, abelam mulmet ding in apawtkhia a; huan Rakil in apa milimte aguksak hi.
english: Now Laban had gone to shear his sheep; and Rachel stole the teraphim that were her father’s.

paite: Siria mi Laban theih louh kal in Jakob in aguk paimangsan a, apaimangsan ding thu ahilh kei hi.
english: Jacob deceived Laban the Syrian, in that he didn’t tell him that he was running away.

paite: Huchi in aneih tengteng toh ataikheta hi. Athou a, Luipi akan a, Gilead tang lam zuan in apaita hi.
english: So he fled with all that he had. He rose up, passed over the River, and set his face toward the mountain of Gilead.

paite: Ani thum ni in Jakob ataikhia chih Laban ahilh uh.
english: Laban was told on the third day that Jacob had fled.

paite: Asanggamte api a, ni sagih lam tan adelh a; Gilead tang ah adelhphata hi.
english: He took his relatives with him, and pursued him seven days’ journey. He overtook him in the mountain of Gilead.

paite: Siria mi Laban kiang ah zan in amang in Pathian ahong a, akiang ah, "Jakob kiang ah asia hi in apha hitaleh bangmah gen lou ding in pilvang in," achi hi. Laban in Jakob adelhphata ade hi.
english: God came to Laban the Syrian in a dream of the night, and said to him, “Be careful that you don’t speak to Jacob either good or bad.”

paite: Jakob in tang ah apuanin akai khin a; Laban in leng asanggamte toh Gilead tang ah akai uhi.
english: Laban caught up with Jacob. Now Jacob had pitched his tent in the mountain, and Laban with his relatives encamped in the mountain of Gilead.

paite: Laban in Jakob kiang ah, "Na thilhih bangchidan ahia oi? Ka theih louh kal a na guk paimang a, namsau a lak salte bang mai a ka tanute na pimang?
english: Laban said to Jacob, “What have you done, that you have deceived me, and carried away my daughters like captives of the sword?

paite: Bangziak a hon taimangsan a, hon guk paisan a, nopsaknate toh, late toh, khuangtate toh, kaihgingte toh ka hon khaktheihna ding a na hon hilh louh?
english: Why did you flee secretly, and deceive me, and didn’t tell me, that I might have sent you away with mirth and with songs, with tambourine and with harp;

paite: Ka tute leh ka tanute ka tawp na phal kei. Haihuaitak in thil na hih hi.
english: and didn’t allow me to kiss my sons and my daughters? Now you have done foolishly.

paite: Hon hihse thei ka hi a; himahleh na pa Pathian in tuzan in, 'Jakob kiang ah asia, apha bangmah gen lou ding in pilvang in,' chi in hon houpih hi.
english: It is in the power of my hand to hurt you, but the God of your father spoke to me last night, saying, ‘Be careful that you don’t speak to Jacob either good or bad.’

paite: Na pa inn na ngaih mahmah tak ziak a, pai ut hi tawk lechin leng bang ding a ka pathiante hon guksak na hia?" achi hi.
english: Now, you want to be gone, because you greatly longed for your father’s house, but why have you stolen my gods?”

paite: Jakob in adawng a, Laban kiang ah, "Ka lauh ziak ahi. Na tanute kei a pan na hon suhsak kha ding ka chi a ahi.
english: Jacob answered Laban, “Because I was afraid, for I said, ‘Lest you should take your daughters from me by force.’

paite: Kuapeuh tung a na pathiante na muhna ahing kei ding. I unaute mitmuh in nang thilte ka kiang a om a-omleh, enchian inla, la in,” achi hi. Rakil in huaite na gu ahih lam Jakob in athei ngal kei a.
english: Anyone you find your gods with shall not live. Before our relatives, discern what is yours with me, and take it.” For Jacob didn’t know that Rachel had stolen them.

paite: Jakob puaninte ah, Leah puaninte ah leh sikhanu nihte puaninte ah Laban alut a; himahleh amu kei. Leah puanin a kipan apawtkhia a, Rakil puanin ah alut hi.
english: Laban went into Jacob’s tent, into Leah’s tent, and into the tent of the two female servants; but he didn’t find them. He went out of Leah’s tent, and entered into Rachel’s tent.

paite: Rakil in milimte ana la a, sangawngsau van lak ah ana koih a, ana tutkhum hi. Laban in apuanin sung tengteng amaisuak vek a, himahleh amu kei hi.
english: Now Rachel had taken the teraphim, put them in the camel’s saddle, and sat on them. Laban felt around all the tent, but didn’t find them.

paite: Ama'n apa kiang ah, "Na ma a ka din ngap louh ziak in ka toupa, heh ke'n aw; numei omdan ngeina ka tung a a-om laitak ahi ngal a," achi hi. Azongzong a, himahleh milimte amuzouta kei hi.
english: She said to her father, “Don’t let my lord be angry that I can’t rise up before you; for I’m having my period.” He searched, but didn’t find the teraphim.

paite: Huchi in Jakob aheh a, Laban asalta hi. Jakob in Laban kiang ah, "Ka tatlekna bang ahia? Ka khelhna bang hi ahia, na hon hichi delh kin?
english: Jacob was angry, and argued with Laban. Jacob answered Laban, “What is my trespass? What is my sin, that you have hotly pursued me?

paite: Ka vante teng na pheklek nung in, na insung van bang na mu a? Ei gel kal a thu akhentheihna ding un ka unaute leh nang unaute ma ah na muh pen hon koihkhia in.
english: Now that you have felt around in all my stuff, what have you found of all your household stuff? Set it here before my relatives and your relatives, that they may judge between us two.

paite: Kum sawmnih vingveng na kiang ah ka omta a; na belampite leh na kelpite'n nou aneikhial ngei kei uh. Na belamhonte lak a apate leng ka ne ngei kei.
english: “These twenty years I have been with you. Your ewes and your female goats have not cast their young, and I haven’t eaten the rams of your flocks.

paite: Gamsa keih leng na kiang ah ka hon tun ngei ngal kei a: amangte sik in ke'n ka thuak zaw zel a; sun a guk hiam, zan a guk hiam lah ka dit na hon phut gige zomah hi.
english: That which was torn of animals, I didn’t bring to you. I bore its loss. Of my hand you required it, whether stolen by day or stolen by night.

paite: Hichibang in ka om zel a; sun nisa leh zan khovot in hon hihgim thei mahmah a; ihmut leng ka mu ngei kei.
english: This was my situation: in the day the drought consumed me, and the frost by night; and my sleep fled from my eyes.

paite: Kum sawmnih sung teng na inn ah ka om a; na tanu nihte loh ding in kum sawm-le-li na nna ka sem a, na gante loh ding in kum guk ka sem nawn a; ka loh ding in kum sawm-le-li na nna ka sem a, na gante loh ding in kum guk ka sem nawn a; ka loh sawmvei na hihlamdang hi.
english: These twenty years I have been in your house. I served you fourteen years for your two daughters, and six years for your flock, and you have changed my wages ten times.

paite: Ka pa' Pathian, Abraham' Pathian leh Isak' Pathian lauhna ka kiang a om lou hileh houh, tu'n vuaktang lel a hon paisak ngeingei ding na hi. Pathian in ka haksat thuakdan leh ka sepgimdan amu a, tuzan a nang hon sal ahi," achi hi.
english: Unless the God of my father, the God of Abraham, and the fear of Isaac, had been with me, surely now you would have sent me away empty. God has seen my affliction and the labor of my hands, and rebuked you last night.”

paite: Laban in adawng a, Jakob kiang ah, "Hiai tanute ka tanute ahi ua, hiai naupangte ka naupangte ahi uh. Hiai gante kei gante ahi ua, na muh tengteng kei a vek ahi uh. Tuni in hiai ka tanute tung ah leh ata neihte uh tung ah bang ka hihthei dia?
english: Laban answered Jacob, “The daughters are my daughters, the children are my children, the flocks are my flocks, and all that you see is mine! What can I do today to these my daughters, or to their children whom they have borne?

paite: Kisa in, kei leh nang in thukhun i bawl ding; kei leh nang kikal ah theihpihna hi hen," achi hi.
english: Now come, let’s make a covenant, you and I. Let it be for a witness between me and you.”

paite: Huchi in Jakob in suang ala a, suangphuh in aphut hi.
english: Jacob took a stone, and set it up for a pillar.

paite: Jakob in atanaute kiang ah, "Suang lakhawm un,” achi hi. Suang ala ua, achiangkhawm ua, asuang chiankhawm kiang ah an ane uhi.
english: Jacob said to his relatives, “Gather stones.” They took stones, and made a heap. They ate there by the heap.

paite: Laban in huai suang chiankhawm, Jegar-sahadutha asa a; Jakob in bel Galeed asa hi.
english: Laban called it Jegar Sahadutha, but Jacob called it Galeed.

paite: Laban in, “Hiai suang chiankhawm tu in kei leh nang kikal ah theihpihtu ahi,” achi hi. Huaiziak in amin Galeed chih ahita hi.
english: Laban said, “This heap is witness between me and you today.” Therefore it was named Galeed

paite: "Kikhen a i om hun chiang in TOUPA'N hon veng tuaktuak hen," achih ziak in Mizpah leng achi hi.
english: and Mizpah, for he said, “Yahweh watch between me and you, when we are absent one from another.

paite: "Ka tanute na sukgentheih a, ka tanute lou zi dang na neihleh, ka tanute chih louh kuamah i kiang ah a-om kei na ua, en in, Pathian, kei leh nang kal hon theihpihpa ahi," achi ngal hi.
english: If you afflict my daughters, or if you take wives in addition to my daughters, no man is with us; behold, God is witness between me and you.”

paite: Laban mah in, "Hiai suang chiankhawm en inla, keimah leh nangmah kikal a ka phuh, suangphuh leng en in.
english: Laban said to Jacob, “See this heap, and see the pillar, which I have set between me and you.

paite: Poi kikhoihsak ding in, kei hiai suang pel in na kiang ah ka hong pai kei ding, chih leh nang leng hiai suang chiankhawm leh hiai suangphuh pel in ka kiang ah na hong pai kei ding, chih, hiai suang chiankhawm atheihpihtu hi henla, hiai suangphuh leng atheihpihtu mah hi hen.
english: May this heap be a witness, and the pillar be a witness, that I will not pass over this heap to you, and that you will not pass over this heap and this pillar to me, for harm.

paite: Abraham' Pathian, Nahor Pathian, apa uh Pathian in i kal ah thu khen hen," achi hi. Huchi in Jakob in apa Isak lauhpa min lou in akichiamta hi.
english: The God of Abraham, and the God of Nahor, the God of their father, judge between us.” Then Jacob swore by the fear of his father, Isaac.

paite: Jakob in tang ah kithoihna alan a, atanaute tanghou ne ding in asamkhawm a; tanghou ane ua, tang ah agiak chiat uhi.
english: Jacob offered a sacrifice in the mountain, and called his relatives to eat bread. They ate bread, and stayed all night in the mountain.

paite: Zingsang in beltak in Laban athou a, atute leh atanute atawp a, avualzawl hi. Laban apaikhia a, amah omna ah akik nawnta hi.
english: Early in the morning, Laban rose up, and kissed his sons and his daughters, and blessed them. Laban departed and returned to his place.

paite: Jakob apai zel a, Pathian angelte ana tuak uhi.
english: Jacob went on his way, and the angels of God met him.

paite: Jakob in amaute amuh in, "Hiai Pathian giahphual ahi,” achi a; huai mun Mahanaim asa hi.
english: When he saw them, Jacob said, “This is God’s army.” He called the name of that place Mahanaim.

paite: Jakob in Edom gam, tua Seir gam ah ama ah thangkoute Esau kiang ah asawl hi.
english: Jacob sent messengers in front of him to Esau, his brother, to the land of Seir, the field of Edom.

paite: Akiang uah ka toupa Esau kiang ah hichi in na gen ding uh, "Na sikha Jakob in hichi in achi: Laban kiang ah mikhual ka hi a, tutan ka om nilouh hi.
english: He commanded them, saying, “This is what you shall tell my lord, Esau: ‘This is what your servant, Jacob, says. I have lived as a foreigner with Laban, and stayed until now.

paite: Bawngtalte, sabiltungte leh belamte, sikhapate leh sikhanute ka nei hi. Na mitmuh a deihsakna ka tan theihna ding a ka toupa hilh ding in mite ka hon sawl hi,” chi in.
english: I have cattle, donkeys, flocks, male servants, and female servants. I have sent to tell my lord, that I may find favor in your sight.’”

paite: Jakob kiang ah thangkoute ahong kik nawn ua, "Na u Esau kiang ka va tung ua, mi zali toh nang dawn ding in ahong pai hi," chi in agen uhi.
english: The messengers returned to Jacob, saying, “We came to your brother Esau. He is coming to meet you, and four hundred men are with him.”

paite: Jakob in alau mahmah a, alungkhamta hi. Akiang a mi omte, belamhonte, bawnghonte leh sangawngsaute pawl nih in akhen hi.
english: Then Jacob was greatly afraid and was distressed. He divided the people who were with him, along with the flocks, the herds, and the camels, into two companies.

paite: "Esau ahong pai a, pawl khat athahleh leng taimang thei ding pawl khat om lai," achi hi.
english: He said, “If Esau comes to the one company, and strikes it, then the company which is left will escape.”

paite: Jakob mah in, "Aw ka pa Abraham' Pathian, ka pa Isak' Pathian, TOUPA, na gam ah leh na tanaute kiang ah pai nawnta in, ka hon hihhoih ding hon chipa,
english: Jacob said, “God of my father Abraham, and God of my father Isaac, Yahweh, who said to me, ‘Return to your country, and to your relatives, and I will do you good,’

paite: na sikha tung a hehpihna na muhsakleh thutak tengteng na muhsak lak a, aneupen leng mu tak ka hi kei. Hiai Jordan lui ka chiangkhun kia toh ka kan a; tu in zaw pawl nih hial ka hong hita uhi.
english: I am not worthy of the least of all the loving kindnesses, and of all the truth, which you have shown to your servant; for with just my staff I crossed over this Jordan; and now I have become two companies.

paite: Hehpih in ka u khut a kipan, Esau khut a kipan, hon humbit in. Huchi lou in zaw kei leh numei naupangte tan in ahon that kha ding, chih ka lau hi.
english: Please deliver me from the hand of my brother, from the hand of Esau; for I fear him, lest he come and strike me and the mothers with the children.

paite: Nang ka hon hihhoih ngeingei ding a, na suante tuipi a piaunel sim zoh louh tan hial a atam bang in ka bawl ding na hon chi ngal a," achi hi.
english: You said, ‘I will surely do you good, and make your offspring as the sand of the sea, which can’t be counted because there are so many.’”

paite: Huai zan in huai ah agiakta a; aneihte lak a kipan a-u Esau a ding thilpiak alakhia hi.
english: He stayed there that night, and took from that which he had with him a present for Esau, his brother:

paite: Kelpi zanih, keltal sawmnih, belampi zanih leh belampa sawmnih,
english: two hundred female goats and twenty male goats, two hundred ewes and twenty rams,

paite: sangawngsau zat lai sawmthum anoute toh, bawngpi sawmli leh bawngtal sawmkhat, sabiltungpi sawmnih leh sabiltungnou sawmkhat.
english: thirty milk camels and their colts, forty cows, ten bulls, twenty female donkeys and ten foals.

paite: Hiaite pawl chih atuam chiat in asikhate khut ah akemsak a, asikhate kiang ah, "Ka ma ah pai galkah unla, pawl chih kal neisak zel un," achi hi.
english: He delivered them into the hands of his servants, every herd by itself, and said to his servants, “Pass over before me, and put a space between herd and herd.”

paite: Amakaipa kiang ah, "Ka u Esau in ahon tuah a, na kiang a, kua na hia? Koi a hoh dek na hia? Na ma a om kuate ahi ua? chi a ahon dotleh,
english: He commanded the foremost, saying, “When Esau, my brother, meets you, and asks you, saying, ‘Whose are you? Where are you going? Whose are these before you?’

paite: ‘Na sikha Jakob a ahi ua; hiaite ka pu Esau, nang ka toupa a ding a ahon khak thilpiakte ahi uh. Ngai in, amah ka nung uah a om,' na chi ding," chi in thu apia hi.
english: Then you shall say, ‘They are your servant, Jacob’s. It is a present sent to my lord, Esau. Behold, he also is behind us.’”

paite: Anihna leh athumna leh ganhon hawlte tengteng kiang ah leng, "Esau na muh chiang un huchibang mah in na gen ding uh.
english: He commanded also the second, and the third, and all that followed the herds, saying, “This is how you shall speak to Esau, when you find him.

paite: 'Ngai in, na sikha Jakob ka nung uah a-om,' chi chiat un," chi in thu ape chiat hi. "Thilpiak ka ma ah paileh alung ka damsak ding a, huai nung in amel ka mu ding. Huchi in ahon na kipahpih ding,” achi hi.
english: You shall say, ‘Not only that, but behold, your servant, Jacob, is behind us.’” For, he said, “I will appease him with the present that goes before me, and afterward I will see his face. Perhaps he will accept me.”

paite: Huchi in thilpiak ama ah apai masasak a; amah huai zan in apawlte lak ah agiak hi.
english: So the present passed over before him, and he himself stayed that night in the camp.

paite: Zan in athou a, azi nihte leh asikhanu nihte leh atapa sawm-le- khatte api a, Jabbok lui ngahna ah akanta hi.
english: He rose up that night, and took his two wives, and his two servants, and his eleven sons, and crossed over the ford of the Jabbok.

paite: Amaute api a, lui akan ua, aneih tengteng leng akansak vek hi.
english: He took them, and sent them over the stream, and sent over that which he had.

paite: Jakob amah kia in a-omta a, mi khat toh phalvak tan akibuan uhi.
english: Jacob was left alone, and wrestled with a man there until the breaking of the day.

paite: Azou kei chih akitheih in Jakob pheipi guhtuah akhoihsak a, akibuan lai un Jakob pheipi guhtuah akilawita hi.
english: When he saw that he didn’t prevail against him, the man touched the hollow of his thigh, and the hollow of Jacob’s thigh was strained as he wrestled.

paite: Ama'n, "Hon khah in, phalvak ding ahita," achi hi. Huchi in ama'n, "N'on vualzawl keileh ka hon khah kei ding," achi hi.
english: The man said, “Let me go, for the day breaks.” Jacob said, “I won’t let you go unless you bless me.”

paite: Ama'n akiang ah, "Na min bang ahia?" achi a; ama'n, "Jakob," achi hi.
english: He said to him, “What is your name?” He said, “Jacob”.

paite: Ama'n, "Na min Jakob ahi nawn kei ding a, Israel ahon chi zawta ding uh: Pathian leh mihingte na buan a, na zouta ngal a," achi hi.
english: He said, “Your name will no longer be called Jacob, but Israel; for you have fought with God and with men, and have prevailed.”

paite: Jakob in amah adong a, "Hehpih in na min hon hilh in,” achi hi. Ama'n, "Bangziak in ahia ka min na hon dot?" achi hi. Huchi in huai ah avualzawlta hi.
english: Jacob asked him, “Please tell me your name.” He said, “Why is it that you ask what my name is?” So he blessed him there.

paite: Jakob in huai mun min, “Peniel,” asa hi. "Pathian amai chin mahmah ah ka mu a; ka hinna ahawi ziak in," achi hi.
english: Jacob called the name of the place Peniel; for he said, “I have seen God face to face, and my life is preserved.”

paite: Peniel akhen lai in, ni ahong suak a, amah ahon sun a, apheipi ziak in abaita hi.
english: The sun rose on him as he passed over Peniel, and he limped because of his thigh.

paite: Huaiziak in Jakob pheipi guhtuah a sadual tak akhoihsak ziak in, tuni tanpha Israel suante'n pheipi guhtuah a sadual om ane ngei kei uhi.
english: Therefore the children of Israel don’t eat the sinew of the hip, which is on the hollow of the thigh, to this day, because he touched the hollow of Jacob’s thigh in the sinew of the hip.

paite: Huan Jakob dakkhia a a-etleh, ngai in, akiang ah mi zali toh Esau ahong pai hi. Huchi in Leah, Rakil leh sikhanu nihte kiang ah atate a-omsak khipkhep hi.
english: Jacob lifted up his eyes, and looked, and, behold, Esau was coming, and with him four hundred men. He divided the children between Leah, Rachel, and the two servants.

paite: Sikhanute leh atate amakai in akoih a, azom in Leah leh atate, huan Rakil leh Joseph bel ananungpen in akoih hi.
english: He put the servants and their children in front, Leah and her children after, and Rachel and Joseph at the rear.

paite: Amah ama uah apai a, a-u kiang chin atun masiah sagihvei lei si in akun hi.
english: He himself passed over in front of them, and bowed himself to the ground seven times, until he came near to his brother.

paite: Himahleh Esau amah mu ding in atai a, apom a, angawng a kun in atawp a, akap uhi.
english: Esau ran to meet him, embraced him, fell on his neck, kissed him, and they wept.

paite: Esau dakkhia a a-etleh, numeite leh naupangte amu a, "Hiai n'on tonpihte kuate ahi ua?" achi hi. Ama'n, "Pathian in hehpihtak a na sikha kiang a apiak naupangte ahi uh," achi hi.
english: He lifted up his eyes, and saw the women and the children; and said, “Who are these with you?” He said, “The children whom God has graciously given your servant.”

paite: Sikhanute leh atate uh ahong pai ua, akun uhi.
english: Then the servants came near with their children, and they bowed themselves.

paite: Leah leng atate toh ahong pai nai ua, akun ua, huai khit in Joseph leh Rakil leng ahong pai nai ua, akun uhi.
english: Leah also and her children came near, and bowed themselves. After them, Joseph came near with Rachel, and they bowed themselves.

paite: Esau in, "Ka ganhon kituahpih tengpi bang na chihna ahia?" achi hi. Ama'n, "Ka toupa, na mitmuh a deihsakna ka tan theihna ding in ka chi a ahi," achi hi.
english: Esau said, “What do you mean by all this company which I met?” Jacob said, “To find favor in the sight of my lord.”

paite: Esau in, "Ke'n leng hau veng e, bawi aw, na neih tengteng nang a hi hen," achi hi.
english: Esau said, “I have enough, my brother; let that which you have be yours.”

paite: Jakob in, "Hilou e, na mitmuh a deihsakna ka tan theihleh hehpih in ka hon thilpiakte hon sansak in. Pathian mel mu bang in na mel ka mu a, ka tung ah lah na kipak ngal a.
english: Jacob said, “Please, no, if I have now found favor in your sight, then receive my present at my hand, because I have seen your face, as one sees the face of God, and you were pleased with me.

paite: Pathian in hon hehpih ziak leh akiching ka neih ziak in ka hon thilpiakte sang in,” achi hi. Huchi in akun teitei a, ama'n asangta hi.
english: Please take the gift that I brought to you, because God has dealt graciously with me, and because I have enough.” He urged him, and he took it.

paite: Esau in, “Kisa in, pai ni, na ma ah ka pai ding," achi hi.
english: Esau said, “Let’s take our journey, and let’s go, and I will go before you.”

paite: Ama'n akiang ah, "Naupangte aneu laidan uleh belamhon ka kiang a omte anou ahihdan uh, ka toupa'n na thei hi. Ni khat lel leng hat lua a, ahawl uleh ganhon tengteng si vek ding uh ahi.
english: Jacob said to him, “My lord knows that the children are tender, and that the flocks and herds with me have their young, and if they overdrive them one day, all the flocks will die.

paite: Ka toupa, hehpih in na sikha ma ah pai inla; ke'n Seir tang ah, ka toupa, na kiang ka tun mateng, ka ma a gante apai zoh dandan uleh naupangte apai theihdan bang zel un, awlawl in ka hon masuan zel ding,” achi hi.
english: Please let my lord pass over before his servant, and I will lead on gently, according to the pace of the livestock that are before me and according to the pace of the children, until I come to my lord to Seir.”

paite: Esau in, "Ka kiang a om mi khenkhat hon nutsiat leng ake," achi hi. Ama'n, "Apoimoh khol a hia? Ka toupa mitmuh in deihsakna hon musak in,” achi hi.
english: Esau said, “Let me now leave with you some of the people who are with me.” He said, “Why? Let me find favor in the sight of my lord.”

paite: Huai ni mah in Seir tang lam zuan in Esau akik nawnta hi.
english: So Esau returned that day on his way to Seir.

paite: Sukkoth mun ah Jakob apai a, amah a ding in inn alam a, agante a ding in leng aidakbukte alam hi. Huaiziak in huai mun min Sukkoth asa hi.
english: Jacob traveled to Succoth, built himself a house, and made shelters for his livestock. Therefore the name of the place is called Succoth.

paite: Padan-aram gam a kipan Jakob ahong paikhiak nung, lungmuangtak in Kanaan gam a om Shekem khua atung a, huai khopi ma ah apuanin azakta hi.
english: Jacob came in peace to the city of Shechem, which is in the land of Canaan, when he came from Paddan Aram; and encamped before the city.

paite: Shekem pa Hamor tapate a kipan dangka zakhat in apuanin zakna mun alei hi.
english: He bought the parcel of ground where he had spread his tent, at the hand of the children of Hamor, Shechem’s father, for one hundred pieces of money.

paite: Huai ah maitam adoh a, amin El-Elohe-Israel asa hi.
english: He erected an altar there, and called it El Elohe Israel.

paite: Huan Leah tanu Dinah, Jakob nesak, hai gaunate mu ding in apawtkhia hi.
english: Dinah, the daughter of Leah, whom she bore to Jacob, went out to see the daughters of the land.

paite: Hiv mi Hamor, huai gam vaihawmpa tapa Shekem in amah ana mu a, pummat in aluppih a, ahihninta hi.
english: Shechem the son of Hamor the Hivite, the prince of the land, saw her. He took her, lay with her, and humbled her.

paite: Jakob tanu Dinah tung ah alungsim a- omden a, huai nungak a-it mahmah a, kamsiamtak in ahoupih hi.
english: His soul joined to Dinah, the daughter of Jacob, and he loved the young lady, and spoke kindly to the young lady.

paite: Shekem in apa Hamor ahoupih a, "Ka zi ding in huai nungak hon pisak in," achi hi.
english: Shechem spoke to his father, Hamor, saying, “Get me this young lady as a wife.”

paite: Jakob in atanu Dinah aninsak khin chih aza a, gamlak ah aganhonte lak uah atapate a-om uhi. Huchi in ahong tun mateng uh Jakob adai dide hi.
english: Now Jacob heard that he had defiled Dinah, his daughter; and his sons were with his livestock in the field. Jacob held his peace until they came.

paite: Jakob houpih ding in Shekem pa Hamor akiang ah ahoh hi.
english: Hamor the father of Shechem went out to Jacob to talk with him.

paite: Jakob tapate'n azaktak un gamlak a kipan ahong pai ua, Jakob tanu kithuahpih in Israelte lak a thil gilou haihuaitak, thilhih het louh ding, ahih ziak in adah ua, aheh mahmah uhi.
english: The sons of Jacob came in from the field when they heard it. The men were grieved, and they were very angry, because he had done folly in Israel in lying with Jacob’s daughter, a thing that ought not to be done.

paite: Hamor in amau ahoupih a, "Ka tapa Shekem lungsim na tanu uh tung ah a-om tinten a, hehpih in azi ding in neisak ve ua.
english: Hamor talked with them, saying, “The soul of my son, Shechem, longs for your daughter. Please give her to him as a wife.

paite: Kilatuah ve ni e; na tanute uh hon lasak unla, ka tanute uh leng la sam un.
english: Make marriages with us. Give your daughters to us, and take our daughters for yourselves.

paite: "Ka kiang uah na teng ding ua; gam leng akiching gige ding. Hiai ah teng unla, sum sin unla, hiai ah kihih inbul un," achi hi.
english: You shall dwell with us, and the land will be before you. Live and trade in it, and get possessions in it.”

paite: Shekem in nungak' pa leh asanggampate kiang ah, "Na deihsakna uh hon musak unla, huan ka kiang a na gen peuh uh ka hon pe ding.
english: Shechem said to her father and to her brothers, “Let me find favor in your eyes, and whatever you will tell me I will give.

paite: Man leh thilpiak zaw bangzah gen le uchin, na chih bangbang uh ka hon pe ding. Akoi abang hitaleh, nungak pen zi ding in hon neisak phot un," achi hi.
english: Ask me a great amount for a dowry, and I will give whatever you ask of me, but give me the young lady as a wife.”

paite: Jakob tapate'n asanggamnu uh Dinah anitsak ziak in Shekem leh apa Hamor khembawl in adawng ua, akiang uah,
english: The sons of Jacob answered Shechem and Hamor his father with deceit when they spoke, because he had defiled Dinah their sister,

paite: "Hiai thil zeksum louh mi kiang a ka tanu uh piak pen ka hihthei kei ding uh; huai lah koute a ding in minsiatna ahi ngal a.
english: and said to them, “We can’t do this thing, to give our sister to one who is uncircumcised; for that is a reproach to us.

paite: Hichibang a kichiam kia in na thu uh pha ka sa ding uh. Na lak ua pasal peuhpeuh koute bang a zeksum in om uhen.
english: Only on this condition will we consent to you. If you will be as we are, that every male of you be circumcised,

paite: Huchi in ka tanute uh na nei ding ua, kou leng na tanute uh ka nei sam ding uh. Na kiang uah ka teng ding ua, chi khat i hi ding.
english: then will we give our daughters to you; and we will take your daughters to us, and we will dwell with you, and we will become one people.

paite: Himahleh, zeksum thu a ka thu uh na zuih kei ding uleh, ka tanu uh ka pi ding ua, ka pai mai ding uh," achi uhi.
english: But if you will not listen to us and be circumcised, then we will take our sister, and we will be gone.”

paite: Athugen un Hamor leh Hamor tapa Shekem akipaksak hi.
english: Their words pleased Hamor and Shechem, Hamor’s son.

paite: Tangval in Jakob tanu adeih mahmah ziak in huai thil sawt hal lou in ahihta hi. Amah apa inkuan tengteng lak a mite zahtak pen ahi.
english: The young man didn’t wait to do this thing, because he had delight in Jacob’s daughter, and he was honored above all the house of his father.

paite: Hamor leh atapa Shekem in akhokulh kongkhak uh apha ua, akhote uh ahoupih uhi.
english: Hamor and Shechem, his son, came to the gate of their city, and talked with the men of their city, saying,

paite: "Hiai mite ei toh kilemtak in a-om uh. Huaiziak in hiai gam a teng in, hiai ah sum sin uhen. Ngai un, amaute a ding in gam lah aza ngal a. Atanute uh zi in nei lehang, i tanute uh leng neisak sam ni.
english: “These men are peaceful with us. Therefore let them live in the land and trade in it. For behold, the land is large enough for them. Let’s take their daughters to us for wives, and let’s give them our daughters.

paite: Himahleh nam khat i hong hihna ding a i kiang a tentheihna ding un hichibang a i chiam kia in huai mite'n pha ahon sakpih ding uhi; zeksum ahih bang ua i lak ua pasal peuhpeuh zeksum hong hita lehang.
english: Only on this condition will the men consent to us to live with us, to become one people, if every male among us is circumcised, as they are circumcised.

paite: Agante uh, asumte uh, asa tengteng uh ei a ahi vek kei dia hia? Athu uh pha sakpih mai ve ni e, huchi in i kiang uah ateng ding uh," achi uhi.
english: Won’t their livestock and their possessions and all their animals be ours? Only let’s give our consent to them, and they will dwell with us.”

paite: Hamor leh atapa Shekem thu a khokulh kongkhak a pawtkhe tengteng in azui ua; akhokulh kongkhak a pawtkhe tengteng, pasal peuhpeuh zek asumsak uhi.
english: All who went out of the gate of his city listened to Hamor, and to Shechem his son; and every male was circumcised, all who went out of the gate of his city.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, ani thum ni a, nat athuak lai un, Jakob tapate lak a nih, Dinah sanggampa Simeon leh Levi in anamsau uh tawi tuak in aguk in khua ava sualta ua, pasal tengteng athatgam uhi.
english: On the third day, when they were sore, two of Jacob’s sons, Simeon and Levi, Dinah’s brothers, each took his sword, came upon the unsuspecting city, and killed all the males.

paite: Namsau hiam in Hamor leh atapa Shekem athat ua, Shekem inn a kipan Dinah api ua, apawtta uhi.
english: They killed Hamor and Shechem, his son, with the edge of the sword, and took Dinah out of Shechem’s house, and went away.

paite: Jakob tapate'n amithahte uh ava pha nawn ua, atanu uh anitsak ziak un huai khua alokta uhi.
english: Jacob’s sons came on the dead, and plundered the city, because they had defiled their sister.

paite: Abelamhonte uh, abawnghonte uh, asabiltungte uh, akhua ua thil omte leh alou ua thil omte alaksak uhi.
english: They took their flocks, their herds, their donkeys, that which was in the city, that which was in the field,

paite: Asum tengteng uleh ata-anau neu chikchikte leh azite tengteng uh sal in aman ua, insung a om tengteng alok uhi.
english: and all their wealth. They took captive all their little ones and their wives, and took as plunder everything that was in the house.

paite: Jakob in Simeon leh Levi kiang ah, "Nou hiai gam a tengte lak a, Kanaante leh Perizte lak ah, huat na hon posak ua, na hon lungzingsak mahmah uh. Kei tawmchik ka hih ziak in hon sual ding in akikhawmkhawm ding ua, ahon that mai ding uhi. Huchi in hihmang in ka om ding, kei leh ka inkuanpihte toh,” achi hi.
english: Jacob said to Simeon and Levi, “You have troubled me, to make me odious to the inhabitants of the land, among the Canaanites and the Perizzites. I am few in number. They will gather themselves together against me and strike me, and I will be destroyed, I and my house.”

paite: Amau, "Ka sanggamnu uh kizuak bang a abawl ding ahi a hia?" achi uhi.
english: They said, “Should he deal with our sister as with a prostitute?”

paite: Huan Pathian in Jakobiang hohtou in, huai ah teng in. Na u Esau a kipan na taimang lai a, na kiang a kilak Pathian a ding in huai mun ah maitam doh in," achi hi.
english: God said to Jacob, “Arise, go up to Bethel, and live there. Make there an altar to God, who appeared to you when you fled from the face of Esau your brother.”

paite: Jakob in a-inkuanpihte leh akiang a om tengteng kiang ah, "Na lak ua om gamdang pathiante koihmang unla, kihihsiangthou unla, na puansilhte uh kheng un.
english: Then Jacob said to his household, and to all who were with him, “Put away the foreign gods that are among you, purify yourselves, and change your garments.

paite: I thou ding ua, Bethel ah i paitou ding uh. Ka lungzin lai a hon dawng, ka paina a ka kiang a om zel Pathian a ding in maitam ka doh ding," achi hi.
english: Let’s arise, and go up to Bethel. I will make there an altar to God, who answered me in the day of my distress, and was with me on the way which I went.”

paite: Huchi in gamdang pathiante akhut ua om tengteng leh abil ua bilbah abah tengteng uh Jakob kiang ah apekhe vek uhi. Jakob in Shekem kho kiang a tosaw nuai ah aphum hi.
english: They gave to Jacob all the foreign gods which were in their hands, and the rings which were in their ears; and Jacob hid them under the oak which was by Shechem.

paite: Apai ua, akim ua khuate'n alau mahmah ua, Jakob tapate adelh kei uhi.
english: They traveled, and a terror of God was on the cities that were around them, and they didn’t pursue the sons of Jacob.

paite: Jakob leh akiang a om tengteng toh, Kanaan gam a om Luz khua, huai Bethel kichi atung a,
english: So Jacob came to Luz (that is, Bethel), which is in the land of Canaan, he and all the people who were with him.

paite: huai ah maitam adoh a, a-u a kipan ataimang lai a, akiang a Pathian akilak ziak in huai mun min El-bethel asa hi.
english: He built an altar there, and called the place El Beth El; because there God was revealed to him, when he fled from the face of his brother.

paite: Huan Rebekah donnu Deborah asi a, Bethel khang a tosaw nuai ah avui ua; tosaw min Allon-bakuth asa uhi.
english: Deborah, Rebekah’s nurse, died, and she was buried below Bethel under the oak; and its name was called Allon Bacuth.

paite: Padan-aram gam a kipan Jakob ahong tun in akiang ah Pathian akilak nawn a, avualzawl hi.
english: God appeared to Jacob again, when he came from Paddan Aram, and blessed him.

paite: Pathian in akiang ah, "Na min Jakob ahi a; na min Jakob ahi nawn kei ding a, na min Israel ahi zawta ding,” achi hi. Huchi in amin Israel asata hi.
english: God said to him, “Your name is Jacob. Your name shall not be Jacob any more, but your name will be Israel.” He named him Israel.

paite: Pathian mah in akiang ah, "Kei Pathian Bangkim hihthei ka hi. Chi tampi suang in hong pung in. Nam, chih tham ngial leh nam tuamtuam omkhawmte leng nang ah ahong om ding ua, na khal a kipan kumpipate leng ahong pawt ding uhi.
english: God said to him, “I am God Almighty. Be fruitful and multiply. A nation and a company of nations will be from you, and kings will come out of your body.

paite: Abraham leh Isak kiang a ka gam piak na kiang ah ka hon pe ding. Na om louh nung chiang in na suante kiang ah leng gam ka pe zel ding," achi hi.
english: The land which I gave to Abraham and Isaac, I will give it to you, and to your offspring after you I will give the land.”

paite: Pathian in ahoupihna mun a kipan Jakob apaitouh santa hi.
english: God went up from him in the place where he spoke with him.

paite: Ahoupihna mun ah Jakob in suangkhuam aphut a; atung ah dawn thillat abuak a, atung ah sathau leng abuak hi.
english: Jacob set up a pillar in the place where he spoke with him, a pillar of stone. He poured out a drink offering on it, and poured oil on it.

paite: Jakob in Pathian in ahoupihna mun min Bethel asa hi.
english: Jacob called the name of the place where God spoke with him “Bethel”.

paite: Bethel a kipan apaikhia ua; Ephrath kho tunna ding gamlatak ahih lai in Rakil in nau avei a, anak vei mahmah hi.
english: They traveled from Bethel. There was still some distance to come to Ephrath, and Rachel travailed. She had hard labor.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, agim laitak in naudommi'n, "Lau ke'n, tapa nei nawn ding na hi," achi hi.
english: When she was in hard labor, the midwife said to her, “Don’t be afraid, for now you will have another son.”

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, alaitah ding kuan in, (amah lah si dek ahi ngal a), amin Ben-oni asa a; himahleh apa'n Benjamin asa hi.
english: As her soul was departing (for she died), she named him Benoni, but his father named him Benjamin.

paite: Rakil asita a, Ephrath lampi ah avui uh; huai Ephrath khua Bethlehem ahi.
english: Rachel died, and was buried on the way to Ephrath (also called Bethlehem).

paite: Ahan tung ah Jakob in suang aphut a; huai tuni tan in Rakil hansuang ahiden hi.
english: Jacob set up a pillar on her grave. The same is the Pillar of Rachel’s grave to this day.

paite: Israel apai zel a, Migdol Eder khen lam ah apuanin akai hi.
english: Israel traveled, and spread his tent beyond the tower of Eder.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, Israel huai gam a a-om lai in Reuben in apa mei Bilhah ava kithuahpih a; Israel in huai aza hi.
english: While Israel lived in that land, Reuben went and lay with Bilhah, his father’s concubine, and Israel heard of it. Now the sons of Jacob were twelve.

paite: Jakob tapate sawm- le-nih ahi uh. Leah tapate Reuben (Jakob tapa upapen), Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issakar leh Zebulun ahi uh.
english: The sons of Leah: Reuben (Jacob’s firstborn), Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, and Zebulun.

paite: Rakil tapate Joseph leh Benjamin ahi uh.
english: The sons of Rachel: Joseph and Benjamin.

paite: Rakil sikhanu Bilhah tapate Dan leh Naphtali ahi uh.
english: The sons of Bilhah (Rachel’s servant): Dan and Naphtali.

paite: Leah sikhanu Zilpah tapate Gad leh Asher ahi ua; hiaite Jakob tapa, Padan-aram gam a aneihte ahi uhi.
english: The sons of Zilpah (Leah’s servant): Gad and Asher. These are the sons of Jacob, who were born to him in Paddan Aram.

paite: Kiriath-arba a Abraham leh Isak omna Mamre ah apa Isak kiang ah Jakob atungta a; Kiriath-arba khua Hebron leng kichi ahi.
english: Jacob came to Isaac his father, to Mamre, to Kiriath Arba (which is Hebron), where Abraham and Isaac lived as foreigners.

paite: Isak damsung kum zakhat-le-sawmgiat ahi.
english: The days of Isaac were one hundred eighty years.

paite: Isak in akha akhahta a, upapi tekkun a dam in asi a, huan achipihte kiang ah pi in a-omta hi. Atapate Esau leh Jakob in amah avui uhi.
english: Isaac gave up the spirit and died, and was gathered to his people, old and full of days. Esau and Jacob, his sons, buried him.

paite: Huan hiaite Esau suante ahi ua (huai tuh Edom kichi ahi).
english: Now this is the history of the generations of Esau (that is, Edom).

paite: Esau in azite Kanaan gam a nungakte lak a aneih ahi: Hit mi Elon tanu Adah leh Hiv mi Zibeon tanu Anah tanu Aholibamah ahi ua;
english: Esau took his wives from the daughters of Canaan: Adah the daughter of Elon, the Hittite; and Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, the Hivite;

paite: huan Ishmael tanu, Nebajoth sanggamnu Basemath toh.
english: and Basemath, Ishmael’s daughter, sister of Nebaioth.

paite: Adah in Esau a ding in Eliphaz aneihsak a; Basemath in Reuel aneihsak hi.
english: Adah bore to Esau Eliphaz. Basemath bore Reuel.

paite: Aholibamah in Jeush, Jaalam leh Korah anei a; hiaite Esau tapate, Kanaan gam a aneihte ahi uh.
english: Oholibamah bore Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. These are the sons of Esau, who were born to him in the land of Canaan.

paite: Esau in azite, atapate, atanute, a-inn a mi tengteng, agante tengteng, asa tengteng leh athil neih tengteng, Kanaan gam a amuhte apaipih a, anau Jakob kiang a kipan gamdang ah apaimangta hi.
english: Esau took his wives, his sons, his daughters, and all the members of his household, with his livestock, all his animals, and all his possessions, which he had gathered in the land of Canaan, and went into a land away from his brother Jacob.

paite: Athil neihte uh athupi lua a, a-omkhawm thei kei uhi. Agante uh ziak in mikhual a a-omna gam un achinta kei hi.
english: For their substance was too great for them to dwell together, and the land of their travels couldn’t bear them because of their livestock.

paite: Seir tang ah Esau atengta hi: Esau ahihleh Edom ahi.
english: Esau lived in the hill country of Seir. Esau is Edom.

paite: Hiaite Seir tang a Edomte suangpa Esau suante ahi uh.
english: This is the history of the generations of Esau the father of the Edomites in the hill country of Seir:

paite: Hiai Esau tapate minte ahi: Esau zi Adah tapa Eliphaz; Esau zi Basemath tapa Reuel.
english: these are the names of Esau’s sons: Eliphaz, the son of Adah, the wife of Esau; and Reuel, the son of Basemath, the wife of Esau.

paite: Eliphaz tapate: Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam leh Kenaz ahi uh.
english: The sons of Eliphaz were Teman, Omar, Zepho, and Gatam, and Kenaz.

paite: Timna ahihleh Esau tapa Eliphaz mei ahi a; ama'n Amalek, Eliphaz aneihsak hi. Hiaite Esau zi Adah suante ahi uh.
english: Timna was concubine to Eliphaz, Esau’s son; and she bore to Eliphaz Amalek. These are the descendants of Adah, Esau’s wife.

paite: Hiaite Reuel tapate ahi uh: Nahath leh Zerah, Shammah leh Mizzah. Hiaite Esau zi Basemath suante ahi uh.
english: These are the sons of Reuel: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah. These were the descendants of Basemath, Esau’s wife.

paite: Hiaite Zibeon tanu Anah tanu Esau zi Aholibamah tapate ahi uh: Ama'n Esau Jeush, Jaalam leh Korah aneihsak hi.
english: These were the sons of Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah, the daughter of Zibeon, Esau’s wife: she bore to Esau Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.

paite: 15 Hiaite Esau tapate lak a hausa makaite ahi uh: Esau ta masapen Eliphaz tapate: hausa makai Teman, hausa makai Omar, hausa makai Zepho, hausa makai Kenaz,
english: These are the chiefs of the sons of Esau: the sons of Eliphaz the firstborn of Esau: chief Teman, chief Omar, chief Zepho, chief Kenaz,

paite: hausa makai Korah, hausa makai Gatam leh hausa makai Amalek. Hiaite Edom gam a Eliphaz a kipan pawt hausa makaite ahi ua, hiaite Adah suante ahi uh.
english: chief Korah, chief Gatam, chief Amalek. These are the chiefs who came of Eliphaz in the land of Edom. These are the sons of Adah.

paite: Hiaite Esau tapa Reuel suante ahi ua: Hausa makai Nahath, hausa makai Zerah, hausa makai Shammah leh hausa makai Mizzah. Hiaite Edom gam a Reuel a kipan a pawt hausa makaite ahi ua; Esau zi Basemath suante ahi uh.
english: These are the sons of Reuel, Esau’s son: chief Nahath, chief Zerah, chief Shammah, chief Mizzah. These are the chiefs who came of Reuel in the land of Edom. These are the sons of Basemath, Esau’s wife.

paite: Hiaite Esau zi Aholibamah suante ahi ua: Hausa makai Jeush, hausa makai Jaalam leh hausa makai Korah. Huaite hausa makai Anah tanu Esau zi Aholibamah suante ahi uh.
english: These are the sons of Oholibamah, Esau’s wife: chief Jeush, chief Jalam, chief Korah. These are the chiefs who came of Oholibamah the daughter of Anah, Esau’s wife.

paite: Huaite Edom leng kichi Esau tapate ahi ua; hiaite ahausa makaite ahi uh.
english: These are the sons of Esau (that is, Edom), and these are their chiefs.

paite: Hiaite Hor mi Seir tapa gam luahte ahi uh: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,
english: These are the sons of Seir the Horite, the inhabitants of the land: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah,

paite: Dishon, Ezer leh Dishan. Huaite Edom gam a Seir tapa Horte hausa makaite ahi uh.
english: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These are the chiefs who came of the Horites, the children of Seir in the land of Edom.

paite: Lotan tapate Hor leh Hemam ahi ua; Lotan sanggamnu Timna ahi.
english: The children of Lotan were Hori and Heman. Lotan’s sister was Timna.

paite: Hiaite Shobal tapate ahi uh: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho leh Onam.
english: These are the children of Shobal: Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.

paite: Hiaite Zibeon tapate ahi uh: Aiah leh Anah. Hiai Anah, apa Zibeon sabiltungte akhah lai a gamdai a tuisa khukte mukhepa ahi.
english: These are the children of Zibeon: Aiah and Anah. This is Anah who found the hot springs in the wilderness, as he fed the donkeys of Zibeon his father.

paite: Hiaite Anah tate ahi uh: Dishon leh Anah tanu Aholibamah.
english: These are the children of Anah: Dishon and Oholibamah, the daughter of Anah.

paite: Hiaite Dishon tapate ahi uh: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran leh Cheran.
english: These are the children of Dishon: Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.

paite: Hiaite Ezer tapate ahi uh: Bilhan, Zaavan leh Akan.
english: These are the children of Ezer: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.

paite: Hiaite Dishan tapate ahi uh: Uz leh Aran.
english: These are the children of Dishan: Uz and Aran.

paite: Hiaite Horte hausa makaite ahi uh: Hausa makai Lotan, hausa makai Shobal, hausa makai Zibeon leh hausa makai Anah,
english: These are the chiefs who came of the Horites: chief Lotan, chief Shobal, chief Zibeon, chief Anah,

paite: hausa makai Dishon, hausa makai Ezer leh hausa makai Dishan. Hiaite Seir gam a hausa makai ahihdan bang a Horte hausa makaite ahi uh.
english: chief Dishon, chief Ezer, and chief Dishan. These are the chiefs who came of the Horites, according to their chiefs in the land of Seir.

paite: Hiaite kumpipa kuamah in Israel suante tung a vai ahawm ma ua, Edom gam a vaihawm kumpite ahi uh.
english: These are the kings who reigned in the land of Edom, before any king reigned over the children of Israel.

paite: Beor tapa Bela in Edom gam ah vai ahawm a, akhopi min Dinhabah ahi.
english: Bela, the son of Beor, reigned in Edom. The name of his city was Dinhabah.

paite: Bela asi a, Bozrah mi Zerah tapa Jobab in asik in vai ahawm hi.
english: Bela died, and Jobab, the son of Zerah of Bozrah, reigned in his place.

paite: Jobab asi a, Temante gam a mi Husham in asik in vai ahawm hi.
english: Jobab died, and Husham of the land of the Temanites reigned in his place.

paite: Husham asi a, Bedad tapa Hadad, Moab loubuk a Midiante thatpa'n asik in vai ahawm a, akhopi min Avith ahi.
english: Husham died, and Hadad, the son of Bedad, who struck Midian in the field of Moab, reigned in his place. The name of his city was Avith.

paite: Hadad asi a, Masrekah mi Samlah in asik in vai ahawm hi.
english: Hadad died, and Samlah of Masrekah reigned in his place.

paite: Samlah asi a, Luipi gei a Rehoboth mi Saul in asik in vai ahawm hi.
english: Samlah died, and Shaul of Rehoboth by the river, reigned in his place.

paite: Saul asi a, Akbor tapa Baal-hanan in asik in vai ahawm hi.
english: Shaul died, and Baal Hanan the son of Achbor reigned in his place.

paite: Akbor tapa Bal-hanan asi a, Hadar in asik in vai ahawm a, akhopi min Pau ahi. Azi min Mehetabel ahi a, amah Mezahab tanu Matred tanu ahi.
english: Baal Hanan the son of Achbor died, and Hadar reigned in his place. The name of his city was Pau. His wife’s name was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred, the daughter of Mezahab.

paite: Hiaite a-inkuan uh dungzui zel leh amun dungzui zel uh leh amin dungzui zel ua Esau suan hausa makaite min ahi. Hausa makai Timnah, hausa makai Alvah leh hausa makai Jetheth,
english: These are the names of the chiefs who came from Esau, according to their families, after their places, and by their names: chief Timna, chief Alvah, chief Jetheth,

paite: hausa makai Aholibamah, hausa makai Elah, hausa makai Pinon,
english: chief Oholibamah, chief Elah, chief Pinon,

paite: hausa makai Kenaz, hausa makai Teman, hausa makai Mibzar,
english: chief Kenaz, chief Teman, chief Mibzar,

paite: hausa makai Magdiel leh hausa makai Iram. Hiaite agam neih uah a-omna uh dungzui zel in Edom suan hausa makaite ahi uh, amah Edomte pa Esau ahi.
english: chief Magdiel, and chief Iram. These are the chiefs of Edom, according to their habitations in the land of their possession. This is Esau, the father of the Edomites.

paite: Apa mikhual a a-omna gam Kanaan ah Jakob ateng hi.
english: Jacob lived in the land of his father’s travels, in the land of Canaan.

paite: Hiaite Jakob suante ahi uh. Joseph, kum sawm-le-sagih a upa ahih in, asanggamte toh ganhon akhah uhi. Amah naupang ahi lai a, apa' zite Bilhah leh Zilpah tapate kiang ah a-om a; Joseph in agitlouhna thu uh apa uh kiang ah atun hi.
english: This is the history of the generations of Jacob. Joseph, being seventeen years old, was feeding the flock with his brothers. He was a boy with the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah, his father’s wives. Joseph brought an evil report of them to their father.

paite: Israel in Joseph, atek lam ta ahih ziak in atapate tengteng sang in a-itzaw a; puanaktual ze tuamtuam a gial abawlsak hi.
english: Now Israel loved Joseph more than all his children, because he was the son of his old age, and he made him a tunic of many colors.

paite: Apa un asanggamte tengteng sang in amah a-itzaw chih asanggamte'n athei uhi; amah amudah ua, kampha himhim in ahoupih thei kei uhi.
english: His brothers saw that their father loved him more than all his brothers, and they hated him, and couldn’t speak peaceably to him.

paite: Joseph in mang anei a, asanggamte ahilh a, amah amudah semsem uhi.
english: Joseph dreamed a dream, and he told it to his brothers, and they hated him all the more.

paite: Ama'n akiang uah, “Hehpih in ka mang ngai dih uh.
english: He said to them, “Please hear this dream which I have dreamed:

paite: Ngai un, lou ah buhphalte i na gak ua, ngai dih uh, kei buhphal athoutou a, adingh nemnom hi. Ngai un, nou buhphalte'n ahong um ua, kei buhphal ma ah akun chiat uh," achi hi.
english: for behold, we were binding sheaves in the field, and behold, my sheaf arose and also stood upright; and behold, your sheaves came around, and bowed down to my sheaf.”

paite: Asanggamte'n akiang ah, "Nang sop lai in ka tung uah vai na hawm mahmah ding maw? Nang sop lai in ka tung uah thu na nei mahmah ding maw?" achi uh. Huchi in amang ziak in amah amudah semsem uhi.
english: His brothers asked him, “Will you indeed reign over us? Will you indeed have dominion over us?” They hated him all the more for his dreams and for his words.

paite: Mang dang anei nawn a, asanggamte ahilh nawn hi, "Ngai un, mang ka nei nawn hi. Ni, kha leh aksi sawm-le-khatte ka mai ah akun uhi," achi hi.
english: He dreamed yet another dream, and told it to his brothers, and said, “Behold, I have dreamed yet another dream: and behold, the sun and the moon and eleven stars bowed down to me.”

paite: Apa leh asanggamte ahilh hi. Apa'n atai a, akiang ah, "Mang na neih bangchi mang ahia? Kei leh na nu leh na sanggamte lei si in na mai ah ka kun taktak ding uh maw?" achi hi.
english: He told it to his father and to his brothers. His father rebuked him, and said to him, “What is this dream that you have dreamed? Will I and your mother and your brothers indeed come to bow ourselves down to the earth before you?”

paite: Asanggamte'n amah ahaza ua, apa'n bel athugen alungsim in apai nilouh hi.
english: His brothers envied him, but his father kept this saying in mind.

paite: Asanggamte Shekem ah apa uh ganhon khah in ahoh uhi.
english: His brothers went to feed their father’s flock in Shechem.

paite: Israel in Joseph kiang ah, "Na sanggamte'n Shekem ah ahi maw ganhon akhah uh? Hong pai dih, akiang uah ka hon sawl ding," achi hi. Huan ama'n, "Hiai ah ka om," achi hi.
english: Israel said to Joseph, “Aren’t your brothers feeding the flock in Shechem? Come, and I will send you to them.” He said to him, “Here I am.”

paite: Ama'n akiang ah, "Na sanggamte adamdam na uhiam, ganhon leng adamdam na hiam va en inla, atanchin uh hong hilh nawn in," achi hi. Hebron Phaizang a kipan asawlkhia a, Shekem ava pha hi.
english: He said to him, “Go now, see whether it is well with your brothers, and well with the flock; and bring me word again.” So he sent him out of the valley of Hebron, and he came to Shechem.

paite: Mi kuahiam in amah gamlak a vakvak amu hi. Huai mi'n, "Bang zong na hia?" chi in adong hi.
english: A certain man found him, and behold, he was wandering in the field. The man asked him, “What are you looking for?”

paite: Ama'n, "Ka sanggamte zong ka hi. Hehpih in ganhon akhahna uh hon hilh ve," achi hi.
english: He said, “I am looking for my brothers. Tell me, please, where they are feeding the flock.”

paite: Huai mi'n, “Hiai a kipan pawt hi ve un, Dothan ah i hoh ding uh, achih uh ka za,” achi hi. Joseph in asanggamte adelhzui a, Dothan ah ava mu hi.
english: The man said, “They have left here, for I heard them say, ‘Let’s go to Dothan.’” Joseph went after his brothers, and found them in Dothan.

paite: Amau gamlapi a kipan ana galmuh ua, akiangnai uh atun ma in, amah thah ana sawm khin uhi.
english: They saw him afar off, and before he came near to them, they conspired against him to kill him.

paite: Amau, "En un, hiai ah mang neipa ahong pai.
english: They said to one another, “Behold, this dreamer comes.

paite: Hong un, i that ding ua, kokhuk khat ah i khe ding uh. Gamsa gilou in ane, chi na ni. Amangte bangchibang in a-om a, chih i thei mai ding uh," akichi uhi.
english: Come now therefore, and let’s kill him, and cast him into one of the pits, and we will say, ‘An evil animal has devoured him.’ We will see what will become of his dreams.”

paite: Reuben in huai ana za a, akhut ua pan ahunkheta hi. "Thah zaw i that hial kei ding uh," achi hi.
english: Reuben heard it, and delivered him out of their hand, and said, “Let’s not take his life.”

paite: Reuben mah in apa uh kiang a, apitheihna ding a, akhut ua pan ahotkhiak theihna ding in, akiang uah, "Sisan zaw suah kei un, gamdai ah kokhuk ah khia un, atung ah khut kha kei un," achi hi.
english: Reuben said to them, “Shed no blood. Throw him into this pit that is in the wilderness, but lay no hand on him”—that he might deliver him out of their hand, to restore him to his father.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, Joseph asanggamte kiang atun in, Joseph puanaktual ze tuamtuam a gial asilh, ana suahsak uhi.
english: When Joseph came to his brothers, they stripped Joseph of his tunic, the tunic of many colors that was on him;

paite: Amah api ua, kokhuk ah akheta uhi. Huai kokhuk avuak ahi a, tui om louhna ahi.
english: and they took him, and threw him into the pit. The pit was empty. There was no water in it.

paite: An ne ding in atu chiat ua, adak ua, a-en ua, ngai in, Gilead gam a kipan Ishmael khualzin mite, asangawngsau ua thil gimnamtui, singnai damdawi leh murrah pua in Aigupta gam a paisuk dingte ahong pai uhi.
english: They sat down to eat bread, and they lifted up their eyes and looked, and saw a caravan of Ishmaelites coming from Gilead, with their camels bearing spices and balm and myrrh, going to carry it down to Egypt.

paite: Judah in asanggamte kiang ah, "I naupa uh i thah ua, asisan suak i iim un bang phattuamna om ding ahia?
english: Judah said to his brothers, “What profit is it if we kill our brother and conceal his blood?

paite: Hong un, atung a khut kha lou in, Ishmaelte kiang ah i zuak zaw ding uh; amah lah i sanggam uh, i sa ngeingei uh ahi ngal a," achi hi. Huchi in asanggamte'n athu azuita uhi.
english: Come, and let’s sell him to the Ishmaelites, and not let our hand be on him; for he is our brother, our flesh.” His brothers listened to him.

paite: Midian sumsin mite ahong pai ua; kokhuk a kipan Joseph akaikhia ua, Ishmaelte kiang ah dangka sawmnih in Joseph akhawngta uhi. Amau Aigupta gam ah Joseph api uhi.
english: Midianites who were merchants passed by, and they drew and lifted up Joseph out of the pit, and sold Joseph to the Ishmaelites for twenty pieces of silver. The merchants brought Joseph into Egypt.
