paite: Kokhuk ah Reuben ahong pai nawn a, ngai in, kokhuk ah Joseph ana omta kei a; apuansilhte abotkek hi.
english: Reuben returned to the pit, and saw that Joseph wasn’t in the pit; and he tore his clothes.

paite: Asanggamte kiang ah ahong kik nawn a, "I naupa uh a-om nawn kei. Kei koi a paita ding ka hia oi?" achi hi.
english: He returned to his brothers, and said, “The child is no more; and I, where will I go?”

paite: Joseph puanaktual ala ua, kelnou agou ua, asi ah apuanaktual adiah uhi.
english: They took Joseph’s tunic, and killed a male goat, and dipped the tunic in the blood.

paite: Huai puanaktual ze tuamtuam a gial akhak ua, apa uh kiang ah ahon la ua, "Hiai lel ka mu ua, na tapa puanaktual ahi hia, hilou, en mah dih," achi uh.
english: They took the tunic of many colors, and they brought it to their father, and said, “We have found this. Examine it, now, and see if it is your son’s tunic or not.”

paite: Ama'n ana thei pah a, "Ka tapa puanaktual ahi ve. Gamsa gilou in ne ahi ve. Joseph bohnen vek a om hi mahmah ding ahi ve," achi hi.
english: He recognized it, and said, “It is my son’s tunic. An evil animal has devoured him. Joseph is without doubt torn in pieces.”

paite: Jakob in apuansilhte abotkek a, sai-ip puan ateng a, ni tamtak atapa asuun hi.
english: Jacob tore his clothes, and put sackcloth on his waist, and mourned for his son many days.

paite: Atapa tengteng leh atanu tengteng amah lungmuan ding in athou ua; himahleh amah lungmuan a-ut kei, "Suun kawm in han ah ka tapa kiang ah ka paisuk ding," achi hi. Amah ngai in apa akap hi.
english: All his sons and all his daughters rose up to comfort him, but he refused to be comforted. He said, “For I will go down to Sheol to my son, mourning.” His father wept for him.

paite: Midiante'n Aigupta gam ah Joseph alutpih ua, Pharaoh nuai a heutu khat, vengmi pawl heutu Potiphar kiang ah azuak uhi.
english: The Midianites sold him into Egypt to Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh’s, the captain of the guard.

paite: Huai lai in hichi ahong hi a, asanggamte kiang a kipan Judah apaisuk a, Adullam mi khat amin Hirah ava bel hi.
english: At that time, Judah went down from his brothers, and visited a certain Adullamite, whose name was Hirah.

paite: Judah in huai ah Kanaan mi khat tanu amin Shuah amu a; akitenpih a, akithuahpih hi.
english: There, Judah saw the daughter of a certain Canaanite man named Shua. He took her, and went in to her.

paite: Huchi in agai a, tapa anei a; Judah in amin Er asa hi.
english: She conceived, and bore a son; and he named him Er.

paite: Agai nawn a, tapa anei nawn a; anu'n amin Onan asa hi.
english: She conceived again, and bore a son; and she named him Onan.

paite: Tapa anei nawn a, amin Shelah asa a; amah aneih lai in Kezib ah Judah a-om hi.
english: She yet again bore a son, and named him Shelah. He was at Chezib when she bore him.

paite: Judah in ata masa Er a ding in zi apisak a, amin Tamar ahi.
english: Judah took a wife for Er, his firstborn, and her name was Tamar.

paite: TOUPA mitmuh in Judah ta masa Er agilou a; TOUPA'N amah athat hi.
english: Er, Judah’s firstborn, was wicked in Yahweh’s sight. So Yahweh killed him.

paite: Judah in Onan kiang ah, "Na upa zi kitenpih inla kithuahpih in, na upa a ding in chi suahsak in," achi hi.
english: Judah said to Onan, “Go in to your brother’s wife, and perform the duty of a husband’s brother to her, and raise up offspring for your brother.”

paite: Onan in chisuah ding pen ama suan ahi kei ding chih athei hi. Huan hichi ahong hi a, a-upa zi akithuahpih teng in a-upa a ding a chi asuahsaklouhna ding in lei ah achi akesak zel hi.
english: Onan knew that the offspring wouldn’t be his; and when he went in to his brother’s wife, he spilled his semen on the ground, lest he should give offspring to his brother.

paite: Athilhih in TOUPA alungkimsak kei a, huaiziak in amah leng TOUPA'N athat hi.
english: The thing which he did was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and he killed him also.

paite: Judah in amounu Tamar kiang ah, "Ka tapa Shelah apichin mateng na pa inn ah meithai in va om tadih phot in. Huchi lou in zaw amah leng asanggamte bang in asi kha ding,” achi hi. Huchi in Tamar apai a, apa inn ah ava omta hi.
english: Then Judah said to Tamar, his daughter-in-law, “Remain a widow in your father’s house, until Shelah, my son, is grown up;” for he said, “Lest he also die, like his brothers.” Tamar went and lived in her father’s house.

paite: Anung in Shuah tanu Judah zi asi a; Judah ahong khamuantak in, Timnah ah abelam mulmette kiang ah alawm Adullam mi Hirah toh ahohtou uhi.
english: After many days, Shua’s daughter, the wife of Judah, died. Judah was comforted, and went up to his sheep shearers to Timnah, he and his friend Hirah, the Adullamite.

paite: Mi'n Tamar, "Na pasal pa, abelam mul met ding in Timnah ah ahohtou," chi in ahilh uhi.
english: Tamar was told, “Behold, your father-in-law is going up to Timnah to shear his sheep.”

paite: Apasal suunna puansilhte asuah a, kikhuhna puan in akikhuh a, akituam bikbek a, Enaim kulh kongpi a Timnah kho lampi ah ana tu hi. Shelah apichingta ngal a, apa'n azi ding in amah apisak kei, chih athei hi.
english: She took off the garments of her widowhood, and covered herself with her veil, and wrapped herself, and sat in the gate of Enaim, which is on the way to Timnah; for she saw that Shelah was grown up, and she wasn’t given to him as a wife.

paite: Judah in amah amuh in kizuak hi in teh achi a; amai lah akikhuh bikbek ngal a.
english: When Judah saw her, he thought that she was a prostitute, for she had covered her face.

paite: Lampi gei a om huai numei ava zuan a, "Kisa in, hehpih in i lumkhawm ding," achi hi (amou mah ahi chih lah athei ngal kei a). Ama'n, "Hon kithuahpih leng bang na hon pe dia?" achi hi.
english: He turned to her by the way, and said, “Please come, let me come in to you,” for he didn’t know that she was his daughter-in-law. She said, “What will you give me, that you may come in to me?”

paite: Ama'n, "Ganhon lak a kipan kelnou ka hon khak ding,” achi hi. Ama'n, "Huai na hon khak ma in kichiamna bang na hon pe dia?” achi hi.
english: He said, “I will send you a young goat from the flock.” She said, “Will you give me a pledge, until you send it?”

paite: Ama'n, "Kichiamna bang ka hon pe dia?” achi hi. Ama'n, "Na minsawnna leh na taute leh na chiangkhun," achi hi. Huchi in hiaite apia a, akithuahpih a, amah a kipan nau apaita hi.
english: He said, “What pledge will I give you?” She said, “Your signet and your cord, and your staff that is in your hand.” He gave them to her, and came in to her, and she conceived by him.

paite: Athou a, akikhuhna puan asuah a, ameithai puansilhte asilh nawnta hi.
english: She arose, and went away, and put off her veil from her, and put on the garments of her widowhood.

paite: Judah in akichiamna numei khut a kipan la ding in alawmpa Adullam mi khut ah kelnou akhak a, himahleh ama'n huai numei ava muzouta kei hi.
english: Judah sent the young goat by the hand of his friend, the Adullamite, to receive the pledge from the woman’s hand, but he didn’t find her.

paite: Huchi in numei omna mun a mite kiang ah, "Lampi gei a Enaim a kizuaknu koi a omta ahia?" chi in adong hi. Amau, “Hiai ah kizuak om kei," achi uhi.
english: Then he asked the men of her place, saying, “Where is the prostitute, that was at Enaim by the road?” They said, “There has been no prostitute here.”

paite: Huchi in Judah kiang ah akik nawn a, "Amah ka muzou kei. Amun a mite'n leng kizuak mawngmawng hiai ah a-om kei ana chi uh,” achi hi.
english: He returned to Judah, and said, “I haven’t found her; and also the men of the place said, ‘There has been no prostitute here.’”

paite: Judah in, "Ama'n nei den mai hen, huchi lou in zaw i zahlak kha ding. Ngai in, hiai kelnou khak ing a, amah lah muzou lou chin a,” achi hi.
english: Judah said, “Let her keep it, lest we be shamed. Behold, I sent this young goat, and you haven’t found her.”

paite: Kha thum vel nung in mi'n, "Judah, na mounu, Tamar kizuak ve aw; huai lou leng, ngai in, sawn apai hi," chi in ahilh uhi. Judah in, “Pikhia hen, unla, hallup in om hen,” achi hi.
english: About three months later, Judah was told, “Tamar, your daughter-in-law, has played the prostitute. Moreover, behold, she is with child by prostitution.” Judah said, “Bring her out, and let her be burned.”

paite: Apikhiak uleh, Tamar in, “Hiai thilte neipa a kipan ahi nau ka pai," chi in apasal pa kiang ah mi asawl hi. Amah mah in, "Hehpih in hiai minsawnna, taute leh chiangkhun, kua a ahia, ana enchian ding in ka hon ngen," achi hi.
english: When she was brought out, she sent to her father-in-law, saying, “I am with child by the man who owns these.” She also said, “Please discern whose these are—the signet, and the cords, and the staff.”

paite: Judah in huai thilte amah a ahi, chih ana thei hi. "Kei sang a amah diktatzaw ahi. Ka tapa Shelah lah amah toh ka na kitengsakta kei a," achi hi. Huchi in Judah in amah akithuahpih nawn het kei hi.
english: Judah acknowledged them, and said, “She is more righteous than I, because I didn’t give her to Shelah, my son.” He knew her again no more.

paite: Huan anau suah hun ahong tun in hichi ahong hi a, ngai in, asul ah phik ana om uhi.
english: In the time of her travail, behold, twins were in her womb.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, nau avei lai in khat in akhut ahon golhkhia a; naudommi in, “Hiai pen apawt masazaw ahi," chi in ana len a, akhut ah khau san abunsak hi.
english: When she travailed, one put out a hand, and the midwife took and tied a scarlet thread on his hand, saying, “This came out first.”

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, akhut alakkik toh kiton in, ngai in, asanggampa ahong suakkhia hi. Naudommi in, "Bangchidan a nang hon phusuak mawk na hia? Nang amoh khu in," achi hi. Huaiziak in amin Perez asa uhi.
english: As he drew back his hand, behold, his brother came out, and she said, “Why have you made a breach for yourself?” Therefore his name was called Perez.

paite: Huai nung in asanggampa, akhut a khau san bun pen ahong pawt nawn a, amin Zerah asa uhi.
english: Afterward his brother came out, who had the scarlet thread on his hand, and his name was called Zerah.

paite: Huan Aigupta gam ah Joseph apisuk ua; Pharaoh nuai a heutu khat, vengtu pawl heutu, Aigupta mi, Potiphar in ahon pisuk Ishmaelte khut a kipan aleita hi.
english: Joseph was brought down to Egypt. Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh’s, the captain of the guard, an Egyptian, bought him from the hand of the Ishmaelites that had brought him down there.

paite: Joseph kiang ah TOUPA a-om a, amah mi lohchingtak ahi a; apu Aigupta mi inn ah a-om hi.
english: Yahweh was with Joseph, and he was a prosperous man. He was in the house of his master the Egyptian.

paite: Apu in, TOUPA akiang ah a-om a, athilhih peuhmah TOUPA'N akhut ah alohchingsak chih athei hi.
english: His master saw that Yahweh was with him, and that Yahweh made all that he did prosper in his hand.

paite: Huchi in Joseph in apu mitmuh in deihsakna atang a, a-inn ah nna asem zel hi. Ama'n a-inkuante tung ah heutu in abawl a, aneih tengteng akhut ah akoih vek hi.
english: Joseph found favor in his sight. He ministered to him, and Potiphar made him overseer over his house, and all that he had he put into his hand.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, a-inn leh aneih tengteng tung a heutu ding a abawl nungsiah Joseph ziak in TOUPA'N Aigupta mi insung avualzawlta hi. Inn lam leh gam lam a aneih tengteng ah TOUPA'N avualzawl hi.
english: From the time that he made him overseer in his house, and over all that he had, Yahweh blessed the Egyptian’s house for Joseph’s sake. Yahweh’s blessing was on all that he had, in the house and in the field.

paite: Huchi in aneih tengteng Joseph khut ah akoih a, aneih teng, a-an nek kia lou ngal bangmah atheihpih kei hi. Joseph pianhoih leh melhoihtak ahi.
english: He left all that he had in Joseph’s hand. He didn’t concern himself with anything, except for the food which he ate. Joseph was well-built and handsome.

paite: Huai nung in hichi ahong hi a, apu zi in Joseph angaih et a, "Hon kithuahpih in," achi hi.
english: After these things, his master’s wife set her eyes on Joseph; and she said, “Lie with me.”

paite: Himahleh a-ut kei a, apu zi kiang ah, "Ka pu in hiai inn ah ka kiang ah bangbang a-om a chih lah athei ngal kei a, aneih tengteng ka khut ah akoih vek hi.
english: But he refused, and said to his master’s wife, “Behold, my master doesn’t know what is with me in the house, and he has put all that he has into my hand.

paite: Hiai insung ah kei sang a lianzaw kuamah a-om kei. Azi na hih ziak in nang kia lou ngal, kei a kipan bangmah it anei kei hi. Bangchi in hiai khelhna khawktak hih in Pathian tung ah thil ka hihkhial thei dia?" achi hi.
english: No one is greater in this house than I am, and he has not kept back anything from me but you, because you are his wife. How then can I do this great wickedness, and sin against God?”

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, niteng in Joseph houpih zel mahleh amah kithuahpih lam thu hiam, ama kiang a om lam thu hiam alimsak nuam kei hi.
english: As she spoke to Joseph day by day, he didn’t listen to her, to lie by her, or to be with her.

paite: Huchih lai in hichi ahong hi a, a-nna sem ding in insung ah ava lut a; insung ah mi himhim kuamah a-om kei hi.
english: About this time, he went into the house to do his work, and there were none of the men of the house inside.

paite: Huchi in ama'n, "Hon kithuahpih in," chi in apuansilh ah ana man a, ama'n apuansilh akhut a nusia in ataikhia hi.
english: She caught him by his garment, saying, “Lie with me!” He left his garment in her hand, and ran outside.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, apuansilh akhut a nusia in ataikhia, chih atheihtak in,
english: When she saw that he had left his garment in her hand, and had run outside,

paite: A-inn a mite asam a, akiang uah, "En un, hon zahlaksak ding in Hebru mi khat i kiang ua hon pi ahita ve. Hon kithuahpih tum in ka kiang ah ahong lut a, huchi in ngaihtak in ka kikouta hi.
english: she called to the men of her house, and spoke to them, saying, “Behold, he has brought a Hebrew in to us to mock us. He came in to me to lie with me, and I cried with a loud voice.

paite: Huan hichi ahi a, aw suah a ngaihtak a ka kikou azaktak in hiai ka kiang ah apuansilh anusia a, ataikheta,” achi hi.
english: When he heard that I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garment by me, and ran outside.”

paite: Joseph pu ahong tun masiah apuansilh akiang ah ana koih gige hi.
english: She laid up his garment by her, until his master came home.

paite: Akiang ah hiai thu ana gen a, "Hebru sikha i kiang a na hon pi in hon zahlaksak tum in ka kiang ah ahong lut hi.
english: She spoke to him according to these words, saying, “The Hebrew servant, whom you have brought to us, came in to me to mock me,

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, aw suah a ka kikoutak in hiai apuansilh ka kiang a nusia in ataikheta,” achi hi.
english: and as I lifted up my voice and cried, he left his garment by me, and ran outside.”

paite: Huan hichi ahi a, Joseph pu in azi in akiang a, "Na sikha in hichi in ahon bawl," chi a, athugen azak in, ahehna asou hi.
english: When his master heard the words of his wife, which she spoke to him, saying, “This is what your servant did to me,” his wrath was kindled.

paite: Huchi in Joseph pu in amah api a, suangkul, kumpi suangkul tangte khumna mun ah akhum a; huchi in suangkul ah a-omta hi.
english: Joseph’s master took him, and put him into the prison, the place where the king’s prisoners were bound, and he was there in custody.

paite: Himahleh Joseph kiang ah TOUPA a-om a, atung ah azahngai a, suangkul vengmi mitmuh in deihsakna atang hi.
english: But Yahweh was with Joseph, and showed kindness to him, and gave him favor in the sight of the keeper of the prison.

paite: Huchi in suangkul vengmi in suangkul a tang tengteng Joseph khut ah akemsakta hi. Huchi in huai a thil kihih peuhmah ama hih ahong hita.
english: The keeper of the prison committed to Joseph’s hand all the prisoners who were in the prison. Whatever they did there, he was responsible for it.

paite: Joseph kiang ah TOUPA a-om a, athilhih peuhmah TOUPA'N alohchinsak ziak in suangkul vengmi in akhut a thil om himhim a-enta kei hi.
english: The keeper of the prison didn’t look after anything that was under his hand, because Yahweh was with him; and that which he did, Yahweh made it prosper.

paite: Huan Adam in azi Evi athei a; huchi in agai a, Kain anei a, "TOUPA panpihna in ta pasal ka neita," achi hi.
english: The man knew Eve his wife. She conceived, and gave birth to Cain, and said, “I have gotten a man with Yahweh’s help.”

paite: Asanggampa Abel ahon nei nawn hi. Abel belamchingmi ahi a, Kain bel leiletmi ahi.
english: Again she gave birth, to Cain’s brother Abel. Abel was a keeper of sheep, but Cain was a tiller of the ground.

paite: Anung in hichi ahong hi a, Kain in TOUPA kiang a lat ding in lou a piang leigahte ahon tawi hi.
english: As time passed, Cain brought an offering to Yahweh from the fruit of the ground.

paite: Abel in leng abelamhon lak a piang masapen leh athau pen ahón tawi a, TOUPA'N Abel leh athillat akipahpih hi.
english: Abel also brought some of the firstborn of his flock and of its fat. Yahweh respected Abel and his offering,

paite: Himahleh Kain leh athillat akipahpih kei. Kain aheh mahmah a, amel aliap hi.
english: but he didn’t respect Cain and his offering. Cain was very angry, and the expression on his face fell.

paite: TOUPA'N Kain kiang ah, "Bangziak a heh na hia? Bangziak a na mel liap ahia?
english: Yahweh said to Cain, “Why are you angry? Why has the expression of your face fallen?

paite: Hihhoih lechin pahtak na loh kei dia hia? Na hihhoih keileh kongkhak bul ah khelhna akual nilouh a, adeihlam nangmah ahi dia, atung ah thu na nei ding ahi," achi hi.
english: If you do well, won’t it be lifted up? If you don’t do well, sin crouches at the door. Its desire is for you, but you are to rule over it.”

paite: Kain in anau Abel ahoupih a, hichi ahong hi a, lou a a-om lai un Kain in anau Abel asual a, athatta hi.
english: Cain said to Abel, his brother, “Let’s go into the field.” While they were in the field, Cain rose up against Abel, his brother, and killed him.

paite: TOUPA'N Kain kiang ah, "Na sanggampa Abel koi a om ahia?" achi hi. Ama'n, "Ka thei kei, ka sanggampa dontu ka hi a hia?" achi hi.
english: Yahweh said to Cain, “Where is Abel, your brother?” He said, “I don’t know. Am I my brother’s keeper?”

paite: TOUPA'N, "Bang hih na tamai a? Na sanggampa' sisan aw in lei a kipan hon sam ahi.
english: Yahweh said, “What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries to me from the ground.

paite: Huaiziak in na khut a kipan na sanggampa' sisan sang ding a kam ana ka, lei a pan hamsiat na hita hi.
english: Now you are cursed because of the ground, which has opened its mouth to receive your brother’s blood from your hand.

paite: Lei na leh in leng ahoihna ahon pe nawn kei ding a, leitung ah galtai leh vakvai na hita ding," achi hi.
english: From now on, when you till the ground, it won’t yield its strength to you. You will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth.”

paite: Kain in TOUPA kiang ah, "N'on gawtna ana mahmah a, ka thuakzou kei ding.
english: Cain said to Yahweh, “My punishment is greater than I can bear.

paite: "Ngai in, tuni in leitung a kipan na hon delhkheta a, na mitmuh phak louh a sel a om ding ka hita. Lei ah taimang leh vakvai hi ding ka hita hi. Hichi ahong hi ding a, kuapeuh kei hon mu in ahon that mai ding uh," achi hi.
english: Behold, you have driven me out today from the surface of the ground. I will be hidden from your face, and I will be a fugitive and a wanderer on the earth. Whoever finds me will kill me.”

paite: TOUPA'N akiang ah, "Huchi ahihleh, Kain that kuapeuh amun sagih in atung ah phu lak ahi ding," achi hi. Huan mi amah mu kuahiam in athahlouhna ding in TOUPA'N Kain achiamtehta hi.
english: Yahweh said to him, “Therefore whoever slays Cain, vengeance will be taken on him sevenfold.” Yahweh appointed a sign for Cain, so that anyone finding him would not strike him.

paite: TOUPA kiang a kipan Kain apawt a, Eden suahlam a Nod gam ah atengta hi.
english: Cain left Yahweh’s presence, and lived in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

paite: Kain in azi athei a; huchi in agai a, Enok anei hi. Khua asat a, akho min atapa tamsak in Enok asa hi.
english: Cain knew his wife. She conceived, and gave birth to Enoch. He built a city, and named the city after the name of his son, Enoch.

paite: Enok in tapa Irad anei a; Irad in tapa Mahujael anei hi. Mahujael in tapa Methusael anei a; Methusael in tapa Lamekh anei hi.
english: Irad was born to Enoch. Irad became the father of Mehujael. Mehujael became the father of Methushael. Methushael became the father of Lamech.

paite: Lamekh in zi nih anei a; khat min Adah ahi a, akhat pen min Zillah ahi.
english: Lamech took two wives: the name of the first one was Adah, and the name of the second one was Zillah.

paite: Adah in Jabal anei a; amah puanin a om ganvulmite suangpa ahi.
english: Adah gave birth to Jabal, who was the father of those who dwell in tents and have livestock.

paite: Asanggampa' min Jubal ahi a, amah kaihging leh tamngai tummi tengteng suangpa ahi.
english: His brother’s name was Jubal, who was the father of all who handle the harp and pipe.

paite: Zillah in leng Tubal-kain, dal leh sik, tuzat-heizat chiteng sekmi anei hi. Tubal-kain sanggamnu Naamah ahi.
english: Zillah also gave birth to Tubal Cain, the forger of every cutting instrument of bronze and iron. Tubal Cain’s sister was Naamah.

paite: Lamekh in azite kiang ah, "Adah leh Zillahte aw, ka aw za unla; Lamekh zite aw, ka thugen ngaikhia un. Ahon liamsak ziak in mi khat ka that a, ahon sidupsak ziak in valnou khat ka that hi.
english: Lamech said to his wives, “Adah and Zillah, hear my voice. You wives of Lamech, listen to my speech, for I have slain a man for wounding me, a young man for bruising me.

paite: Kain' phu bawn amun sagih a lak ding ahihleh, Lamekh' phu amun sawmsagih-le-sagih a lak ahi ding,” achi hi.
english: If Cain will be avenged seven times, truly Lamech seventy-seven times.”

paite: Adam in azi athei nawn a; tapa anei nawn a; amin Seth asa hi, "Pathian in Abel sik in chisuan ding ahon sehsakta; Kain in lah amah athatta ngal a," achi hi.
english: Adam knew his wife again. She gave birth to a son, and named him Seth, saying, “for God has given me another child instead of Abel, for Cain killed him.”

paite: Seth in leng tapa anei a; amin Enosh asa hi. Huai a kipan mite'n TOUPA min alou panta uhi.
english: A son was also born to Seth, and he named him Enosh. At that time men began to call on Yahweh’s name.

paite: Huan huai thil khit in hichi ahong hi a, Aigupta kumpipa uain pepa leh atanghou bawlpa'n apu uh Aigupta kumpipa alungkimsak kei uhi.
english: After these things, the butler of the king of Egypt and his baker offended their lord, the king of Egypt.

paite: Pharaoh, asikha heutu nihte tung ah, a-uain pia heutupen tung ah leh atanghou bawl heutupen tung ah ahehta hi.
english: Pharaoh was angry with his two officers, the chief cup bearer and the chief baker.

paite: Huchi in vengmi pawl heutu inn, Joseph hen a a-omna suangkul ah, atangsakta hi.
english: He put them in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, into the prison, the place where Joseph was bound.

paite: Vengmi pawl heutu in amau Joseph akemsak a, amau a-nna asepsak ua, bang tan hiamtak atang uhi.
english: The captain of the guard assigned them to Joseph, and he took care of them. They stayed in prison many days.

paite: Suangkul a hen a om, Aigupta kumpipa uain pepa leh tanghou bawlpa'n zan khat khiakna tuam tuak mang anei uhi.
english: They both dreamed a dream, each man his dream, in one night, each man according to the interpretation of his dream, the cup bearer and the baker of the king of Egypt, who were bound in the prison.

paite: Azing in akiang uah Joseph ava lut a, amau ava mu a, ngai in, ana lungkham mahmah uhi.
english: Joseph came in to them in the morning, and saw them, and saw that they were sad.

paite: Ama'n, "Bangchi na hi ua, tuni in lungkham mel pu na tel uchia?" chi in Pharaoh sikha heutu suangkul a tangte adong hi.
english: He asked Pharaoh’s officers who were with him in custody in his master’s house, saying, “Why do you look so sad today?”

paite: Amau akiang ah, "Mang ka nei tuak ua, hon hilhchiansak thei kuamah lah a-om ngal kei a ahi," achi uh. Joseph in akiang uah, "Mang hilhchetnate Pathian a ahi kei maw? Hehpih in na mang uh hon hilh un," achi hi.
english: They said to him, “We have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it.” Joseph said to them, “Don’t interpretations belong to God? Please tell it to me.”

paite: Huchi in uain pia heutupen in amang Joseph ahilh a, akiang ah, "Ngai dih, ka mang in, ka ma ah grepgui ahong om hi.
english: The chief cup bearer told his dream to Joseph, and said to him, “In my dream, behold, a vine was in front of me,

paite: Grepgui ah kahiang thum a-om a, ahong selnou ua, ahong pak ua, apakbomte'n grep minte ahon piangsak uhi.
english: and in the vine were three branches. It was as though it budded, it blossomed, and its clusters produced ripe grapes.

paite: Huan ka khut ah Pharaoh nou ahong om a; grep gahte ka lou a, Pharaoh nou sung ah ka suk a, huai nou Pharaoh khut ah ka na pia,” achi hi.
english: Pharaoh’s cup was in my hand; and I took the grapes, and pressed them into Pharaoh’s cup, and I gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand.”

paite: Joseph in akiang ah, ahilhchetna hiai ahi: "Kahiang thumte ni thum ahi.
english: Joseph said to him, “This is its interpretation: the three branches are three days.

paite: Tu a kipan ni thum in Pharaoh in na lutang adomkang ding a, na nasep mah ahon semsak nawn ding. A-uain pepa na hih lai a, na piak ngeina bang in akhut ah Pharaoh nou na pe nawn ding.
english: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head, and restore you to your office. You will give Pharaoh’s cup into his hand, the way you did when you were his cup bearer.

paite: Himahleh na dinmun ahong hoih hun chiang in hon theigige inla, hehpih in hehpihna ka tung a langsak in, Pharaoh kiang ah ka tungtang hon gen inla, huan hiai inn a kipan hon pikhia in.
english: But remember me when it is well with you. Please show kindness to me, and make mention of me to Pharaoh, and bring me out of this house.

paite: Hebrute gam a kipan mi'n aguk a, ahon gukmang uh ka hi a; hiai gam ah leng kokhuk sung a ahon khumna ding in bangmah ka hihkhial kei," achi hi.
english: For indeed, I was stolen away out of the land of the Hebrews, and here also I have done nothing that they should put me into the dungeon.”

paite: Tanghou bawlpa'n hilhchetna ahoih chih atheih in, Joseph kiang ah, "Ke'n leng mang ka nei a, ngai in, lohbeu thum ka lu in ka na pua hi.
english: When the chief baker saw that the interpretation was good, he said to Joseph, “I also was in my dream, and behold, three baskets of white bread were on my head.

paite: Lohbeu tungnungpen ah Pharaoh an, tanghou bawlpa bawl, chi chih ana om hi. Huaite vasate'n lohbeu ka lu a ka puak a kipan ana ne souhsouh uh," achi hi.
english: In the uppermost basket there were all kinds of baked food for Pharaoh, and the birds ate them out of the basket on my head.”

paite: Joseph in adawng a, “Hiai ahilhchetna ahi: Lohbeu thum ni thum ahi.
english: Joseph answered, “This is its interpretation. The three baskets are three days.

paite: Tu a kipan ni thum in Pharaoh in na pumpi a kipan na lutang adomkang ding a, sing dawn ah akhai ding. Huchi in vasate'n na sa ane souhsouh ding uh," achi hi.
english: Within three more days, Pharaoh will lift up your head from off you, and will hang you on a tree; and the birds will eat your flesh from off you.”

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, ani thum ni, Pharaoh pian champha ni in, ama'n asikha tengteng a ding in ankuang alui hi. Asikhate lak a uain pia heutupen lutang adomkangta hi.
english: On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday, he made a feast for all his servants, and he lifted up the head of the chief cup bearer and the head of the chief baker among his servants.

paite: Uain pia heutupen uain pemi mah in apangsak nawn a; Pharaoh khut ah nou apeta hi.
english: He restored the chief cup bearer to his position again, and he gave the cup into Pharaoh’s hand;

paite: Himahleh Joseph in amau ahilhchet bangtak in, tanghou bawl heutupen akhailumta hi.
english: but he hanged the chief baker, as Joseph had interpreted to them.

paite: Himahleh, uain pia heutupen in Joseph atheigige kei a, amangngilhta hi.
english: Yet the chief cup bearer didn’t remember Joseph, but forgot him.

paite: Huan kum nih vingveng nung in hichi ahong hi a, Pharaoh in mang anei a; ngai in, lui gei ah ana dingh hi.
english: At the end of two full years, Pharaoh dreamed, and behold, he stood by the river.

paite: Ngai in, bawngpi sagih hoih taktak, thau taktak ngen tui a kipan ahong pawtkhetou ua, loupa nou lak ah ahong gamta uhi.
english: Behold, seven cattle came up out of the river. They were sleek and fat, and they fed in the marsh grass.

paite: Ngai in, bawngpi dang sagih kil theuthou, gawng gemgom ahong pawtkhe nawn ua, bawngpi dangte kiang, lui gei ah adingh uhi.
english: Behold, seven other cattle came up after them out of the river, ugly and thin, and stood by the other cattle on the brink of the river.

paite: Huan bawngpi kil theuthoute'n bawngpi hoih taktak, thau taktakte anegai maimah uhi.
english: The ugly and thin cattle ate up the seven sleek and fat cattle. So Pharaoh awoke.

paite: Huchi in Pharaoh akhanglou a, a-ihmu nawn a, mang anei nawn hi. Ngai in, buh kung khat ah avui sagih lian pipi, hoih liahluah ahong omkhia hi.
english: He slept and dreamed a second time; and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, healthy and good.

paite: Ngai in, huai nung in vui sagih ngat giuhgeuh suahlam huih in anuai eksa nung ahong omkhe nawn hi.
english: Behold, seven heads of grain, thin and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.

paite: Avui ngat giuhgeuhte'n avui sagih lian pipi, hoih liahluahte avalh khin maimah uhi. Huchi in Pharaoh akhanglou a; ngai in, mang ana hi.
english: The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven healthy and full ears. Pharaoh awoke, and behold, it was a dream.

paite: Azingsang in hichi ahong hi a, alungsim abuai mahmah a; mi asawl a, Aigupta gam a mitkhialdawi siam tengteng leh mipil tengteng asamkhawm hi. Pharaoh in amang amau ana hilh a; himahleh Pharaoh mangte hilhchian thei kuamah a-om kei uhi.
english: In the morning, his spirit was troubled, and he sent and called for all of Egypt’s magicians and wise men. Pharaoh told them his dreams, but there was no one who could interpret them to Pharaoh.

paite: Huchih lai in uain pia heutupen in Pharaoh kiang ah, "Tuni in ka hihkhelh ka theikhia hi.
english: Then the chief cup bearer spoke to Pharaoh, saying, “I remember my faults today.

paite: Khatvei asikhate tung ah Pharaoh aheh a, huchi in vengmi pawl heutu inn ah kei leh tanghou bawl heutupen ahon tangsak hi.
english: Pharaoh was angry with his servants, and put me in custody in the house of the captain of the guard, with the chief baker.

paite: Kei leh ama'n zan khat mang ka nei ua, akhiakna tuam tuak ahi ka mat uh.
english: We dreamed a dream in one night, he and I. Each man dreamed according to the interpretation of his dream.

paite: Huai ah ka kiang uah vengmi pawl heutu sikha, Hebru mi, tangval khat a-om a; amah ka hilh ua, ama'n ka mangte uh ahilhchian hi. Ka mang uh toh kituak in ahon hilhchetsak hi.
english: There was with us there a young man, a Hebrew, servant to the captain of the guard, and we told him, and he interpreted to us our dreams. He interpreted to each man according to his dream.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, kei ka nasep mah ahon semsak nawn a, amah akhailumta hi,” achi hi.
english: As he interpreted to us, so it was. He restored me to my office, and he hanged him.”

paite: Pharaoh in Joseph asamsak pah a, kintak in suangkul a kipan apikheta uhi. Amah akimet ngil a, apuansilh akhek a, Pharaoh kiang ah ava lut hi.
english: Then Pharaoh sent and called Joseph, and they brought him hastily out of the dungeon. He shaved himself, changed his clothing, and came in to Pharaoh.

paite: Pharaoh in Joseph kiang ah, "Mang ka nei a, ahilhchian thei kuamah a-om kei uh. Nang mang thu na zak chiang in na hilhchian thei chih na tungtangmi gen ka na za hi,” achi hi.
english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I have dreamed a dream, and there is no one who can interpret it. I have heard it said of you, that when you hear a dream you can interpret it.”

paite: Joseph in Pharaoh adawng a, "Huai ahihleh kei a om ahi kei hi. Pathian in lungkimhuaitak in Pharaoh adawng zaw ding," achi hi.
english: Joseph answered Pharaoh, saying, “It isn’t in me. God will give Pharaoh an answer of peace.”

paite: Pharaoh in Joseph kiang ah, "Ka mang in, ngai in, lui gei ah ka na dingh hi.
english: Pharaoh spoke to Joseph, “In my dream, behold, I stood on the brink of the river;

paite: Ngai in, bawngpi sagih hoih taktak, thau taktak ngen tui a kipan ahong pawtkhetou ua, loupa nou lak ah ahong gamta uhi.
english: and behold, seven fat and sleek cattle came up out of the river. They fed in the marsh grass;

paite: Bawngpi dang sagih gina lou leh deihhuai lou leh gawng siatsuat, huchibang tel a hoih lou Aigupta gam tengteng a leng ka muh ngei louh, anung uah ahong pawtkhetou nawn uhi.
english: and behold, seven other cattle came up after them, poor and very ugly and thin, such as I never saw in all the land of Egypt for ugliness.

paite: Bawngpi gawng siatsuat deihhuai lou pipite'n bawngpi sagih thau taktak hong pawt masate anegai maimah uhi.
english: The thin and ugly cattle ate up the first seven fat cattle;

paite: Anekgaih khit nung un leng, ane uh chih akithei tuan kei hi. Atung lai mah bang in deihhuai loutak in a-om lailai uhi. Huchi in ka khanglouta hi.
english: and when they had eaten them up, it couldn’t be known that they had eaten them, but they were still ugly, as at the beginning. So I awoke.

paite: Ka mang in, ngai in, buh kung khat ah vui sagih lian pipi, hoih pipi ahong vuikhia hi.
english: I saw in my dream, and behold, seven heads of grain came up on one stalk, full and good;

paite: Ngai in, huai nung in vui sagih vuai ningniang, neu chikchik, suahlam huih in anuai hong vuikhe nawn hi.
english: and behold, seven heads of grain, withered, thin, and blasted with the east wind, sprung up after them.

paite: Avui ngat ngiungeute'n avui sagih hoih taktakte avalh khit maimah uh ka mu hi. Mitkhialdawi siamte ka hilh a, himahleh hon hilhchian thei kuamah a-om kei uh," chi in agen hi.
english: The thin heads of grain swallowed up the seven good heads of grain. I told it to the magicians, but there was no one who could explain it to me.”

paite: Joseph in Pharaoh kiang ah, "Pharoah mang khat ahi a, Pathian in hih ding a akisak Pharaoh theisak ahi.
english: Joseph said to Pharaoh, “The dream of Pharaoh is one. What God is about to do he has declared to Pharaoh.

paite: Bawng sagih hoih taktakte kum sagih ahi ua; vui sagih hoih taktakte leng kum sagih mah ahi uh. Huai mang khat ahi.
english: The seven good cattle are seven years; and the seven good heads of grain are seven years. The dream is one.

paite: Anung ua bawng sagih tek taktak, deihhuai lou taktak hong pawtkhetoute kum sagih ahi ua, vui sagih ahawm ngen suahlam huih nuaite toh; huaite kial kum, kum sagih ding ahi.
english: The seven thin and ugly cattle that came up after them are seven years, and also the seven empty heads of grain blasted with the east wind; they will be seven years of famine.

paite: Hiai ahi Pharaoh kiang a ka gen. Pathian in hih ding a akisak Pharaoh kiang a theisak ahi.
english: That is the thing which I have spoken to Pharaoh. God has shown Pharaoh what he is about to do.

paite: Ngai in, Aigupta gamsung pumpi ah niang-le-tai a om kum, kum sagih ahong tung ding.
english: Behold, seven years of great plenty throughout all the land of Egypt are coming.

paite: Huai nung in kial kum, kum sagih ahong om nawn ding. Huchi in Aigupta gam ah niang-le-tai a omna mangngilh vek ahita ding. Kial in gam anegawp vek ding hi.
english: Seven years of famine will arise after them, and all the plenty will be forgotten in the land of Egypt. The famine will consume the land,

paite: Niang leh tai kum hon zui kial pen anasat mahmah ding ziak in mite'n hiai gam hauhsak lai hun athei nawnta kei ding uh.
english: and the plenty will not be known in the land by reason of that famine which follows; for it will be very grievous.

paite: Pharaoh mang nihvei aneih tuansakna ahihleh hiai ziak ahi. Thilhih ding Pathian in ahihkip a, Pathian in atungsak pah ding hi.
english: The dream was doubled to Pharaoh, because the thing is established by God, and God will shortly bring it to pass.

paite: "Tu in Pharaoh in mi khat, teitak leh piltak zongkhia henla, Aigupta gam tung ah heutu in omsak hen.
english: “Now therefore let Pharaoh look for a discreet and wise man, and set him over the land of Egypt.

paite: Pharaoh in hiai hih hen. Gam tung ah heutute sep henla, niang-le-tai a om kum, kum sagih sung Aigupta gam buh mun nga a khen mun khat zel kaikhawm hen.
english: Let Pharaoh do this, and let him appoint overseers over the land, and take up the fifth part of the land of Egypt’s produce in the seven plenteous years.

paite: Amau huai kum hoih kum hong tung ding a buh tengteng kaikhawm in Pharaoh nuai a om ding in khuate ah tunung a nek ding in buh sungkhawm henla, kholkhawm hen.
english: Let them gather all the food of these good years that come, and store grain under the hand of Pharaoh for food in the cities, and let them keep it.

paite: Kial ziak a gam amanlouhna ding in, buh kial kum, kum sagih Aigupta gam a hong tun hun a ding in hiai gam a ding a kiginkholhna ahi ding," achi hi.
english: The food will be to supply the land against the seven years of famine, which will be in the land of Egypt; so that the land will not perish through the famine.”

paite: Pharaoh leh asikha tengteng in hiai thusawm hoih asaklamtak uh ahi.
english: The thing was good in the eyes of Pharaoh, and in the eyes of all his servants.

paite: Pharaoh in asikhate kiang ah, "Hichibang Pathian kha omna mi i muzou ding ua hia?" achi hi.
english: Pharaoh said to his servants, “Can we find such a one as this, a man in whom is the Spirit of God?”

paite: Pharaoh mah in Joseph kiang ah, "Pathian in hiai tengteng hon theihsak ziak in, nang bang a tei leh pil himhim a-om kei uh.
english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Because God has shown you all of this, there is no one so discreet and wise as you.

paite: Nang ka inkote tung ah heutu in na om ding a, ka khua-le-tui tengteng na thu bang zel in a-om ding uh. Laltutphah a tut thu ah kia nang sang in ka lianzaw ding," achi hi.
english: You shall be over my house. All my people will be ruled according to your word. Only in the throne I will be greater than you.”

paite: Pharaoh mah in Joseph kiang ah, "En in, Aigupta gam tengteng tung ah heutu in ka hon bawl hi,” achi hi.
english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Behold, I have set you over all the land of Egypt.”

paite: Pharaoh in akhut a kipan aminsawnna zungbuh atolkhia a, Joseph khut ah abunsak a, puanmalngat a kibawl puansilhte asilhsak a, angawng ah dangka-eng khainiang a-oksak lai hi.
english: Pharaoh took off his signet ring from his hand, and put it on Joseph’s hand, and arrayed him in robes of fine linen, and put a gold chain about his neck.

paite: Akangtalai neih nihna ah atuangsak a, "Ama ah khukdin un," chi in mi akikousak hi. Huchi in Aigupta gam tengteng tung ah heutu in abawlta hi.
english: He made him ride in the second chariot which he had. They cried before him, “Bow the knee!” He set him over all the land of Egypt.

paite: Pharaoh in Joseph kiang ah, "Kei Pharaoh ka hi, na thu lou in Aigupta gamsung pumpi ah kuamah in akhut uh hiam, akhe uh hiam alik kei ding," achi hi.
english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “I am Pharaoh. Without you, no man shall lift up his hand or his foot in all the land of Egypt.”

paite: Pharaoh in Joseph min Zaphnath-Paneah asa a; azi ding in On kho siampu Potiphera tanu Asenath apia hi. Joseph apawt a, Aigupta gamsung pumpi asiksuak hi.
english: Pharaoh called Joseph’s name Zaphenath-Paneah. He gave him Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On as a wife. Joseph went out over the land of Egypt.

paite: Aigupta gam kumpipa Pharaoh ma a Joseph adin lai in kum sawmthum a upa ahi. Pharaoh a kipan Joseph apawt a, Aigupta gamsung pumpi asiksuak hi.
english: Joseph was thirty years old when he stood before Pharaoh king of Egypt. Joseph went out from the presence of Pharaoh, and went throughout all the land of Egypt.

paite: Hauh kum, kum sagih sung, lei in buh tampi atungsak hi.
english: In the seven plenteous years the earth produced abundantly.

paite: Aigupta gam ah hauh kum, kum sagih ahong tung a, buh tengteng adongkhawm a, huai buhte khuate ah asungkhawmta hi. Akim a om kho chih lou a buhte asungkhawm chiat hi.
english: He gathered up all the food of the seven years which were in the land of Egypt, and laid up the food in the cities. He stored food in each city from the fields around that city.

paite: Joseph in buh tampi, tuipi piaunel zah bang in asungkhawm venvon a, asim leng atawp hial hi; sim zoh vual louh ahih tak ziak in.
english: Joseph laid up grain as the sand of the sea, very much, until he stopped counting, for it was without number.

paite: Kial ahong tun ma in Joseph in tapa nih anei a, huaite On kho siampu Potiphera tanu Asenath in aneihsakte ahi uh.
english: To Joseph were born two sons before the year of famine came, whom Asenath, the daughter of Potiphera priest of On, bore to him.

paite: Joseph in atapa masa min Manasseh asa a, "Pathian in ka sepgimna leh ka pa insung mite tengteng ahon mangngilhsakta," achi hi.
english: Joseph called the name of the firstborn Manasseh, “For”, he said, “God has made me forget all my toil, and all my father’s house.”

paite: Atapa nihna min Ephraim asa a, “Pathian in ka gimthuakna gam ah chi ahon suangsakta,” achi hi.
english: The name of the second, he called Ephraim: “For God has made me fruitful in the land of my affliction.”

paite: Hauh kum, kum sagih Aigupta gam a hong tung abeita hi.
english: The seven years of plenty, that were in the land of Egypt, came to an end.

paite: Huan kial kum, kum sagih ding, Joseph gen bang in ahong tung panta hi. Gam chih ah kial ahong keta a; Aigupta gamsung teng ah bel nek ding a-om hi.
english: The seven years of famine began to come, just as Joseph had said. There was famine in all lands, but in all the land of Egypt there was bread.

paite: Aigupta gam a mi tengteng akialtak un, Pharaoh kiang ah nek ding ngen in akikou uhi. Pharaoh in Aigupta mite kiang ah, "Joseph kiang ah hoh unla; na kiang ua agen peuhmah hih un," achi hi.
english: When all the land of Egypt was famished, the people cried to Pharaoh for bread, and Pharaoh said to all the Egyptians, “Go to Joseph. What he says to you, do.”

paite: Leitung pumpi ah kial aketa hi. Joseph in sunkhawmna buh innte ahong a, Aigupta gam ah leng kial anak kiak mahmah hi.
english: The famine was over all the surface of the earth. Joseph opened all the store houses, and sold to the Egyptians. The famine was severe in the land of Egypt.

paite: Leitung pumpi a kial anak kiak luat ziak in gam chih a mite buh lei ding in Aigupta gam a Joseph kiang ah ahong zel uhi.
english: All countries came into Egypt, to Joseph, to buy grain, because the famine was severe in all the earth.

paite: Huan Jakob in Aigupta gam ah buh a-om chih atheihtak in, Jakob in atapate kiang ah, "Bangziak a ki-en maimah na hi ua?" achi hi.
english: Now Jacob saw that there was grain in Egypt, and Jacob said to his sons, “Why do you look at one another?”

paite: Amah mah in, "Ngai un, Aigupta gam ah buh a-om chih ka za hi. Si lou a i hinkhiak theihna ding in huai ah va hohsuk unla, huai a kipan ei a ding in buh va lei un," achi hi.
english: He said, “Behold, I have heard that there is grain in Egypt. Go down there, and buy for us from there, so that we may live, and not die.”

paite: Joseph sanggam sawmte Aigupta ah buh lei ding in ahohsuk uhi.
english: Joseph’s ten brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.

paite: Jakob in asanggamte kiang ah Joseph nau Benjamin ahohsak kei; tuahsia ava tuak kha ding, achih ziak in.
english: But Jacob didn’t send Benjamin, Joseph’s brother, with his brothers; for he said, “Lest perhaps harm happen to him.”

paite: Huchi in Israel tapate mi ava hohte lak ah buh lei ding in ahoh ua; Kanaan gam ah leng kial ake ngal a.
english: The sons of Israel came to buy among those who came, for the famine was in the land of Canaan.

paite: Aigupta gam tung a heutu Joseph ahi a; amah huai gammi tengteng kiang a buh zuakpa ahi. Joseph sanggamte ahong pai ua, lei si in amai ah akun uhi.
english: Joseph was the governor over the land. It was he who sold to all the people of the land. Joseph’s brothers came, and bowed themselves down to him with their faces to the earth.

paite: Joseph in asanggamte ana mu a, amau ana thei lai hi. Himahleh akiang uah midang bang in akibawl a, khauhtak in amaute ahoupih hi. Akiang uah, "Koi a kipan a hong na hi ua?" achi hi. Amau, “Buh lei ding a Kanaan gam a kipan hong pai ka hi uh," achi uhi.
english: Joseph saw his brothers, and he recognized them, but acted like a stranger to them, and spoke roughly with them. He said to them, “Where did you come from?” They said, “From the land of Canaan, to buy food.”

paite: Joseph in asanggamte ana thei lai a, amaute'n ahihleh amah athei kei uh.
english: Joseph recognized his brothers, but they didn’t recognize him.

paite: Joseph in amau tungtang thu, mang a amatte atheikheta hi. Akiang uah, "Enkhe mite na hi uh. Gam venlouhna munte en ding a hong kuan na hi uh," achi hi.
english: Joseph remembered the dreams which he dreamed about them, and said to them, “You are spies! You have come to see the nakedness of the land.”

paite: Amau akiang ah, "Ka toupa, hilou e, na sikhate buh lei ding a hong kuan ka hi uh.
english: They said to him, “No, my lord, but your servants have come to buy food.

paite: Mi khat ta vek ka hi ua, midiktak ka hi uh. Na sikhate enkhe mite ka hi zenzen kei uh," achi uhi.
english: We are all one man’s sons; we are honest men. Your servants are not spies.”

paite: Ama'n akiang uah, "Ka taksang kei, gam venlouhna munte en ding a hong pai himah uteh," achi hi.
english: He said to them, “No, but you have come to see the nakedness of the land!”

paite: Amau, “Kou na sikhate unau sawm-le-nih, Kanaan gam a om, mi khat tapate ka hi uh. Ngai in, ka nautumpen uh tu in ka pa uh kiang ah a-om hi. Khat pen ahihleh a-om nawnta kei,” achi uhi.
english: They said, “We, your servants, are twelve brothers, the sons of one man in the land of Canaan; and behold, the youngest is today with our father, and one is no more.”

paite: Joseph in akiang uah, "Enkhe mite na hi uh ka hon chih na hi mahmah uhi.
english: Joseph said to them, “It is like I told you, saying, ‘You are spies!’

paite: Hichibang a ettel na hi ding uh. Na nautumpen uh hiai a ahong pai keileh Pharaoh hinna a kichiam in hiai a kipan na pawtkhe kei hial ding uh, ka hon chi ahi.
english: By this you shall be tested. By the life of Pharaoh, you shall not go out from here, unless your youngest brother comes here.

paite: Nou ah thutak a-om hia, om lou chetna ding in na lak ua khat kisawl unla, na nau uh hon pi hen. Nou bel hen in na om phot ding uh. Huchi lou in zaw Pharaoh hinna lou a kichiam in, enkhe mite na hi mahmah uh ka hon chi ding," achi hi.
english: Send one of you, and let him get your brother, and you shall be bound, that your words may be tested, whether there is truth in you, or else by the life of Pharaoh surely you are spies.”

paite: Huchi in avek un ni thum atangsak chiat hi.
english: He put them all together into custody for three days.

paite: Ani thum ni in Joseph in akiang uah, "Ke'n Pathian ka lau ziak in, hichi in hih le uchin na hing ding uh.
english: Joseph said to them the third day, “Do this, and live, for I fear God.

paite: Midiktat na hih ualeh na unau lak uah khat na suangkul tanin uah hen in om hen.
english: If you are honest men, then let one of your brothers be bound in your prison; but you go, carry grain for the famine of your houses.

paite: Na nautumpen uh ka kiang ah hon pi un. Huchi in na thu uh atel ding a, na si kei ding uh," achi hi. Huan huchibang in ahihta uhi.
english: Bring your youngest brother to me; so will your words be verified, and you won’t die.” They did so.

paite: Amau, "I nau tung a i thilhih uh moh petmah i hi, hehpih ding a ahon nget ngutngut lai a, alungtang mangbatdan mu napi a, i ngaihkhiaksak nop louh uh. Huaiziak in hiai mangbatna in hon buak ahita," akichi uhi.
english: They said to one another, “We are certainly guilty concerning our brother, in that we saw the distress of his soul, when he begged us, and we wouldn’t listen. Therefore this distress has come upon us.”

paite: Reuben in, "Naupang tung ah thil hihkhial kei un, chi in na kiang uah ka gen kei maw? Na ngaikhe nuam kei ua ahi. Huaiziak in ngai un, asisan phu i tung ua lak ahita ve," chi in amau adawng hi.
english: Reuben answered them, saying, “Didn’t I tell you, saying, ‘Don’t sin against the child,’ and you wouldn’t listen? Therefore also, behold, his blood is required.”

paite: Akal ua paulet mi a-om ziak in Joseph in athugen uh athei chih athei kei uhi.
english: They didn’t know that Joseph understood them; for there was an interpreter between them.

paite: Ama'n amau alehngatsan a, akapta hi. Akiang uah ahong kik nawn a, amau ahoupih a, alak ua pan Simeon apituam a, amitmuh un ahenta hi.
english: He turned himself away from them, and wept. Then he returned to them, and spoke to them, and took Simeon from among them, and bound him before their eyes.

paite: Joseph in a-ipte uh buh a hihdim ding leh adangkate uh a-ip ua koih nawn chiat ding in leh lampi a nek ding pe ding in thu apia hi. Huchi in huchibang in ahihsakta hi.
english: Then Joseph gave a command to fill their bags with grain, and to restore each man’s money into his sack, and to give them food for the way. So it was done to them.

paite: Abuh uh asabiltungte aposak ua, huai a kipan apawtkheta uhi.
english: They loaded their donkeys with their grain, and departed from there.

paite: Alak ua mi khat in agiahbuk ua asabiltung an pe ding a a-ip ahonleh, adangka amuta hi. Ngai in, a-ipgong bul ah ana om hi.
english: As one of them opened his sack to give his donkey food in the lodging place, he saw his money. Behold, it was in the mouth of his sack.

paite: Asanggamte kiang ah, "Ka dangka na koih nawn uh hi veh e. Ngai un, ka ip sung ah ana om mawk hi," achi hi. Alunglel ua, "Pathian in hichibang a eite ahon bawl bangchidan adiam aw?" chi in ling kawm in aki-entuah uhi.
english: He said to his brothers, “My money is restored! Behold, it is in my sack!” Their hearts failed them, and they turned trembling to one another, saying, “What is this that God has done to us?”

paite: Kanaan gam a apa uh kiang ahong tung ua, atung ua thil tung tengteng ahilh uhi.
english: They came to Jacob their father, to the land of Canaan, and told him all that had happened to them, saying,

paite: "Huai mi, agam heutupa un, khauhtak in hon houpih a, enkhe mite ding in hon koih hi.
english: “The man, the lord of the land, spoke roughly with us, and took us for spies of the country.

paite: Kou akiang ah, midiktak ka hi uh. ‘Enkhe mite ka hi zenzen kei uh.'
english: We said to him, ‘We are honest men. We are no spies.

paite: Unau sawm-le-nih ka hi ua, ka pa uh tapate ka hi vek uh. Khat a-om nawn kei a, ka nautumpen uh tu in Kanaan gam ah ka pa uh kiang ah a-om," ka chi uhi.
english: We are twelve brothers, sons of our father; one is no more, and the youngest is today with our father in the land of Canaan.’

paite: Huai mi, agam heutupa un ka kiang uah, "Hichi in midiktak na hi uh chih ka hon thei ding. Na sanggampa uh khat ka kiang ah nusia unla, na inkuanpih kialte a ding in buh pua unla, paita un.
english: The man, the lord of the land, said to us, ‘By this I will know that you are honest men: leave one of your brothers with me, and take grain for the famine of your houses, and go your way.

paite: Na nautumpen uh ka kiang ah hon pi un. Huchi in enkhe mite na hi kei ua, midiktak na hi zaw uh, chih ka thei ding. Huchi in na sanggampa uh ka hon pe nawn ding a, hiai gam ah sum na sinta ding uh," ahon chi, achi uhi.
english: Bring your youngest brother to me. Then I will know that you are not spies, but that you are honest men. So I will deliver your brother to you, and you shall trade in the land.’”

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, a-ipte uh abutkhiak lai un, ngai in, a-ipsung uah adangka tun chiat uh ana om hi. Amau leh apa un adangka tunte uh amuh un alau mahmah uhi.
english: As they emptied their sacks, behold, each man’s bundle of money was in his sack. When they and their father saw their bundles of money, they were afraid.

paite: Apa uh Jakob in akiang uah, "Noute'n ka tate hon tansak na hi uh. Joseph a-om nawn kei. Simeon lah a-om nawn kei, Benjamin nangawn lah pimang na tum nawn ngal ua. Hiai thil tengteng in hon kiakkhum ahita ve," achi hi.
english: Jacob, their father, said to them, “You have bereaved me of my children! Joseph is no more, Simeon is no more, and you want to take Benjamin away. All these things are against me.”

paite: Reuben in apa kiang ah, "Na kiang a ka hon pikik nawn keileh ka tapa nihte that mai in. Amah ka khut ah hon kemsak inla, na kiang ah ka hon pikik nawn mai ding," achi hi.
english: Reuben spoke to his father, saying, “Kill my two sons, if I don’t bring him to you. Entrust him to my care, and I will bring him to you again.”

paite: Ama'n, "Ka tapa na kiang uah ahong suk kei ding. A-upa asita a, amah kia lah ahita ngal a. Na paina lam lak ah tuahsia tuak taleh ka samkangpi toh lungkhamna in han ah na tumsak ding uh," achi hi.
english: He said, “My son shall not go down with you; for his brother is dead, and he only is left. If harm happens to him along the way in which you go, then you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.”

paite: Huan gamsung ah kial anak kiak mahmah lai hi.
english: The famine was severe in the land.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, Aigupta gam a kipan a buh apuaktouh uh anekgaih nung un, apa un, akiang uah, "Kuan nawn unla buh tawmchik bek ei a ding in va lei nawn un," achi hi.
english: When they had eaten up the grain which they had brought out of Egypt, their father said to them, “Go again, buy us a little more food.”

paite: Huchi in Judah in akiang ah, "Huai mi'n, na naupa uh na hon tonpih kei uleh, ka mel na mu kei ding uh, chi in hon kalh giugeu hi.
english: Judah spoke to him, saying, “The man solemnly warned us, saying, ‘You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.’

paite: Ka naupa uh na hon zuihsak dingleh, buh ka hon va leisak ding uh.
english: If you’ll send our brother with us, we’ll go down and buy you food;

paite: N'on zuihsak nop kei dingleh zaw, ka hoh dah mai ding uh. Huai mi'n ka kiang uah, na nau uh na hon tonpih kei uleh, ka mel na mu kei ding uh, achita ngal a," chi in agen hi.
english: but if you don’t send him, we won’t go down, for the man said to us, ‘You shall not see my face, unless your brother is with you.’”

paite: Israel in, "Bangziak in ahia nau dang na neih lai tantan na hilh chitchiat uh? Kei a dia hoih lou na hih uh?" achi hi.
english: Israel said, “Why did you treat me so badly, telling the man that you had another brother?”

paite: Amau, "Huai mi'n, na pa uh dam lai hia? Unau dang na nei lai uhia? chi in i tanchin leh i tanaute tanchin ahon dong hi. Ahon thudot bang zel in ka hilh uhi. Na nau uh hon pisuk un, achi ding chih kua'n athei chitchiat dia?" achi uhi.
english: They said, “The man asked directly concerning ourselves, and concerning our relatives, saying, ‘Is your father still alive? Have you another brother?’ We just answered his questions. Is there any way we could know that he would say, ‘Bring your brother down’?”

paite: Judah in apa Israel kiang ah, "Ka naupa uh hon zuisak in. Huchi in ka kisa ding ua, ka kuan ding uh. Kou leh nang leh ka taneu chikchikte uh leng si lou a i hintheihna ding un.
english: Judah said to Israel, his father, “Send the boy with me, and we’ll get up and go, so that we may live, and not die, both we, and you, and also our little ones.

paite: Atungtang thu keimah in bultum na ning. Ka khut a kipan mahmah ah amah hon phut in. Amah na kiang a ka hon pikik nawn louh a, na ma a ka hon dinsak nawn keileh, tangtawn in amoh ka po ding hi.
english: I’ll be collateral for him. From my hand will you require him. If I don’t bring him to you, and set him before you, then let me bear the blame forever;

paite: Om sawt lou hi le ung, anihveina hong tung nawn khinta ding hi ung a,” achi hi.
english: for if we hadn’t delayed, surely we would have returned a second time by now.”

paite: Apa uh Israel in akiang uah, "Huchibang ahih vanglakleh hichi in hih un. Na seng un hiai gam a thil hoih khenkhat singnai damdawi, khuaizu, gimnamtui, murrah, theihawk leh makha gah, neukha chiat bek huai mi a ding thilpiak tawisuk un.
english: Their father, Israel, said to them, “If it must be so, then do this: Take from the choice fruits of the land in your bags, and carry down a present for the man, a little balm, a little honey, spices and myrrh, nuts, and almonds;

paite: Dangka amun nih in tawi unla, na ipgong bul ua ahon dangka piak nawn leng tawi nawn un; amuhkhelh ahi kha ding.
english: and take double money in your hand, and take back the money that was returned in the mouth of your sacks. Perhaps it was an oversight.

paite: Na naupa uh leng pi un, thou unla, huai mi kiang ah va hoh nawn un.
english: Take your brother also, get up, and return to the man.

paite: Na sanggampa uh khat pen leh Benjamin ahon khahsakna ding in Pathian Bangkim hihthei in huai mi hon zahngaisak hen. Ka tate suun ka hihleh suun ka hita mai kei dia," achi hi.
english: May God Almighty give you mercy before the man, that he may release to you your other brother and Benjamin. If I am bereaved of my children, I am bereaved.”

paite: Huchi in thilpiak atawi ua, dangka leng amun nih atawi ua, Benjamin leng api uhi. Athou ua, Aigupta gam ah ahohsuk ua, Joseph ma ah adingh nawn uhi.
english: The men took that present, and they took double money in their hand, and Benjamin; and got up, went down to Egypt, and stood before Joseph.

paite: Joseph in akiang ua Benjamin om amuhtak in, a-inkemmi kiang ah, "Huai mite insung ah pilut inla, gan gou inla, bawl in, huai mite'n sun chiang in ka kiang ah an ane ding uh," achi hi.
english: When Joseph saw Benjamin with them, he said to the steward of his house, “Bring the men into the house, and butcher an animal, and prepare; for the men will dine with me at noon.”

paite: Huchi in ama'n Joseph thupiak bang in ahihta a; Joseph inn ah apilutta hi.
english: The man did as Joseph commanded, and the man brought the men to Joseph’s house.

paite: Joseph inn a pilut a a-om ziak un alau ua, "I hoh masak lai a, i ip ua dangka hong kik nawnte ziak in ei ve ahon pilut uh. I tung ua siatna zong a, hon sual in, ei leh i sabiltungte toh sikha ding a mat hon tum ahita ve," achi uhi.
english: The men were afraid, because they were brought to Joseph’s house; and they said, “Because of the money that was returned in our sacks the first time, we’re brought in; that he may seek occasion against us, attack us, and seize us as slaves, along with our donkeys.”

paite: Joseph inkemmi kiang ah ava hoh ua, kongbul ah ahoupih uhi.
english: They came near to the steward of Joseph’s house, and they spoke to him at the door of the house,

paite: "Ka toupa aw, ka hong masak lai ua buh lei ding lel a hong suk ka hi uh.
english: and said, “Oh, my lord, we indeed came down the first time to buy food.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, giahbuk ka tun un ka ipte uh ka hong ua, ngai in, ka dangka chiat uh ka ipgong bul uah ana om hi. Ka dangka uh abuk ngeingei in ana om a, huchi in ka hon tawi uhi.
english: When we came to the lodging place, we opened our sacks, and behold, each man’s money was in the mouth of his sack, our money in full weight. We have brought it back in our hand.

paite: Buh leina ding in dangka dang ka hon tawi ua, ka dangka uh lah kua'n ahia ka ip ua koih ka thei ngal kei ua," achi uhi.
english: We have brought down other money in our hand to buy food. We don’t know who put our money in our sacks.”

paite: Ama'n, "Lungmuangtak in om unla, lau kei un. Na Pathian, na pa uh Pathian in na ipte uah gou ahon pia ahi mai ve. Na dangka uh lah ka mu ngal a," achi hi. Huchi in akiang uah Simeon hon pikhia hi.
english: He said, “Peace be to you. Don’t be afraid. Your God, and the God of your father, has given you treasure in your sacks. I received your money.” He brought Simeon out to them.

paite: Huai mi in Joseph insung ah amaute apilut a, tui apia hi. Akhe uh asil ua; asabiltungte uh leng an apia hi.
english: The man brought the men into Joseph’s house, and gave them water, and they washed their feet. He gave their donkeys fodder.

paite: Athilpiak tawi uh Joseph sun an ne ding a ahong pai ma in ana bawlkhol ua; huai ah an ane ding uh chih lah aza ngal ua.
english: They prepared the present for Joseph’s coming at noon, for they heard that they should eat bread there.

paite: Joseph a-inn a ahong paitak in, akhut ua thilpiakte, insung ah akiang ah atawilut ua, lei si in amai ah akun chiat uhi.
english: When Joseph came home, they brought him the present which was in their hand into the house, and bowed themselves down to the earth before him.

paite: Ama'n atanchin uh adong a, "Na pa uh tanchin na gen uh, huai putek ahoih na maw? Adam lai hia?" achi hi.
english: He asked them of their welfare, and said, “Is your father well, the old man of whom you spoke? Is he yet alive?”

paite: Amau, "Na sikha ka pa uh damtheihna ahoih in, adam laitak ahi," achi uh. Huchi in alu uh akunsak ua, zahtakna apia uhi.
english: They said, “Your servant, our father, is well. He is still alive.” They bowed down humbly.

paite: Amah adak a, anau Benjamin, anu tapa amu a, "Hiai na nautumpen uh, atanchin na hon hilh uhia?" achi hi. Amah mah in, "Ka tapa, Pathian in hon hehpih hen," achi hi.
english: He lifted up his eyes, and saw Benjamin, his brother, his mother’s son, and said, “Is this your youngest brother, of whom you spoke to me?” He said, “God be gracious to you, my son.”

paite: Joseph in anaupa amuh in akhase mahmah a, kintak in kahna ding mun azong pah a, adantan sung ah alut a, huai ah akapkheta hi.
english: Joseph hurried, for his heart yearned over his brother; and he sought a place to weep. He entered into his room, and wept there.

paite: Amai aphiat a, ava pawt nawn a, akidek teitei a, "An nek bawl un," achi hi.
english: He washed his face, and came out. He controlled himself, and said, “Serve the meal.”

paite: Huchi in amah a ding atuam in, amaute a ding atuam in, Aigupta mi anekpihte a ding atuam in abawlta uhi. Aiguptate'n lah Hebrute anekpih thei ngal kei ua; huchibang hih lah Aiguptate a ding in thilsiang lou ahi.
english: They served him by himself, and them by themselves, and the Egyptians who ate with him by themselves, because the Egyptians don’t eat with the Hebrews, for that is an abomination to the Egyptians.

paite: Huchi in a-upapen ta masa ahihna bang in, anaupangpen nautumpen ahihna bang dungzui zel in Joseph ma ah atu ua; huchi in lamdang asa chiat uhi.
english: They sat before him, the firstborn according to his birthright, and the youngest according to his youth, and the men marveled with one another.

paite: Joseph in ama a mite a kipan tantuan an aban piaksak a, Benjamin tantuan houh amaute tantuan tengteng sang in amun nga in atam tuam hi. Uain adawn ua, nuam asa chiat uhi.
english: He sent portions to them from before him, but Benjamin’s portion was five times as much as any of theirs. They drank, and were merry with him.

paite: Huan ama'n a-inkemmi kiang in ah, “Huai mite ip in apuak zoh zahzah buh in dimsak inla, adangka chiat uh a-ipgong bul chiat uah koih in.
english: He commanded the steward of his house, saying, “Fill the men’s sacks with food, as much as they can carry, and put each man’s money in his sack’s mouth.

paite: Ka nou, huai dangka nou, anaupangpenpa ipgong bul ah koih in, abuh man dangka toh," chi in thu apia hi. Huchi in ama'n Joseph thugen bang in ahihta hi.
english: Put my cup, the silver cup, in the sack’s mouth of the youngest, with his grain money.” He did according to the word that Joseph had spoken.

paite: Khua avaktak in amau asabiltungte uh toh apaisakta hi.
english: As soon as the morning was light, the men were sent away, they and their donkeys.

paite: Khua a kipan apaikhiak ua gamla atun ma un, Joseph in a-inkemmi kiang ah, "Thou inla, huai mite va delh in. Na va phak chiang in akiang uah, 'Bangchidan a thil hoih, thil hoih lou a thuk na hi ua?
english: When they had gone out of the city, and were not yet far off, Joseph said to his steward, “Up, follow after the men. When you overtake them, ask them, ‘Why have you rewarded evil for good?

paite: Huai ka pu uain dawnna leh a-aisanna mahmah hilou ahi maw? Hichibang na hih uh na gilou uhi,' chi in," achi hi.
english: Isn’t this that from which my lord drinks, and by which he indeed divines? You have done evil in so doing.’”

paite: Huan adelhphaktak in, huai thute akiang uah agen hi.
english: He overtook them, and he spoke these words to them.

paite: Amau akiang ah, "Pu, bangchidan ahia hiai bang thute na gen? Na sikhate'n huchibang thil ka hihlouhdan ding uh.
english: They said to him, “Why does my lord speak such words as these? Far be it from your servants that they should do such a thing!

paite: Ngai in, ka ipgong bul ua dangka ka muhte uh leng Kanaan gam a kipan na kiang ah ka hon tawi ve ua oi. Bangchidan in na pu inn a dangka hiam dangka-eng hiam gu mawk ding ka hi ua?
english: Behold, the money, which we found in our sacks’ mouths, we brought again to you out of the land of Canaan. How then should we steal silver or gold out of your lord’s house?

paite: Na sikhate lak ah kuapeuh na muhna penpen si hen, huan kou leng ka pu uh sikha in ka om mai ding uh," achi uhi.
english: With whomever of your servants it is found, let him die, and we also will be my lord’s slaves.”

paite: Ama'n, "Hi hen, na thu bang zel un hi hen. Himahleh kuapeuh ka hon muhna penpen ka sikha in om hen. Nou ahihleh dembei na hi ding uh," achi hi.
english: He said, “Now also let it be according to your words. He with whom it is found will be my slave; and you will be blameless.”

paite: Huaitak in amau ip chiat uh kintak in lei ah angakhia ua, amau ip chiat ahong uhi.
english: Then they hurried, and each man took his sack down to the ground, and each man opened his sack.

paite: Ama'n a-upapen ah apan a, anaupangpen pha in azong a; huchi in Benjamin ip ah nou amuta hi.
english: He searched, beginning with the oldest, and ending at the youngest. The cup was found in Benjamin’s sack.

paite: Huaitak in apuansilhte uh abotkek ua, amau sabiltung chiat aposak nawn ua, khua ah akik nawnta uhi.
english: Then they tore their clothes, and each man loaded his donkey, and returned to the city.

paite: Judah leh asanggamte'n Joseph inn ava pha ua; amah huai ah ana om lai hi. Huchi in amai ah abokkhup chiat uh.
english: Judah and his brothers came to Joseph’s house, and he was still there. They fell on the ground before him.

paite: Joseph in akiang uah, "Bang thil ahi mai a na hih uh? Kei bang mi in, aisan a hichibang thil mukhe thei ka hi, chih na thei kei ua hia?" achi hi.
english: Joseph said to them, “What deed is this that you have done? Don’t you know that such a man as I can indeed do divination?”

paite: Judah in, "Ka toupa kiang ah bang ka genta ding ua? Bang ka hon hilhta ding ua? Bangchibang in ka kigenvengta ding ua? Pathian in na sikhate tatlekna amukheta. Ngai in, ka toupa sikhate ka hita mai uh. Kou leh akhut a nou amuhna pen uh leng," achi hi.
english: Judah said, “What will we tell my lord? What will we speak? How will we clear ourselves? God has found out the iniquity of your servants. Behold, we are my lord’s slaves, both we and he also in whose hand the cup is found.”

paite: Ama'n, "Huchibang a ka hih louh ding dan. Akhut a nou amuhna pen kia ka sikha in a-om ding a, nou zaw lungmuangtak in na pa uh kiang ah paitouta un,” achi hi.
english: He said, “Far be it from me that I should do so. The man in whose hand the cup is found, he will be my slave; but as for you, go up in peace to your father.”

paite: Huaitak in, Judah in Joseph ava naih a, "Ka toupa aw, hehpihtak in, kei na sikha, ka toupa bil a na zak ding in thu kam khat hon gensak inla, na hehna na sikha tung ah kuangsak ke'n, nang lah Pharaoh bang hial na hita ngal a.
english: Then Judah came near to him, and said, “Oh, my lord, please let your servant speak a word in my lord’s ears, and don’t let your anger burn against your servant; for you are even as Pharaoh.

paite: Ka toupa'n, 'Pa hiam sanggam hiam na nei uhia?' chi in na sikhate na hon dong hi.
english: My lord asked his servants, saying, ‘Have you a father, or a brother?’

paite: Ka toupa kiang ah, 'Pa putektak leh atek lam a neih naupang chik ka nei uh. Huai mipa upa asita a, anu neih lak ah amah kia a-om lai a, apa'n lah amah a-it mahmah hi,' ka chi uhi.
english: We said to my lord, ‘We have a father, an old man, and a child of his old age, a little one; and his brother is dead, and he alone is left of his mother; and his father loves him.’

paite: Nang na sikhate kiang ah, 'Ka mit a amah ka muhtheihna ding in ka kiang ah hon pisuk un,' na chi hi.
english: You said to your servants, ‘Bring him down to me, that I may set my eyes on him.’

paite: Ka toupa kiang ah, 'Ka naupa un apa anuse thei kei ding; apa paisanleh apa asi mai ding,' ka chi uhi.
english: We said to my lord, ‘The boy can’t leave his father, for if he should leave his father, his father would die.’

paite: Nang na sikhate kiang ah, 'Na nautumpen uh na hon tonpih kei uleh, ka mel na mu nawn kei ding uh,' na chi hi.
english: You said to your servants, ‘Unless your youngest brother comes down with you, you will see my face no more.’

paite: "Huan hichi ahong hi a, na sikha ka pa uh kiang ka va tun un, ka toupa thute ka hilh uhi.
english: When we came up to your servant my father, we told him the words of my lord.

paite: Ka pa un, 'Kuan nawn unla, buh tawmchik bek ei a ding in va lei nawn un,' ahon chi hi.
english: Our father said, ‘Go again and buy us a little food.’

paite: Kou, 'Ka hohsuk thei nawn kei ding uh. Ka nautumpen uh ahong dingleh bel ka hohsuk ding ua, ka nautumpen un ahong pai keileh zaw huai mi mel mu thei lou ding ka hi uh,' ka chi uhi.
english: We said, ‘We can’t go down. If our youngest brother is with us, then we will go down: for we may not see the man’s face, unless our youngest brother is with us.’

paite: Na sikha ka pa un ka kiang uah, 'Ka zi in tapa nih ahon neihsak chih na thei uhi.
english: Your servant, my father, said to us, ‘You know that my wife bore me two sons.

paite: Akhat pen ka kiang a kipan apaikhia a, bohzan vek a om hi ngei ding ahi, ka chi hi. Huai nungsiah amah mu lou vengveng ka hi.
english: One went out from me, and I said, “Surely he is torn in pieces;” and I haven’t seen him since.

paite: Huchi in hiai mi leng ka kiang a kipan na pikhiak ua, tuahsia va tuak taleh lungkhamtak a han a ka samkangpi toh hon tumsak ding na hi uh,' achi hi.
english: If you take this one also from me, and harm happens to him, you will bring down my gray hairs with sorrow to Sheol.’

paite: "Huchi in ka nau in kou hon zui lou in, na sikha ka pa uh kiang va tung leng, ka nau uh hinna toh ahinna akizop ziak in,
english: Now therefore when I come to your servant my father, and the boy is not with us; since his life is bound up in the boy’s life;

paite: hichi ahong hi ding a, naupang in ahon zui kei, chih atheih chiang in asi mai ding. Huchi in na sikhate'n na sikha ka pa uh samkangpi toh lungkhamna a han a tumsak ding ka hi uh.
english: it will happen, when he sees that the boy is no more, that he will die. Your servants will bring down the gray hairs of your servant, our father, with sorrow to Sheol.

paite: Na sikha in na kiang a ka hon pikik nawn keileh, amoh tangtawn in ka pa lak ah ka po ding, chi in ka pa kiang ah ka nau uh tungtang thu ah abultumpa in ka kibawlta hi.
english: For your servant became collateral for the boy to my father, saying, ‘If I don’t bring him to you, then I will bear the blame to my father forever.’

paite: Huchi in hehpih in na sikha ka nau uh sik in, ka toupa sikha in hon omsak zaw inla, ka nau asanggamte zuitousak in.
english: Now therefore, please let your servant stay instead of the boy, my lord’s slave; and let the boy go up with his brothers.

paite: Ka naupa'n hon zui lou in bangchi in ka pa kiang ah ka paitou thei dia? Atung a siatna tung mu ding ka kei hiam," achi hi.
english: For how will I go up to my father, if the boy isn’t with me?—lest I see the evil that will come on my father.”

paite: Huan akiang a dinghte ma ah Joseph akidek zouta kei, “Mi tengteng ka kiang a kipan pawtkhesak vek un," chi in akikoukhia hi. Joseph asanggamte kiang a akigen sung teng akiang ah kuamah adingh kei uhi.
english: Then Joseph couldn’t control himself before all those who stood before him, and he called out, “Cause everyone to go out from me!” No one else stood with him, while Joseph made himself known to his brothers.

paite: Akap loloih a, Aiguptate'n aza ua, Pharaoh inkuanpihte'n leng aza uh.
english: He wept aloud. The Egyptians heard, and the house of Pharaoh heard.

paite: Joseph in asanggamte kiang ah, "Keimah Joseph ka hi. Ka pa adam lai na maw?" achi hi. Himahleh asanggamte'n adawng thei kei ua, ama ah buaitak in a-om uhi.
english: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Does my father still live?” His brothers couldn’t answer him; for they were terrified at his presence.

paite: Joseph mah in asanggamte kiang ah, "Hehpih in hon naih un," achi hi. Huchi in ava naih ua, ama'n, "Na unaupa uh Joseph, Aigupta gam a lutpih ding a na khotpa uh ka hi.
english: Joseph said to his brothers, “Come near to me, please.” They came near. He said, “I am Joseph, your brother, whom you sold into Egypt.

paite: Himahleh hiai a pai ding a na hon khot ziak un lungkham kei unla, kihehkhum tuan sam kei un. Mite hinna hondam ding in Pathian in na ma ua hon sawl masa ahi.
english: Now don’t be grieved, nor angry with yourselves, that you sold me here, for God sent me before you to preserve life.

paite: Hiai kum nih sung hiai gam ah kial aketa a; kum nga in asam lai hi. Huai sung in leileh a-om kei ding a, buhlak leng a-om kei ding.
english: For these two years the famine has been in the land, and there are yet five years, in which there will be no plowing and no harvest.

paite: Tunung khang om zel ding hawisak ding leh noute hotdamna thupitak a hingdam a ka hon omsak theihna ding in Pathian in na ma uah kei ahon sawl masa hi.
english: God sent me before you to preserve for you a remnant on the earth, and to save you alive by a great deliverance.

paite: Huchi in hiai a hon sawl noute na hi kei ua, Pathian ahi zaw. Ama'n Pharaoh pa in leh a-inkuanpih tengteng heutu in leh Aigupta gam tengteng vaihawmtu in ahon bawlta hi.
english: So now it wasn’t you who sent me here, but God, and he has made me a father to Pharaoh, lord of all his house, and ruler over all the land of Egypt.

paite: "Kintak in ka pa kiang ah va pai unla, akiang ah, na tapa Joseph in hichi in achi: Pathian in Aigupta gam tengteng heutu in ahon bawlta a, ka kiang ah hong paisuk in, sawt hon hal ke'n.
english: Hurry, and go up to my father, and tell him, ‘This is what your son Joseph says, “God has made me lord of all Egypt. Come down to me. Don’t wait.

paite: Huchi in Goshen gam ah na teng ding a, ka kiang ngei ah na om ding; nang, na tate, na tute, na belamhonte, na bawnghonte leh na neih tengteng toh.
english: You shall dwell in the land of Goshen, and you will be near to me, you, your children, your children’s children, your flocks, your herds, and all that you have.

paite: Hiai ah keimah in ka hon vak ding; kial lah kum nga om lai ding ahi ngal a. Huchi lou in zaw nang leh na inkuanpihte leh na neih tengteng toh na kialgawp kha ding uh," hon chi un.
english: There I will provide for you; for there are yet five years of famine; lest you come to poverty, you, and your household, and all that you have.”’

paite: "Ngai un, noumau mit ngei leh ka nau Benjamin mit ngei in keimah kam mahmah in agen lai na mu kilkel uhi.
english: Behold, your eyes see, and the eyes of my brother Benjamin, that it is my mouth that speaks to you.

paite: Aigupta gam a ka thupina tengteng thu leh na thil muh tengteng thu uh ka pa na hilh ding ua; kintak in hiai ah ka pa na hon pisuk pah ding uh ahi," achi hi.
english: You shall tell my father of all my glory in Egypt, and of all that you have seen. You shall hurry and bring my father down here.”

paite: Anau Benjamin ngawng a kun in akap a; Benjamin leng ama ngawng a kun in akap hi.
english: He fell on his brother Benjamin’s neck and wept, and Benjamin wept on his neck.

paite: Asanggamte tengteng atawp a, akahkhum chiat a, huai khit in asanggamte'n thu vantang agenpih uhi.
english: He kissed all his brothers, and wept on them. After that his brothers talked with him.

paite: Joseph sanggamte ahong uh chih thu thuthang Pharaoh inkote'n ana za uhi. Huai in Pharaoh leh asikhate akipaksak mahmah hi.
english: The report of it was heard in Pharaoh’s house, saying, “Joseph’s brothers have come.” It pleased Pharaoh well, and his servants.

paite: Pharaoh in Joseph kiang ah, "Na sanggamte kiang ah huchi in hih in. Na gante uh buh posak unla, pawt unla, Kanaan gam ah pai un.
english: Pharaoh said to Joseph, “Tell your brothers, ‘Do this: Load your animals, and go, travel to the land of Canaan.

paite: Na pa uh leh na inkuanpihte uh hon pi unla, ka kiang ah hong pai un. Aigupta gam a thil hoihte ka hon pe ding a, hiai gam a thil om hoihpente na ne ding uh.
english: Take your father and your households, and come to me, and I will give you the good of the land of Egypt, and you will eat the fat of the land.’

paite: Thu ka hon pia ahi, 'Hichibang in hih un: Na taneu chikchikte uh a ding leh na zite uh a ding Aigupta gam a kipan kangtalaite la unla, na pa uh pi ding in va kuan un.
english: Now you are commanded to do this: Take wagons out of the land of Egypt for your little ones, and for your wives, and bring your father, and come.

paite: Na van uh leng ngaihtuah nuam dah un, Aigupta gam tengteng thil hoih peuhmah nou a ahi ngal a,' " achi hi.
english: Also, don’t concern yourselves about your belongings, for the good of all the land of Egypt is yours.”

paite: Israel suante'n huchibang in ahih ua, Joseph in Pharaoh thupiak bang in akiang uah kangtalaite apia a, lampi a nek ding leng apia hi.
english: The sons of Israel did so. Joseph gave them wagons, according to the commandment of Pharaoh, and gave them provision for the way.

paite: Avek ua kiang ah puansilh kikhenna ding ape chiat a; Benjamin kiang ngial ah houh dangka zathum leh puansilh kikhenna ding nga apia hi.
english: He gave each one of them changes of clothing, but to Benjamin he gave three hundred pieces of silver and five changes of clothing.
