paite: Ka unaute aw, i i Toupa Jesu Khrist, thupina Toupa gingta kawm in, mite khentuam kei un.
english: My brothers, don’t hold the faith of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ with partiality.

paite: Na kikhopkhawmna inn uah mi dangka-eng zungbuh bun, puan hoihtak silh hong lut henla, huan migenthei puansetak silh hong lut samleh;
english: For if a man with a gold ring, in fine clothing, comes into your synagogue, and a poor man in filthy clothing also comes in,

paite: puan hoihtak silhmi na limsak ua akiang ah, "Nang hiai mun hoih ah tu in," na chi ua, migenthei kiang ah bel, "Nang huai ah na dingh in, ahihkeileh, ka khe ngakna nuai ah tu in,” na chih uleh,
english: and you pay special attention to him who wears the fine clothing and say, “Sit here in a good place;” and you tell the poor man, “Stand there,” or “Sit by my footstool”

paite: na lungsim uah khentuam nei leh ngaihtuahna giloupu, gense mite na hong hi kei ding ua hia?
english: haven’t you shown partiality among yourselves, and become judges with evil thoughts?

paite: Ka unau deihtakte aw, Pathian in hiai khovel a gentheite ginna a hau ding leh amah itte kiang a achiam gam luah ding in achi kei a hia?
english: Listen, my beloved brothers. Didn’t God choose those who are poor in this world to be rich in faith and heirs of the Kingdom which he promised to those who love him?

paite: Nou bel migentheite na zahlaksak zaw uhi. Mihaute hilou uhia nou hon nuaisiah? Mihaute hilou uhia vaihawmna a nou hon kailut?
english: But you have dishonored the poor man. Don’t the rich oppress you and personally drag you before the courts?

paite: Amaute hilou uhia minhoih na put uh gensete?
english: Don’t they blaspheme the honorable name by which you are called?

paite: Himahleh Laisiangthou in, "Nangmah na ki-it bang in na vengte na it ding ahi," chih kumpi dan na zop uleh na hihhoih uhi.
english: However, if you fulfill the royal law according to the Scripture, “You shall love your neighbor as yourself,” you do well.

paite: Himahleh mi khentuam na neih uleh, na hihkhial uhi, dan in talekte na hih uh ahon theisak zawta hi.
english: But if you show partiality, you commit sin, being convicted by the law as transgressors.

paite: Kuapeuh in dan zuikim mahleh mun khat a ahihkhelhleh avek ah siam louh tang in a-om khin hi.
english: For whoever keeps the whole law, and yet stumbles in one point, he has become guilty of all.

paite: "Ang kawm ke'n," chipa'n, "Tualthat ke'n," achi lai hi. Huchi in angkawm kei mah lechin tual na thah in, dan a talekpa na hita hi.
english: For he who said, “Do not commit adultery,” also said, “Do not commit murder.” Now if you do not commit adultery but do murder, you have become a transgressor of the law.

paite: Huaiziak in noplenna dan a vai hawmsak dingte bang in thu gen unla, thilhih behlap un.
english: So speak and so do as men who are to be judged by the law of freedom.

paite: Zahngaihna suahloumi tuh zahngaihna bei a vaihawmkhum hi ding ahi ngal a. Vaihawmna tung a vualzou zahngaihna ahi.
english: For judgment is without mercy to him who has shown no mercy. Mercy triumphs over judgment.

paite: Ka unaute aw, mi'n ginna ka nei chi mahleh thilhih aneih keileh bang aphatuam dia? Huchibang ginna in amah ahondam thei dia hia?
english: What good is it, my brothers, if a man says he has faith, but has no works? Can faith save him?

paite: Unaupa hiam, unaunu hiam, vuaktang a om in aniteng an nek tasam le uh,
english: And if a brother or sister is naked and in lack of daily food,

paite: na lak ua kuahiam in akiang ah, "Khamuangtak in pai inla, lumtak leh vahtak in om in," chi in asa a ding a thil kiphamoh pe tuan keileh bang aphatuam dia?
english: and one of you tells them, “Go in peace. Be warmed and filled;” yet you didn’t give them the things the body needs, what good is it?

paite: Huchi mah bang in ginna leng thilhih nei lou a amah kia a a-omleh si ahi.
english: Even so faith, if it has no works, is dead in itself.

paite: Ahi, mi kuahiam in, "Nang ginna na nei a, ke'n thilhih ka nei hi," na ginna na thilhih pang lou in hon ensak inla, ke'n thilhih in ka ginna ka hon ensak ding achi thei hi.
english: Yes, a man will say, “You have faith, and I have works.” Show me your faith without works, and I will show you my faith by my works.

paite: Pathian khat kia ahi chih na gingta maw? Na hihhoih e; dawite'n leng agingta ua, aling zel uh, achi ding hi.
english: You believe that God is one. You do well. The demons also believe—and shudder.

paite: Mithulim lou aw, thilhih pang lou a ginna lel bangmah ahi kei chih na thei nuam hia?
english: But do you want to know, vain man, that faith apart from works is dead?

paite: I pu uh Abraham in maitam tung a atapa Isak alat lai in thilhih ziak a siamtang ahi kei a hia?
english: Wasn’t Abraham our father justified by works, in that he offered up Isaac his son on the altar?

paite: Ginna in thilhih toh asemkhawm a, thilhih ziak in ginna abukimta chih i thei uhi.
english: You see that faith worked with his works, and by works faith was perfected.

paite: "Abraham in Pathian agingta a, huai ginna adiktatna a sim ahi," chih Laisiangthou hihkim in a-om hi; huchi in amah Pathian lawm chih in a-om hi.
english: So the Scripture was fulfilled which says, “Abraham believed God, and it was accounted to him as righteousness,” and he was called the friend of God.

paite: Ginna ziak kia hilou in, thilhih ziak zaw in mi'n siam atang zel uh chih na theita uhi.
english: You see then that by works a man is justified, and not only by faith.

paite: Huchibang in, Rahab kizuaknu'n leng sawltakte ana kipahpih a lam tuam a apaisak lai in, thilhih ziak in siamtang ahi kei maw?
english: In the same way, wasn’t Rahab the prostitute also justified by works when she received the messengers and sent them out another way?

paite: Kha pang lou in pumpi si ahih bang in, thilhih pang lou ginna leng si ahi.
english: For as the body apart from the spirit is dead, even so faith apart from works is dead.

paite: Ka unaute aw, na lak uah mi tampi heutu in hong om kei un, heutu in vaihawmna thupi sem atuak ding chih i thei uhi.
english: Let not many of you be teachers, my brothers, knowing that we will receive heavier judgment.

paite: Thil tampi ah i vek un i gilou nak uhi. Kuapeuh thugen lam a agitlouh keileh mi piching ahi a, apumpi vengtheimi ahi.
english: For we all stumble in many things. Anyone who doesn’t stumble in word is a perfect person, able to bridle the whole body also.

paite: Ngai un, sakolte'n i thu aman theihna ding ua akam ua kamkaihna sikkual i batleh apumpi uh i kaihei hi.
english: Indeed, we put bits into the horses’ mouths so that they may obey us, and we guide their whole body.

paite: Longpite leng ngaihtuah sam un, alian mahmah ua, huih hat mutleng in a-om nak uhi, himahleh alonghekpa'n apaisak utna lam peuh ah ahekna neuchik petmah in akiheisak hi.
english: Behold, the ships also, though they are so big and are driven by fierce winds, are yet guided by a very small rudder, wherever the pilot desires.

paite: Hichibang in leitung pumpi hiang neuchik ahi a, nakpitak in aki-uangsak nak hi. Ngai un, meikuang neuchik phet in gammang nak katsak na tel e!
english: So the tongue is also a little member, and boasts great things. See how a small fire can spread to a large forest!

paite: Huan lei tuh meikuang ahi, pumpi hiangte lak a gitlouhna lumpi, pumpi avek a ninsak a, mihing kisuansawndan pianphungpi kangsak ahi; huai lei mah in gawtmun mei toh apeh hi.
english: And the tongue is a fire. The world of iniquity among our members is the tongue, which defiles the whole body, and sets on fire the course of nature, and is set on fire by Gehenna.

paite: Sa chi chih, vasa chi chih, ganhing chi chih tuipi ate khoizual theih ahi ua, mite khoizual in a-om uhi.
english: For every kind of animal, bird, creeping thing, and sea creature is tamed, and has been tamed by mankind;

paite: Himahleh lei zaw kuamah in akhoizual thei kei uhi; sihna gu a dim gilou om kinken thei lou ahi.
english: but nobody can tame the tongue. It is a restless evil, full of deadly poison.

paite: Huai lei in Pa Pathian i phat ua; huai mah in Pathian bang a bawl mihingte i hamsiat uhi.
english: With it we bless our God and Father, and with it we curse men who are made in the image of God.

paite: Kam khat a kipan in phatna leh hamsia apawt nak hi. Ka unaute aw, huchibang ding hilou ahi.
english: Out of the same mouth comes blessing and cursing. My brothers, these things ought not to be so.

paite: Tuikhuk khat in nak khat mah a kipan in tui lim leh lim lou asuaksak zel a hia?
english: Does a spring send out from the same opening fresh and bitter water?

paite: Ka unaute aw, theipi kung ah olive thei agah thei a hia? Ahihkeileh grepgui ah theipi agah thei a hia? Huchibang in chikhuk in tui al lou asuaksak thei sam kei hi.
english: Can a fig tree, my brothers, yield olives, or a vine figs? Thus no spring yields both salt water and fresh water.

paite: Na lak uah kua apil in, thu atheithei a? Thunuailut leh piltak in athilhihte omdan hoih in ensak hen.
english: Who is wise and understanding among you? Let him show by his good conduct that his deeds are done in gentleness of wisdom.

paite: Himahleh na lungtang uah hazatna thupitak leh kidemna na neih uleh thudik zuausan kei un.
english: But if you have bitter jealousy and selfish ambition in your heart, don’t boast and don’t lie against the truth.

paite: Huai bang pilna zaw tunglam a kipan a hong paisuk ahi kei a, lei lam thil, khamitlouhna leh dawi lam thil a kipan ahi zaw hi.
english: This wisdom is not that which comes down from above, but is earthly, sensual, and demonic.

paite: Hazatna leh kidemna omna ah buaina leh thilhihkhelhna chiteng a-om hi.
english: For where jealousy and selfish ambition are, there is confusion and every evil deed.

paite: Tunglam a kipan pilna bel, atung in asiangthou phot a, huai khit in kituah a-ut a, anunnem a, achihnuam a, zahngaihna leh gah hoih in adim a, khentuam anei kei a, alepchiah kei hi.
english: But the wisdom that is from above is first pure, then peaceful, gentle, reasonable, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.

paite: Huan diktatna gah zaw lemna bawlmi in lemna a atuh ahi.
english: Now the fruit of righteousness is sown in peace by those who make peace.

paite: Na lak ua kidounate leh kinaknate koi a kipan hong suak ahi ua? Hiaite na pumpi hiangte ua kidouna bawl nak, na nopsak utna ua kipan a hong suakkhete ahi kei ua hia?
english: Where do wars and fightings among you come from? Don’t they come from your pleasures that war in your members?

paite: Na lunggulh ua, na nei tuan kei ua, huchi in tual na that uh. Na eng ua, na ngah thei tuan kei ua, huchi in na kidou ua, gal na bawl uh. Na nget louh ziak un, na nei kei uh.
english: You lust, and don’t have. You murder and covet, and can’t obtain. You fight and make war. You don’t have, because you don’t ask.

paite: Na ngen ua, na nget diklouh ziak un na ngah kei uh, na nopsak bawlna ding lel ua zat na tup ziak un.
english: You ask, and don’t receive, because you ask with wrong motives, so that you may spend it on your pleasures.

paite: Nou angkawm hatte aw, khovel lawm hihna zaw Pathian melma hihna ahi chih na thei kei ua hia? Huaiziak in khovel lawm hih ut peuhmah Pathian melma in akibawl nak hi.
english: You adulterers and adulteresses, don’t you know that friendship with the world is hostility toward God? Whoever therefore wants to be a friend of the world makes himself an enemy of God.

paite: Ahihkeileh eimah a teng Kha in, "Haza khop hial in ahon deih chih Laisiangthou in agen bangmah lou in na ngaihtuah ua hia?"
english: Or do you think that the Scripture says in vain, “The Spirit who lives in us yearns jealously”?

paite: Himahleh ama'n hehpihna tamsem ahon pia hi. Huaiziak in Laisiangthou in, "Pathian in mikisatheite adou a, kingaineute bel hehpihna ape nak hi," achih.
english: But he gives more grace. Therefore it says, “God resists the proud, but gives grace to the humble.”

paite: Huaiziak in Pathian ah kitulut un. Diabol dou un, hileh noute ahon taimangsan ding hi.
english: Be subject therefore to God. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

paite: Pathian naih unla, huchi in ama'n ahon naih ding. Khialte aw, na khut uh silsiang un; lungsim thuah neite aw, na lungtang uh hihsiangthou un.
english: Draw near to God, and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, you sinners. Purify your hearts, you double-minded.

paite: Lungkham unla, suun unla, kapkhia un. Na nuih uh suunna suak henla, na lungnopna uh lungngaihna suak hen.
english: Lament, mourn, and weep. Let your laughter be turned to mourning and your joy to gloom.

paite: Toupa mitmuh in kingaineu un, huchi in ahon hihlian ding hi.
english: Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you.

paite: Unaute aw, kigensetuah kei un. Kuapeuh in a-unau agensiat hiam vai ahawmkhumleh, dan gensia a vaihawmkhum ahi; dan na gensiatleh dan zuimi na hi kei a, vaihawmpa na hi zaw hi.
english: Don’t speak against one another, brothers. He who speaks against a brother and judges his brother, speaks against the law and judges the law. But if you judge the law, you are not a doer of the law but a judge.

paite: Dan pepa leh vaihawmpa, amah hondam theipa leh hihmang theipa khat lel a-om hi; nang na vengte vaihawmkhum kua kisa na hia?
english: Only one is the lawgiver, who is able to save and to destroy. But who are you to judge another?

paite: Tu'n ah noute'n ngai un, "Tuni hiam zingchiang hiam in, huai khopi ah i hoh ding ua, huai ah kum khat i va taam ding ua, i sumsin ding ua, punna i mu ding," chite aw.
english: Come now, you who say, “Today or tomorrow let’s go into this city and spend a year there, trade, and make a profit.”

paite: Zingchiang a bang hong om ding ahia chih na thei kei uhi. Na hinna uh bang ahia? Tuimei sawt lou kal a hong dawk a, mang nawn lel bang na hi uhi.
english: Yet you don’t know what your life will be like tomorrow. For what is your life? For you are a vapor that appears for a little time and then vanishes away.

paite: Huchi in "Toupa'n pha asakleh i dam dia, hiai hiam, huai hiam i hih ding," na chih ding uh ahi.
english: For you ought to say, “If the Lord wills, we will both live, and do this or that.”

paite: Himahleh na ki-otsaknate uh na suang zaw ua, huai bang suanna tengteng gilou ahi.
english: But now you glory in your boasting. All such boasting is evil.

paite: Huchi in kuapeuh thil hoih ding thei a hih tuan lou zaw amah a ding in khelhna ahi.
english: To him therefore who knows to do good and doesn’t do it, to him it is sin.

paite: Mihausate aw, ngai dih uh, na tung ua gimthuakna hong tung ding ziak a kap in, mau tuaituai un.
english: Come now, you rich, weep and howl for your miseries that are coming on you.

paite: Na goute uh aseta a, na puante uh leikha in ne khinta hi.
english: Your riches are corrupted and your garments are moth-eaten.

paite: Na dangka-eng uleh na dangkate uh atui-ek khinta hi; huan atui-ek uh nou hon theihpihtu ahi ding ua, meikang bang in na taksa uh akangse zou ding hi.
english: Your gold and your silver are corroded, and their corrosion will be for a testimony against you and will eat your flesh like fire. You have laid up your treasure in the last days.

paite: Ngai un, na lou ua buh at a kilohte loh amau khem a na piak louh uh akikou ua, buh atte mangbang kikou aw Sepaihte' Toupa bil ah alutta hi.
english: Behold, the wages of the laborers who mowed your fields, which you have kept back by fraud, cry out; and the cries of those who reaped have entered into the ears of the Lord of Armies.

paite: Khovel ah nuamsatak leh noptaltak in na hing ua, na thah ni bang un na lungtang uh na taisak uhi.
english: You have lived in luxury on the earth, and taken your pleasure. You have nourished your hearts as in a day of slaughter.

paite: Midiktat, nou hon douloute siam louh tangsak in na that uhi.
english: You have condemned and you have murdered the righteous one. He doesn’t resist you.

paite: Huchi in unaute aw, Toupa hong pai mateng kuhkaltak in om un. Ngai un, louneimi in vuahtui ke masa leh nanung amuh mateng leigah hoihtak angak zel hi.
english: Be patient therefore, brothers, until the coming of the Lord. Behold, the farmer waits for the precious fruit of the earth, being patient over it, until it receives the early and late rain.

paite: Nou leng kuhkaltak in om un; na lungtang uh hihkip un; Toupa hong paina ding anaita hi.
english: You also be patient. Establish your hearts, for the coming of the Lord is at hand.

paite: Unaute aw, siam louh tang a na omlouhna ding un, kiphunkhum kei un; ngai un, kongkhak bul ah vaihawmpa adingh hi.
english: Don’t grumble, brothers, against one another, so that you won’t be judged. Behold, the judge stands at the door.

paite: Unaute aw, Toupa min a thugenmi zawlneite thuakdan leh akuhkaldan uh zuih ding in nei un.
english: Take, brothers, for an example of suffering and of perseverance, the prophets who spoke in the name of the Lord.

paite: Ngai un, athuak mite tuh nuamsa i chi uhi; Job kuhkaldan na zata ua, Toupa'n atawp a ahihdan leh Toupa hehpihna a adimdan leh azahngaih theihdan leng na mu uhi.
english: Behold, we call them blessed who endured. You have heard of the perseverance of Job and have seen the Lord in the outcome, and how the Lord is full of compassion and mercy.

paite: Himahleh ka unaute aw, bang teng tung ah, kichiam kei un; van lou in hiam, lei lou in hiam, thil dang himhim lou in hiam kichiam kei un, hiamhleh "hi" na chih uh "hi" henla, "hilou" na chih uh "hilou" hi hen; huchi lou in zaw siam louh tang in na om kha ding uhi.
english: But above all things, my brothers, don’t swear—not by heaven, or by the earth, or by any other oath; but let your “yes” be “yes”, and your “no”, “no”, so that you don’t fall into hypocrisy.

paite: Na lak uah thil hoih lou thuak a-om uhia? Thum uhen. Kipak a om uhia? Phatna la sa uhen.
english: Is any among you suffering? Let him pray. Is any cheerful? Let him sing praises.

paite: Na lak uah damlou a-om uhia? Saptuam Upa samsak uhenla, ama'n Toupa min a sathau nilh in atung ah thum hen.
english: Is any among you sick? Let him call for the elders of the assembly, and let them pray over him, anointing him with oil in the name of the Lord;

paite: Huan ginna a thumna in damlou adam ding a, Toupa'n amah akaithou ding; thil ahihkhelh takleh ngaihdam ahi ding hi.
english: and the prayer of faith will heal him who is sick, and the Lord will raise him up. If he has committed sins, he will be forgiven.

paite: Huchi in hihdam a na omtheihna ding un, na khelhnate uh thupha kitawituah unla, kithumsaktuah un. Midiktat thumna in thil thupitak ahih zel hi.
english: Confess your sins to one another and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The insistent prayer of a righteous person is powerfully effective.

paite: Elijah leng eimah piandan bang pu mihing ahi a, vuah zuklouhna ding in phatuamngaitak in athum a, kum thum leh kha guk sung teng leitung ah vuah azu kei hi.
english: Elijah was a man with a nature like ours, and he prayed earnestly that it might not rain, and it didn’t rain on the earth for three years and six months.

paite: Athum nawn a, van in vuah azusak a, lei in agahte ahon suah hi.
english: He prayed again, and the sky gave rain, and the earth produced its fruit.

paite: Ka unaute aw, na lak ua mi kuapeuh thutak a kipan in pialmang henla kuahiam in pikik nawnleh,
english: Brothers, if any among you wanders from the truth and someone turns him back,

paite: mikhial alamhaihna a kipan a kiheisakpa'n sihna a kipan akha ahondam ding a, khelhna tampi akhuhsak lai ding chih kithei hen.
english: let him know that he who turns a sinner from the error of his way will save a soul from death and will cover a multitude of sins.

paite: Juda, Jesu Khrist sikha leh Jakob unau in, Pa Pathian sehtuam siangthoute leh Jesu Khrist a kep leh sap a omte kiang ah:
english: Jude, a servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James, to those who are called, sanctified by God the Father, and kept for Jesus Christ:

paite: Zahngaihna, khamuanna leh itna na tung uah hihkhan in om hen.
english: May mercy, peace, and love be multiplied to you.

paite: Deihtakte aw, i kikop hotdamna thu na kiang ua gelh teitei ka tup lai in, misiangthoute kiang a ginna khatvei kepsak a om thu a, phatuamngaitak a humbit a pang ding a hon hanthawn ding in, na kiang ua laigelh kiphamoh ahi chih ka na thei hi.
english: Beloved, while I was very eager to write to you about our common salvation, I was constrained to write to you exhorting you to contend earnestly for the faith which was once for all delivered to the saints.

paite: Mi kuate hiam aguk a hong lut a-om ua, nidanglai a pan hiai siam louh tanna dia sehte; huaite'n thangtatna dia Pathian hehpihna kaikawi in, Toupa Pathian omsun leh i Toupa Jesu Khrist akitheihmohbawl behlap uhi.
english: For there are certain men who crept in secretly, even those who were long ago written about for this condemnation: ungodly men, turning the grace of our God into indecency, and denying our only Master, God, and Lord, Jesus Christ.

paite: Huan bangkim khatvei in thei vek mah le uchin, Toupa'n Aigupta gam a kipan mite asuahtaksak a, huai nung a gingtaloute ahihmanthatdan, nou hon theihsak nawn ka ut hi.
english: Now I desire to remind you, though you already know this, that the Lord, having saved a people out of the land of Egypt, afterward destroyed those who didn’t believe.

paite: Huan angelte, amau sawltak hihna zui lou a, a-omna ngei uh paisante ni thupi vaihawmna a ding a mial nuai a tangtawn gawtna a hen kawm in asit hi.
english: Angels who didn’t keep their first domain, but deserted their own dwelling place, he has kept in everlasting bonds under darkness for the judgment of the great day.

paite: Sodom leh Gomorrah leh akiangnai ua khuate kingaihna a kipumpiak a, gitlouhna lek lua, amau mihinpihloute nangawn enlah a adelh tak ziak un, tangtawn mei a gawt a om dingte etsakna ding in suankhiak in a-om uhi.
english: Even as Sodom and Gomorrah and the cities around them, having in the same way as these given themselves over to sexual immorality and gone after strange flesh, are shown as an example, suffering the punishment of eternal fire.

paite: Himahleh huaite'n leng huchibang mah in, hiai mite'n leng, mang a kinga in sa ahihthanghuai ua, thuneihna anial ua, thupina neite agense nak uhi.
english: Yet in the same way, these also in their dreaming defile the flesh, despise authority, and slander celestial beings.

paite: Himahleh Mikael, angel tungnungpen in bawn, diabol toh kisel a, Mosi luang thu a akinak lai un atungthu gensak in amah agense ngam kei a, "Toupa'n hon tai zaw hen," achi zawta hi.
english: But Michael, the archangel, when contending with the devil and arguing about the body of Moses, dared not bring against him an abusive condemnation, but said, “May the Lord rebuke you!”

paite: Huai mite'n bel thil atheih louh peuh uh agensia ua, ngaihtuahna nei lou ganhingte bang a theihsiamna pianpih aneihte un, huai lam pang ah amau akihihsia uhi.
english: But these speak evil of whatever things they don’t know. They are destroyed in these things that they understand naturally, like the creatures without reason.

paite: Atung uh agik hi! Kain lampi azui ua, punna delh in Balaam mohna ah atai ua, Korah thukalhna ah amangthangta uhi.
english: Woe to them! For they went in the way of Cain, and ran riotously in the error of Balaam for hire, and perished in Korah’s rebellion.

paite: Hiaite ahi uh na itna ankuangluina ua hihmelhemtu leh lauhuai kiselte, amau mah kikhem, angsung ngaihtuah a, maingaltak a tathangte; meipi tuipai lou, huih mutlengte; phavang a singgah lou, nihvei sisa, azung toh bohkhiakte ahi uh.
english: These are hidden rocky reefs in your love feasts when they feast with you, shepherds who without fear feed themselves; clouds without water, carried along by winds; autumn trees without fruit, twice dead, plucked up by the roots;

paite: Tuipi kihot vonvon, amau zahlakna thankhia ahi ua; aksi vialvak, amau a dia tangtawn mial bing bikbek sitsakte ahi uh.
english: wild waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, for whom the blackness of darkness has been reserved forever.

paite: Huan Enok, Adam a kipan akhang sagihna in hiai mite tungtang ah, "Ngai un, Toupa amisiangthou sangsawmte toh ahong pai, chi in ana genkhol hi.
english: About these also Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied, saying, “Behold, the Lord came with ten thousands of his holy ones,

paite: Mi tengteng tung a vaihawm ding leh Pathian limsakloute tengteng Pathian limsaklouhna leh Pathian limsakloute tung a asep tengteng uah leh Pathian limsak lou mikhialte'n atung a thu khauhtak agen tengteng ua siam louh tangsak ding in," achi hi.
english: to execute judgment on all, and to convict all the ungodly of all their works of ungodliness which they have done in an ungodly way, and of all the hard things which ungodly sinners have spoken against him.”

paite: Huaite phunhatte leh ngohhatte ahi ua, amau utna bang zel in a-om ua, akamte un leng ki-otsakna thu agen gawpgawp ua, punna deih ziak in mite maitangphat adeih uhi.
english: These are murmurers and complainers, walking after their lusts—and their mouth speaks proud things—showing respect of persons to gain advantage.

paite: Himahleh deihtakte aw, nou zaw i Toupa Jesu Khrist sawltakte'n thu agenkholhte uh theigige un.
english: But you, beloved, remember the words which have been spoken before by the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ.

paite: "Hun nanung ah Pathian limsaklouhna lam a amau utna bang zel a om, nuihsan hatte ahong om ding uh," chih na kiang ua agendante uh.
english: They said to you, “In the last time there will be mockers, walking after their own ungodly lusts.”

paite: Hiai sa mite ahi, Kha nei lou, pawl tuam bawlte.
english: These are those who cause divisions and are sensual, not having the Spirit.

paite: Himahleh deihtakte, nou zaw na ginna siangthou tung a noumau leh noumau kilemtou in; Kha Siangthou a thum in,
english: But you, beloved, keep building up yourselves on your most holy faith, praying in the Holy Spirit.

paite: tangtawn hinna neihsakna khop i Toupa Jesu Khrist zahngaihna ngak in, Pathian itna ah kikemhoih un.
english: Keep yourselves in God’s love, looking for the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ to eternal life.

paite: Khenkhatte, ginglah a omte hehpih unla;
english: On some have compassion, making a distinction,

paite: khenkhatte, mei a kipan in lakhe zok unla, hondam un; khenkhatte, asa thanghuai banna uh puansilh lam leng kih in, lau kawm in hehpih un.
english: and some save, snatching them out of the fire with fear, hating even the clothing stained by the flesh.

paite: Tu in, na puklouhna ding ua hon veng thei leh athupina ma a nakpitak a nuamsa leh nin baang lou a noute hon koihtheipa,
english: Now to him who is able to keep them from stumbling, and to present you faultless before the presence of his glory in great joy,

paite: apil omsun Hondampa, Pathian tak kia kiang ah, i Toupa Jesu Khrist ziak in, hun himhim om ma leh tu leh tangtawn dong in pahtawina, leh thupina, leh vaihawmna, thuneihna omta hen, Amen.
english: to God our Savior, who alone is wise, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and forever. Amen.

paite: Joshua sih nung in hichi ahong hi a, Israel suante'n, "Kanaante dou a ei a dia hon sualsak ding in kua akuantou masa dia?" chi in TOUPA adong uhi.
english: After the death of Joshua, the children of Israel asked of Yahweh, saying, “Who should go up for us first against the Canaanites, to fight against them?”

paite: TOUPA'N, "Judah va kuan hen. Ngai un, akhut ah gam ka peta," achi hi.
english: Yahweh said, “Judah shall go up. Behold, I have delivered the land into his hand.”

paite: Judah in a-unau Simeon kiang ah, "Kanaante dou ding in ka gam tantuam ah hong paitou in. Kei leng na gam tantuam ah ka hong pai sam ding," achi hi. Huchi in Simeon akiang ah ahohta hi.
english: Judah said to Simeon his brother, “Come up with me into my lot, that we may fight against the Canaanites; and I likewise will go with you into your lot.” So Simeon went with him.

paite: Huchi in Judah ava hoh a; Kanaante leh Perizte TOUPA'N akhut uah apeta hi. Bezek ah mi singkhat athat uhi.
english: Judah went up, and Yahweh delivered the Canaanites and the Perizzites into their hand. They struck ten thousand men in Bezek.

paite: Bezek ah Adoni- bezek amu ua, adou ua, Kanaante leh Perizte athat uhi.
english: They found Adoni-Bezek in Bezek, and they fought against him. They struck the Canaanites and the Perizzites.

paite: Himahleh Adoni-bezek atai a; anungdelh ua, aman ua, akhutpi leh akhepi atansak uhi.
english: But Adoni-Bezek fled. They pursued him, caught him, and cut off his thumbs and his big toes.

paite: Adoni-bezek in, "Kumpipa sawmsagihte khutpi leh khepi ka tankhiaksakte'n ka dohkan nuai ah anneng atawm uh. Ka hih bang geih a Pathian in hon thuk ahita ve," achi hi. Jerusalem ah api ua, huai ah asita hi.
english: Adoni-Bezek said, “Seventy kings, having their thumbs and their big toes cut off, scavenged under my table. As I have done, so God has done to me.” They brought him to Jerusalem, and he died there.

paite: Judah suante'n Jerusalem khua dou in ala ua, namsau a sual in akhopi ahal uhi.
english: The children of Judah fought against Jerusalem, took it, struck it with the edge of the sword, and set the city on fire.

paite: Huai nung in Judah suante tanggam simlam leh phaizang a teng Kanaante dou ding in akuansuk uhi.
english: After that, the children of Judah went down to fight against the Canaanites who lived in the hill country, and in the South, and in the lowland.

paite: Judah in Kanaante Hebron a tengte ava dou a, (ama in Hebron min Kiriath-arba ahi) Sheshai, Ahiman leh Talmai athat uhi.
english: Judah went against the Canaanites who lived in Hebron. (The name of Hebron before that was Kiriath Arba.) They struck Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.

paite: Huai a pan Debir khomite adou uh, ama in Debir kho min Kiriath-sepher ahi.
english: From there he went against the inhabitants of Debir. (The name of Debir before that was Kiriath Sepher.)

paite: Kaleb in, "Kuapeuh Kiriath-sepher khua dou a, la peuhmah ka tanu Aksah azi ding in ka pe ding," achi hi.
english: Caleb said, “I will give Achsah my daughter as wife to the man who strikes Kiriath Sepher, and takes it.”

paite: Kaleb nau Kenaji tapa Othniel in alazou a, azi ding in atanu Aksah apeta hi.
english: Othniel the son of Kenaz, Caleb’s younger brother, took it, so he gave him Achsah his daughter as his wife.

paite: uan hichi ahong hi a, akiang ava tun in gam ngen thei ding in apa akunzou hi. Sabiltung a pan akumkhia a; Kaleb in akiang ah, "Bang na deih a?" achi hi.
english: When she came, she got him to ask her father for a field. She got off her donkey; and Caleb said to her, “What would you like?”

paite: Ama'n akiang ah, "Hon vualzawl in. Simlam gam lah na hon peta ngal a, tui nak neite leng hon pe lai in," achi hi. Kaleb in tui nak nei tungnungte leh khangnungte apeta hi.
english: She said to him, “Give me a blessing; because you have set me in the land of the South, give me also springs of water.” Then Caleb gave her the upper springs and the lower springs.

paite: Mosi puzon Ken suante Arad simlam a om Judah gamdai ah Judah suante toh tum sing khopi a pan ahohtou ua; mipite lak ah ava teng uhi.
english: The children of the Kenite, Moses’ brother-in-law, went up out of the city of palm trees with the children of Judah into the wilderness of Judah, which is in the south of Arad; and they went and lived with the people.

paite: Judah bel a-unau Simeon toh akisa ua, Zephath a om Kanaante ava that ua, ahihchimit vek uhi. Huai khopi min Hormah chih ahi.
english: Judah went with Simeon his brother, and they struck the Canaanites who inhabited Zephath, and utterly destroyed it. The name of the city was called Hormah.

paite: Judah in Gaza khua leh abialte, Ashkelon khua leh abialte leh Ekron khua leh abialte tan in ala hi.
english: Also Judah took Gaza with its border, and Ashkelon with its border, and Ekron with its border.

paite: TOUPA Judah kiang ah a-om a; tanggam a tengte adelhkhia a; phaizang a tengte bel sik kangtalaite aneih ziak un adelhkhe zou kei hi.
english: Yahweh was with Judah, and drove out the inhabitants of the hill country; for he could not drive out the inhabitants of the valley, because they had chariots of iron.

paite: Mosi in ana gensa bang in Hebron khua Kaleb apia ua, ama'n huai a pan Anak tapa thumte adelhkhia hi.
english: They gave Hebron to Caleb, as Moses had said, and he drove the three sons of Anak out of there.

paite: Benjamin suante'n Jebuste, Jerusalem a tengte adelhkhe kei ua, Jebuste Benjamin suante toh tuni tan in Jerusalem ah atengkhawm uhi.
english: The children of Benjamin didn’t drive out the Jebusites who inhabited Jerusalem, but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Benjamin in Jerusalem to this day.

paite: Joseph inkuante leng Bethel khua dou ding in akisatou ua, akiang uah TOUPA a-om hi.
english: The house of Joseph also went up against Bethel, and Yahweh was with them.

paite: Joseph inkuante'n Bethel ah enkhe mite asawl uhi. Ama in huai kho min Luz ahi.
english: The house of Joseph sent to spy out Bethel. (The name of the city before that was Luz.)

paite: Enkhe mite'n mi khat khosung a pan hong pawtkhia amu ua, akiang ah, "Hehpih in khopi sung lutna hon ensak dih ve, huchi in ka hon hehpih ding uh," achi uhi,
english: The watchers saw a man come out of the city, and they said to him, “Please show us the entrance into the city, and we will deal kindly with you.”

paite: Khopi sung lutna a-ensak a, namsau in huai khua adou ua; huai mipa leh a-inkuanpihte teng bel ahinghawi uhi,
english: He showed them the entrance into the city, and they struck the city with the edge of the sword; but they let the man and all his family go.

paite: Huai mipa Hitte gam a lut in khua asat a, huai kho min Luz asa a; tuni tan in hiai min apu lai hi.
english: The man went into the land of the Hittites, built a city, and called its name Luz, which is its name to this day.

paite: Manasseh in Beth-shean khua leh akhopel a tengte, Taanak khua leh akhopel a tengte, Dor khua leh akhopel a tengte, Ibleam khua leh akhopel a tengte, Meggiddo khua leh akhopel a tengte adelhkhe kei hi. Huai gam ah Kanaante ateng uhi.
english: Manasseh didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Beth Shean and its towns, nor Taanach and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Dor and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Ibleam and its towns, nor the inhabitants of Megiddo and its towns; but the Canaanites would dwell in that land.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, Israel suante ahong hat un anasem ding un Kanaante a omsak ua, adelhkhe siang vek kei uhi.
english: When Israel had grown strong, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, and didn’t utterly drive them out.

paite: Ephraim in Gezer a teng Kanaante adelhkhe kei a; Gezer ah alak uah Kanaante ateng zawta uh.
english: Ephraim didn’t drive out the Canaanites who lived in Gezer, but the Canaanites lived in Gezer among them.

paite: Zebulun in Kitron a tengte leh Nahalol a tengte adelhkhe kei a; Kanaante alak uah ateng sam ua, anasem ding un a-om zawta uhi.
english: Zebulun didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Kitron, nor the inhabitants of Nahalol; but the Canaanites lived among them, and became subject to forced labor.

paite: Asher in Akko a tengte, Zidon a tengte, Ahlab a tengte, Akjib a tengte, Helbah a tengte, Aphik a tengte leh Rehob a tengte adelhkhe kei hi.
english: Asher didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Acco, nor the inhabitants of Sidon, nor of Ahlab, nor of Achzib, nor of Helbah, nor of Aphik, nor of Rehob;

paite: Asher suante huai gam a teng Kanaante lak ah ateng samta uhi; amau lah adelhkhe ngal kei ua.
english: but the Asherites lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land, for they didn’t drive them out.

paite: Naphtali in Beth-shemesh a tengte, Beth-anath a tengte adelhkhe kei. Huai gam a teng Kanaante lak ah ateng samta uhi. Beth-shemesh a tengte leh Beth-anath a tengte nasem ding in a-omta uhi.
english: Naphtali didn’t drive out the inhabitants of Beth Shemesh, nor the inhabitants of Beth Anath; but he lived among the Canaanites, the inhabitants of the land. Nevertheless the inhabitants of Beth Shemesh and of Beth Anath became subject to forced labor.

paite: Amorte'n Dan suante tanggam ah ahawltou uh; phaizang a apaisuk uh aphal ngal kei ua.
english: The Amorites forced the children of Dan into the hill country, for they would not allow them to come down to the valley;

paite: Amorte Aijalon a Heres tang leh Shaalbim ah ateng ua, Joseph inkuante'n amau azou ua, anasem ding un alak uah ateng uhi.
english: but the Amorites would dwell in Mount Heres, in Aijalon, and in Shaalbim. Yet the hand of the house of Joseph prevailed, so that they became subject to forced labor.

paite: Amorte gam chiang Akrabbim tungkahna a pan, suangpi a pan leh Sela a pan ahi.
english: The border of the Amorites was from the ascent of Akrabbim, from the rock, and upward.

paite: Huan Abimelek sih nung in Israelte hunkhe ding in Issakar mi Tola ahong dingkhia a; amah Puah tapa ahi. Puah bel Dodo tapa ahi. Amah Ephraim tanggam Shamir ah ateng hi.
english: After Abimelech, Tola the son of Puah, the son of Dodo, a man of Issachar, arose to save Israel. He lived in Shamir in the hill country of Ephraim.

paite: Kum sawmnih-le-thum sung Israelte tung ah vai ahawm a, huchi in asita a, Shamir ah avui uhi.
english: He judged Israel twenty-three years, and died, and was buried in Shamir.

paite: Huai nung in Gilead mi Jair ahong dingkhia a, kum sawmnih-le-nih sung Israelte tung ah vai ahawm hi.
english: After him Jair, the Gileadite, arose. He judged Israel twenty-two years.

paite: Ama'n sabiltungnou tung a tuang tapa sawmthum anei a, amau Gilead gam ah khua sawmthum anei ua, huaite tuni tan in Havothjair achi lai uhi.
english: He had thirty sons who rode on thirty donkey colts. They had thirty cities, which are called Havvoth Jair to this day, which are in the land of Gilead.

paite: Jair asi a, Kamon ah avui uhi.
english: Jair died, and was buried in Kamon.

paite: Israel suante'n TOUPA mitmuh in thil gilou hih nawn in Baal leh Ashtaroth, Siriate pathian, Zidonte pathian, Moabte pathian, Ammon suante pathian leh Philistiate pathian nna asem uhi. Huchi in TOUPA alehngatsan ua, ama nna asemta kei uhi.
english: The children of Israel again did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight, and served the Baals, the Ashtaroth, the gods of Syria, the gods of Sidon, the gods of Moab, the gods of the children of Ammon, and the gods of the Philistines. They abandoned Yahweh, and didn’t serve him.

paite: Huchi in TOUPA Israelte tung ah ahehta mahmah a, Philistiate leh Ammon suante kiang ah amaute akhawngta hi.
english: Yahweh’s anger burned against Israel, and he sold them into the hand of the Philistines and into the hand of the children of Ammon.

paite: Huai kum in amau Israel suante hihbuai in anuaisiah uhi. Jordan gal Gilead gam a Amorte gam a Israel suan om tengteng kum sawm-le-giat sung anuaisiah uhi.
english: They troubled and oppressed the children of Israel that year. For eighteen years they oppressed all the children of Israel that were beyond the Jordan in the land of the Amorites, which is in Gilead.

paite: Ammon suante bel Judahte, Benjaminte, Ephraim inkote dou ding in Jordan agalkah ua; huchi in Israelte alungzing mahmah uhi.
english: The children of Ammon passed over the Jordan to fight also against Judah, and against Benjamin, and against the house of Ephraim, so that Israel was very distressed.

paite: Israel suante'n, "I Pathian in Baalte nna i na sep ziak un hon lehngatsanta, atung ah thil i hihkhialta uh," chi in TOUPA asam uhi.
english: The children of Israel cried to Yahweh, saying, “We have sinned against you, even because we have forsaken our God, and have served the Baals.”

paite: TOUPA'N Israel suante kiang ah, "Aiguptate a pan, Amorte a pan, Ammon suante a pan leh Philistiate a pan noute ka hon hunkhe kei maw?
english: Yahweh said to the children of Israel, “Didn’t I save you from the Egyptians, and from the Amorites, from the children of Ammon, and from the Philistines?

paite: Sidonte, Amalekte leh Ammonte'n leng noute ahon nuaisiah ua; na hon sam ua, huchi in akhut ua kipan ka hon hunkhia hi.
english: The Sidonians also, and the Amalekites, and the Maonites, oppressed you; and you cried to me, and I saved you out of their hand.

paite: Himahleh noute'n na hon lehngatsan ua, pathian dangte nna na sem zawta uh. Huaiziak in ka hon hunkhe nawn kei ding.
english: Yet you have forsaken me and served other gods. Therefore I will save you no more.

paite: Na pathian telte uh samta unla, amau na gimthuak hun un hon hunkhia uhen," achi hi.
english: Go and cry to the gods which you have chosen. Let them save you in the time of your distress!”

paite: Israel suante'n TOUPA kiang ah, "Thil ka na hihkhialta uh. Nang pha na sak bangbang in ka tung uah hih in. Himahleh ka hong thum uhi, tuni in hon hunkhe lai in," chi in.
english: The children of Israel said to Yahweh, “We have sinned! Do to us whatever seems good to you; only deliver us, please, today.”

paite: Huchi in alak ua namdang pathiante akoihmang ua, TOUPA nna asemta uh. Ama'n Israelte lungzinna athuakzou nawnta kei hi.
english: They put away the foreign gods from among them and served Yahweh; and his soul was grieved for the misery of Israel.

paite: Ammon suante akikhawm ua, Gilead gam ah ava kikulh ua, Israel suante leng akikhawm ua, Mizpah ah akikulh uhi.
english: Then the children of Ammon were gathered together and encamped in Gilead. The children of Israel assembled themselves together and encamped in Mizpah.

paite: Mipite leh Gilead gam a miliante akihou ua, Ammon suante dou pan ding kua a-om a? Huai mi Gilead gam tengteng tung ah heutu ahi ding, akichi uhi.
english: The people, the princes of Gilead, said to one another, “Who is the man who will begin to fight against the children of Ammon? He shall be head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”

paite: Gilead mi Jephthah mihat hangsan ahi a, kizuaknu tapa ahi. Gilead in Jephthah asuang hi.
english: Now Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valor. He was the son of a prostitute. Gilead became the father of Jephthah.

paite: Gilead zi in tapate asuansak a; azi tapate ahong pichin un Jephthah adelhkhia ua, akiang ah, "Nang zaw ka pa uh inn ah gou na luah thei kei ding. Numei tuam khat tapa na hih ziak in," achi uhi.
english: Gilead’s wife bore him sons. When his wife’s sons grew up, they drove Jephthah out and said to him, “You will not inherit in our father’s house, for you are the son of another woman.”

paite: Huchi in Jephthah a-unaute a pan ataimang a, Tob gam ah ateng hi. Jephthah kiang ah mithulim lou pipi atengkhawm ua, amah azui zel uh.
english: Then Jephthah fled from his brothers and lived in the land of Tob. Outlaws joined up with Jephthah, and they went out with him.

paite: Huai nung deuh in Ammon suante'n Israelte adouta uhi.
english: After a while, the children of Ammon made war against Israel.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, Ammon suante'n Israelte adou uleh, Gilead upate Tob gam a Jephthah pi ding in apaikheta uhi.
english: When the children of Ammon made war against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to get Jephthah out of the land of Tob.

paite: Jephthah kiang ah, "Ammon suante ka dou theihna ding un ka heutupen ding un hong om in," achi uhi.
english: They said to Jephthah, “Come and be our chief, that we may fight with the children of Ammon.”

paite: Jephthah in Gilead upate kiang ah, "N'on hua ua, ka pa inn a pan na hon delhkhia uh ahi kei maw? Bang achia na buaitak ua ka kiang a hong na hi ua?" achi hi.
english: Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, “Didn’t you hate me, and drive me out of my father’s house? Why have you come to me now when you are in distress?”

paite: Gilead upate'n Jephthah kiang ah, "Huaiziaktak ahi, tua nang lam ka hong ngat nawn uh. Ammon suante dou dia ka kiang ua na paitheihna ding in; Gilead gam a teng tengtengte tung ah ka heutu ding un na om ding," achi uhi.
english: The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “Therefore we have turned again to you now, that you may go with us and fight with the children of Ammon. You will be our head over all the inhabitants of Gilead.”

paite: Jephthah in Gilead upate kiang ah, "Ammon suante dou dia na hon pikik nawn ua, TOUPA'N amau ahon piakleh na heutu ding un maw ka om ding?" achi hi.
english: Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, “If you bring me home again to fight with the children of Ammon, and Yahweh delivers them before me, will I be your head?”

paite: Gilead upate'n Jephthah kiang ah, "Na thu bangbang a ka hih kei uleh i kikal uah hon theihpihpa TOUPA ahi ding,” achi uhi.
english: The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, “Yahweh will be witness between us. Surely we will do what you say.”

paite: Huchi in Jephthah bel Gilead upate kiang ah ahohta a, mite'n heutu ding leh api penpen ding in ana bawlta uhi. Jephthah in Mizpah ah TOUPA ma ah athu teng agenta hi.
english: Then Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and chief over them. Jephthah spoke all his words before Yahweh in Mizpah.

paite: Jephthah in Ammon suante kumpipa kiang ah, "Bangchidan a hichibang a ka gam hong dou dia ka kiang a hong pai mawk na hia?" chi in palai asawl hi.
english: Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the children of Ammon, saying, “What do you have to do with me, that you have come to me to fight against my land?”

paite: Ammon suante kumpipa'n, "Israelte Aigupta gam a pan ahong pawt lai ua, ka gam ahon laksak ziak uh ahi. Arnon a pan Jabok leh Jordan tan in. Huaiziak in huai gamte lungdam in hon pe nawn mai in," chi in Jephthah palaite ana dawng hi.
english: The king of the children of Ammon answered the messengers of Jephthah, “Because Israel took away my land when he came up out of Egypt, from the Arnon even to the Jabbok, and to the Jordan. Now therefore restore that territory again peaceably.”

paite: Huchi in Jephthah in Ammon suante kumpipa kiang ah palai asawl nawn hi.
english: Jephthah sent messengers again to the king of the children of Ammon;

paite: Akiang ah, Jephthah in hichi in achi, “Israelte'n Moab gam alaksak kei ua, Ammon suante gam leng alaksak sam kei uh.
english: and he said to him, “Jephthah says: Israel didn’t take away the land of Moab, nor the land of the children of Ammon;

paite: Himahleh, Aigupta gam a pan Israelte ahong pawt un gamdai tawn in Tuipi San ahong tung ua, huai a pan Kadesh ah ahong pai uhi.
english: but when they came up from Egypt, and Israel went through the wilderness to the Red Sea, and came to Kadesh,

paite: Israelte'n Edom kumpipa kiang ah, 'Hehpih in na gam ah ka paisuak ding uh,' chi in palai asawl uh. Himahleh Edom kumpipa in ana ngaikhe nuam kei. Huchi mah bang in Moab kumpipa kiang ah asawl nawn a, himahleh pha ana sa kei hi. Huchi in Kadesh ah Israelte a-omta uhi.
english: then Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, ‘Please let me pass through your land;’ but the king of Edom didn’t listen. In the same way, he sent to the king of Moab, but he refused; so Israel stayed in Kadesh.

paite: Huchi in gamdai ah apaisuak ua, Edom gam leh Moab gam kimvel in apai ua, Moab gam suahlam pang ah apai ua, Arnon lehlam pang ah giahphual asat uhi. Moab gamsung ah alut kei hial uh; Arnon bel Moab gamgi chiang ahi.
english: Then they went through the wilderness, and went around the land of Edom, and the land of Moab, and came by the east side of the land of Moab, and they encamped on the other side of the Arnon; but they didn’t come within the border of Moab, for the Arnon was the border of Moab.

paite: Israelte'n Amorte kumpipa Sihon leh Heshbon kumpipa kiang ah palai asawl uhi. Israelte'n akiang ah, ka hong thum uhi, 'Ka mun ua ka paina ding un hehpih in na gam tawn in hon paisuaksak in,' achi uhi.
english: Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, the king of Heshbon; and Israel said to him, ‘Please let us pass through your land to my place.’

paite: Himahleh Sihon in Israelte agam a paisuak ding in amuangzou kei. Sihon in ami tengteng akaikhawm a, Jahaz ah akikulh a, Israelte adouta hi.
english: But Sihon didn’t trust Israel to pass through his border; but Sihon gathered all his people together, and encamped in Jahaz, and fought against Israel.

paite: TOUPA, Israelte' Pathian in Sihon leh ami tengteng Israelte khut ah apia a, amaute athat uhi. Huchi in Israelte'n huai gam a om Amorte gam tengteng atangta uhi.
english: Yahweh, the God of Israel, delivered Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they struck them. So Israel possessed all the land of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that country.

paite: Huchi in Amorte gamgi chiang tengteng Arnon a pan Jabok pha in, gamdai a pan Jordan pha in atangvekta uhi.
english: They possessed all the border of the Amorites, from the Arnon even to the Jabbok, and from the wilderness even to the Jordan.

paite: Huchi in TOUPA, Israelte' Pathian in ami Israelte ma ah Amorte ahawlkhia a, bangziak a nang hiai gam luah thei ding na hia?
english: So now Yahweh, the God of Israel, has dispossessed the Amorites from before his people Israel, and should you possess them?

paite: Na pathian Kemos in nang a tuam dia ahon sehsaksa tang ding hilou na hi maw? Huchi in TOUPA ka Pathian un ka ma ua ahawlkhiakte uh ka tang ding uhi.
english: Won’t you possess that which Chemosh your god gives you to possess? So whoever Yahweh our God has dispossessed from before us, them will we possess.

paite: Moab kumpipa Zippor tapa Balak sang in na hatzaw a hia? Ama'n Israelte kinakpih in ahihkeileh adou ngei himhim a hia?
english: Now are you anything better than Balak the son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever strive against Israel, or did he ever fight against them?

paite: Heshbon leh akhotate, Aroer leh akhotate, Arnon gamgi naih khopi tengteng a kum zathum tak aten lai ua, bangziak a nang ana lakik lou nilouh na hia?
english: Israel lived in Heshbon and its towns, and in Aroer and its towns, and in all the cities that are along the side of the Arnon for three hundred years! Why didn’t you recover them within that time?

paite: Huaiziak in na tung ah thil bangmah ka hihkhial kei. Nangma'n hon dou na tup ziak in ka tung ah thil na hihkhial ahi zaw. TOUPA, Vaihawmpa in tuni in Israel suante leh Ammon suante kal ah thu ngaihtuah hen," achi hi.
english: Therefore I have not sinned against you, but you do me wrong to war against me. May Yahweh the Judge be judge today between the children of Israel and the children of Ammon.”

paite: Himahleh Ammon suante kumpipa'n Jephthah thukhah ana ngaikhe nuam kei hi.
english: However, the king of the children of Ammon didn’t listen to the words of Jephthah which he sent him.

paite: Huchi in Jephthah tung ah TOUPA kha ahong tung a, Gilead leh Manasseh gam ah apaisuak a, Gilead a Mizpah ah apaisuak a, Gilead gam Mizpah a pan Ammon suante kiang ah apai zel hi.
english: Then Yahweh’s Spirit came on Jephthah, and he passed over Gilead and Manasseh, and passed over Mizpah of Gilead, and from Mizpah of Gilead he passed over to the children of Ammon.

paite: TOUPA kiang ah Jephthah akichiam a, "Ammon suante ka khut a na hon piakleh,
english: Jephthah vowed a vow to Yahweh, and said, “If you will indeed deliver the children of Ammon into my hand,

paite: hichi ahi ding a, Ammon suante a pan galmuang a ka paikik nawn chiang in bangpeuh ka inn kongpi a pan hon dawn masa penpen TOUPA a ahi dia, halmang thillat ding in ka zang ngeingei ding,” achi hi.
english: then it shall be, that whatever comes out of the doors of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the children of Ammon, it shall be Yahweh’s, and I will offer it up for a burnt offering.”

paite: Huchi in Jephthah bel Ammon suante dou ding in akuanta hi. TOUPA'N akhut ah amaute apeta hi.
english: So Jephthah passed over to the children of Ammon to fight against them; and Yahweh delivered them into his hand.

paite: Aroer a pan Minnith pha leh Abel-keramim kal a khopi sawmnih azou vek a, mi tampi athat hi. Huchi in Israel suante'n Ammon suante anuaisiahta uhi.
english: He struck them from Aroer until you come to Minnith, even twenty cities, and to Abelcheramim, with a very great slaughter. So the children of Ammon were subdued before the children of Israel.

paite: Jephthah, atenna khua Mizpah a a-inn ah apai a, ngai in, atanu in khuangtate toh lam in ana dawn hi. Ata neihsun ahi a; amah lou tapa hiam tanu dang himhim anei kei hi.
english: Jephthah came to Mizpah to his house; and behold, his daughter came out to meet him with tambourines and with dances. She was his only child. Besides her he had neither son nor daughter.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, amah amuhtak in apuante abotkek a, "Ehe, ka tanu! N'on niamkiaksak mahmah ve. Hon mangbangsak mite lak a khat na hita. TOUPA ma ah lah ka kam ka na kata ngal a, huai lah zukkik thei ka hita kei," achi hi.
english: When he saw her, he tore his clothes, and said, “Alas, my daughter! You have brought me very low, and you are one of those who trouble me; for I have opened my mouth to Yahweh, and I can’t go back.”

paite: Ama'n akiang ah, "Pa aw, TOUPA kiang a thu na chiam tak ahihleh, na kam a thupawt bang in ka tung ah hih in. TOUPA'N lah na melma Ammon suante tung ah na phu ahon laksakta ngal a," achi hi.
english: She said to him, “My father, you have opened your mouth to Yahweh; do to me according to that which has proceeded out of your mouth, because Yahweh has taken vengeance for you on your enemies, even on the children of Ammon.”

paite: Ama'n apa kiang ah, "Hichibang in kei a ding in kihih hen. Kha nih sung ka tang-om dia, tangte ah asuk atou in ka pai dia, ka nungak siangthou hihna ka suun ding, kei leh ka lawmte'n," achi hi.
english: Then she said to her father, “Let this thing be done for me. Leave me alone two months, that I may depart and go down on the mountains, and bewail my virginity, I and my companions.”

paite: Ama'n, "Pai ve," achi hi. Huchi in kha nih taam ding in asawlkhia a; apawt a, amah leh alawmte'n tangte ah anungak siangthou hihna ava suun uhi.
english: He said, “Go.” He sent her away for two months; and she departed, she and her companions, and mourned her virginity on the mountains.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, kha nih nung in apa kiang ah ahong kik nawn a, ama'n ana kichiamsa bang in atung ah ahih hi. Atanu nungak siangthou in a-omdenta a, pasal toh alumkhawm ngei kei hi.
english: At the end of two months, she returned to her father, who did with her according to his vow which he had vowed. She was a virgin. It became a custom in Israel

paite: Israel tanute'n Gilead mi Jephthah tanu kum teng in ni li sung asuun zel uhi. Hiai Israelte lak ah ngeina in aneita uhi.
english: that the daughters of Israel went yearly to celebrate the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite four days in a year.

paite: Huan Ephraimte akikaikhawm ua, mallam zuan in apai ua; Jephthah kiang ah, "Bangziak a Ammon suante dou dia hong paiphei a, na kiang a hoh dia hon chial sam lou? Na inn toh ka hon buhalkhawm ding uh,” achi uhi.
english: The men of Ephraim were gathered together, and passed northward; and they said to Jephthah, “Why did you pass over to fight against the children of Ammon, and didn’t call us to go with you? We will burn your house around you with fire!”

paite: Jephthah in akiang uah, "Ammon suante ka mite toh theihtawp suah in ka dou ua; ka hon sap lai in akhut ua kipan in lah na hon hunkhe ut kei ua.
english: Jephthah said to them, “I and my people were at great strife with the children of Ammon; and when I called you, you didn’t save me out of their hand.

paite: Huchi in na hon hunkhe nuam kei uh chih ka theihtak in, sih khawk sa lou hial in ka pang a, Ammon suante dou ding in ka kuan a, huchi in TOUPA'N amaute ka khut ah ahon pia hi. Huaiziak in bangziak a hon dou dia tuni a hong kuan na hi ua?" achi hi.
english: When I saw that you didn’t save me, I put my life in my hand, and passed over against the children of Ammon, and Yahweh delivered them into my hand. Why then have you come up to me today, to fight against me?”

paite: Huchi in Jephthah in Gilead mi tengteng akaikhawm a, Ephraimte adouta hi. Gileadte'n Ephraimte athat uhi. "Nou Gileadte, Ephraimte leh Manassehte lak a galtai vakvai maimaite na hi uh," achih ziak un.
english: Then Jephthah gathered together all the men of Gilead, and fought with Ephraim. The men of Gilead struck Ephraim, because they said, “You are fugitives of Ephraim, you Gileadites, in the middle of Ephraim, and in the middle of Manasseh.”

paite: Gileadte'n Ephraimte ma in Jordan lui kainate ana la ua; hichi ahong hi a, Ephraim mi suaktate'n, "Ka hong galkah ding uh," achih chiang un Gileadte'n akiang ah, "Ephraim mi na hi hia?” ana chi zel uh. Ama'n, "Hilou e,” achihleh,
english: The Gileadites took the fords of the Jordan against the Ephraimites. Whenever a fugitive of Ephraim said, “Let me go over,” the men of Gilead said to him, “Are you an Ephraimite?” If he said, “No;”

paite: akiang ah, "Shiboleth, chi mah dih," ana chi ua, ama'n, "Siboleth," achi zaw zel a; alouchian thei kei hi. Huchi in aman ua, Jordan lui kainate ah ana that zel uh. Huchi in huai tung in Ephraimte singli-le-sangnih athat uhi.
english: then they said to him, “Now say ‘Shibboleth;’” and he said “Sibboleth”; for he couldn’t manage to pronounce it correctly, then they seized him and killed him at the fords of the Jordan. At that time, forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell.

paite: Jephthah in Israelte tung ah kum guk vai ahawm a, huchi in asita a, Gilead gam a khua khat ah avui uhi.
english: Jephthah judged Israel six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died, and was buried in the cities of Gilead.

paite: Anung in Bethlehem a mi Ibzan in Israelte tung ah vai ahawm hi.
english: After him Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel.

paite: Ama'n tapa sawmthum leh tanu sawmthum anei hi. Atanute gamdang ah asawl a, atapate a ding in gamdang a pan tanu sawmthum apisak hi. Ama'n Israelte tung ah kum sagih vai ahawm hi.
english: He had thirty sons. He sent his thirty daughters outside his clan, and he brought in thirty daughters from outside his clan for his sons. He judged Israel seven years.

paite: Ibzan asita a, Bethlehem ah avui uh.
english: Ibzan died, and was buried at Bethlehem.

paite: Anung in Zebulun mi Elon in Israelte tung ah vai ahawm a; Israelte tung ah kum sawm vai ahawm hi.
english: After him, Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel; and he judged Israel ten years.

paite: Zebulun mi Elon asita a, Zebulun gam a Aijalon ah avui uhi.
english: Elon the Zebulunite died, and was buried in Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.

paite: Huai nung in Pirathon mi, Hilel tapa Abdon in Israelte tung ah vai ahawm hi.
english: After him, Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.

paite: Ama'n tapa sawmli leh sabiltungnou sawmsagih tung a tuang zel tupa sawmthum anei hi. Ama'n Israelte tung ah kum giat vai ahawm hi.
english: He had forty sons and thirty sons’ sons who rode on seventy donkey colts. He judged Israel eight years.

paite: Pirathon mi, Hilel tapa Abdon asita a, Ephraim gam, Amalek mite tanggam ah Pirathon ah avuita uh.
english: Abdon the son of Hillel the Pirathonite died, and was buried in Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.

paite: Huan Israel suante'n TOUPA mitmuh in thil gilou ahih nawn ua; huchi in TOUPA'N Philistiate khut ah amaute kum sawmli sung apia hi.
english: The children of Israel again did that which was evil in Yahweh’s sight; and Yahweh delivered them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.

paite: Zorah ah Dan nam mi khat a-om a, amin Manoah ahi a, azi bel achiing a, nau anei kei hi.
english: There was a certain man of Zorah, of the family of the Danites, whose name was Manoah; and his wife was barren, and childless.

paite: Numei kiang ah TOUPA angel ahong kilak a, akiang ah, "Ngai in, na chiing a, nau nei thei lou himah lechin na gai dia, tapa na nei ding hi.
english: Yahweh’s angel appeared to the woman, and said to her, “See now, you are barren and childless; but you shall conceive and bear a son.

paite: Huchi in pilvang in, uain leh zu hat leh siang lou thil himhim ne het ke'n.
english: Now therefore please beware and drink no wine nor strong drink, and don’t eat any unclean thing;

paite: 'Ngai in, na gai dia, tapa nei ding na hi ngal a. Alu ah mulmet tem himhim zat ahi kei ding; naupang bel sul a a-om lai a pan Pathian a dia Nazarit hi ding ahi ngal a.' Ama'n Israelte Philistia mite khut a pan hutkhiak apan ding," achi hi.
english: for, behold, you shall conceive and give birth to a son. No razor shall come on his head, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb. He shall begin to save Israel out of the hand of the Philistines.”

paite: Numei in apasal kiang ah, "Pathian mipa khat ka kiang ah ahong a, amel Pathian angel mel bang ahi a, kihtakhuaitak ahi. Koilam mi ahia chih bel ka dong chitchiat kei a, ama'n lah amin ahon hilh sam kei hi.
english: Then the woman came and told her husband, saying, “A man of God came to me, and his face was like the face of the angel of God, very awesome. I didn’t ask him where he was from, neither did he tell me his name;

paite: Himahleh ka kiang ah, Ngai in, na gai dia, tapa na nei ding. Huchi in uain leh zu hat himhim dawn ke'nla, siang lou thil himhim leng ne het ke'n. Naupang sul a a-om lai a pan asih tan in Pathian a dia Nazarit mi hi ding ahi, achi,” chi in agen hi.
english: but he said to me, ‘Behold, you shall conceive and bear a son; and now drink no wine nor strong drink. Don’t eat any unclean thing, for the child shall be a Nazirite to God from the womb to the day of his death.’”

paite: Huchi in Manoah in TOUPA kiang ah nget chihtak in angen a, akiang ah, "Aw TOUPA hehpih in huai Pathian mipa na hon sawl ka kiang uah hong nawn henla, naupang hong piang ding bang ka chih ding ua hong sinsak hen," achi hi.
english: Then Manoah entreated Yahweh, and said, “Oh, Lord, please let the man of God whom you sent come again to us, and teach us what we should do to the child who shall be born.”

paite: Pathian in Manoah thugen ana ngaikhia hi. Loubuk a numei atut lai in akiang ah Pathian angel ahong nawn hi. Apasal Manoah bel akiang ah a-om kei hi.
english: God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the angel of God came again to the woman as she sat in the field; but Manoah, her husband, wasn’t with her.

paite: Numei kintak in atai pah a, apasal ava hilh a, akiang ah, "Ngai in, zanlam a ka kiang a hong hohpa ka kiang ah ahong kilak nawn," achi hi.
english: The woman hurried and ran, and told her husband, saying to him, “Behold, the man who came to me that day has appeared to me.”

paite: Huchi in Manoah athou a, azi azui a, huai mi kiang ava tung uhi. Akiang ah, "Numei kiang a thu gen nang na hi maw?" achi hi. Ama'n, "Hi e,” achi hi.
english: Manoah arose and followed his wife, and came to the man, and said to him, “Are you the man who spoke to my wife?” He said, “I am.”

paite: Manoah in, “Na thu bang zel in hong tung hen. Naupang omdan ding bangchibang ahi dia, asep ding bang ahi dia le?" achi hi.
english: Manoah said, “Now let your words happen. What shall the child’s way of life and mission be?”

paite: TOUPA angel in Manoah kiang ah, "Numei kiang a ka gen tengteng ah amah pilvang hen.
english: Yahweh’s angel said to Manoah, “Of all that I said to the woman let her beware.

paite: Grepgui a pan mawngmawng ane ding ahi kei a, uain leh zu hat adawn ding ahi kei. Siang lou thil mawngmawng leng ane ding ahi kei. Ka thupiak tengteng zui hen," achi hi.
english: She may not eat of anything that comes of the vine, neither let her drink wine or strong drink, nor eat any unclean thing. Let her observe all that I commanded her.”

paite: Manoah in TOUPA angel kiang ah, "Ka hong thum uh. Hehpih in hon ompih lai in, kelnou ka hon bawlsak khit matan uh," achi hi.
english: Manoah said to Yahweh’s angel, “Please stay with us, that we may make a young goat ready for you.”

paite: TOUPA angel in Manoah kiang ah, "Hon khou lechin leng na an zaw ka ne kei ding. Haltum thil lan ding na hihleh TOUPA kiang a na lat ngeingei ding ahi,” achi hi. Manoah in lah TOUPA angel ahi chih athei ngal kei hi.
english: Yahweh’s angel said to Manoah, “Though you detain me, I won’t eat your bread. If you will prepare a burnt offering, you must offer it to Yahweh.” For Manoah didn’t know that he was Yahweh’s angel.

paite: Manoah in TOUPA angel kiang ah, "Na min bang ahia, na thugen bang a hong tun chiang a ka hon pahtawi theihna ding un?" achi hi.
english: Manoah said to Yahweh’s angel, “What is your name, that when your words happen, we may honor you?”

paite: TOUPA angel in akiang ah, "Bangziak a ka min hon dong na hia, lamdang ahi chih theizen napi a?" achi hi.
english: Yahweh’s angel said to him, “Why do you ask about my name, since it is incomprehensible?”

paite: Huchi in Manoah in kelnou khat leh nek ding thillat ala a; suangpi tung ah TOUPA kiang ah alan hi. Angel in thillamdangtak ahih a, Manoah leh azi in a-en nilouh uhi.
english: So Manoah took the young goat with the meal offering, and offered it on the rock to Yahweh. Then the angel did an amazing thing as Manoah and his wife watched.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, maitam a pan meikuang van lam a akahtouh lai in, maitam a meikuang ah TOUPA angel apaitouta hi. Manoah leh azi in a-en nilouh ua, amaitang un lei asi uhi.
english: For when the flame went up toward the sky from off the altar, Yahweh’s angel ascended in the flame of the altar. Manoah and his wife watched; and they fell on their faces to the ground.

paite: Himahleh TOUPA angel Manoah leh azi kiang ah ahong kilak nawn kei hi. Huchi in Manoah in TOUPA angel ahi chih atheita hi.
english: But Yahweh’s angel didn’t appear to Manoah or to his wife any more. Then Manoah knew that he was Yahweh’s angel.

paite: Manoah in azi kiang ah, "Pathian i muh ziak in i si ngeingei ding,” achi hi.
english: Manoah said to his wife, “We shall surely die, because we have seen God.”

paite: Himahleh azi in akiang ah, "TOUPA'N hon hihlup tum hileh halmang thillat leh nek ding thillat i latte asang kei ding. Hiai thil tengteng leng ahon ensak kei ding a, tu hun in hiai thilte leng hon hilh kei ding," achi hi.
english: But his wife said to him, “If Yahweh were pleased to kill us, he wouldn’t have received a burnt offering and a meal offering at our hand, and he wouldn’t have shown us all these things, nor would he have told us such things as these at this time.”

paite: Numei in tapa aneita a, amin Samson asa uh. Naungek ahong khanglian a, TOUPA'N avualzawl hi.
english: The woman bore a son and named him Samson. The child grew, and Yahweh blessed him.

paite: Zorah leh Eshtaol kikal ah Mahaneh Dan mun ah TOUPA kha in atokthouta hi.
english: Yahweh’s Spirit began to move him in Mahaneh Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

paite: Huan Samson bel Timnah ah ahohsuk a, Timnah ah Philistiate tanute lak ah numei khat ava mu hi.
english: Samson went down to Timnah, and saw a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines.

paite: Ahong paitouh nawn in anu leh apa ahilh hi. "Timnah khua ah, Philistiate tanute lak ah numei khat ka mu a; ka zi ding in hon pisak un," achi hi.
english: He came up, and told his father and his mother, saying, “I have seen a woman in Timnah of the daughters of the Philistines. Now therefore get her for me as my wife.”

paite: Huchi in anu leh apa'n akiang ah, "Na unaute tanute lak ah hiam, ka mipite lak a hiam numei om het lou hia? Zeksum louh Philistiate lak a zi ding na va zon maimah?" achi uhi. Samson in apa kiang ah, "Hon pisak mai in; ama'n hon lungkimsak mahmah ahi," achi hi.
english: Then his father and his mother said to him, “Isn’t there a woman among your brothers’ daughters, or among all my people, that you go to take a wife of the uncircumcised Philistines?” Samson said to his father, “Get her for me, for she pleases me well.”

paite: Himahleh anu leh apa'n, hiai TOUPA a pan ahi chih athei kei uh; ama'n Philistiate tung a phulakna ding hun lemtang zong lah ahi ngal a. Huai lai in Philistiate'n Israelte tung ah vai ahawm uhi.
english: But his father and his mother didn’t know that it was of Yahweh; for he sought an occasion against the Philistines. Now at that time the Philistines ruled over Israel.

paite: Huchi in Samson bel anu leh apa toh Timnah ah ahohsuk ua, Timnah a grephuan ava tung uhi. Ngai in, humpinelkai lun lai ana humham hi.
english: Then Samson went down to Timnah with his father and his mother, and came to the vineyards of Timnah; and behold, a young lion roared at him.

paite: TOUPA Kha atung ah nakpitak in ahong tung hi. Huchi in kelnou balnen bang mai in abalnen maimah hi; bangmah lah atawi ngal kei a. Himahleh athilhih anu leh apa ahilh kei hi.
english: Yahweh’s Spirit came mightily on him, and he tore him as he would have torn a young goat with his bare hands, but he didn’t tell his father or his mother what he had done.

paite: Ahohsuk a, huai numei ahoupih hi. Ama'n Samson akipaksak mahmah hi.
english: He went down and talked with the woman, and she pleased Samson well.

paite: Anung in va pi ding in ahoh nawn a, humpinelkai luang en ding in ava pial hi. Ngai in, humpinelkai luang ah khuai hon leh azu ana om hi.
english: After a while he returned to take her, and he went over to see the carcass of the lion; and behold, there was a swarm of bees in the body of the lion, and honey.

paite: Huai ala a, apai nawn a, apai kawm in ane kawmkawm hi. Anu leh pa kiang atungtou a, amau leng apia a, amau leng ane sam uhi. Himahleh huai khuaizu humpinelkai luang a pan alak ahi chih ahilh kei hi.
english: He took it into his hands, and went on, eating as he went. He came to his father and mother and gave to them, and they ate, but he didn’t tell them that he had taken the honey out of the lion’s body.

paite: Huchi in huai numei kiang ah apa ava hohsuk a, huai ah Samson in ankuang alui hi. Huai ahihleh tangvalte hihdan ahi him hi.
english: His father went down to the woman; and Samson made a feast there, for the young men used to do so.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, amah amuhtak un, akiang a om ding in mi sawmthum api uhi.
english: When they saw him, they brought thirty companions to be with him.

paite: Samson in akiang uah, "Tu in thuhaksa hon dong ning e. Ankuanglui ni, ni sagih sung a na hon hilhchet theih ua, na theihkhiak theih uleh puanmalngat silh sawmthum ka hon pe ding.
english: Samson said to them, “Let me tell you a riddle now. If you can tell me the answer within the seven days of the feast, and find it out, then I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing;

paite: Himahleh na hon hilhchet theih kei uleh, puanmalngat silh sawmthum leh kikhenna puan sawmthum na hon piak ding uh ahi,” achi hi. Amau akiang ah, "Na thuhaksa gen dih ve le, ka na ngaikhe ding uh," achi uhi.
english: but if you can’t tell me the answer, then you shall give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothing.” They said to him, “Tell us your riddle, that we may hear it.”

paite: Ama'n akiang uah, "Netu a pan nek ding hong pawt, hattak a pan thil khumtak hong pawt," achi hi.
english: He said to them, “Out of the eater came out food. Out of the strong came out sweetness.” They couldn’t in three days declare the riddle.

paite: Ni thum sung in huai thuhaksa ahilhchian thei kei uh. Huan hichi ahong hi a, ani sagih ni in Samson zi kiang ah, "Ka kiang ua hiai thuhaksa hilhchetna puangkhe ding in na pasal kun in. Huchi lou in zaw nang leh na pa inkote ka hon hal ding uh. Ka neihsa uh la dia hon sam na hi kei maw?" achi uhi.
english: On the seventh day, they said to Samson’s wife, “Entice your husband, that he may declare to us the riddle, lest we burn you and your father’s house with fire. Have you called us to impoverish us? Isn’t that so?”

paite: Huchi in Samson zi ama ah akap a, "N'on it kei a, na hon ho zaw ve. Ka chite lah thuhaksa na dong ngal a, kei na hon hilhchian kei," achi hi. Ama'n akiang ah, "Ngai in, ka nu leh pa leng ka hilh kei a; nang ka hon hilh dia hia?" achi hi.
english: Samson’s wife wept before him, and said, “You just hate me, and don’t love me. You’ve told a riddle to the children of my people, and haven’t told it to me.” He said to her, “Behold, I haven’t told my father or my mother, so why should I tell you?”

paite: A-ankuanglui uh, ni sagih sung teng ama ah akapkap hi. Huan hichi ahong hi a, ani sagih ni in anget ngutngut ziak in ahilh khongkhong hi. Ama'n thuhaksa hilhchetna achipihte ava hilhta hi.
english: She wept before him the seven days, while their feast lasted; and on the seventh day, he told her, because she pressed him severely; and she told the riddle to the children of her people.

paite: Ani sagih ni, nitum ma in huai khua a mite'n akiang ah, "Khuaizu sang a khumzaw bang ahia? Humpinelkai sang a hatzaw bang ahia?" achi uhi. Ama'n akiang uah, "Ka bawngla in lei let kei le uchin zaw, ka thuhaksa theikhe lou ding hi ve uchin," achi hi.
english: The men of the city said to him on the seventh day before the sun went down, “What is sweeter than honey? What is stronger than a lion?” He said to them, “If you hadn’t plowed with my heifer, you wouldn’t have found out my riddle.”

paite: TOUPA Kha atung ah nakpitak in ahong tung a, Ashkelon ah ahohsuk hi. Mi sawmthum ava that a, apuansilhte uh ahawksak a, kikhenna puante thuhaksa hilhchiante apia hi. Huchi in aheh mahmah a, apa inn ah apaitou hi.
english: Yahweh’s Spirit came mightily on him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck thirty men of them. He took their plunder, then gave the changes of clothing to those who declared the riddle. His anger burned, and he went up to his father’s house.

paite: Himahleh Samson zi pen akitenna ua theihpih a pang Samson lawmpa kiang ah zi ding in piak in a-om hi.
english: But Samson’s wife was given to his companion, who had been his friend.

paite: Himahleh hichi ahong hi a, anung sawt lou in, buhlak hun in, Samson in kelnou tawi in azi ava veh hi. "Dantan sung ah ka zi kiang ah ka va lut ding," achi hi. Himahleh apa'n alut aphalta kei hi.
english: But after a while, in the time of wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife with a young goat. He said, “I will go in to my wife’s room.” But her father wouldn’t allow him to go in.

paite: Apa'n, “Amah na ho mahmah ka sa a, huaiziak in na lawmpa kiang ah ka peta hi. Anau amah sang in amelhoih zaw hilou hia?" achi hi.
english: Her father said, “I most certainly thought that you utterly hated her; therefore I gave her to your companion. Isn’t her younger sister more beautiful than she? Please, take her instead.”

paite: Samson in, "Tutung in Philistiate khoih leng amau sang in dem ka kai kei zaw ding," achi hi.
english: Samson said to them, “This time I will be blameless in the case of the Philistines when I harm them.”

paite: Huchi in Samson in sihal zathum ava man a, meisel ala a, amei uleh mei apehkhawm a, amei uh kikal chiat ah meisel akoih chiat hi.
english: Samson went and caught three hundred foxes, and took torches, and turned tail to tail, and put a torch in the middle between every two tails.

paite: Meiselte adettak in Philistiate buhlak ah atailutsak a, buhphal leh buh dingh laite, olive munte toh nangawn in akang vek hi.
english: When he had set the torches on fire, he let them go into the standing grain of the Philistines, and burned up both the shocks and the standing grain, and also the olive groves.

paite: Huchi in Philistiate'n, "Kua hih ahia?" achi uh. Amau, "Timnah a mi makpapa Samson hih ahi. Huai Timnah a mi in Samson zi alawmpa zi dia apiak man ahi," akichi uhi. Huchi in Philistiate ahong kuan ua apata un ahallumta uhi.
english: Then the Philistines said, “Who has done this?” They said, “Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he has taken his wife and given her to his companion.” The Philistines came up, and burned her and her father with fire.

paite: Samson in akiang uah, "Hichibang na hih uh leh na tung uah phu ka la sam ding, huai khit in ka tawp ding," achi hi.
english: Samson said to them, “If you behave like this, surely I will take revenge on you, and after that I will cease.”

paite: Huchi in nakpitak in asual a, tampi athat a, apaisuk a, Etam suangpi tung ah a-omta hi.
english: He struck them hip and thigh with a great slaughter; and he went down and lived in the cave in Etam’s rock.

paite: Huchi in Philistiate ahohtou ua, Judah gam ah ava kikulh ua, Lehi mun ah akiphalh uhi.
english: Then the Philistines went up, encamped in Judah, and spread themselves in Lehi.

paite: Judah gam a mite'n, "Bangchidan ahia kou sual dia na hong kuan mawk uh?" achi uhi. Amau, "Samson khaukhih a ka tung ua ahih mah bang a ama tung a leng hih ding in ka hong uh," achi uhi.
english: The men of Judah said, “Why have you come up against us?” They said, “We have come up to bind Samson, to do to him as he has done to us.”

paite: Huchi in Judah gam a mi sangthum Etam suangpi tung ah ahoh ua, Samson kiang ah, "Philistiate i tung ua vaihawmte ahih uh thei lou na maw? Bangchidan a hichibang a ka tung ua thil hon hihta mai na hia oi?" achi uhi. Ama'n akiang uah, "Ka tung a, ahih bang ua ke'n leng amau tung a hih sam ka hi,” achi hi.
english: Then three thousand men of Judah went down to the cave in Etam’s rock, and said to Samson, “Don’t you know that the Philistines are rulers over us? What then is this that you have done to us?” He said to them, “As they did to me, so I have done to them.”

paite: Amau akiang ah, "Nang hon khaukhih a, Philistiate khut a hon pe dia hong kuan ka hi uh," achi uhi. Samson in akiang uah, "Noute'n hon that lou ding in ka kiang ah kichiam un," achi hi.
english: They said to him, “We have come down to bind you, that we may deliver you into the hand of the Philistines.” Samson said to them, “Swear to me that you will not attack me yourselves.”

paite: Amau akiang ah, "That lou e. Himahleh ka hon khaukhih tinten ding ua, akhut ua hon pe ding ka hi uh. Thah zaw ka hon that kei hial ding uh," achi uhi. Huchi in khauzen thak nih in akhih ua, suangpi a pan apita uhi.
english: They spoke to him, saying, “No, but we will bind you securely and deliver you into their hands; but surely we will not kill you.” They bound him with two new ropes, and brought him up from the rock.

paite: Lehi mun ahong tun in, Philistiate'n ana dawn ua, ana kikou zuazua uhi. TOUPA kha atung ah nakpitak in ahong tung a, huchi in aban a gakna khauzen ziza zang mei in kangtat bang mai ahong hita a, agaknate a khut a pan akekhe niang maimah uhi.
english: When he came to Lehi, the Philistines shouted as they met him. Then Yahweh’s Spirit came mightily on him, and the ropes that were on his arms became as flax that was burned with fire; and his bands dropped from off his hands.

paite: Sabiltung khaguh thak amu a, asawk a, ala a, huai in mi sangkhat asatlum hi.
english: He found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, put out his hand, took it, and struck a thousand men with it.

paite: Samson in, "Sabiltung khaguh in ka chiang vum venvon a, sabiltung khaguh in mi sangkhat ka satlum,” achi hi.
english: Samson said, “With the jawbone of a donkey, heaps on heaps; with the jawbone of a donkey I have struck a thousand men.”

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, athugen khit in akhaguh tawi apai a; huai mun Ramath Lehi asa hi.
english: When he had finished speaking, he threw the jawbone out of his hand; and that place was called Ramath Lehi.

paite: Adang atak mahmah a, TOUPA asam a, "Nang na sikha khut zang in thupitak in na hon hunkheta hi. Tu in dangtak in ka si mai ding maw? Zeksumlouhte khut ah ka puklut dia hia?" achi hi.
