paite: Laisiangthou in: "Ngai in, Zion ah kisuihna suang leh pukna suangpi ka koih a, kuapeuh amah gingta tuh azahlak kei ding," chih gelh bang in.
english: even as it is written, “Behold, I lay in Zion a stumbling stone and a rock of offense; and no one who believes in him will be disappointed.”

paite: Vaihawm mite'n vai ahawm lai un hichi ahong ahi. Huai gam ah kial akia hi. Judah gam a Bethlehem mi khat Moab gam a teng tadih ding in amah leh azi leh atapate nih toh ahoh uhi.
english: In the days when the judges judged, there was a famine in the land. A certain man of Bethlehem Judah went to live in the country of Moab with his wife and his two sons.

paite: Huai mi min Elimelek ahi, azi min Naomi ahi, atapate nih min Mahlon leh Kilon ahi. Amau Judah gam a Bethlehem, Ephrath mi ahi uh. Moab gam ah ahoh ua, huai ah a-om nilouh uhi.
english: The name of the man was Elimelech, and the name of his wife Naomi. The names of his two sons were Mahlon and Chilion, Ephrathites of Bethlehem Judah. They came into the country of Moab and lived there.

paite: Elimelek, Naomi pasal asi a, amah leh atapate nih kia ahita uh.
english: Elimelech, Naomi’s husband, died; and she was left with her two sons.

paite: Amau Moab gam numei zi in anei ua, akhat pen min Orpah ahi a, akhat pen min Ruth ahi. Huai ah kum sawm a-omta uhi.
english: They took for themselves wives of the women of Moab. The name of the one was Orpah, and the name of the other was Ruth. They lived there about ten years.

paite: Mahlon leh Kilon asi tuaktuak ua; huchi in huai numei atapate nih leh apasal in asihsanta uhi.
english: Mahlon and Chilion both died, and the woman was bereaved of her two children and of her husband.

paite: Huchi in amoute toh Moab gam a pan kik nawn ding in akisa uh; TOUPA'N nek ding pia a mite avehdan Moab gam a pan ana zak ziak in.
english: Then she arose with her daughters-in-law, that she might return from the country of Moab; for she had heard in the country of Moab how Yahweh had visited his people in giving them bread.

paite: Huchi in a-omna a pan amoute nih toh apawt ua; Judah gam a kik nawn ding in apaita uhi.
english: She went out of the place where she was, and her two daughters-in-law with her. They went on the way to return to the land of Judah.

paite: Naomi in amou nihte kiang ah, "Na nute uh inn tuak ah pai nawnta un. Misi tung leh ka tung a siamtak a na hih bang un TOUPA'N na tung uah hih hen.
english: Naomi said to her two daughters-in-law, “Go, return each of you to her mother’s house. May Yahweh deal kindly with you, as you have dealt with the dead and with me.

paite: TOUPA'N na nih un na pasalte uh inn a khawlna na muhtheihna ding un hon hehpih hen," achi hi. Huchi in atawp a, aw suah hial in akapta uhi.
english: May Yahweh grant you that you may find rest, each of you in the house of her husband.” Then she kissed them, and they lifted up their voices, and wept.

paite: Amau akiang ah, "Pai kei ni ung, na chite kiang a na paina ah ka tel sam ding uh," achi uhi.
english: They said to her, “No, but we will return with you to your people.”

paite: Naomi in, "Ka tanute aw, pai nawn zaw un. Bangziak a ka kiang a hong pai lai mahmah ding na hi ua? Na pasal ding uh tapate ka pai thei nawn dia hia?
english: Naomi said, “Go back, my daughters. Why do you want to go with me? Do I still have sons in my womb, that they may be your husbands?

paite: Ka tanute aw, kisa unla, pai un; pasal nei ding in lah ka upa lota ngal a. Lametna ka nei chi mah leng, tuzan mahmah in leng pasal nei in tapate leng nei mah leng,
english: Go back, my daughters, go your way; for I am too old to have a husband. If I should say, ‘I have hope,’ if I should even have a husband tonight, and should also bear sons,

paite: apichin tan ua om ding na hi ding uam? Pasal lou in na om nilouh ding ua hia? Hi tel lou e, ka tanute aw; nou ziak in ka lungkhamna a-uang semsem hi. TOUPA khut ka tung a tu ahita ve," achi hi.
english: would you then wait until they were grown? Would you then refrain from having husbands? No, my daughters, for it grieves me seriously for your sakes, for Yahweh’s hand has gone out against me.”

paite: A-aw uh suah in akap nawn leuleu uhi. Huchi in Orpah in api atawp a; Ruth in bel alen tinten hi.
english: They lifted up their voices and wept again; then Orpah kissed her mother-in-law, but Ruth stayed with her.

paite: Ama'n, "Ngai in, na moupihnu achite kiang leh apathian kiang ah apaikik nawnta. Nang leng na moupihnu delh inla, pai nawnta in," achi hi.
english: She said, “Behold, your sister-in-law has gone back to her people and to her god. Follow your sister-in-law.”

paite: Ruth in, "Nang khen ding leh nang zui lou a kik nawn ding in hon kun ke'n. Na paina peuh ah ka pai dia; na giahna peuh ah ka giak dia; na chite ka chite ahi ding ua, na Pathian ka Pathian ahi ding.
english: Ruth said, “Don’t urge me to leave you, and to return from following you, for where you go, I will go; and where you stay, I will stay. Your people will be my people, and your God my God.

paite: Na sihna peuh ah ka si dia, huai ah na hon vui sam ding ahi. Nang leh kei sihna lou ngal thil dang in ahon khenleh TOUPA'N ahihhih in hon hih henla, hiai sang a thupizaw in leng," achi hi.
english: Where you die, I will die, and there I will be buried. May Yahweh do so to me, and more also, if anything but death parts you and me.”

paite: Huchi in akiang a pai atum tinten chih atheih in adaihsanta hi.
english: When Naomi saw that she was determined to go with her, she stopped urging her.

paite: Huchi in Bethlehem tan apaikhawmta uh. Huan hichi ahong hi a, Bethlehem atun un, akhozang un aling ua, numeite'n, "Hiai Naomi ahi maw?" achi uhi.
english: So they both went until they came to Bethlehem. When they had come to Bethlehem, all the city was excited about them, and they asked, “Is this Naomi?”

paite: Ama'n akiang uah, "Naomi hon chi kei un. Mara hon chi zaw un, Bangkim hihtheipa'n lah khatak in ahon hihta ngal a," achi hi.
english: She said to them, “Don’t call me Naomi. Call me Mara, for the Almighty has dealt very bitterly with me.

paite: "Buchingtak in ka pawt a, ToUPA'N avuak in hon pi nawn hi. TOUPA'N ka tung ah alungkimlouhna ahihlang a, Bangkim hihtheipa'n ahon hihgentheihdan theigige napi a bangziak a Naomi hon chi lailai na hi ua?" achi hi.
english: I went out full, and Yahweh has brought me home again empty. Why do you call me Naomi, since Yahweh has testified against me, and the Almighty has afflicted me?”

paite: Huchi in Naomi ahong kik a, amounu Moab mi Ruth toh Moab gam a pan ahong kik uhi. Barli buhlak pat tung lai in Bethlehem atung uhi.
english: So Naomi returned, and Ruth the Moabitess, her daughter-in-law, with her, who returned out of the country of Moab. They came to Bethlehem in the beginning of barley harvest.

paite: Huan Naomi in apasal tanau, Elimelek beh, mineizoutak tanau anei a; amin Boaz ahi.
english: Naomi had a relative of her husband’s, a mighty man of wealth, of the family of Elimelech, and his name was Boaz.

paite: Moab mi Ruth in Naomi kiang ah, "Lou ah ka va hoh dia, buhsang ka va zong ding aw, hon deihsakmi kuate hiam va tuak moh lou ka hi,” achi hi. Ama'n akiang ah, "Hoh in, ka tanu," achi hi.
english: Ruth the Moabitess said to Naomi, “Let me now go to the field, and glean among the ears of grain after him in whose sight I find favor.” She said to her, “Go, my daughter.”

paite: Huchi in ahohta a, buh la mite lakmaih ava zong a; huchi in Elimelek beh Boaz lou ah ava hoh kha geih hi.
english: She went, and came and gleaned in the field after the reapers; and she happened to come to the portion of the field belonging to Boaz, who was of the family of Elimelech.

paite: Huchi in ngai in, Bethlehem a pan Boaz ava hoh a, buh la mite kiang ah, “Na kiang uah TOUPA om hen," achi hi. Amau, “TOUPA'N nang hon vualzawl hen,” chi in adawng uhi.
english: Behold, Boaz came from Bethlehem, and said to the reapers, “May Yahweh be with you.” They answered him, “May Yahweh bless you.”

paite: Huchi in Boaz in asikha, buh la mite tung a heutu kiang ah, “Hiai kua nungaknou ahia oi?” achi hi.
english: Then Boaz said to his servant who was set over the reapers, “Whose young lady is this?”

paite: Abuh la mite tung a heutu asikha in, "Moab nungaknou, Moab gam a pan Naomi toh hong pai ahi.
english: The servant who was set over the reapers answered, “It is the Moabite lady who came back with Naomi out of the country of Moab.

paite: Ama'n, 'hon hehpih inla, na buhsang ka zong dia, buh la mite'n abuhphal uh alakkhawm khit chiang un ka zong zel ding aw' achi hi. Huchi in ahong pai a, inn a tomchik a-om chih louh zingsang a pan a-om nilouh hi," chi in adawng hi.
english: She said, ‘Please let me glean and gather after the reapers among the sheaves.’ So she came, and has continued even from the morning until now, except that she rested a little in the house.”

paite: Huchi in Boaz in Ruth kiang ah, "Ka tanu, ngai dih, buhsang zong in lou dang ah hoh ke'nla, hiai a pan paisuan ke'n. Ka sikha nungakte kiang ah om gige in.
english: Then Boaz said to Ruth, “Listen, my daughter. Don’t go to glean in another field, and don’t go from here, but stay here close to my maidens.

paite: Abuhlak uh en gige inla, anung uh sui zel in. Tangvalte nang bangmah hon chih lou ding in thu ka pevekta hi. Na dangtak peuh chiang in tuibel a tangvalte tui tawisa dawn zel in," achi hi.
english: Let your eyes be on the field that they reap, and go after them. Haven’t I commanded the young men not to touch you? When you are thirsty, go to the vessels, and drink from that which the young men have drawn.”

paite: Huchi in akun a, lei si in abokkhup a, akiang ah, "Namdang hinapi ing a, nang hichibang a na hon theihnop a, na mitmuh a deihsakna ka tan bangchidan ahia?" achi hi.
english: Then she fell on her face and bowed herself to the ground, and said to him, “Why have I found favor in your sight, that you should take knowledge of me, since I am a foreigner?”

paite: Boaz in adawng a, akiang ah, "Na pasal sih nungsiah na pi tung a na thilhihdan tengteng mi'n ahon hilh vek uh. Na nu leh na pa leh na pianna gam paisan atum a lam a na mi theih ngeilouhte kiang a na hong paidante leng.
english: Boaz answered her, “I have been told all about what you have done for your mother-in-law since the death of your husband, and how you have left your father, your mother, and the land of your birth, and have come to a people that you didn’t know before.

paite: TOUPA'N na thilhih hon din henla, TOUPA, Israelte' Pathian, kihumbitna dia akha nuai na muan in kipahman tampi hon pia hen," achi hi.
english: May Yahweh repay your work, and a full reward be given to you from Yahweh, the God of Israel, under whose wings you have come to take refuge.”

paite: Ama'n, "Ka toupa, na mitmuh in deihsakna ka tang a, na hon lungmuan a, na sikha nungakte lak a mi hi kei mah leng, na sikhanu hoihtak in na hon houpihta ngal a,” achi hi.
english: Then she said, “Let me find favor in your sight, my lord, because you have comforted me, and because you have spoken kindly to your servant, though I am not as one of your servants.”

paite: An nek hun in Boaz in akiang ah, "Hong pai inla, tanghoute hong ne sam inla, tanghou themte uain thuk ah hong diah in,” achi hi. Huchi in buh la mite kiang ah atu a; buhkan apia a; ane a, anek nung in leng akhamval lai hi.
english: At meal time Boaz said to her, “Come here, and eat some bread, and dip your morsel in the vinegar.” She sat beside the reapers, and they passed her parched grain. She ate, was satisfied, and left some of it.

paite: Buhsang zong dia adin nawn in, Boaz in atangvalte kiang ah, "Buhphalte lak ah leng tawmsak zel unla, tai kei un.
english: When she had risen up to glean, Boaz commanded his young men, saying, “Let her glean even among the sheaves, and don’t reproach her.

paite: Alomte leng dohkhiaksak unla, nutsiat zel unla, tom henla, tai kei un," chỉ in thu apia hi.
english: Also pull out some for her from the bundles, and leave it. Let her glean, and don’t rebuke her.”

paite: Huchi in lou a buhsang nitaklam tan in azong hi. Azonsa akhen a, barli buh ephah khat hiamtak apha hi.
english: So she gleaned in the field until evening; and she beat out that which she had gleaned, and it was about an ephah of barley.

paite: Avan kisuan in khopi ah apaita hi. Api in abuhsang zon ana mu a; ama'n anek kham val asitte asuahkhia a, apia hi.
english: She took it up, and went into the city. Then her mother-in-law saw what she had gleaned; and she brought out and gave to her that which she had left after she had enough.

paite: Api in akiang ah, "Tuni a koilam a buhsang zong na hia? Koi ah ahia na va sep? Ahon na theinuampa vualzawl in om hen," achi hi. Ama'n kua kiang ah ahia ava sep chih api ahilh hi. "Tuni a nna ka va sepna pa min Boaz ahi,” achi hi.
english: Her mother-in-law said to her, “Where have you gleaned today? Where have you worked? Blessed be he who noticed you.” She told her mother-in-law with whom she had worked, “The man’s name with whom I worked today is Boaz.”

paite: Naomi in amounu kiang ah, "TOUPA, mihing leh misi tung a ahehpihna tawp tuan ngei lou in amah vualzawl hen,” achi hi. Naomi in akiang ah, "Huai mi, i kinaihpih, i tanau bul ei ve,” achi hi.
english: Naomi said to her daughter-in-law, “May he be blessed by Yahweh, who has not abandoned his kindness to the living and to the dead.” Naomi said to her, “The man is a close relative to us, one of our near kinsmen.”

paite: Moab mi Ruth in, "Kei kiang a leng hon chi ei ve,” achi hi.
english: Ruth the Moabitess said, “Yes, he said to me, ‘You shall stay close to my young men until they have finished all my harvest.’”

paite: Naomi in amounu Ruth kiang ah, "Ka tanu, lou dang a ahon muh hetlouhna ding in asikha nungakte lak ngen ah pai lechin ahoih ding," achi hi.
english: Naomi said to Ruth her daughter-in-law, “It is good, my daughter, that you go out with his maidens, and that they not harm you in any other field.”

paite: Huchi in barli buh leh buhpi lak khit mateng Boaz sikha nungakte lak kia ah buhsang zong in ahoh a, api kiang ah ateng hi.
english: So she stayed close to the maidens of Boaz, to glean to the end of barley harvest and of wheat harvest; and she lived with her mother-in-law.

paite: Huan api Naomi, apasal nu'n akiang ah, "Ka tanu, nang a ding in khawlna ka hon zonsak kei dia hia, huchi in nang a ding in ahoih ding hi.
english: Naomi her mother-in-law said to her, “My daughter, shall I not seek rest for you, that it may be well with you?

paite: I tanaupa Boaz, asikha nungakte toh nna na sepna pa om hilou hia? Ngai in, tuzan in phual ah barli buh azapsiang ding hi.
english: Now isn’t Boaz our kinsman, with whose maidens you were? Behold, he will be winnowing barley tonight on the threshing floor.

paite: Huchi in kisil inla, thau kinilh inla, na kizepna puan silh inla, phual ah va hohsuk in. Himahleh an ne a, adawn khit masiah akiang ah kitheisak ke'n.
english: Therefore wash yourself, anoint yourself, get dressed, and go down to the threshing floor; but don’t make yourself known to the man until he has finished eating and drinking.

paite: Huan hichi ahi ding a, alup chiang in alupna chiamteh inla, lut inla, akhe lem inla, va lum in. Ama'n na hih ding ahon hilh ding," achi hi.
english: It shall be, when he lies down, that you shall note the place where he is lying. Then you shall go in, uncover his feet, and lie down. Then he will tell you what to do.”

paite: Ama'n akiang ah, "Na gen teng ka hih ding," achi hi.
english: She said to her, “All that you say, I will do.”

paite: Huchi in phual ah ahohsuk a, api hilh bang in ava hihta hi.
english: She went down to the threshing floor, and did everything that her mother-in-law told her.

paite: Boaz in an ne a, adawn khit in alungtang akipak a, buhvum bul a lum ding in apaita a, huan, minu leng awlawl in ahong pai a, akhe alem a, alumta hi.
english: When Boaz had eaten and drunk, and his heart was merry, he went to lie down at the end of the heap of grain. She came softly, uncovered his feet, and lay down.

paite: Huan hichi ahong hi a, ngai in, akhe kiang ah numei khat ana lumta mai a, zan lai in huai mipa kiguih in akihei hi.
english: At midnight, the man was startled and turned himself; and behold, a woman lay at his feet.

paite: Ama'n, "Kua na hia?” achi hi. Ama'n, "Na sikhanu Ruth ka hi. Huchi in na sikhanu na puan hon zawn in, ka tanau bul lah na hi ngal a," achi hi.
english: He said, “Who are you?” She answered, “I am Ruth your servant. Therefore spread the corner of your garment over your servant; for you are a near kinsman.”

paite: Ama'n, "Ka tanu, TOUPA'N nang hon vualzawl hen. Tangval zawng hiam, hausa hiam na zuih louh in atung lai sang in anunglam ah hoihna na hihlang zaw hi.
english: He said, “You are blessed by Yahweh, my daughter. You have shown more kindness in the latter end than at the beginning, because you didn’t follow young men, whether poor or rich.

paite: Huchi in ka tanu, lau ke'n. Na gen bang in na tung ah ka hih ding. I khua a mi tengteng in numei kizentak na hi chih athei vek ngal ua.
english: Now, my daughter, don’t be afraid. I will do to you all that you say; for all the city of my people knows that you are a worthy woman.

paite: Kitanau nai i hi ngut hi. Himahleh kei sang a naizaw a-om hi.
english: Now it is true that I am a near kinsman. However, there is a kinsman nearer than I.

paite: Tuzan zaw om peuhmah inla, zingchiang zingsang in na tung a ama'n atanau hih ding ahihnopleh ahoih hi. Himahleh tanau hih ding na tung a ahihnop keileh, tanau hih ding pen TOUPA ahin bang in ke'n ka hih ding. Zingsang tan lum nilouh in,” achi hi.
english: Stay this night, and in the morning, if he will perform for you the part of a kinsman, good. Let him do the kinsman’s duty. But if he will not do the duty of a kinsman for you, then I will do the duty of a kinsman for you, as Yahweh lives. Lie down until the morning.”

paite: Huchi in zingsang tan in akhebul ah alum hi. Kuamah akimuh chet theih ma in athoukhia hi. Ama'n, "Phual ah numei a hong chih himhim kuamah in thei kei hen," achi hi.
english: She lay at his feet until the morning, then she rose up before one could discern another. For he said, “Let it not be known that the woman came to the threshing floor.”

paite: Akiang ah, "Na puansilh la inla, doh in," achi hi. Huchi in adoh a, barli buh tehna guk atehsak a, asuan a; huchi in khua ah apaita hi.
english: He said, “Bring the mantle that is on you, and hold it.” She held it; and he measured six measures of barley, and laid it on her; then he went into the city.

paite: Api kiang atun in, "Ka tanu, bang na hong chi a?" ana chi hi. Ama'n, huai mipa in atung a thil ana hih tengteng ahilhta hi.
english: When she came to her mother-in-law, she said, “How did it go, my daughter?” She told her all that the man had done for her.

paite: "Hiai barli buh tehna guk ahon pia a, 'na pi kiang ah avuak in pai ke'n,' ahon chi," achi hi.
english: She said, “He gave me these six measures of barley; for he said, ‘Don’t go empty to your mother-in-law.’”

paite: Ama'n, "Ka tanu, bangchibang in ahia thil ahong om ding na theih ma in tu maimai in. Tuni a hiai thil ahih khit mateng huai mipa dai mai lou ding ahi," achi hi.
english: Then she said, “Wait, my daughter, until you know what will happen; for the man will not rest until he has settled this today.”

paite: Huchi in Boaz kulh kongpi ah ahohtou a, huai ah atu hi. Ngai in, atanau bul uh atungtang thu Boaz in agen ahong pai hi. Huai mi kiang ah, "Eh! Nang na hi maw! Hong pai inla, hong tu dih ve," achi hi. Amah hong pai in atuta hi.
english: Now Boaz went up to the gate and sat down there. Behold, the near kinsman of whom Boaz spoke came by. Boaz said to him, “Come over here, friend, and sit down!” He came over, and sat down.

paite: Huai khua a upate lak a mi sawm api a, akiang uah, "Hiai ah tu dih ua," achi a, huchi in amau atuta uhi.
english: Boaz took ten men of the elders of the city, and said, “Sit down here,” and they sat down.

paite: Atanau bul uh kiang ah, "Moab gam a pan hong kik Naomi in i unaupa Elimelek gam azuak hi.
english: He said to the near kinsman, “Naomi, who has come back out of the country of Moab, is selling the parcel of land, which was our brother Elimelech’s.

paite: Huchi in khomite mitmuh leh ka mite upate mitmuh in lei in. Na tat nopleh tan in. Himahleh na tatnop keileh ka theihtheihna ding in hon hilh in. Nang lou lah kuamah atan dia kilawm a-om ngal kei ua. Nang zom in kei ka hi chih nang hon theihsak kiphamoh in ka thei,” achi hi. Ama'n, "Ka tan ding," achi hi.
english: I thought I should tell you, saying, ‘Buy it before those who sit here, and before the elders of my people.’ If you will redeem it, redeem it; but if you will not redeem it, then tell me, that I may know. For there is no one to redeem it besides you; and I am after you.” He said, “I will redeem it.”

paite: Boaz in, "Naomi khut a pan huai gam na lei ni'n, misi zi, Moab numei Ruth a pan misi min bei lou a, agouluah ding mi a-om zel theihna ding in na lei tel ding ahi," achi hi.
english: Then Boaz said, “On the day you buy the field from the hand of Naomi, you must buy it also from Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of the dead, to raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance.”

paite: Atanau bulpa in, "Kei a ding in zaw ka tan thei kei. Huchi lou in zaw keimah gouluah ka mansuah kha ding. Ka tattheihna nang tang mai in. Ke'n zaw tan thei lou ka himai hi,” achi hi.
english: The near kinsman said, “I can’t redeem it for myself, lest I endanger my own inheritance. Take my right of redemption for yourself; for I can’t redeem it.”

paite: Nidanglai a Israelte lak a thil bangkim ahihkipna ding ua akitatdan uleh akikhendan uh hichi ahi. Khedap aphel ua, avengte uh apia ua, huai Israelte lak a ahihdan uh ahi.
english: Now this was the custom in former time in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning exchanging, to confirm all things: a man took off his sandal, and gave it to his neighbor; and this was the way of formalizing transactions in Israel.

paite: Huchi in atanau bulpa un Boaz kiang ah, "Nang a ding in lei zaw in," achi hi. Huchi in akhedap aphelta hi.
english: So the near kinsman said to Boaz, “Buy it for yourself,” then he took off his sandal.

paite: Boaz in upate leh mipi tengteng kiang ah, "Tuni in noute Elimelek thil neih tengteng leh Kilon leh Mahlon thil neih tengteng Naomi khut a pan ka lei chih theihpihtute na hi uh.
english: Boaz said to the elders and to all the people, “You are witnesses today, that I have bought all that was Elimelech’s, and all that was Chilion’s and Mahlon’s, from the hand of Naomi.

paite: Huai kia hilou in misi min amanlouhna ding in Moab numei Ruth, Mahlon zi ka zi ding in ka lei a, huai, tuni in noute atheihpihtute na hi uh," achi hi.
english: Moreover, Ruth the Moabitess, the wife of Mahlon, I have purchased to be my wife, to raise up the name of the dead on his inheritance, that the name of the dead may not be cut off from among his brothers and from the gate of his place. You are witnesses today.”

paite: Kulh kongpi a mipi tengteng leh upate'n, "Theihpihtute ka hi uh. Na inn a numei hong lut Rakil leh Leah, Israel inkuan dingsak nihte bang in TOUPA'N bawl hen. Nang Ephrathah ah suanhuaitak in hong om inla, Bethlehem ah minthangtak in hong om in.
english: All the people who were in the gate, and the elders, said, “We are witnesses. May Yahweh make the woman who has come into your house like Rachel and like Leah, which both built the house of Israel; and treat you worthily in Ephrathah, and be famous in Bethlehem.

paite: TOUPA'N hiai nungaknou a pan suan ahon bawlsak ding ziak in na inkuan uh Tamar in Judah asuansak Perez inkuan bang hong hi hen," achi uhi.
english: Let your house be like the house of Perez, whom Tamar bore to Judah, of the offspring which Yahweh will give you by this young woman.”

paite: Huchi in Boaz in Ruth api a, azi ahong hita hi. Huchi in akithuahpih a, TOUPA'N nau apaisak a, tapa anei hi.
english: So Boaz took Ruth and she became his wife; and he went in to her, and Yahweh enabled her to conceive, and she bore a son.

paite: Numeite'n Naomi kiang ah, "Tuni mahmah a tanau nai bei a hon omsak lou, TOUPA phat in om hen. Israelte lak ah amin hong thang hen.
english: The women said to Naomi, “Blessed be Yahweh, who has not left you today without a near kinsman. Let his name be famous in Israel.

paite: Amah na hinna tungdingpa leh na tek lam a hon vakpa ahong hi dia; na mounu nang hon itnu, tapa sagihte sang a nang a dia hoih in amah lah asuangta ngal a," achi uhi.
english: He shall be to you a restorer of life and sustain you in your old age; for your daughter-in-law, who loves you, who is better to you than seven sons, has given birth to him.”

paite: Naomi in nau ala a, apom a, adonta hi.
english: Naomi took the child, laid him in her bosom, and became nurse to him.

paite: A-inveng numeite'n amin aphuak ua, "Naomi a ding in tapa ahong piangta," chi in amin Obed asa uhi. Amah, David pa Jesse pa ahi.
english: The women, her neighbors, gave him a name, saying, “A son is born to Naomi”. They named him Obed. He is the father of Jesse, the father of David.

paite: Hiaite Perez suante ahi uh. Perez in Hezron asuang;
english: Now this is the history of the generations of Perez: Perez became the father of Hezron,

paite: Hezron in Ram asuang; Ram in Amminadab asuang;
english: and Hezron became the father of Ram, and Ram became the father of Amminadab,

paite: Amminadab in Nashon asuang a, Nashon in Salmon asuang;
english: and Amminadab became the father of Nahshon, and Nahshon became the father of Salmon,

paite: Salmon in Boaz asuang a, Boaz in Obed asuang;
english: and Salmon became the father of Boaz, and Boaz became the father of Obed,

paite: Obed in Jesse asuang a, Jesse in David asuang hi.
english: and Obed became the father of Jesse, and Jesse became the father of David.

paite: Late la, Solomon' a.
english: The Song of songs, which is Solomon’s.

paite: Atawpna kam in hon tawp hen aw! Na itna lah uain sang in ahoihzaw ngal a.
english: Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth; for your love is better than wine.

paite: Na kinuhte'n gimlim hoihtak anei a, na min kinuh butkhiak bang ahi a, huaiziak in nungak siangthoute'n nang ahon it uhi.
english: Your oils have a pleasing fragrance. Your name is oil poured out, therefore the virgins love you.

paite: Hon kai in, nang ka hon delh ding; kumpipa'n adantante sung ah ahon pita a, nang ah ka kipak un nuam ka sa ding uh, uain sang in na itna ka genkhe mun zaw ding ua; adikte'n nang ahon it uhi.
english: Take me away with you. Let’s hurry. The king has brought me into his rooms. Friends We will be glad and rejoice in you. We will praise your love more than wine! Beloved They are right to love you.

paite: Ka vom a, himahleh ka mel ahoih hi, Aw nou Jerusalem tanute, Kedar puaninte bang, Solomon puankhaite bang.
english: I am dark, but lovely, you daughters of Jerusalem, like Kedar’s tents, like Solomon’s curtains.

paite: Ka vom ziak in hon en ke'n, ni in ahon hai ziak in. Ka nu tapate ka tung ah athangpai ua, grephuante kem in ahon bawl ua; himahleh keimah grephuan leng ka kem kei.
english: Don’t stare at me because I am dark, because the sun has scorched me. My mother’s sons were angry with me. They made me keeper of the vineyards. I haven’t kept my own vineyard.

paite: Hon hilh ve, aw nang ka kha in a-it, na ganhon vakna mun, sun lai a na khawlsakna mun; bang ding a na kithuahpihte lak a ganhon kiang a maituam bang a kei om ding ka hia?
english: Tell me, you whom my soul loves, where you graze your flock, where you rest them at noon; for why should I be as one who is veiled beside the flocks of your companions?

paite: Na theih keileh, Aw nang numeite lak a kilawmpen, ganhonte khapte zui in kuankhia inla, belamchingte puanin kiang ah na kelnoute vak in.
english: If you don’t know, most beautiful among women, follow the tracks of the sheep. Graze your young goats beside the shepherds’ tents.

paite: Aw ka it, Pharaoh kangtalaite lak a sakol toh ka hon teh hi.
english: I have compared you, my love, to a steed in Pharaoh’s chariots.

paite: Na kicheinate toh na biang akilawm a, na ngawng suangmantam khite toh.
english: Your cheeks are beautiful with earrings, your neck with strings of jewels.

paite: Dangka-eng samphekte dangka siatte toh ka hon bawlsak ding uh.
english: We will make you earrings of gold, with studs of silver.

paite: Kumpipa adohkan a atut lai in, ka spiknardi gimlim in anamtuina asawlkhia.
english: While the king sat at his table, my perfume spread its fragrance.

paite: Ka ngaihnou kei a ding in murrah gimlim bang ahi a, ka nawite kikal a om.
english: My beloved is to me a sachet of myrrh, that lies between my breasts.

paite: Ka ngaihnou kei a ding in Engedi grephuante a henna pak bawk bang ahi.
english: My beloved is to me a cluster of henna blossoms from the vineyards of En Gedi.

paite: Ngai in, na kilawm, ka it; ngai in, na kilawm; na mitte vahui bang ahi uh.
english: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves.

paite: Ngai in, na kilawm ka ngaihnou, ahi, anuam; i tutna nem leng ahing.
english: Behold, you are beautiful, my beloved, yes, pleasant; and our couch is verdant.

paite: Sidar singte i inkamte ahi a, i insunte meilah singte ahi.
english: The beams of our house are cedars. Our rafters are firs.

paite: Sharon pak ka hi, phaizang lili pak.
english: I am a rose of Sharon, a lily of the valleys.

paite: Ling lak a lili pak bang in, huchibang in tanute lak ah ka it a-om hi.
english: As a lily among thorns, so is my love among the daughters.

paite: Gamlak singte lak a epul kung bang in, huchibang in tapate lak ah ka ngaihnou a-om hi. Nakpi a kipahna toh aliim nuai ah ka tu a, agah ka chep in akhum hi.
english: As the apple tree among the trees of the wood, so is my beloved among the sons. I sat down under his shadow with great delight, his fruit was sweet to my taste.

paite: Ankuangluina inn ah ahon pi a, ka tung a kizak puanlap a-itna ahi.
english: He brought me to the banquet hall. His banner over me is love.

paite: Grep phoukeu in hon khou unla, epul thei in hon nem un; zawlngai in ka chi ana ngal a.
english: Strengthen me with raisins, refresh me with apples; for I am faint with love.

paite: Akhut veilam ka lu nuai ah a-om a, akhut taklam in ahon kawi hi.
english: His left hand is under my head. His right hand embraces me.

paite: Zuktal leh gam a zukpite ka hon ngen hi, Aw Jerusalem tanute, ka it hihbuai kei unla, phawng kei un, alungkim matan.
english: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.

paite: Ka ngaihnou aw! Ngai un, ahong hi, tangte tung ah atawm a, mual tungte ah adiang hi.
english: The voice of my beloved! Behold, he comes, leaping on the mountains, skipping on the hills.

paite: Ka ngaihnou zaw zuktal hiam ahihkeileh sakhi tuailai bang ahi; Ngai in, ka kulhbaang nunglam uah adingh a, tohlette ah a-en a, anannate ah amah akimusak.
english: My beloved is like a roe or a young deer. Behold, he stands behind our wall! He looks in at the windows. He glances through the lattice.

paite: Ka ngaihnou in thu agen a, ka kiang ah, "Pasal thou in, ka it, ka kilawmnou, hong pai meng in," achi hi.
english: My beloved spoke, and said to me, “Rise up, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.

paite: Ngai in, phalbi lah abeita ngal a, vuah atheuta a, apaimangta hi;
english: For behold, the winter is past. The rain is over and gone.

paite: Leitung ah pakte hong kilang a; vasate lasak hun ahong tung a, i gam uah vakhu aw akizata hi.
english: The flowers appear on the earth. The time of the singing has come, and the voice of the turtledove is heard in our land.

paite: Theipi kung in gahhingte aminsak a, grep guite apaklun uhi, agimlimte uh asuaksak uhi. Thou ve, ka it, ka kilawmnou hong pai meng in.
english: The fig tree ripens her green figs. The vines are in blossom. They give out their fragrance. Arise, my love, my beautiful one, and come away.”

paite: Mun sang a suangpi heng a om, vakhu bang na hi, na mel hon musak inla, na aw hon zasak in, na aw akhum a, na mel ahoih hi.
english: My dove in the clefts of the rock, in the hiding places of the mountainside, let me see your face. Let me hear your voice; for your voice is sweet and your face is lovely.

paite: Sehalte, grephuan hihsia, sehal neute hon matsak ve; ka grephuan uh apaklun ngal a.
english: Catch for us the foxes, the little foxes that plunder the vineyards; for our vineyards are in blossom.

paite: Ka ngaihnou kei a ahi, kei amah a ka hi; lili pak lak ah aganta aching a,
english: My beloved is mine, and I am his. He browses among the lilies.

paite: Ni ahong nem a, limliapte aman matan, ka ngaihnou, kihei inla, Bether mual tung a zuktal hiam sakhi tuailai bang in om in.
english: Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, turn, my beloved, and be like a roe or a young deer on the mountains of Bether.

paite: Zan a ka lupna tung a ka ihmut in, ka mang in ka it ka mu hi; amah ka zongzong a, himahleh ka mu kei.
english: By night on my bed, I sought him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.

paite: Ka thou ding a, khopi kim ah ka pai dia, kongzing leh lampi ah, amah ka kha in a-it ka zong ding, ka chi a ka zong hi, himahleh amah muh zoh in a-omta kei.
english: I will get up now, and go about the city; in the streets and in the squares I will seek him whom my soul loves. I sought him, but I didn’t find him.

paite: Khopi a vialpai veng mite'n ahon mu ua; akiang uah, "Amah ka kha in a-it na mu uhia?" ka chi a.
english: The watchmen who go about the city found me; “Have you seen him whom my soul loves?”

paite: Amaute ka paisan sawt louchik ahi, huan amah ka kha in a-it ka mu hi; ka paisak kei, ka nu insung, hon painu dantan sung a amah ka pilut masiah.
english: I had scarcely passed from them, when I found him whom my soul loves. I held him, and would not let him go, until I had brought him into my mother’s house, into the room of her who conceived me.

paite: Zuktal leh gam a zukpite in ka hon ngen hi, Aw Jerusalem tanute aw, ka it hihbuai kei unla, phawng kei un, alungkim matan.
english: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the roes, or by the hinds of the field, that you not stir up nor awaken love, until it so desires.

paite: Gamdai a kipan a meikhu kitung bang a hong pai murrah leh begaw kinuh a, sumsinmi nuhngou vui kinuh hiai kua ahia?
english: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness like pillars of smoke, perfumed with myrrh and frankincense, with all spices of the merchant?

paite: Ngai in, Solomon lupna ahi; akim ah mihat sawmguk, Israel mihatte a kipan a-om uh.
english: Behold, it is Solomon’s carriage! Sixty mighty men are around it, of the mighty men of Israel.

paite: Namsau atawi chiat ua, kidouna a kivate ahi uhi. Michih in apheipi tung ah namsau atawi chiat ua, zan a launa ziak in.
english: They all handle the sword, and are expert in war. Every man has his sword on his thigh, because of fear in the night.

paite: Kumpipa Solomon in Lebanon sing in kangtalai akibawl hi.
english: King Solomon made himself a carriage of the wood of Lebanon.

paite: Huai a khuamte dangka in abawl a, anuai dangka-eng, atutphah asandup, alaizang, Jerusalem tanute a kipan a- itna toh aphah ahi.
english: He made its pillars of silver, its bottom of gold, its seat of purple, the middle of it being paved with love, from the daughters of Jerusalem.

paite: Aw nou Zion tanute, pawtkhia unla, kumpipa Solomon en un, azineih ni leh alungtang kipahna ni a, anu'n amah lallukhu akhuksak toh.
english: Go out, you daughters of Zion, and see King Solomon, with the crown with which his mother has crowned him, in the day of his weddings, in the day of the gladness of his heart.

paite: Ngai in, na kilawm hi, ka it; ngai in, na kilawm hi; na maituamna liah ah na mitte vahui bang ahi ua; na sam kelhon bang ahi, Gilead tang pang a kualte.
english: Behold, you are beautiful, my love. Behold, you are beautiful. Your eyes are like doves behind your veil. Your hair is as a flock of goats, that descend from Mount Gilead.

paite: Na hate mulmet thak belamnu hon bang ahi ua, sil khit phet a hong paitoute; huai ah amaute chiat in phik anei ua, alak ua kuamah aching a-om kei uh.
english: Your teeth are like a newly shorn flock, which have come up from the washing, where every one of them has twins. None is bereaved among them.

paite: Na mukte khau san-au abang ua, na kam akilawm a; na mit laivomte theibuhfai them bang ahi, na maituamna liah ah.
english: Your lips are like scarlet thread. Your mouth is lovely. Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.

paite: Na ngawng David galvan koihna insang kilam bang ahi, lumbem neute sangkhat kikhaina mun, mihat lum in akivan uh.
english: Your neck is like David’s tower built for an armory, on which a thousand shields hang, all the shields of the mighty men.

paite: Na nawite zuktal nou nih phikte abang ua, lili pak lak a tate.
english: Your two breasts are like two fawns that are twins of a roe, which feed among the lilies.

paite: Ni anem a limliap aman mateng murrah tang ah leh, begaw mual ah ka hoh ding.
english: Until the day is cool, and the shadows flee away, I will go to the mountain of myrrh, to the hill of frankincense.

paite: Na kilawm hi, ka it; nang ah thilnin bangmah a-om kei hi.
english: You are all beautiful, my love. There is no spot in you.

paite: Lebanon a kipan hon zui in, ka mou, Lebanon a pan kei toh, Amana vum a kipan dak in, Shenir leh Hermon vum a kipan, humpinelkaite kua a kipan, gialbemte mual a kipan.
english: Come with me from Lebanon, my bride, with me from Lebanon. Look from the top of Amana, from the top of Senir and Hermon, from the lions’ dens, from the mountains of the leopards.

paite: Ka lungtang na tuahmangta, ka sanggamnu, ka mou; na mitte lak a khat in ka lungtang na tuahmangta hi, na ngawng a khainiang khat in.
english: You have ravished my heart, my sister, my bride. You have ravished my heart with one of your eyes, with one chain of your neck.

paite: Na itna kilawm na tel e, ka sanggamnu, ka mou! Na itna uain sang in nakpi in ahoihzaw! Na kinuh gim, gimlim chiteng sang in ahoihzaw.
english: How beautiful is your love, my sister, my bride! How much better is your love than wine, the fragrance of your perfumes than all kinds of spices!

paite: Na mukte, Aw ka mou, khuaikhak bang in atakkhia a; na lei nuai ah khuaizu leh nawitui a-om; na puansilh gim Lebanon gim ahi.
english: Your lips, my bride, drip like the honeycomb. Honey and milk are under your tongue. The smell of your garments is like the smell of Lebanon.

paite: Huan umsuak ka sanggamnu, ka mou; tui nak kihu, tui kivuh.
english: My sister, my bride, is a locked up garden; a locked up spring, a sealed fountain.

paite: Na huansung theibuhfai, gah manphate toh ahi; spiknardi sing suan toh henna pak ahi.
english: Your shoots are an orchard of pomegranates, with precious fruits, henna with spikenard plants,

paite: Spiknardi leh pak gimlim, kepbuk leh singnamtui begaw sing tengteng; murrah leh aloe, gimlim pipen teng toh.
english: spikenard and saffron, calamus and cinnamon, with every kind of incense tree; myrrh and aloes, with all the best spices,

paite: Huan atuikhuk na hi a, tuihing lui, Lebanon a kipan a lui luangte.
english: a fountain of gardens, a well of living waters, flowing streams from Lebanon.

paite: Khanglou in, Aw mallam huih; huan hong in, nang simlam; ka huan tung ah hong nung in, Na gimnamtuite aluankhiak theihna ding in. Ka ngaihnou ahuansung ah hong pai henla, atheigah manphate ne hen aw.
english: Awake, north wind, and come, you south! Blow on my garden, that its spices may flow out. Let my beloved come into his garden, and taste his precious fruits.

paite: Ka huansung ah ka hong pai hi, ka sanggamnu, ka mou; ka murrah ka gimnamtui toh ka lakhawmta; ka khuaikhak ka khuaizu toh ka neta a; ka uain ka nawitui toh ka dawnta. Aw, lawmte. Ne un; dawn un, ahi, tampi dawn un, Aw ka ngaihnou.
english: I have come into my garden, my sister, my bride. I have gathered my myrrh with my spice; I have eaten my honeycomb with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Friends Eat, friends! Drink, yes, drink abundantly, beloved.

paite: Ka ihmu a, himahleh ka lungtang ahak; Tua aw, ka ngaihnou kiuhna aw ahi. Pasal' Hon hon in, ka sanggamnu, ka it, ka vahui, ka nin baang lou; ka lutang daitui in adim a, ka samtum lah zan a tui tak in.
english: I was asleep, but my heart was awake. It is the voice of my beloved who knocks: “Open to me, my sister, my love, my dove, my undefiled; for my head is filled with dew, and my hair with the dampness of the night.”

paite: Ka puanak tung ka suahta a; bangchi in ka silh nawn dia? Ka khepekte ka silta a; bangchi in ka hihnin dia?
english: I have taken off my robe. Indeed, must I put it on? I have washed my feet. Indeed, must I soil them?

paite: Ka ngaihnou in kongkhak awng ah akhut ahon golhlut a, amah ziak in ka lungtang hihlin in a-om hi.
english: My beloved thrust his hand in through the latch opening. My heart pounded for him.

paite: Ka ngaihnou hon ding in ka thouta a; ka khutte murrah in atak a, ka khutzungte murrah tui in, kalhna hekna tung ah.
english: I rose up to open for my beloved. My hands dripped with myrrh, my fingers with liquid myrrh, on the handles of the lock.

paite: Ka ngaihnou ka honta a; himahleh ka ngaihnou ana kik nawn a, a-omta kei hi. Thu agen lai in ka kha in ahon zuausan a; amah ka zong a, himahleh hon dawng kei hi.
english: I opened to my beloved; but my beloved left, and had gone away. My heart went out when he spoke. I looked for him, but I didn’t find him. I called him, but he didn’t answer.

paite: Khopi a vialvak veng mite'n ahon mu ua, ahon khen ua, ahon liamsak uh; kulhbaang ngakte'n ka puanak ahon lakmangsak uh.
english: The watchmen who go about the city found me. They beat me. They bruised me. The keepers of the walls took my cloak away from me.

paite: K'on ngen ahi, Aw Jerusalem tanute, Ka ngaihnou na muh uleh, zawlngai in ka chi ana chih, amah na hilh un aw.
english: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, If you find my beloved, that you tell him that I am faint with love.

paite: Na ngaihnou, ngaihnou dang sang a atuansemna bang ahia? Aw nang numeite lak a kilawmpen? Na ngaihnou, ngaihnou dang sang a atuansemna bang ahia, huchibang na hon nget?
english: How is your beloved better than another beloved, you fairest among women? How is your beloved better than another beloved, that you do so adjure us?

paite: Ka ngaihnou zaw asan hiuhiau a, singkhat lak a makai lianpen ahi.
english: My beloved is white and ruddy. The best among ten thousand.

paite: Alutang dangka-eng hoihpen abang a, asamtumte alian a, va-ak bang in avom hi.
english: His head is like the purest gold. His hair is bushy, black as a raven.

paite: Amitte luita tui kiang a vahui bang ahi a; nawitui a sil, kituaktak a bulh ahi.
english: His eyes are like doves beside the water brooks, washed with milk, mounted like jewels.

paite: Abiangte gimnamtui omna bang ahi a, loupa gimlim bang; amukte lili pak bang ahi a, murrah tui takkhesak in.
english: His cheeks are like a bed of spices with towers of perfumes. His lips are like lilies, dropping liquid myrrh.

paite: Akhutte dangka-eng zungbuh beril suangmantam siatna bang ahi; apumpi saiha a bawl sapphir suangmantam a luan bang ahi.
english: His hands are like rings of gold set with beryl. His body is like ivory work overlaid with sapphires.

paite: Akhete suangpak khuam, dangka-eng hoihte kuak a kitung bang ahi; Akilatdan Lebanon bang, sidar bang a thupi ahi.
english: His legs are like pillars of marble set on sockets of fine gold. His appearance is like Lebanon, excellent as the cedars.

paite: Akam akhum penpen a; ahi, angaihhuai tuntun hi. Hiai ka ngaihnou ahi a, hiai ka lawm ahi. Aw Jerusalem tanute.
english: His mouth is sweetness; yes, he is altogether lovely. This is my beloved, and this is my friend, daughters of Jerusalem.

paite: Na ngaihnou koilam a pai ahia, Aw nang numeite lak a kilawm penpen? Amah na ngaihnou koilam a kiheita ahia, amah ka hon zonpih theihna ding un?
english: Where has your beloved gone, you fairest among women? Where has your beloved turned, that we may seek him with you?

paite: Ka ngaihnou ahuan ah ahohsuk a, gimnamtui mun ah, huansung a vak in, lili pak lakhawm ding in.
english: My beloved has gone down to his garden, to the beds of spices, to pasture his flock in the gardens, and to gather lilies.

paite: Ka ngaihnou a ka hi a, ka ngaihnou kei a ahi; lili pak lak ah aganta aching hi.
english: I am my beloved’s, and my beloved is mine. He browses among the lilies.

paite: Na kilawm hi, Aw ka it, Tirzah bang a kilawm, Jerusalem bang a deihhuai, na lauhuaina sepaih pawl puanlapte bang in ahi.
english: You are beautiful, my love, as Tirzah, lovely as Jerusalem, awesome as an army with banners.

paite: Kei a kipan na mitte lakik in, amau lah ahon zouta ua. Na sam Gilead pang a kual kelhon bang ahi.
english: Turn away your eyes from me, for they have overcome me. Your hair is like a flock of goats, that lie along the side of Gilead.

paite: Na hate belamnuhon bang ahi ua, sil khit phet a hong paitoute; huai ah amaute chiat in phik anei ua, alak uah kuamah aching a-om kei uh.
english: Your teeth are like a flock of ewes, which have come up from the washing, of which every one has twins; not one is bereaved among them.

paite: Na mit laivomte theibuhfai them na maituamna liah a om bang ahi.
english: Your temples are like a piece of a pomegranate behind your veil.

paite: Kumpinu sawmguk a-om ua, mei sawmgiat, huan nungak siangthou sim seng louh.
english: There are sixty queens, eighty concubines, and virgins without number.

paite: Ka vahui, ka nin baang lou, khat kia ahi; anu lak a amah kia ahi; amah suang lak a ahoihpen ahi. Tanute'n amah amu ua, nuamsa achi uhi, ahi, kumpinute leh ameite'n amah aphat uhi.
english: My dove, my perfect one, is unique. She is her mother’s only daughter. She is the favorite one of her who bore her. The daughters saw her, and called her blessed. The queens and the concubines saw her, and they praised her.

paite: Zingsang bang a dakkhia amah kua ahia? khapi bang a kilawm, ni bang a siang, sepaihhon puanlap bang a lauhuai?
english: Who is she who looks out as the morning, beautiful as the moon, clear as the sun, and awesome as an army with banners?

paite: Makhatang huan ah ka paisuak a, phaizang a sing suan hingte en ding in, grep apakmum hiam chih leh theibuhfai apakpalhta hiam chih en ding in.
english: I went down into the nut tree grove, to see the green plants of the valley, to see whether the vine budded, and the pomegranates were in flower.

paite: Ahihkeileh ka theihkhiak ma in ka kha in ka lunglutna ka mipite kangtalai lak ah ahon koihta hi.
english: Without realizing it, my desire set me with my royal people’s chariots.

paite: Hong kik in, hong kik in, aw Shulam mi; hong kik in, hong kik in, ka hon ettheihna ding un. Numei' Bangziak a Mahanaim mite lam en bang a Shulam mi en ding na hi ua?
english: Return, return, Shulammite! Return, return, that we may gaze at you. Lover Why do you desire to gaze at the Shulammite, as at the dance of Mahanaim?

paite: Khedap tung nei lou ah na khepekte kilawm hi na mahmah e, Aw kumpi tanu; na phei guhtuah suangmantam bang ahi ua, nasem mipil khut nasep bang.
english: How beautiful are your feet in sandals, prince’s daughter! Your rounded thighs are like jewels, the work of the hands of a skillful workman.

paite: Na lai noubem bang ahi, huai ah uain hel akitasam ngei kei a; na gilpi huit buh hum lili pak siat dim abang hi.
english: Your body is like a round goblet, no mixed wine is wanting. Your waist is like a heap of wheat, set about with lilies.

paite: Na nawi zuktal nou nih phik abang uhi.
english: Your two breasts are like two fawns, that are twins of a roe.

paite: Na ngawng saiha insang abang; na mitte Barthrabbim kongpi a, Heshbon a om dilte abang uh; na nak Lebanon a insang abang a Damaskas lam muhsukna om.
english: Your neck is like an ivory tower. Your eyes are like the pools in Heshbon by the gate of Bathrabbim. Your nose is like the tower of Lebanon which looks toward Damascus.

paite: Na tung a na lutang Karmel abang a, na lu a sam sandup abang; huai sampha lak ah kumpipa sal a mat in a-om hi.
english: Your head on you is like Carmel. The hair of your head like purple. The king is held captive in its tresses.

paite: Aw it, kipahna ding in nak kilawm in nak nop hi na mahmah chia!
english: How beautiful and how pleasant you are, love, for delights!

paite: Na sandan tum sing bang ahi a, na nawite grep gahbomte bang.
english: This, your stature, is like a palm tree, your breasts like its fruit.

paite: tum sing ah ka kaltou ding a, huai a hiangte ka len ding, ka chi a; na nawi grepgui gahbom bang hi henla, huan na nawi gim epul bang;
english: I said, “I will climb up into the palm tree. I will take hold of its fruit.” Let your breasts be like clusters of the vine, the smell of your breath like apples.

paite: Na kam uain hoihpen pen abang hi. Numei' Ka ngaihnou a dia nemtak a paisuk, ihmute muk a tolh paisuak.
english: Your mouth is like the best wine, that goes down smoothly for my beloved, gliding through the lips of those who are asleep.

paite: Ka ngaihnou a ka hi a, adeihlam kei lam ah a-om.
english: I am my beloved’s. His desire is toward me.

paite: Hong in, ka ngaihnou, gam ah i paikhe ding a; khoneute ah i giak ding.
english: Come, my beloved! Let’s go out into the field. Let’s lodge in the villages.

paite: Grephuan lam ah zingkhang in i thou ding a; Grepgui apakmumta hia, apakpalh akihongta hia i va en ding, huan theibuhfai apakkheta hia; huai ah ka itna ka hon pe ding hi.
english: Let’s go early up to the vineyards. Let’s see whether the vine has budded, its blossom is open, and the pomegranates are in flower. There I will give you my love.

paite: Zawlzongpak in gimnamtui asuaksak a, ka kongkhak uah thei manpha chikim, athak leh alui a-om, nang a ding in ka na kholkhawm, aw ngaihnou.
english: The mandrakes produce fragrance. At our doors are all kinds of precious fruits, new and old, which I have stored up for you, my beloved.

paite: Aw ka nu nawi ne, ka unaupa bang hi lechin maw! Polam a ka hon muhleh, ka hon tawp ding; Ahi, kuamah in ahon musit kei ding uh.
english: Oh that you were like my brother, who nursed from the breasts of my mother! If I found you outside, I would kiss you; yes, and no one would despise me.

paite: Nang ka hon pi ding a, ka nu inn sung ah ka hon lalut ding a, ama'n kei ahon hilh ding; uain namtui ka hon dawnsak ding a, ka theibuhfai tuining.
english: I would lead you, bringing you into the house of my mother, who would instruct me. I would have you drink spiced wine, of the juice of my pomegranate.

paite: Akhut veilam ka lu nuai ah a-om ding a, akhut taklam in ahon kawi ding hi.
english: His left hand would be under my head. His right hand would embrace me.

paite: K'on ngen hi, Aw Jerusalem tanute, ka it, hihbuai kei unla, phawng kei un, alungkim matan.
english: I adjure you, daughters of Jerusalem, that you not stir up, nor awaken love, until it so desires.

paite: Gamdai a kipan a hong tou hiai angaihnou tung a kingai kua ahia? Numei' Epul sing nuai ah ka hon phawng a; huai ah na nun nang ahon vei a, huai ah nang hon piangsak amah nauvei in a-om hi.
english: Who is this who comes up from the wilderness, leaning on her beloved? Beloved Under the apple tree I awakened you. There your mother conceived you. There she was in labor and bore you.

paite: Na lungtang a suai bang in, na ban a suai bang in kei hon koih in; itna lah sihna bang in ahat ngal a; han bang in agilou a; huai a kuangte meikuang TOUPA meikuang bang ahi uhi.
english: Set me as a seal on your heart, as a seal on your arm; for love is strong as death. Jealousy is as cruel as Sheol. Its flashes are flashes of fire, a very flame of Yah.

paite: Tui tampi in itna aphelh thei kei a, tui khangte'n atum thei kei hi; itna ziak in min a-inn a vante pe ding hitaleh, nakpitak a muhsit in a-om ding hi.
english: Many waters can’t quench love, neither can floods drown it. If a man would give all the wealth of his house for love, he would be utterly scorned.

paite: Sanggamnu neu ka nei ua, nawi anei kei. Atungtang kigen ni in ka sanggamnu uh a ding in bang ka hih ding ua?
english: We have a little sister. She has no breasts. What shall we do for our sister in the day when she is to be spoken for?

paite: Kulhbaang hileh bel, amah tung ah dangka insang neu khat ka lam ding ua; kongkhak hitaleh, amah sidar singpek in ka sungkhum ding uh.
english: If she is a wall, we will build on her a turret of silver. If she is a door, we will enclose her with boards of cedar.

paite: Kulhbaang ka hi a, ka nawite huai a insang bang ahi uh; huchih lai in mi muanna musa bang in amit ah ka om hi.
english: I am a wall, and my breasts like towers, then I was in his eyes like one who found peace.

paite: Baal-hamon ah Solomon in grephuan anei hi; kem mite kiang ah grephuan akhelsak a; huai a agah a ding in michih in dangka sangkhat ngen ahon tawi ding uh ahi.
english: Solomon had a vineyard at Baal Hamon. He leased out the vineyard to keepers. Each was to bring a thousand shekels of silver for its fruit.

paite: Grephuan, kei a ahi a, ka ma ah a-om; aw Solomon, nang, sang na nei ding a, huai a theigah kemte'n zanih.
english: My own vineyard is before me. The thousand are for you, Solomon, two hundred for those who tend its fruit.

paite: Nang huante sung a teng, na kithuahpihte'n na aw angai ua, huai hon zasak in.
english: You who dwell in the gardens, with friends in attendance, let me hear your voice!

paite: Kin meng in, ka ngaihnou, gimlim mual tung a zuktal hiam sakhi tuailai hiam bang in om in.
english: Come away, my beloved! Be like a gazelle or a young stag on the mountains of spices!

paite: Paul, Pathian sikha leh Jesu Khrist sawitak, Pathian mitelte, aginna uh lamtou ding leh Pathian limsakna toh kithuah thutak theisak ding a sem in;
english: Paul, a servant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the faith of God’s chosen ones and the knowledge of the truth which is according to godliness,

paite: huai tangtawn hinna lametna a kinga, Pathian zuaugen thei lou in khovel om ma a achiam,
english: in hope of eternal life, which God, who can’t lie, promised before time began;

paite: himahleh amah huntak ah thugenna zang in athu ahihlangta, huai thugenna Pathian i Hondampa thupiak bang zel a kepsak ka hi.
english: but in his own time revealed his word in the message with which I was entrusted according to the commandment of God our Savior,

paite: Ginna kibang a ka tapa diktak Titas kiang ah, Pathian leh Khrist Jesu i Hondampa kiang a kipan hehpihna, zahngaihna leh khamuanna om hen.
english: to Titus, my true child according to a common faith: Grace, mercy, and peace from God the Father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Savior.

paite: Hiai ziak in ahi huai Kret tuikulh a nang ka hon nutsiat, thilhih zoh nailouhte na hihzoh theihna ding leh thu ka hon piak bang a, khua teng a upate na sehtheihna ding in.
english: I left you in Crete for this reason, that you would set in order the things that were lacking and appoint elders in every city, as I directed you—

paite: Upa ding zaw gensiatbei, zi khat nei, tate Pathian gingta, nopsak bawl luatna lamsang a gensiat loh lou, dan bang lou a om lou, nei ahih peuhmah uleh,
english: if anyone is blameless, the husband of one wife, having children who believe, who are not accused of loose or unruly behavior.

paite: saptuam heutu Pathian nasep enkaimi ahih ziak in gensiatbei ahih ding ahi; migenhak, lunggam, uain khamhat, mivuak hat, punna nin a huaihammi hi ding hilou ahi.
english: For the overseer must be blameless, as God’s steward, not self-pleasing, not easily angered, not given to wine, not violent, not greedy for dishonest gain;

paite: Mi kipahpihdan siam, hoih lam deih, lungsim diktak, midiktat, misiangthou, kidektheimi ahih ding ahi.
english: but given to hospitality, a lover of good, sober minded, fair, holy, self-controlled,

paite: Asinsa thuhilhna dik midang sinsak thei leh selhat mite siam louh tangsak thei ding a sinsak a om thugin muanhuai lenkip mi ahi ding hi.
english: holding to the faithful word which is according to the teaching, that he may be able to exhort in the sound doctrine, and to convict those who contradict him.

paite: Dan bang lou a om, thu mawk gengen leh mikhem chingmi tampi, abik in zeksumte lak a mi a-om uhi.
english: For there are also many unruly men, vain talkers and deceivers, especially those of the circumcision,

paite: Huai mite kam humsak ding ahi, punna nin deih ziak a thuhilh louh ding hilh in, mite a-inkuankuan un apisia uhi.
english: whose mouths must be stopped: men who overthrow whole houses, teaching things which they ought not, for dishonest gain’s sake.

paite: Amaute lak a mi azawlnei khat un houh: "Kret tuikulh a mite zaw zuautheite, gamsa giloute, thadah anhaite ahi uh," achi hi.
english: One of them, a prophet of their own, said, “Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, and idle gluttons.”

paite: Hiai theihpihna adik ahi. Huaiziak in ginna a adiktheihna ding un leh,
english: This testimony is true. For this cause, reprove them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith,

paite: Judate tangthu phuahtawmte a kisubuai lou ding leh thutak nungngatsan nakte thupiak alimsaklouhna ding un naktak in taihilh in.
english: not paying attention to Jewish fables and commandments of men who turn away from the truth.

paite: Siangthoute a ding in bangkim asiangthou hi; himahleh minin leh gingloute a ding in bangmah siangthou a-om kei, alungsim uh asia-le-pha theihna uh leng anin hi.
english: To the pure, all things are pure, but to those who are defiled and unbelieving, nothing is pure; but both their mind and their conscience are defiled.

paite: Pathian thei akichi ua, himahleh athilhih un anawlkhin nak uhi. Kihhuaite, thumangloute, thil hoih sep ding peuhmah a deihlouhte ahi uhi.
english: They profess that they know God, but by their deeds they deny him, being abominable, disobedient, and unfit for any good work.

paite: Nang zaw thuhilhna hoih toh kituak thu gen in.
english: But say the things which fit sound doctrine,

paite: Putekte kidek thei, zahtakhuai, lungsim hoihtak, ginna leh itna leh kuhkalna a diktak hi ding in hanthawn in.
english: that older men should be temperate, sensible, sober minded, sound in faith, in love, and in perseverance,

paite: Pitekte leng huchibang in, sianthouna toh kimeh, khohei a zahdan siam ding leh heh hat lou, uain hai lou, thil hoihte zilsakte hi zaw ding in hanthawn in.
english: and that older women likewise be reverent in behavior, not slanderers nor enslaved to much wine, teachers of that which is good,

paite: Nungak deuhte tuh apasalte uh leh atate uh it ding leh lungsim hoihtak pu a om ding a ahilhtheihna ding un,
english: that they may train the young wives to love their husbands, to love their children,

paite: Pathian thu gensiat a a-omlouhna ding in theisiamtak a kithunun thei, beven lou, amau insung kem hiathiat, chingkam leh apasalte thuthu a om ding a athuhilh theihna ding in.
english: to be sober minded, chaste, workers at home, kind, being in subjection to their own husbands, that God’s word may not be blasphemed.

paite: Huai bang in, tangvalte lungsim hoihtak pu ding in hasuan in.
english: Likewise, exhort the younger men to be sober minded.

paite: Thil bangkim a thil hoih hih lam a etton ding in kibawl inla; na thugin sinsakna ah diktatna, chihtakna leh,
english: In all things show yourself an example of good works. In your teaching, show integrity, seriousness, incorruptibility,

paite: gensiat vual louh paukamte langsak lechin alehlam a nang hon demte'n nang tungtang thu a thusia gen ding nei lou a azumtheihna ding un.
english: and soundness of speech that can’t be condemned, that he who opposes you may be ashamed, having no evil thing to say about us.

paite: Sikhate, apute uh sel lou a athuthu a om ding leh bangkim a akipahna ding ua om ding in thuhilh in.
english: Exhort servants to be in subjection to their own masters and to be well-pleasing in all things, not contradicting,

paite: Pathian i hondampa thuhilhna thu bangkim a akilawmsak theihna ding un, khut them nei lou ding, muanhuai a nna hoih tengteng hihlang zaw ding in sinsak in.
english: not stealing, but showing all good fidelity, that they may adorn the doctrine of God, our Savior, in all things.

paite: Mi tengteng kiang ah hotdamna hon tun in i Pathian hehpihna ahong tungta hi.
english: For the grace of God has appeared, bringing salvation to all men,

paite: Pathian limsaklouhna leh khovel duhgawlna tawpsan in, tulai khovel ah kidek leh diktattak leh Pathian limsak in i om ding uh chih theisak in.
english: instructing us to the intent that, denying ungodliness and worldly lusts, we would live soberly, righteously, and godly in this present age;

paite: Lametna kipahhuai, i Pathian thupi leh Hondampa Jesu Khrist thupina kilakna ngak in.
english: looking for the blessed hope and appearing of the glory of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ,

paite: Ama'n tatlekna tengteng lak a kipan in ahon tattheihna ding in leh chitel tuam, thil hoih hih a phatuamngai, amah a ding a ahihsiangthou theihna ding in i sik in akipeta hi.
english: who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity and purify for himself a people for his own possession, zealous for good works.

paite: Thuneitak in huai thute hilh inla, hanthawn inla, taihilh in. Kuamah in nang hon musit kei uhen.
english: Say these things and exhort and reprove with all authority. Let no one despise you.

paite: Vaihawmte leh thuneite nuai a kitahlut a thumang ding leh thil hoih chiteng sem ding a mansa a om ding in sinsak inla,
english: Remind them to be in subjection to rulers and to authorities, to be obedient, to be ready for every good work,

paite: kuamah gensiatlouhdan ding, vuallemtak a omdan ding, mi tengteng lak a thunuailutna chiteng hihlang a, nunnem ding in amaute theikhe thaksak nawn in.
english: to speak evil of no one, not to be contentious, to be gentle, showing all humility toward all men.

paite: Ei leng nidanglai in mihai, thumang lou, khem a om, utna leh kipahna chiteng sem, gilou leh hazat hat a om, kihhuai leh kihotuahte i hi uhi.
english: For we were also once foolish, disobedient, deceived, serving various lusts and pleasures, living in malice and envy, hateful, and hating one another.

paite: Himahleh Pathian, i hondampa migitdan leh mihing tung a a-itdan ahong kilat lai in,
english: But when the kindness of God our Savior and his love toward mankind appeared,

paite: diktatna a i thilhihte ziak hilou, azahngaihna ziak a pianthakna a sawp in leh Kha Siangthou a thaksakna in eite ahon hondamta hi.
english: not by works of righteousness which we did ourselves, but according to his mercy, he saved us through the washing of regeneration and renewing by the Holy Spirit,

paite: Huai Kha Siangthou, Jesu Khrist i Hondampa ziak in nakpitak in i tung ah asungbota hi.
english: whom he poured out on us richly through Jesus Christ our Savior;

paite: Huchi a ahehpihna a siamtansak a om in, lametna a tangtawn hinna gouluahte i hihtheihna ding in.
english: that being justified by his grace, we might be made heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

paite: Hiai thugen adik ahi. Hiai thilte na phut tinten ka hon deih hi, huchi a Pathian gingtasate'n thil hoih hih ding a apilvan theihna ding un; hiaite mihingte a ding in ahoih in aphatuam uhi.
english: This saying is faithful, and concerning these things I desire that you insist confidently, so that those who have believed God may be careful to maintain good works. These things are good and profitable to men;

paite: Himahleh dotna haihuai, khangthu suina, kiselna, dan thu a kilaina nungngatsan in; huaite thil phatuam lou leh bangmah lou ahi.
english: but shun foolish questionings, genealogies, strife, and disputes about the law; for they are unprofitable and vain.

paite: Ginna tuam neimi zaw khatvei nihvei hilh nung in deih ke'n.
english: Avoid a factious man after a first and second warning,

paite: Huchibang mi lampial leh gilou ahi chih thei in, amah mah siam louh akitangsak ahi.
english: knowing that such a one is perverted and sinful, being self-condemned.

paite: Artemas hiam, Taikikas hiam, na kiang a ka hon sawl chiang in, Nikopolis ah ka kiang ah hong pai teitei in; hiai mun a phalbi zat ka tum hi.
english: When I send Artemas to you, or Tychicus, be diligent to come to me to Nicopolis, for I have determined to winter there.

paite: Dansiam, Zenas leh Apollos azinna ua bangkim ataksaplouhna ding un, phatuamngaitak in na panpih un.
english: Send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey speedily, that nothing may be lacking for them.

paite: I mite'n leng ataksap khawktakte uh asuktuah theihna ding un leh gah lou a a-omlouhna ding un thil hoih hih a kuhkal ding in zil uhen.
english: Let our people also learn to maintain good works to meet necessary needs, that they may not be unfruitful.

paite: Ka kiang a om tengteng in chibai ahon buk uhi. Ginna a kei hon itte chibai hon buksak in. Na vek ua kiang ah hehpihna om hen, Amen.
english: All who are with me greet you. Greet those who love us in faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.

paite: Darias akum nihna, akha giatna in, iddo tapa, Berekiah tapa, Zekariah, zawlnei kiang ah TOUPA thu ahong tung a,
english: In the eighth month, in the second year of Darius, Yahweh’s word came to the prophet Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, saying,

paite: "Na pipute uh tung ah TOUPA nakpitak in alungkim kei hi," chi in.
english: “Yahweh was very displeased with your fathers.

paite: Huaiziak in nang akiang uah, huchibang in sepaihte' TOUPA'N achi: "Ka kiang ah hong kik un, sepaihte' TOUPA'N achi, huan na kiang uah ka hong kik ding, sepaihte' TOUPA'N achi," chi in.
english: Therefore tell them, Yahweh of Armies says: ‘Return to me,’ says Yahweh of Armies, ‘and I will return to you,’ says Yahweh of Armies.

paite: Hichibang in sepaihte' TOUPA'N achi, "Tu in na omdan gilou ua kipan leh na thilhih giloute ua kipan hong kik un," chi a zawlnei masate'n agenna uh, na pipute uh bang in om kei un; himahleh amau hon za kei ua, hon ngaikhe sam kei uh, sepaihte' TOUPA'N achi.
english: Don’t you be like your fathers, to whom the former prophets proclaimed, saying: Yahweh of Armies says, ‘Return now from your evil ways and from your evil doings;’ but they didn’t hear nor listen to me, says Yahweh.

paite: Na pipute uh tua koi a omta ahi ua? Huan azawlneite uh tangtawn in ahing uhia?
english: Your fathers, where are they? And the prophets, do they live forever?

paite: Himahleh ka thute leh ka dan thusehte, ka sikha zawlneite thupiak a ka piakte, huaite'n na pipute uh delhphata uh ahi kei maw? Huan akihei ua, "Sepaihte' TOUPA'N i tung ua hih dia angaihtuah bang in, i omdan bang zel in leh i thilhihte bang zel a i tung ua hih ahita ve," achi uhi.
english: But my words and my decrees, which I commanded my servants the prophets, didn’t they overtake your fathers? “Then they repented and said, ‘Just as Yahweh of Armies determined to do to us, according to our ways and according to our practices, so he has dealt with us.’”

paite: Darias akum nihna, Sebat kha, akha sawm-le-khat, ani sawmnih-le-li ni in, Iddo tapa, Berekiah tapa Zekariah, zawlnei kiang ah, TOUPA thu ahong tung a,
english: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month, which is the month Shebat, in the second year of Darius, Yahweh’s word came to the prophet Zechariah the son of Berechiah, the son of Iddo, saying,

paite: "Zan in mengmuhna in mi khat sakol san tung a tuang, munliap a om muisingte lak a dingh ka mu a, anunglam ah sakolte a-om ua, asan, asanpuang leh angou ahi uhi.
english: “I had a vision in the night, and behold, a man riding on a red horse, and he stood among the myrtle trees that were in a ravine; and behind him there were red, brown, and white horses.

paite: Huchi in 'Aw ka toupa, hiaite bang ahi ua?' ka chi a, huan kei hon houpih angel in ka kiang ah, ‘Hiaite bang ahi ua ka hon ensak ding,' achi hi.
english: Then I asked, ‘My lord, what are these?’” The angel who talked with me said to me, “I will show you what these are.”

paite: Huai muising lak a dingpa'n adawng a, 'Hiaite leitung a kivialleh a vak dia TOUPA'N asawlte ahi uh,' achi hi.
english: The man who stood among the myrtle trees answered, “They are the ones Yahweh has sent to go back and forth through the earth.”

paite: "Huchi in huai muising lak a dingh TOUPA angel adawng ua, 'Leitung ah kivialleh in ka vakta ua, ngai in, leitung tengteng atu kinken a, akhawl dide hi,' " achi uhi.
english: They reported to Yahweh’s angel who stood among the myrtle trees, and said, “We have walked back and forth through the earth, and behold, all the earth is at rest and in peace.”

paite: Huan TOUPA angel in adawng a, "Aw sepaihte' TOUPA, hiai kum sawmsagih na hehkhum, Jerusalem tung leh Judah khopite tung ah bang tan zahngaihna nei lou ding na hia?" achi hi.
english: Then Yahweh’s angel replied, “O Yahweh of Armies, how long will you not have mercy on Jerusalem and on the cities of Judah, against which you have had indignation these seventy years?”

paite: Huchi in TOUPA'N thuhoihte, thu lungmuanhuaite a kei hon houpih angel adawng hi.
english: Yahweh answered the angel who talked with me with kind and comforting words.

paite: Huchi in kei hon houpih angel in ka kiang ah, hichibang in sepaihte' TOUPA'N achi: "Thikthu setak in Jerusalem leh Zion ka deihthoh ahi, chi in nang kikou in, chi in.
english: So the angel who talked with me said to me, “Proclaim, saying, ‘Yahweh of Armies says: “I am jealous for Jerusalem and for Zion with a great jealousy.

paite: Huan bangmah awlmoh lou namte tung ah ka lungkim kei ding a; neukha lel a ka lung hih louh lai in, siatna athupisak semsem uhi.
english: I am very angry with the nations that are at ease; for I was but a little displeased, but they added to the calamity.”

paite: Huaiziak in hichibang in TOUPA'N achi: Zahngaihnate toh Jerusalem ah ka kik nawnta a, asung ah inn lam ahi ding," chi in.
english: Therefore Yahweh says: “I have returned to Jerusalem with mercy. My house shall be built in it,” says Yahweh of Armies, “and a line shall be stretched out over Jerusalem.”’

paite: Hichibang in sepaihte' TOUPA'N achi: "Hauhsakna ziak in ka khopite akiphalh ding a; TOUPA'N Zion alungmuan in, Jerusalem atel lai ding hi, chi in kikou behlap lai in," chi in.
english: “Proclaim further, saying, ‘Yahweh of Armies says: “My cities will again overflow with prosperity, and Yahweh will again comfort Zion, and will again choose Jerusalem.”’”

paite: Huan ka dak a, ngai in kii li ka mu hi.
english: I lifted up my eyes and saw, and behold, four horns.

paite: Kei hon houpih angel kiang ah, "Hiaite bang hi ding ahia?" ka chi a. Ama'n, "Hiaite Judah, Israel leh Jerusalem hawlzak mite ahi uh," chi in ahon dawng hi.
english: I asked the angel who talked with me, “What are these?” He answered me, “These are the horns which have scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem.”

paite: Huchi in TOUPA'n siksekmi li ahon ensak hi.
english: Yahweh showed me four craftsmen.

paite: Huchi in ke'n, "Bang hih dia hiaite hong uh ahi ua?" ka chi hi. Ama'n thu agen a, "Kuamah in alu adaksaklouhna dia, Judah dalhzaksak hiai kiite ahi uh; himahleh hiaite, dalhzaksak ding a Judah gam tung a akii uh sangsak namte dou ding leh akiite uh paikhe ding a hong paite ahi uh," achi hi.
english: Then I asked, “What are these coming to do?” He said, “These are the horns which scattered Judah, so that no man lifted up his head; but these have come to terrify them, to cast down the horns of the nations that lifted up their horn against the land of Judah to scatter it.”

paite: Vuah nanung hun in TOUPA vuah ngen un, meipite bawlpa TOUPA mahmah, huchi in vuahphinte, gam a loupate kiang ah, amaute ape ding.
english: Ask of Yahweh rain in the spring time, Yahweh who makes storm clouds, and he gives rain showers to everyone for the plants in the field.

paite: Milimte'n bangmah lou thu agen un, aisante'n zuau amu uh; mang zuauthei agen ua, athawn lel in alungmuan uh; huaiziak in belamte bang in amau lampi ah apai ua, belamchingmi a-om louh ziak in hihgim in a-om uhi.
english: For the teraphim have spoken vanity, and the diviners have seen a lie; and they have told false dreams. They comfort in vain. Therefore they go their way like sheep. They are oppressed, because there is no shepherd.

paite: "Belamching mite tung ah ka hehna apuakzak a, aheutute uh ka gawt ding, sepaihte' TOUPA'N Judah inkote, abelamte avehta a, kidouna a sakol hoih bang in amaute abawl ding hi.
english: My anger is kindled against the shepherds, and I will punish the male goats, for Yahweh of Armies has visited his flock, the house of Judah, and will make them as his majestic horse in the battle.

paite: Amah a kipan in aning a suang, amah a kipan puanin khetphim amah a kipan kidouna thalpeu, amah a kipan vaihawm tengteng ahong paikhe ding hi.
english: From him will come the cornerstone, from him the tent peg, from him the battle bow, from him every ruler together.

paite: Kidouna a kongzing a buannawi a amelmate uh childen in, mihatte bang in a-om ding ua; akiang ua TOUPA a-om ziak in adou ding uh; sakol tung a tuangte hih lungzin in a-om ding uhi."
english: They will be as mighty men, treading down muddy streets in the battle. They will fight, because Yahweh is with them. The riders on horses will be confounded.

paite: "Judah inkote ka hatsak ding a, Joseph inkote ka hondam ding, amaute ka hon pi nawn ding a, amau tung ah zahngaihna ka nei; huchi in ka paihkhiak het louh bang ahong hi ding uh; TOUPA a Pathian uh ka hi a, amaute ka dawng ding hi.
english: “I will strengthen the house of Judah, and I will save the house of Joseph. I will bring them back, for I have mercy on them. They will be as though I had not cast them off, for I am Yahweh their God, and I will hear them.

paite: Ephraim mite mihatpa in a-om ding ua, uain ziak in alungtang uh akipak ding a; ahi, atate un huai amu ding ua, akipak ding uh; TOUPA ah alungtang uh akipak ding hi.
english: Ephraim will be like a mighty man, and their heart will rejoice as through wine. Yes, their children will see it and rejoice. Their heart will be glad in Yahweh.

paite: Amau ka khutvan ding a, amau ka kaikhawm ding; amau ka tanta hi; apun khitsa bang un apung ding uh.
english: I will signal for them and gather them, for I have redeemed them. They will increase as they were before.

paite: Namte lak ah hawldalh mah leng; gam gamlate ah kei ahon theigige ding uh; huchi in atate uh toh ka kiang ah ahong kik nawn ding uhi.
english: I will sow them among the peoples. They will remember me in far countries. They will live with their children and will return.

paite: Aigupta gam a pan ka pi nawn ding a, Assuria a kipan ka pikik nawn ding hi; Gilead leh Lebanon gam ah amau ka pilut ding; amaute a dia mun akidaih louh dong in
english: I will bring them again also out of the land of Egypt, and gather them out of Assyria. I will bring them into the land of Gilead and Lebanon; and there won’t be room enough for them.

paite: gimthuakna tuipi apalkai ding ua, tuipi a tui kihawtte khet in a-om ding uh, huchi in Nile luipi thukna tengteng akang vek ding; Assuria kisaktheihna koihniam in a-om dia, Aigupta kumpi chiang apaimang vengveng ding hi.
english: He will pass through the sea of affliction, and will strike the waves in the sea, and all the depths of the Nile will dry up; and the pride of Assyria will be brought down, and the scepter of Egypt will depart.

paite: Huan TOUPA ah amau ka hihhat ding a; amin in avaktou un avaksuk ding uh," TOUPA'N achi.
english: I will strengthen them in Yahweh. They will walk up and down in his name,” says Yahweh.

paite: Aw Le Lebanon, mei in na sidar singte akattum theihna ding in na kongkhakte hong in.
english: Open your doors, Lebanon, that the fire may devour your cedars.

paite: Aw meilah sing, mau vongvong in, Sidar sing apukta ngal a, ahoih tatate hihsiat a a-om ziak un; Aw nou Bashan tosaw singte chiau vongvong un, gammangpi vatpaih ahita hi.
english: Wail, cypress tree, for the cedar has fallen, because the stately ones are destroyed. Wail, you oaks of Bashan, for the strong forest has come down.

paite: Ngai un belamching mite amau vongvong ding ua, na thupina uh loh a a-om ziak in, ngai un humpinelkai ahumham a, Jordan gammang athengta hi!
english: A voice of the wailing of the shepherds! For their glory is destroyed—a voice of the roaring of young lions! For the pride of the Jordan is ruined.

paite: Hichibang in TOUPA ka Pathian in achi hi, "Goh ding belamhon chingpa hong hi in.
english: Yahweh my God says: “Feed the flock of slaughter.

paite: Amau leite'n athat ua, gawt in a-om kei ua; amau zuakte'n TOUPA phat in om hen! Ka hauta uh! Amau chingte'n alainat kei uhi,” achi uhi.
english: Their buyers slaughter them and go unpunished. Those who sell them say, ‘Blessed be Yahweh, for I am rich;’ and their own shepherds don’t pity them.

paite: "Gam a tengte ka hehpih nawn kei ding, TOUPA'N achi. Himahleh ngai in mite michih a-invengte khut ah leh akumpipa khut ah ka pe ding; amau gam agawt ding ua, akhut ua kipan amaute ka hunkhe kei ding," chi in.
english: For I will no more pity the inhabitants of the land,” says Yahweh; “but, behold, I will deliver every one of the men into his neighbor’s hand and into the hand of his king. They will strike the land, and out of their hand I will not deliver them.”

paite: "Huchi in belamte a sumdawngte a dia thah ding a om belamte chingpa ka hong hita hi. Huchi in chiang nih ka kilak a; khat pen 'Deihsakna' ka chi a, adang pen 'Kizopna' ka chi; huchi in belamte ka vak hi.
english: So I fed the flock to be slaughtered, especially the oppressed of the flock. I took for myself two staffs. The one I called “Favor” and the other I called “Union”, and I fed the flock.

paite: Huan kha khat in belamchingmi thum ka satkhia hi. Himahleh ka kha in amau achimtak a, amau kha in leng kei ahon chimtak uhi.
english: I cut off the three shepherds in one month; for my soul was weary of them, and their soul also loathed me.

paite: Huaitak in ke'n, 'K'on vak kei ding, asi dingte, si henla, satkhiak a om dingte, satkhiak in om heh; nutsiatte khat-le-khat sa kinetuah uhen,' ka chita hi.
english: Then I said, “I will not feed you. That which dies, let it die; and that which is to be cut off, let it be cut off; and let those who are left eat each other’s flesh.”

paite: Huan 'Deihsakna' kichi ka chiangkhun ka la a, ka sattan a, mite tengteng toh ka thukhun ka bawl ka suksiat theihna ding in.
english: I took my staff Favor and cut it apart, that I might break my covenant that I had made with all the peoples.

paite: Huchi in huai ni in akitanta, huchi in pawlte lak ah agenthei kei hon limsakte'n TOUPA thu ahi chih athei uhi.
english: It was broken in that day; and thus the poor of the flock that listened to me knew that it was Yahweh’s word.

paite: Ke'n akiang uah, 'Hoih a na ngaihtuah ualeh ka loh tak hon pia, un ahihkeileh, tang un,' ka chi hi. Huchi in ka loh tak ding in 'dangka shekel sawmthum' abuk uhi.
english: I said to them, “If you think it best, give me my wages; and if not, keep them.” So they weighed for my wages thirty pieces of silver.

paite: "Huan TOUPA'N ka kiang ah, 'Ka man ding a aseh uh, man hoih belvelmi kiang ah khia in,' achi hi. Dangka shekel sawmthum ka la a TOUPA' inn a, belvelmi kiang ah ka khia hi.
